chapters.title: Chapter 901
paragraphs: Silence.
Perfect silence settled over the Grand Banquet Hall. Not even the faintest breath could be heard.
Along with it came countless eyes, wide with shock, all fixed on one person.
*What... did he just say?*
*What on earth did I just hear?*
Everyone wondered the same thing. As they stared at the young man, they recalled the words that had just rung through the hall.
“Kill them if you want, or spare them if you want. Isn’t that what Your Majesty does best?”
Everyone had heard him clearly.

They doubted their memories once, twice, ten times, but reality refused to change. Forgetting all about decorum, people gaped at him, barely managing to swallow the curses on the tips of their tongues.
*That crazy bastard.*
Even *crazy bastard* fell far short of describing what Jin Taekyung had done.
He had provoked the Emperor to his face.
Mocked him.
The Emperor, of all people.
The usurper who had cut down tens of thousands of political enemies like a farmer reaping a harvest, then built the strongest centralized regime since Taizu, founder of the Great Nation.
*He’s insane. Completely insane.*

The officials in the lowest seats, their ranks too low to sit anywhere else, and even the high-ranking ministers at the heart of the political world all turned deathly pale and pressed their lips together.
Something had happened that could never be allowed to happen.
Calling it treason would hardly be a stretch. What came next was obvious.
They would die. Die, and die again.
Jin Taekyung and his entire family, along with everyone connected to them, would vanish like dew on the execution ground.
And there was every chance the Embroidered Uniform Guard’s death list would include several people with no connection to any of it.
The late Emperor’s loyal subjects.
It wasn’t hard to predict that some of those who considered Prince Shangshan the rightful heir would become targets.
Evidence? Justification?
Neither mattered.
Both could be manufactured.
Once the torture instruments tore through their flesh and muscle, even the most loyal subject would writhe in pain and beg for death.
The imperial torturers knew how to turn lies into truth and truth into lies. That work had once belonged to the East Depot, but it had long since passed to the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
In other words, the sword was in one man’s hands alone.
The Emperor’s.
One order from him, and it would all be over.
Jin Taekyung had already given him grounds for punishment. No one could say whom the Emperor’s blade might cut down.
Even if the final target were Prince Shangshan.
*How could he do something this absurd? What on earth is he thinking...?*
*Grit.*
Some of the assembled officials clenched their teeth to hold back groans.
Each of them either supported Prince Shangshan in secret or had signed the pledge and dreamed of a restoration. To them, the whole situation felt like a terrible calamity.
Jin Taekyung had entered the imperial court as Prince Shangshan’s guest. The prince wouldn’t be able to escape responsibility, either.
*Heh... So Heaven’s Mandate is leaving the Great Nation.*
Those who knew nothing of the restoration lamented the heavens.
*The plan’s gone off course, but we have no choice. We may have to act right now...*
Those who had signed the pledge steeled themselves and watched Ma Sanbao, their faces rigid. The moment he gave the order, they would move.
But then—
“Yes. You are right.”
The Emperor broke the long silence, plunging everyone into shock once more.
“And a man who wishes to become a sage king does not punish those who speak the truth.”
“Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
Standing at the center of the silence, the Emperor continued evenly.
“In the name of the Son of Heaven, I forgive the disrespect you have shown me.”
Forgive.
He’d said he forgave him.
The very man who had ruthlessly slaughtered tens of thousands.
The cruel Emperor who had launched a rebellion and a great purge.
Everyone who had been at a loss for words stared blankly at the back of the absolute ruler—everyone except one person.
Reading the sliver of emotion the Emperor hadn’t quite managed to hide from his face, Jin Taekyung muttered to himself.
*So that’s how you’re playing it.*
Provoking the Emperor had been a gamble with his life. If it failed, it could throw every plan the restoration army had made into disarray.
*That’s why it had to be now.*
And the gamble had paid off.
He had gained a crucial key. The Emperor’s answer had also settled a question he’d hardly dared ask himself.
*Forgiveness, after that? It makes no sense.*
Except in one case.
Jin Taekyung quietly swallowed the rest of his thought.
The scattered pieces of the puzzle began to fall into place. His head, which had felt ready to burst moments ago, gradually cleared. As his mind settled, a new path came into view.
But he still didn’t have every answer.
*But why on earth...?*
He started to send the Emperor a Sound Transmission.
Or rather, he would have, if someone hadn’t arrived just then.
“How heartening to hear that Your Majesty wishes to become such a merciful sage king.”
Jin Taekyung reacted a little faster than the Emperor. Baek Yeon reacted faster than Taekyung.
Somewhere only five *jang* away, an old man with pale skin appeared without a sound. In a hoarse, aged voice, he continued, cupping his hands toward the Emperor.
“The late Emperor would be pleased as well. Would he not?”
*Rustle.*
The old man slowly raised his head, setting his long white hair swaying.
The Emperor’s stiff face was reflected in gray eyes that held the weight of many years. A dry voice emerged between cracked lips.
“Your servant Wei Zhong, Seal-Holding Eunuch of the East Depot, pays his respects to Your Majesty.”
The moment I saw Wei Zhong, I reflexively thought of an old fantasy movie I’d watched as a kid.
A vast fantasy world. A party of heroes from different races setting out to destroy a certain necklace that was the source of the Demon King’s power.
And one of its central characters: an old mage.
“...Gandalf?”
The white hair that looked long enough to reach his knees. The gray eyes.
Strictly speaking, he looked more like *a very sick Gandalf*, but I couldn’t deny the resemblance.
The slight problem was that I’d said it aloud without realizing.
*Ah.*
I shut my mouth as soon as I caught myself, but it was too late. Everyone who’d briefly looked elsewhere had turned back to me, including the Emperor.
And the very sick Gandalf. Wei Zhong.
“You must be the very man I’ve heard so much about.”
What was I supposed to say to that?
I thought it over for a moment, then gave a small nod instead. Wei Zhong let out a snort and turned back toward the Emperor.
“A truly rude man. Wouldn’t you agree, Your Majesty?”
The Emperor didn’t answer.
He gazed at Wei Zhong with eyes sunk deep in thought, and only spoke once the air around them had grown so cold it seemed frozen.
“I was about to send someone for you, since you were nowhere to be seen... It’s been a long time, Cang Gong. Have you been well?”
“After a rather long period of recuperation, I’ve finally recovered enough to move about. I owe it all to Your Majesty’s grace.”
“My grace? Are you certain?”
“Even the finest physicians couldn’t guarantee I would live. Seeing how much I’ve recovered, surely it must be Heaven’s will. And so I owe it all to Your Majesty, the Son of Heaven.”
“That’s unfortunate. If you’d had the decoction made as the imperial physician I sent advised, you might have overcome your illness sooner.”
“I beg your forgiveness. However, I feared my old body couldn’t withstand the medicine prepared by the imperial physicians, so I had no choice but to recuperate instead. But...”
Concern suddenly clouded Wei Zhong’s face as he studied the Emperor.
“Perhaps it has simply been too long since I last saw you, but Your Majesty does not look well. Has illness taken hold of your august person?”
A chill passed through the Emperor’s eyes, already hard with displeasure.
“There’s no need to worry. It isn’t as bad as you fear.”
“Then I’m greatly relieved. Now that you’ve become a sage king who shows such mercy, you must rule the realm for ten thousand years—ten thousand times ten thousand years.”
I could feel it.
The invisible blades the Emperor and Cang Gong kept trading.
And the immense qi now pouring from the Emperor.
*Rrrrmmm.*
The air around us churned. Several nearby officials went pale and trembled as though seized by a chill.
His title overshadowed it, but the Emperor was a Supreme Peak master who had entered the realm of the superhuman.
But...
*Cang Gong is different. That man is something else.*
I’d known it from the moment he appeared.
That pale old man who looked like Gandalf was a greater master than anyone else here.
*Even Baek Yeon.*
In a fight between Supreme Peak masters, life and death could be decided in an instant.
The fact that Cang Gong had come within five *jang* of us without me sensing him meant he’d all but seized the initiative.
*Now I see why Ma Sanbao was so confident.*

From what I could sense, Cang Gong and So Gyo were evenly matched. If Jeok Cheongang and the other fighters who hadn’t yet reached the Grand Banquet Hall joined the restoration army, they could bring down So Gyo with ease.
Though So Gyo herself had yet to appear.
*She’s probably guarding Prince Shangshan somewhere else.*
The prince was a crucial key. Neither the restoration army nor the Emperor could afford to let him fall into the enemy’s hands.
Apparently, I wasn’t the only one thinking about him.
“Your Majesty. Perhaps the recent storms have made the weather unusually chilly today. Might Your Majesty show some mercy for the sake of those poor officials, who are trembling over there?”
Cang Gong indicated the shivering officials. His manner was respectful and relaxed, but there was a barb in his words. Then he spoke again, as though a thought had just occurred to him.
“By the way, why are Prince Shangshan and the pregnant Consort nowhere to be seen? As members of the imperial family, surely they ought to grace this occasion alongside Your Majesty—”
“Shut your mouth, Wei Zhong.”
Baek Yeon cut him off, his voice hard. He was about to step forward when—
“Enough.”
The Emperor raised a hand to stop him and fixed Wei Zhong with a cold stare.
“You needn’t concern yourself, Cang Gong. Both of them are already on their way.”
“I’m deeply grateful for Your Majesty’s grace. At last, I’ll meet the heir who will one day rule this vast Great Nation.”
“Yes. You will.”
Neither man said anything more.
Nor did either bother to ask the other which heir he truly had in mind, or whom the other considered the heir.
They would wait for the banquet to reach its height. For the fuse to burn all the way down.
And so would I.
“Excuse me. It looks like you two are about done talking. Could I say something, if you don’t mind?”
The Emperor answered.
“What is it?”
“Nothing much. It looks like you’re heading up to the seats of honor, so I was hoping I could move too. Preferably next to Cang Gong.”
“...You want to change seats?”
The officials, who had been frozen in place, all turned to glare at me as though they wanted to tear me apart. While the Emperor searched for words, Cang Gong spoke instead.
“Is there... some particular reason?”
I gave him my most confident, dashing look.
“The seats up there seem to get more side dishes.”
Of course, I didn’t look particularly dashing.

chapters.title: Chapter 902
paragraphs: This might have been a first in the history of the Great Nation.
A ruffian from the martial world who held no official post and didn’t even carry an identity token, seated among the court’s high officials at a grand banquet presided over by the Emperor himself.
*The first, and probably the last.*
Even considering the short history of the Great Nation, which had only lasted three generations so far, it was a feat unlikely ever to be repeated.
Yet almost no one spoke up against this insult to the imperial family’s dignity.
Not unless they were among the handful of ministers with unwavering convictions and courage.
“Your Majesty! Forgive my boldness, but seating that man so close to you—”
“It is the imperial decree.”
“...A wise decision indeed!”
As it turned out, even conviction and courage crumbled like a sandcastle struck by a wave when faced with the Emperor.
Especially when that Emperor’s hobby—and specialty—was purging people.
Thanks to him, I took my seat before an even more lavish spread without further trouble.
*Smack. Smack-smack. Slurp.*
As I inhaled one dish after another, the people around me stared, their eyes twitching at every sound.
When I showed off the godlike noodle-slurping technique I’d honed on ramen, groans broke out all around.
“Good heavens.”
“Have you ever seen such a low-class bastard...?”
“That’s enough to kill what little appetite I had. Look—even Cang Gong hasn’t touched his food.”
At that last remark, I glanced over. Cang Gong was watching me steadily with his gray eyes.
*Hmm. Was that too much?*
“Pay no mind to them. Keep eating. Is it really that good?”
At Cang Gong’s calm question, I answered.
“Definithely delishious.”
“I see. But perhaps you should finish what’s in your mouth first.”
“Oh.”
I swallowed the mouthful crammed into my cheeks, then spoke again.
“It’s definitely good. There are plenty of side dishes, too.”
Cang Gong nodded.
“I understood you the first time. My hearing isn’t that bad. Besides, the imperial chefs have long been renowned for their cooking.”
“Then why aren’t you eating?”
“I don’t have much of an appetite. It’s been that way for some time.”
“Hmm. Well, that’s a relief. I thought I’d put you off your food.”
“Don’t worry about that. I’ve been this way since I was young. Though it is a little disappointing that even the finest, rarest delicacies feel like grains of sand in my mouth now.”
Cang Gong looked away from me and down at the table before him, his face expressionless.
It held enough food to make its legs bow under the weight, yet his hands rested neatly on his knees and never moved toward it.
Hands with no color in them—white, or rather, pale as a corpse’s.
I studied him. Despite sitting right beside me, he barely gave off any sense of presence. Then I quietly moved my lips.
“When are we going to start?”
At that moment—
*Vrrrm.*
A subtle, chilling qi sealed off the space around us. Anyone who wasn’t paying close attention would never have noticed it.
Remarkable.
Cang Gong had shut out sound with a flawless barrier of internal energy. He spoke.
“I’ll give the signal.”
“I think now would be the perfect time.”
“As long as that woman called So Gyo remains by Prince Shangshan’s side, we can’t act rashly. Even if we take the Emperor’s head, everything will be for nothing if we can’t secure His Highness.”
“That’s true.”
“Besides, your master is still waiting outside the banquet hall. The Fire King is essential if we’re to defeat So Gyo.”
“I don’t know about that. I’d say you’re every bit as formidable a master as my teacher.”

“This old man was able to overcome a grave Internal Injury and attend today thanks to the good fortune of gaining insight during my recovery. The more important the matter, the more carefully it must be handled, don’t you think?”
*Yeah, that made sense.*
I nodded naturally and resumed moving the chopsticks I’d set down for a moment.
Cang Gong watched me as if I were some strange creature, then spoke.
“You look like you haven’t eaten in days.”
“You’ve got that right. I’ve barely eaten anything for two days.”
“A master of your caliber should be able to endure a little hunger.”
“Why should I have to? I believe in eating a hearty meal before a fight.”
“Are you nervous?”
“I am. My stomach is.”
“You really do take after your master. It takes quite a nerve to sit here eating like this, just as I’d heard.”
“Did you hear anything else about me?”
“That your martial arts are unparalleled for someone your age, and that you’re resourceful and tenacious enough to survive any crisis.”
“Sounds about right.”
“That was the abbreviated version. The East Depot has eyes and ears throughout the land, and their reports never fail to surprise me. One of the most recent was particularly unexpected.”
“May I ask what it was? What could surprise even Cang Gong?”
“The Murim Alliance reinforcements.”
“Ah.”

“I truly didn’t expect that. I thought the Murim Alliance had already deployed most of its forces throughout the land to deal with sudden attacks by Dark Heaven, which could appear anywhere at any time.”
Instead of answering, I lifted my cup and took a drink. The fragrant aroma of a truly fine liquor filled my mouth, and it went down smoothly.
Any intoxication that should have followed vanished without a trace when it met my Scorching Yang Qi.
“I hear Dark Heaven uses the strangest supernatural powers. Did the Alliance really have enough strength left to form a reserve force?”
“If they didn’t, the reinforcements wouldn’t be coming.”
“They’re coming because the Alliance had the strength to spare... Yes, I suppose so.”
Cang Gong was gazing steadily at me with his gray eyes when—
“Enough.”
The Emperor’s resonant voice rang out, and in the same instant, the beautiful music that had filled the grand banquet hall vanished as if it had been washed away.
Those who had been whispering to one another, those who had been drinking with solemn faces—even the musicians and dancers forcing themselves to perform in that atmosphere—all fell silent.
Everyone stopped moving and turned toward the Emperor, following his voice and gaze.
“My heir approaches. He shall inherit this continent and the Great Nation that will endure for the next thousand years. Receive him with all due ceremony.”
An unmistakable declaration of his heir.
Everyone had expected it, yet some part of them had thought it couldn’t possibly happen. Now that the moment had arrived, shock swept through the banquet hall.
But while their minds raced, their bodies were already bending in the prescribed bows toward a newly arrived eight-horse carriage.
*Boom. Boom-boom. Boom-boom-boom!*
The drummer’s vigorous beat made the air shudder. As anticipation quietly built, the carriage door opened and someone stepped out.
*Swish.*

The hem of a splendid red palace gown brushed the ground. The woman stepped lightly onto the back of a palace attendant prostrated before the carriage and descended. Her alluring beauty drew a low gasp from somewhere in the hall.
“Good heavens.”
“It can’t be...”
It was tactless, but I understood.
The woman was beautiful enough to topple a kingdom.
*No wonder the City Lord of Sichuan Province fell so hard for her.*
I thought to myself as I looked at the woman—or rather, Aehyang.

Until only a few months ago, she had been the City Lord of Sichuan Province’s favored concubine. Now she walked beneath the Embroidered Uniform Guard’s close protection, stroking her belly with an uneasy look on her face.
And while everyone’s eyes followed her, I saw someone else emerge from the still-open carriage door.
A face that still belonged to a child.
Yet his expression and stride were bolder than those of any young man.
Prince Shangshan, Zhu Bao.
As I watched Prince Shangshan stride up the long staircase, I wondered what to say.
How should I greet the young prince after several days apart?
I didn’t have to think for long.
“Have you been well?”
My Sound Transmission crossed the space between us, and Prince Shangshan stopped in his tracks. I let out a quiet laugh to myself and moved my lips again.
“Are you still keeping the item I entrusted to you safe?”
After a brief pause, he started walking again. Prince Shangshan didn’t look my way. Instead, he flicked the sleeve covering the back of his hand.

sentences.text: This might have been a first in the history of the Great Nation.
A ruffian from the martial world who held no official post and didn’t even carry an identity token, seated among the court’s high officials at a grand banquet presided over by the Emperor himself.
*The first, and probably the last.*
Even considering the short history of the Great Nation, which had only lasted three generations so far, it was a feat unlikely ever to be repeated.
Yet almost no one spoke up against this insult to the imperial family’s dignity.
Not unless they were among the handful of ministers with unwavering convictions and courage.
“Your Majesty!
Forgive my boldness, but seating that man so close to you—”
“It is the imperial decree.”
“...A wise decision indeed!”
As it turned out, even conviction and courage crumbled like a sandcastle struck by a wave when faced with the Emperor.
Especially when that Emperor’s hobby—and specialty—was purging people.
Thanks to him, I took my seat before an even more lavish spread without further trouble.
*Smack.
Smack-smack.
Slurp.*
As I inhaled one dish after another, the people around me stared, their eyes twitching at every sound.
When I showed off the godlike noodle-slurping technique I’d honed on ramen, groans broke out all around.
“Good heavens.”
“Have you ever seen such a low-class bastard...?”
“That’s enough to kill what little appetite I had.
Look—even Cang Gong hasn’t touched his food.”
At that last remark, I glanced over.
Cang Gong was watching me steadily with his gray eyes.
*Hmm.
Was that too much?*
“Pay no mind to them.
Keep eating.
Is it really that good?”
At Cang Gong’s calm question, I answered.
“Definithely delishious.”
“I see.
But perhaps you should finish what’s in your mouth first.”
“Oh.”
I swallowed the mouthful crammed into my cheeks, then spoke again.
“It’s definitely good.
There are plenty of side dishes, too.”
Cang Gong nodded.
“I understood you the first time.
My hearing isn’t that bad.
Besides, the imperial chefs have long been renowned for their cooking.”
“Then why aren’t you eating?”
“I don’t have much of an appetite.
It’s been that way for some time.”
“Hmm.
Well, that’s a relief.
I thought I’d put you off your food.”
“Don’t worry about that.
I’ve been this way since I was young.
Though it is a little disappointing that even the finest, rarest delicacies feel like grains of sand in my mouth now.”
Cang Gong looked away from me and down at the table before him, his face expressionless.
It held enough food to make its legs bow under the weight, yet his hands rested neatly on his knees and never moved toward it.
Hands with no color in them—white, or rather, pale as a corpse’s.
I studied him.
Despite sitting right beside me, he barely gave off any sense of presence.
Then I quietly moved my lips.
“When are we going to start?”
At that moment—
*Vrrrm.*
A subtle, chilling qi sealed off the space around us.
Anyone who wasn’t paying close attention would never have noticed it.
Remarkable.
Cang Gong had shut out sound with a flawless barrier of internal energy.
He spoke.
“I’ll give the signal.”
“I think now would be the perfect time.”
“As long as that woman called So Gyo remains by Prince Shangshan’s side, we can’t act rashly.
Even if we take the Emperor’s head, everything will be for nothing if we can’t secure His Highness.”
“That’s true.”
“Besides, your master is still waiting outside the banquet hall.
The Fire King is essential if we’re to defeat So Gyo.”
“I don’t know about that.
I’d say you’re every bit as formidable a master as my teacher.”
“This old man was able to overcome a grave Internal Injury and attend today thanks to the good fortune of gaining insight during my recovery.
The more important the matter, the more carefully it must be handled, don’t you think?”
*Yeah, that made sense.*
I nodded naturally and resumed moving the chopsticks I’d set down for a moment.
Cang Gong watched me as if I were some strange creature, then spoke.
“You look like you haven’t eaten in days.”
“You’ve got that right.
I’ve barely eaten anything for two days.”
“A master of your caliber should be able to endure a little hunger.”
“Why should I have to?
I believe in eating a hearty meal before a fight.”
“Are you nervous?”
“I am.
My stomach is.”
“You really do take after your master.
It takes quite a nerve to sit here eating like this, just as I’d heard.”
“Did you hear anything else about me?”
“That your martial arts are unparalleled for someone your age, and that you’re resourceful and tenacious enough to survive any crisis.”
“Sounds about right.”
“That was the abbreviated version.
The East Depot has eyes and ears throughout the land, and their reports never fail to surprise me.
One of the most recent was particularly unexpected.”
“May I ask what it was?
What could surprise even Cang Gong?”
“The Murim Alliance reinforcements.”
“Ah.”
“I truly didn’t expect that.
I thought the Murim Alliance had already deployed most of its forces throughout the land to deal with sudden attacks by Dark Heaven, which could appear anywhere at any time.”
Instead of answering, I lifted my cup and took a drink.
The fragrant aroma of a truly fine liquor filled my mouth, and it went down smoothly.
Any intoxication that should have followed vanished without a trace when it met my Scorching Yang Qi.
“I hear Dark Heaven uses the strangest supernatural powers.
Did the Alliance really have enough strength left to form a reserve force?”
“If they didn’t, the reinforcements wouldn’t be coming.”
“They’re coming because the Alliance had the strength to spare...
Yes, I suppose so.”

“Enough.”
The Emperor’s resonant voice rang out, and in the same instant, the beautiful music that had filled the grand banquet hall vanished as if it had been washed away.
Those who had been whispering to one another, those who had been drinking with solemn faces—even the musicians and dancers forcing themselves to perform in that atmosphere—all fell silent.
Everyone stopped moving and turned toward the Emperor, following his voice and gaze.
“My heir approaches.

chapters.title: Chapter 903
paragraphs: Some mysteries have no answer, no matter how long you think about them. When that happens, there’s only one thing left to try.
Turn everything upside down.
Forget all the circumstances and clues you’ve gathered so far, and start over from the beginning. That’s the last resort.
Like retracing your steps to find something precious you don’t remember dropping, I went back to the starting point and reconsidered every detail, large and small.
At last, I arrived at a hypothesis.
“The Emperor doesn’t want Prince Shangshan put in danger.”
A faint ripple passed through Cang Gong’s gray eyes.
It appeared and vanished in less time than it took to blink, but I’d been watching his every tiny movement too closely to miss it.
*So it was true.*
The realization struck me, sending a jolt down my spine.
The crowd’s tremendous cheering still hadn’t died down when Cang Gong, who had been gazing steadily at me, spoke.
“When did it start?”
Anyone else might have struggled to understand the question without context. I knew at once what he meant.
When had I started suspecting them?
“So Gyo.”
Yes. That was exactly when.
The day she let me go, despite having every advantage. She couldn’t possibly have failed to stop me.
Nothing I knew, no clue I could find, fully explained her strange behavior. It had stayed with me like a fishbone caught in my throat.
“So Gyo...”
Cang Gong gave a small nod at my brief answer.

“Yes, I suppose it would be. She was the only flaw in this grand scheme. Had I known it would come to this, I should have eliminated that mysterious woman long ago. Even if it meant an all-out war with the Emperor.”
*What?*
I swallowed the question before it could burst out, but I couldn’t hide my momentary shock.
*Even Cang Gong doesn’t know who So Gyo is?*
Cang Gong caught the confusion that had appeared on my face and gave a low laugh.
“From the looks of it, you don’t know who she is either. You don’t even know whether she’s an ally or an enemy.”

“Strange. Very strange. Until just now, I suspected she might be a Murim Alliance spy, but... now I haven’t the faintest idea. Even if she were a master secretly trained by the imperial family, she couldn’t have escaped my notice.”
This time, setting aside the situation I was in, I couldn’t help sharing Cang Gong’s bewilderment.
*Then who is So Gyo?*

If she’d belonged to the Murim Alliance, she would have told me the whole truth before things got to this point. And if she were a master of Dark Heaven or the imperial family, Cang Gong would have known.
But So Gyo was different.
From what I’d been able to determine, she was a third party. Someone who belonged to neither side.
*Who the hell is she?*
Who was So Gyo? What expression was she wearing as she watched us right now? What was she thinking?
And...
*Is she an enemy or an ally?*
I fought the urge to look toward So Gyo, who should have been standing at the top of the stairs in the distance.
Cang Gong and I were only a few steps apart. Taking my eyes off him for even a moment would be suicide.
Of course, the only reason I could afford to stand here provoking him was that I was certain he couldn’t kill me yet.
“You have a fine look in your eyes. Fighting spirit spilling over. But why would that person take an interest in you?”
*That person.*
There was no mistaking the fear and reverence in Cang Gong’s voice as he spoke of someone who wasn’t here.
The Blood Lord, the Western Heaven Demon Lord, and the Southern Heaven Demon Empress had all felt the same way.
Dark Heaven existed because it had a heaven of its own: the Lord of Heaven.

“Tell me. As the person concerned, you might know why that person is searching for you so relentlessly. Is it because you’ve achieved something unprecedented at such a young age? Or is it because of some other worth only that person can recognize?”
His gray eyes, so like a dead man’s, glimmered faintly.
A chill came with that gaze, subtle and terrifying, unlike anything I’d ever felt.
*Hissss.*
I’d stake my life on it: even the Yin-Cold Qi of the Great Snow Fiend, who’d cornered me in Nanman, hadn’t been this intense.
*No. This is different from Yin-Cold Qi.*
Something more primal and pure.
A different kind of power, one I’d never heard of or experienced.
But I overcame my instinctive fear. Enduring the chill seeping into my bones, I answered.
“Why the hell are you asking me, you ball-less bastard?”
Cang Gong stared at me, eyes wide, then smiled faintly.
“Yes, of course you wouldn’t know. How could someone like you presume to fathom that person’s intentions—”
“Yeah. I can look all I want, but I still can’t find your balls.”
“Choose your words carefully. No matter how generously that person has blessed me...”
“Yeah. I could search the whole ocean and still not find your testicles.”
“I chose my words carefully. What’s the problem?”
His faint smile was long gone. Amid the people’s continued cheering, Cang Gong’s tightly shut, pale lips parted.
“What do you think? Surely that person would understand if I merely pulled out your tongue.”
“Sure. The Lord of Heaven might. You’re the one among his followers he worries about most, seeing as you haven’t got any balls. His sore ball—no, his sore finger.”
I nodded in agreement and pointed over Cang Gong’s shoulder.
“But that guy won’t understand.”
In the slowed-down flow of time, everything happened at once.

Cang Gong turned his head to look behind him. I thrust a fist wreathed in flame at him. And a solid palm shot forward like a flash of light, as if reversing time all by itself, intercepting my fist before it could reach anyone.
*BOOM!*
A roar like the sky splitting open brought time rushing back to normal. At the same instant, a powerful shock wave shook the grand banquet hall.
*Crack! Rrrrmm!*
The ground shuddered as though an earthquake had struck.
Screams and shouts erupted on all sides.
Amid the sudden chaos, a pair of gleaming white eyes fixed on me.
“Was that all?”
*Crack.*
His voice was calm, but the immense force squeezing my fist was anything but.
An unknown, ice-cold energy filled his palm, suppressing the flames in mine and snuffing them out.
“Such a shallow trick. I’m disappointed.”
*Crunch. Crunch.*
Agonizing pain shot through my captured fist.
If my muscles and bones hadn’t surpassed the limits of an ordinary human, they would already have been ground to dust.
But I’d endured this much pain more times than I cared to count. And I’d never expected that surprise attack to bring him down.
I’d only needed a signal flare to let everyone know what was happening.
“I’m a little hurt that you think it was just a shallow trick.”
*What?*
“I don’t know if you’ve heard of magic, but I’m about to show you some. Watch closely.”
“What are you—”
The moment Cang Gong frowned—
*BOOOOM!*
Blinding flames swallowed the darkness, and the rock walls that ringed the grand banquet hall like towering ramparts burst apart.
From the place Cang Gong had glanced toward moments earlier, a figure strode out.
“I’ll give you my first and last warning.”
The flames dancing in that damn monk’s eyes looked anything but Buddhist. He swept his gaze across the hall and went on.
“Only step forward if you want your flesh and bones to melt.”
Recognition darkened Cang Gong’s eyes. I smiled.
“Accio, Fire King.”
At the same time, I thrust out my still-free hand toward his chest. He faltered for an instant.
The Flame Divine Palm, at nine-tenths mastery.
*BOOOOM!*
“Huh?”
The young man stopped abruptly and looked back.
Seeing him stare down the road they’d traveled, his brow furrowed, the burly man ahead of him asked, “Hyukmu. What’s wrong?”
“No, it’s just...”
Hyuk Mujin trailed off and clicked his tongue.
“I thought I heard something.”
Taishan raised an eyebrow. “A sound? An enemy?”
“I don’t know. Maybe I imagined it.”
“Then no. That sound Hyukmu heard—Taishan didn’t hear it.”
“But I’m telling you, I’m sure I heard something.”
“Hyukmu. Your martial arts are weak. Taishan could turn you into finely minced five-spice pork if he wanted.”
“...Hey, what the hell? Are you looking down on me?”
“Mm. Honestly, a little.”
“Hyukmu. We can’t stop. We have to go. Everyone’s waiting.”
Hyuk Mujin swallowed his flare of anger and let out a long sigh.
“Yeah, I’m going. I’m going.”
But despite his answer, his steps didn’t come as easily as before.
The road behind him and the walls of the Imperial Capital, growing more distant by the moment, kept appearing before his eyes.
*Damn it. Am I hearing things now, too?*
Annoying as it was, Taishan was probably right that there hadn’t been a sound. If a Peak master a step above him hadn’t heard it, then there was nothing to hear.
Even if Mujin *had* heard something, it must have been the faint noise of an insect or an animal moving.
*Then why do I feel like this?*
Hyuk Mujin frowned harder and thumped his chest.
His heart kept pounding when it hadn’t before, as though an invisible hand were squeezing it tight.
*Something feels wrong.*
Along with the inexplicable unease, the face of someone he’d parted with a few shichen ago suddenly flashed through his mind.
*Just one mission.*
The last voice he’d heard before leaving still echoed in his ears.
*Oh, one more thing.*
*Yes?*
*Be careful. You and everyone else.*
Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung.
Hyuk Mujin had answered the warning with a grin. Then he and the rest of the Fire Dragon Pavilion had left the Imperial Capital, bound for the border between Jiangsu and Zhejiang Provinces.
For the very place written on the note Jin Taekyung had given him.
*The mission’s going fine... so what’s wrong with me?*
Everything was going smoothly, yet his chest felt unbearably tight.
The Captain—Jin Taekyung—had acted so strangely that the memory pricked at him like a fishbone caught in his throat.
Taekyung usually laughed with him over nothing, hit him for getting cheeky, and cursed him without holding back. Today, Mujin had seen none of that.
“Hyukmu!”
Snapping out of his thoughts, Hyuk Mujin realized he’d stopped walking again.
Then he saw his companions waiting a short distance ahead, and his heart sank.
Grave eyes. Troubled faces.
Everyone except Taishan was looking at him the same way.
“Everyone...”
Hyuk Mujin barely swallowed a groan. At last, he thought he understood the unease that had been squeezing his chest.
“Did you all know?”
Namho answered his halting question in a heavy voice.
“Yes. More or less.”
“The Captain told you?”
“No. Senior Jeok gave us a warning beforehand. He knew what choice his Disciple would make.”
“Then why was I the only one—”
“If he’d told you to leave because you’d be a burden, would you have obeyed without a fuss?”
“I don’t like this situation either. No—none of us do.”
For a moment, Hyuk Mujin had nothing to say.
He understood perfectly well how they felt about being burdens instead of help. He understood why Jin Taekyung had lied to send him away.
And it was the truth.
But... but...
*Still, it shouldn’t be like this.*
Hyuk Mujin bit down on his lip until it bled and turned his head. Then, for an instant, he forgot the entire situation and muttered in a dazed voice.
Far away, countless figures moved through the darkness, shaking the forest as they passed.
Too many to count, yet he couldn’t sense a single presence among them.
*What are those?*
The same question arose in everyone’s mind. So did a fear none of them could explain.
This time, instinct rather than reason moved Hyuk Mujin.
No—it moved them all.
*Whoosh!*

I’d stake my life on it: even the Yin-Cold Qi of the Great Snow Fiend, who’d cornered me in Nanman, hadn’t been this intense.
*No.
This is different from Yin-Cold Qi.*
Something more primal and pure.
A different kind of power, one I’d never heard of or experienced.
But I overcame my instinctive fear.
Enduring the chill seeping into my bones, I answered.
“Why the hell are you asking me, you ball-less bastard?”
Cang Gong stared at me, eyes wide, then smiled faintly.
“Yes, of course you wouldn’t know.
How could someone like you presume to fathom that person’s intentions—”
“Yeah.
I can look all I want, but I still can’t find your balls.”
“Choose your words carefully.
No matter how generously that person has blessed me...”
“Yeah.
I could search the whole ocean and still not find your testicles.”
“I chose my words carefully.
What’s the problem?”
His faint smile was long gone.
Amid the people’s continued cheering, Cang Gong’s tightly shut, pale lips parted.
“What do you think?
Surely that person would understand if I merely pulled out your tongue.”
“Sure.
The Lord of Heaven might.
You’re the one among his followers he worries about most, seeing as you haven’t got any balls.
His sore ball—no, his sore finger.”
I nodded in agreement and pointed over Cang Gong’s shoulder.
“But that guy won’t understand.”
In the slowed-down flow of time, everything happened at once.
Cang Gong turned his head to look behind him.
I thrust a fist wreathed in flame at him.
And a solid palm shot forward like a flash of light, as if reversing time all by itself, intercepting my fist before it could reach anyone.
*BOOM!*
A roar like the sky splitting open brought time rushing back to normal.
At the same instant, a powerful shock wave shook the grand banquet hall.
*Crack!
Rrrrmm!*
The ground shuddered as though an earthquake had struck.
Screams and shouts erupted on all sides.
Amid the sudden chaos, a pair of gleaming white eyes fixed on me.
“Was that all?”
*Crack.*
His voice was calm, but the immense force squeezing my fist was anything but.
An unknown, ice-cold energy filled his palm, suppressing the flames in mine and snuffing them out.
“Such a shallow trick.
I’m disappointed.”
*Crunch.
Crunch.*
Agonizing pain shot through my captured fist.
If my muscles and bones hadn’t surpassed the limits of an ordinary human, they would already have been ground to dust.
But I’d endured this much pain more times than I cared to count.
And I’d never expected that surprise attack to bring him down.
I’d only needed a signal flare to let everyone know what was happening.
“I’m a little hurt that you think it was just a shallow trick.”
*What?*
“I don’t know if you’ve heard of magic, but I’m about to show you some.
Watch closely.”
“What are you—”
The moment Cang Gong frowned—
*BOOOOM!*
Blinding flames swallowed the darkness, and the rock walls that ringed the grand banquet hall like towering ramparts burst apart.
From the place Cang Gong had glanced toward moments earlier, a figure strode out.
“I’ll give you my first and last warning.”
The flames dancing in that damn monk’s eyes looked anything but Buddhist.
He swept his gaze across the hall and went on.
“Only step forward if you want your flesh and bones to melt.”
Recognition darkened Cang Gong’s eyes.
I smiled.
“Accio, Fire King.”
At the same time, I thrust out my still-free hand toward his chest.
He faltered for an instant.
The Flame Divine Palm, at nine-tenths mastery.
*BOOOOM!*
“Huh?”
The young man stopped abruptly and looked back.
Seeing him stare down the road they’d traveled, his brow furrowed, the burly man ahead of him asked, “Hyukmu.
What’s wrong?”
“No, it’s just...”
Hyuk Mujin trailed off and clicked his tongue.
“I thought I heard something.”
Taishan raised an eyebrow.
“A sound?
An enemy?”
“I don’t know.
Maybe I imagined it.”
“Then no.
That sound Hyukmu heard—Taishan didn’t hear it.”
“But I’m telling you, I’m sure I heard something.”
“Hyukmu.
Your martial arts are weak.
Taishan could turn you into finely minced five-spice pork if he wanted.”
“...Hey, what the hell?
Are you looking down on me?”
“Mm.
Honestly, a little.”
“Hyukmu.
We can’t stop.
We have to go.
Everyone’s waiting.”
Hyuk Mujin swallowed his flare of anger and let out a long sigh.
“Yeah, I’m going.
I’m going.”
But despite his answer, his steps didn’t come as easily as before.
The road behind him and the walls of the Imperial Capital, growing more distant by the moment, kept appearing before his eyes.
*Damn it.
Am I hearing things now, too?*
Annoying as it was, Taishan was probably right that there hadn’t been a sound.
If a Peak master a step above him hadn’t heard it, then there was nothing to hear.
Even if Mujin *had* heard something, it must have been the faint noise of an insect or an animal moving.
*Then why do I feel like this?*
Hyuk Mujin frowned harder and thumped his chest.
His heart kept pounding when it hadn’t before, as though an invisible hand were squeezing it tight.
*Something feels wrong.*
Along with the inexplicable unease, the face of someone he’d parted with a few shichen ago suddenly flashed through his mind.
*Just one mission.*
The last voice he’d heard before leaving still echoed in his ears.
*Oh, one more thing.*
*Yes?*
*Be careful.
You and everyone else.*
Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung.
Hyuk Mujin had answered the warning with a grin.
Then he and the rest of the Fire Dragon Pavilion had left the Imperial Capital, bound for the border between Jiangsu and Zhejiang Provinces.
For the very place written on the note Jin Taekyung had given him.
*The mission’s going fine... so what’s wrong with me?*
Everything was going smoothly, yet his chest felt unbearably tight.
The Captain—Jin Taekyung—had acted so strangely that the memory pricked at him like a fishbone caught in his throat.
Taekyung usually laughed with him over nothing, hit him for getting cheeky, and cursed him without holding back.
Today, Mujin had seen none of that.
“Hyukmu!”
Snapping out of his thoughts, Hyuk Mujin realized he’d stopped walking again.
Then he saw his companions waiting a short distance ahead, and his heart sank.
Grave eyes.
Troubled faces.
Everyone except Taishan was looking at him the same way.
“Everyone...”
Hyuk Mujin barely swallowed a groan.
At last, he thought he understood the unease that had been squeezing his chest.
“Did you all know?”
Namho answered his halting question in a heavy voice.
“Yes.
More or less.”
“The Captain told you?”
“No.
Senior Jeok gave us a warning beforehand.
He knew what choice his Disciple would make.”
“Then why was I the only one—”
“If he’d told you to leave because you’d be a burden, would you have obeyed without a fuss?”
“I don’t like this situation either.
No—none of us do.”
For a moment, Hyuk Mujin had nothing to say.
He understood perfectly well how they felt about being burdens instead of help.
He understood why Jin Taekyung had lied to send him away.
And it was the truth.
But... but...
*Still, it shouldn’t be like this.*
Hyuk Mujin bit down on his lip until it bled and turned his head.
Then, for an instant, he forgot the entire situation and muttered in a dazed voice.
Far away, countless figures moved through the darkness, shaking the forest as they passed.
Too many to count, yet he couldn’t sense a single presence among them.
*What are those?*
The same question arose in everyone’s mind.
So did a fear none of them could explain.
This time, instinct rather than reason moved Hyuk Mujin.
No—it moved them all.
*Whoosh!*

paragraphs: The situation in the Grand Banquet Hall had already spiraled beyond anyone’s control.
The festive music had long since fallen silent. The threefold cheers of “A thousand years!” celebrating the birth of an heir had given way to screams and shouts.
At last, the fuse had been lit.
The banquet was over.
But another banquet had yet to end.
A Hongmen Banquet, where weapons would replace smiles, and blood would spill instead of wine.
A tremendous roar announced the start of that horrific feast, shaking the hall in every direction.
*BOOOOM!*
The ground shuddered, and a terrible wave of heat erupted. At that moment, a figure shot out from beyond the blazing flames and clouds of dust like a flash of light.
*Whooosh!*
*Crunch!*
The ground crumbled like tofu beneath the foot he barely managed to plant.
Jin Taekyung, the young man who’d just managed to steady himself after being hurled through the air with a sharp blast, spat the blood pooling in his mouth and muttered,
“So you’re a cut above me...”
Speed, strength, a perfectly timed surprise attack—he’d made full use of them all, yet the gap between them was unmistakable.
His hand still tingled as he remembered thrusting out his palm.
Just as his full-power Flame Divine Palm was about to strike Cang Gong’s chest, an icy energy had effortlessly suppressed his Scorching Yang Qi and shaken his entire body.
*What the hell was that?*
Despite all Jin Taekyung had seen—enough to rival many veterans of the martial world—he’d never felt energy like it.
Something more primal. Something he couldn’t describe as merely Yin-Cold Qi.
But he had nowhere near enough to solve that mystery.
Not enough information or experience.
Not enough time, either.
*Step. Step.*
Footsteps rang out clearly, even amid the chaos consuming the Grand Banquet Hall.
Cang Gong strolled across ground left horribly melted by the surge of Scorching Yang Qi. Then he stopped.
Right where he’d stood moments earlier.
“Five steps. Five whole steps.”
There was admiration in his quiet voice.
At an absurdly young age, that martial artist had reached an astonishing level of skill.
*To make this old man retreat five steps, in that battered condition.*
Now that he’d experienced it firsthand, Cang Gong thought he understood why *that person* had taken such an interest in Jin Taekyung.
Why *that person* had ordered them to keep that young brat alive, even after losing two loyal servants—the Western Heaven Demon Lord and the Southern Heaven Demon Empress—in the process.
*As an enemy, he’d be the greatest obstacle. As an ally, he’d soon become a monster who could surpass even the Three Saints.*
Cang Gong had no doubt they could win him over once they captured him.
If Jin Taekyung met the Lord of Heaven—if he felt that irresistible being’s power even once—he would have no choice but to kneel before him.
Just as Cang Gong himself had.
“I must take him to the Lord of Heaven. No matter what.”
The moment he said it, a dry voice cut in.
“Take who to whom?”
*Fwoosh.*
The air for hundreds of feet around them grew scorching hot.
Cang Gong saw a bald, middle-aged man approaching through the heat haze rising from the ground. His pale lips parted.
“Fire King Jeok Cheongang.”
“How dare you toss this old man’s name around, you ball-less bastard?”
“You two really are alike in speech and behavior. I can’t tell whether the disciple learned from the master or the master from the disciple.”
Jeok Cheongang answered flatly. “Usually, the disciple learns from the master. Though a rootless bastard like you wouldn’t know that.”
“Roots, huh? I had those once. A master and fellow disciples who were like family.”
“I see. So did your master teach you to cut off your own balls, too?”
“No.”
A murderous smile spread across Cang Gong’s lips.
“He taught me never to forget my roots, no matter what happened. I haven’t forgotten his words for a single moment.”
“I don’t know what long-winded story you’ve got, but to hell with his teachings. You won’t need to remember them anymore.”
Jeok Cheongang raised his fist and grinned.
“Everyone who’s taken a hit from this old man ended up that way.”
He glanced around and added, “Though it looks like plenty of others would love to tear you apart, too.”
He wasn’t exaggerating.

Nearly two thousand members of the Embroidered Uniform Guard surrounded them in a circle. Every one of them was among the Great Nation’s finest troops, martial artists ranging from Supreme First Rate to Peak.
And that wasn’t all.

The Imperial Guards were considered a cut below the Embroidered Uniform Guard, who protected the Emperor and the imperial family, but they were elite troops in their own right. They’d arrived late, taken positions on the outer walls of the Grand Banquet Hall, and drawn their bows.
Five thousand men in all.
More than enough to call an army—and in quality, they could rival a force of a hundred thousand.
Yet Cang Gong merely looked at the countless spears, swords, and arrowheads surrounding him.
Or rather, he looked past them to the one man watching him from the high platform.
“The hunting dogs have slipped their leashes and are running wild without even knowing where they’ll die, while their cunning master sits back and watches.”
Just as he always had.
Cang Gong laughed aloud.
Then his laughter stopped dead, and a thunderous command burst from his pale lips.
“Attack!”
*BOOOOM!*
The immense internal energy carried in his voice shook the Grand Banquet Hall. At that instant—
*Thrust! Slash!*
A gleaming sword blade burst from an Embroidered Uniform Guard’s chest. Too stunned even to feel the pain, he stared at the steel piercing his golden armor.
Shock and disbelief filled his wide eyes.
Even as death rushed toward him, he wanted to know.
Why was he dying like this? Why had a comrade he’d called hyung for more than ten years stabbed him in the back?
“Ghk. D-Dong hyung?”
Why?
They weren’t related by blood, but they’d promised to treat each other as sworn brothers.
Dozens—hundreds—of times, they’d raised their cups together, encouraging each other, pledging their brotherhood and swearing loyalty to their country and His Majesty the Emperor.
But when he forced out that one call through the blood rising in his throat, the answer came in a flat voice he’d never heard in all their ten years together.
“Heaven above, earth below. All demons bow in reverence.”
Those were the last words he heard.
*Crunch.*
The sword twisted and pulled free. His lifeless body toppled to the ground.
Everywhere.
*Thrust!*
All around—
*Slash!*
Again and again—
*Shhhk!*
Severed heads rolled across the ground. Limbs and blood flew through the air.
In the blink of an eye, hundreds of the two thousand Embroidered Uniform Guards were dead.
Killed by their own comrades. By superiors, subordinates, and men they’d cherished like brothers.
Muffled shouts burst out from every direction. The traitors and the betrayed, those who fought to protect and those who fought to take, clashed with one another.
*Clang-clang-clang!*
*Slash! Thrust!*
“Aaagh!”
Screams echoed as swordlight flashed ceaselessly through the darkness.
Someone’s hand, still clutching a torch, twitched in a pool of blood.
Then another darkness spread over the horrific melee that had erupted beneath the night sky.
*Fwoooooosh.*
Some who heard the sound thought it was rain. Another man, panting as he waited for death, remembered the broad plains of his hometown.
A strong wind sweeping in from far away had made just such a sound across those fields.
The ripe grain and grasses would bow, and the great tree where the village held its festivals would shake its abundant branches and leaves.
But the nameless man realized he’d never return to the hometown he missed.
*Ah.*
The darkness spreading across the sky was no darkness at all. Countless arrows were raining down.
They spread across the sky as they rushed toward the people below—or toward the Emperor they’d sworn their loyalty to.
*Cough.*
He spat blood mixed with fragments of his innards.
*This wasn’t how it was supposed to be.*
He hadn’t left his family and his hometown to die so pointlessly.
*Damn it.*
He stared at the darkness rushing toward him and waited for death to end his pain and despair.
Then he saw it.
*Fwoosh—BOOOOM!*
A great blaze swallowed the darkness.
Countless arrows burned away without a trace. Through that overwhelming heat, a young man plunged toward the ground like a hawk diving for prey.
*BOOM!*
Why did a roar that should have sounded like thunder reach him so faintly, as though it had come from hundreds of yards away?
As his vision dimmed, he tried to remember the young man’s name.
Why couldn’t he say it? Why couldn’t he ask him to save him, to send him home?
With darkness closing over his eyes, all he could do was watch. Flames consumed the unending rain of arrows, and traitors fell like bundles of straw wherever the young man moved.
Two beings began a battle that shook heaven and earth. He could hardly believe they were made of flesh and blood like him.
*Bang! Bang! BOOOOM!*
Scorching heat. Shuddering cold.
Flames and white flashes swept the hall without pause, setting the night ablaze and freezing it over.
The countless bodies still piling up amid sprays of blood served as firewood.
And the life of one unfortunate man, made to suffer a little longer than the rest, as a sacrifice.
But at the end of that horrific wait, the nameless member of the Embroidered Uniform Guard managed to remember the young man’s name—the one he’d almost forgotten.
*Jin Taekyung. Right. It was Jin Taekyung.*
Strange.
He lay dying in a pool of blood, in the middle of a sea of corpses and blood, yet he didn’t feel cold at all.
*It’s warm.*
He watched the flames surging between flashing spears and swords. Then, unable to fight the sleep overtaking him, he closed his eyes.
He thought of the hometown he would never return to.
People who love to talk say only two things can kill a Supreme Peak master: time and his own carelessness.
Right now, I wanted to tell those people one thing.
*Then why don’t you try fighting them?*
A Supreme Peak master is still made of flesh and blood.
To someone who doesn’t know any better, he might look like a superhuman who can take down hundreds or thousands of enemies. But he has limits.
Especially when at least half of those hundreds or thousands are Peak masters.
*Swish! Slice!*

The tip of a spear someone thrust out skimmed past my cheek by a hair. Getting my skin sliced open by the internal energy packed into its blade was just the standard package. My fist returning the favor was a bonus.
*Wham!*
My Flame Divine Palm struck the Embroidered Uniform Guard—no, the traitor planted by Dark Heaven—in the chest. He flew backward like a puppet with its strings cut.
Dead on the spot.
But someone else filled the gap. The others moved more cautiously now, and faster.
*Damn it.*
If they’d only been martial artists, they would’ve been much easier to deal with. But they were soldiers, too—a force with both powerful martial arts and an army’s discipline.
*Slash! Thrust!*
I snatched a spear from someone’s hands and swung it wildly, glaring past the shoulders of the enemies surrounding me.
*Why the hell?!*
I wanted to shout it.
Why weren’t they helping? How could they stand there and watch, even now?
The Emperor stood where I was looking. Baek Yeon and So Gyo remained beside him, guarding him like stone statues.
And now there was someone else in my line of sight.
An unwelcome guest.
*Whoosh!*
A sharp sound cut through the air. A dozen or so Embroidered Uniform Guards who’d been fighting nearby stopped moving.
Their eyes widened in disbelief.
Then, as if to reveal the cold truth, faint lines of blood appeared on their necks, growing darker by the second.
*Gurgle—SHHHK!*
Blood beaded along the cuts, then sprayed like fountains. The man who’d swept past them watched their bodies fall like rotten trees. He looked at me and sighed.
“Why did you do it? If you’d simply trusted me and followed along, everything could have gone smoothly.”
Instead of answering Ma Sanbao’s bullshit—the kind even the mutt next door could understand—I brought my spearhead down.
*Whoosh!*

*It’s warm.*
He watched the flames surging between flashing spears and swords.
Then, unable to fight the sleep overtaking him, he closed his eyes.
He thought of the hometown he would never return to.
People who love to talk say only two things can kill a Supreme Peak master: time and his own carelessness.
Right now, I wanted to tell those people one thing.
*Then why don’t you try fighting them?*
A Supreme Peak master is still made of flesh and blood.
To someone who doesn’t know any better, he might look like a superhuman who can take down hundreds or thousands of enemies.
But he has limits.
Especially when at least half of those hundreds or thousands are Peak masters.
*Swish!
Slice!*
The tip of a spear someone thrust out skimmed past my cheek by a hair.
Getting my skin sliced open by the internal energy packed into its blade was just the standard package.
My fist returning the favor was a bonus.
*Wham!*
My Flame Divine Palm struck the Embroidered Uniform Guard—no, the traitor planted by Dark Heaven—in the chest.
He flew backward like a puppet with its strings cut.
Dead on the spot.
But someone else filled the gap.
The others moved more cautiously now, and faster.
*Damn it.*
If they’d only been martial artists, they would’ve been much easier to deal with.
But they were soldiers, too—a force with both powerful martial arts and an army’s discipline.
*Slash!
Thrust!*
I snatched a spear from someone’s hands and swung it wildly, glaring past the shoulders of the enemies surrounding me.
*Why the hell?!*
I wanted to shout it.
Why weren’t they helping?
How could they stand there and watch, even now?
The Emperor stood where I was looking.
Baek Yeon and So Gyo remained beside him, guarding him like stone statues.
And now there was someone else in my line of sight.
An unwelcome guest.
*Whoosh!*
A sharp sound cut through the air.
A dozen or so Embroidered Uniform Guards who’d been fighting nearby stopped moving.
Their eyes widened in disbelief.
Then, as if to reveal the cold truth, faint lines of blood appeared on their necks, growing darker by the second.
*Gurgle—SHHHK!*
Blood beaded along the cuts, then sprayed like fountains.
The man who’d swept past them watched their bodies fall like rotten trees.
He looked at me and sighed.
“Why did you do it?
If you’d simply trusted me and followed along, everything could have gone smoothly.”
Instead of answering Ma Sanbao’s bullshit—the kind even the mutt next door could understand—I brought my spearhead down.
*Whoosh!*

chapters.title: Chapter 905
paragraphs: The torches wavered. Blood dark enough to see even in the gloom burst out on every side.
*Clang-clang-clang!*
*Thrust!*
Well-honed blades met in flashes of swordlight. Cries of pain followed.
“Gyaaaagh!”
“Ghk, gah!”
With a dying cry that announced the end, someone nameless met their death, and someone else stepped into the empty space they left behind.
Again and again.
A cycle of death that would not end until one side was wiped out.
The Emperor sat on his throne without so much as a tremor, as though to prove the weight of those two words—Son of Heaven. He watched the Grand Banquet Hall turn into a battlefield.
*It’s been a long time since I’ve seen a sight like this.*
He wore a brilliantly embroidered dragon robe now, but little more than a decade ago, he had been a general who crossed battlefields in armor.
The fourth prince of the Great Nation, with neither the prospect nor the desire to inherit the throne.
No one had expected the man who led an army against border warlords and nomads to ascend the throne.
Not even the man himself.
“Strange how things turn out. Truly strange. Wouldn’t you agree?”
At the Emperor’s sudden murmur, Baek Yeon, Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, replied in a heavy voice. He stood beside the throne like an iron tower.
“This subordinate failed in his duty.”

A full third of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, whose duty was to protect the imperial family, had turned their blades against it. The Imperial Guards responsible for the Outer Palace were raining arrows down without pause.
The Emperor had not been entirely unprepared for the existence of traitors, but Cang Gong’s shadow had fallen far darker than he’d expected.
Across the imperial family. No—across the entire Great Nation.
*Shhh-shhh-shh—clang!*
Hundreds of arrows fired straight at the Emperor bounced off harmlessly.
The Emperor moved his lips toward the Embroidered Uniform Guard who had blocked the attack by forming a wall with their massive iron shields.
“Advance.”
One short command was enough.
A hundred martial artists, handpicked from among the finest of the Great Nation’s greatest force, launched themselves forward without hesitation.
Away from the Emperor’s side and into the battlefield stained with death and screams.
*Whoooosh!*
Dozens of yards vanished in an instant.
A hundred spears and swords swung together, flashing as they bore down on the traitors.
*Whiiing!*
*Slice! Thrust!*
“Gyaaaagh!”
Screams and blood erupted without pause.
The martial prowess of warriors at the very brink of the Peak realm—overwhelming, and horribly powerful.
But even that could not turn the tide of battle. At its center, true monsters beyond human limits were running wild.
*BOOOOM!*
*Rrrumble!*
A tremendous roar and tremor shook the area. Beyond a pillar of fire that surged high into the air, piercing the darkness, a painfully white light blazed.
*Shhk!*
Space split open.
Everyone who felt that chill, like frost in the depths of winter, shuddered as if on cue. Then, as their vision slowly tilted, they understood.
*Ah.*
The cold they had just felt was death.
*Rrrumble!*
Dozens of bodies toppled like rotten old trees. Their blood-soaked armor no longer shone gold, and the gray eyes looking down at them were cold.
“Is that all you have?”
*Whump!*
A casual palm strike crushed a man’s whole body.
“The Emperor’s hunting dogs. The might of the imperial family.”
*Craack!*
A light stomp sent the ground rippling for dozens of yards around him.
“I asked if that’s all you have!”
*BWOOOM!*
The shout, charged with immense internal energy, burst through the compressed air. It shook bodies and minds hardened by grueling training and tore at eardrums.
“Ghk.”
Groans rose all around. The Embroidered Uniform Guards staggered, clutching their bleeding ears, as another white flash hurtled toward them.
No—it was just about to.
*Fwoosh.*
Somewhere, flames flickered.
In an instant, the air, cold as ice a moment ago, boiled like lava. Fire swallowed even the darkness.
*BOOM!*
*Would a volcano sound like that if it erupted?*
The thought flashed through everyone’s mind as the flames poured toward one man alone.
An old man with pale skin.
Cang Gong’s gray eyes filled with terrible heat.
*BOOOOM!*
Impact. An explosion.
The dreadful shock wave that followed hurled friend and foe alike through the air. Cang Gong was no exception.
*Shhhhh. Thud.*
Driven back by the immense force, he barely managed to stop himself. He straightened his bent back and fixed his gaze on one man.
“When the situation demands you fight with everything you have, you waste your strength showing off against children. You must’ve eaten your age through your ass.”
Fire King Jeok Cheongang.
As Jeok approached through the heat haze rising around him, Cang Gong’s lips twisted.
“And you’re no different. In the end, didn’t you earn the title of Fire King by killing countless weaklings?”
“Even without balls, you should get your facts straight. The Demonic Cultists I killed weren’t mere weaklings. They were arsonists. Burning them alive wouldn’t have been punishment enough.”
“Then why did you kill the other Demonic Cultists? They had done nothing to you.”
“One day, I woke up to find my ancestral home in flames. How do you think that felt?”
Jeok Cheongang did not wait for an answer.
“Awful. Fucking awful. So I kicked every last one of them in the ass and sent them to the afterlife. That way, even if they were reborn, they’d never set fire to someone else’s home again.”
“In other words, it was personal revenge.”
“That’s right. I didn’t much like what those bastards were doing anyway.”
Jeok Cheongang raised a fist wreathed in rolling flames and added,
“Just like you.”
*Swish—BOOM!*
Thousands of soldiers filled the Grand Banquet Hall, but not one of them saw how Jeok Cheongang moved—or how Cang Gong evaded that terrifying attack.
A tiny handful of people were the exception. They were more than worthy of being called superhuman.
“If I were in his place, how long could I last?”
The Emperor had watched it all. Baek Yeon answered his question.
“A hundred moves.”
“You don’t hesitate to be cruel. I put no small effort into reaching this realm.”
The Emperor gave a bitter smile. Baek Yeon replied evenly.
“It would be the same for anyone. The only question is how long they could last. The outcome would not change.”
“Even if you went out there, Baek Yeon?”
“As Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, I would certainly win. As a lone martial artist, I would lose by a hair.”
“Then which are you now—a martial artist, or the Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard?”
“This subordinate has always been the Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard. I obey only Your Majesty’s commands. And...”
Baek Yeon’s voice fell to a murmur.
“The late Emperor’s final order was for me to plan for the future alongside the fourth prince.”
The Emperor’s eyes trembled.
How could he forget that day? The voice he had heard for the last time?
More than ten years had passed since then.

Frost had settled early on the head of the young man burdened with more than he could bear. The infant who had once been swaddled in blankets had grown into a boy, now sharing this very moment with him.
“What on earth—”
The boy struggled as though he might shake off the palace attendants holding him and rush onto the battlefield.
“What on earth are you thinking?”
His eyes blazed with confusion and anger as he glared at the Emperor.
“Why? Why won’t you help them? They’re risking their lives for Your Majesty...!”
*BOOOOM!*
The rest of his words were swallowed by the roar that burst out with the flames.
The next moment, Prince Shangshan saw a familiar face amid another fierce battle across the hall. The man was rising to his feet, using a spear shaft broken in half as a cane.
Shangshan let out a quiet groan.
“Jin Taekyung.”
He could recognize him at a glance, even from far away.
No. How could he fail to recognize him?
It was Jin Taekyung.
The first person to bring life to the young prince’s dull, unchanging days. The only one who had treated him as someone other than a prince.
Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao clearly remembered the day they had first met.
“Could I become like you?”
After much thought, he had asked Jin Taekyung that question. Jin had answered without hesitation.
“Of course. You can.”
Shangshan had meant it. He wanted to be like Jin Taekyung.

Not simply because Jin was a formidable martial artist. A man once dismissed as his family’s unwanted child had defeated powerful enemies and won everyone’s affection. Shangshan found it astonishing—and enviable.
Though he was a royal more honored than anyone in the world, the young prince had always been lonely. In that young martial artist, he had seen something of himself.
A few days ago, Jin had dared to stroke his hair. Shangshan could still feel the warmth of his hand.
“I hope we meet again. Then I can repay the debt I owe you.”
“Your Highness.”
“Yes?”
“Don’t you know? Friends don’t owe each other anything.”
It had been the first time anyone had called him a friend. The first time anyone had stroked his hair as though he were an ordinary child.
That made him want all the more to keep his promise—to repay what he owed Jin Taekyung and return his kindness.
Jin was his one and only friend.
“Please, please save him.”
Shangshan did not know what was happening or what lay behind it. Still, he bowed his head and fell to his knees without hesitation.
Before his only blood relative.
He pleaded with the ruler of the continent, who could move several Supreme Peak masters with a single word.

“I will do anything you ask of me. If you order your younger brother to leave the Great Nation, I will obey. But please, do not refuse the first and last request this brother of yours will ever make.”
“Save him. Save Jin Taekyung, Your Majesty!”
As the Emperor watched Shangshan prostrate himself and cry out, an indescribable emotion crossed his face.
Relief. Pride. Perhaps even sorrow. Amid that swirl of feelings was something he could not bring himself to say.
*Not ‘Your Majesty’... Wouldn’t you call me ‘older brother’?*
His lips parted, but no words came out. Nor did he nod at Shangshan’s plea.
No—he could not.
Everything that happened on this battlefield today had been entrusted to one person more than a decade ago.
*No matter how I think about it, I can’t understand why you’re doing nothing, even in a situation like this.*
So Gyo answered the Emperor’s quiet Sound Transmission in her ear.
*I’m not standing by. I’m watching.*
Her gaze remained fixed on Jin Taekyung, unwavering as it had been from the start.
*Until he shows his true self.*
