chapters.title: Chapter 906
paragraphs: I didn’t know what to call this.
A melee?
A bloodbath?
Maybe both. Everywhere I stepped, I was trampling the corpse of someone I didn’t know, while enemy spears, swords, and arrowheads came hurtling in without pause, from the ground and the sky alike.
Even now.
“Look out!”
One of the Embroidered Uniform Guards heard my shout and jolted, twisting at the waist.
*Fffft!*
His armor split with a sharp whistle.
The traitor who’d tried to ambush him amid the chaos missed by a hair. Without hesitation, I kicked a crescent blade lying on the ground.
*Whoooosh! Thud!*
There wasn’t even the usual dying cry.

The blade shot out like a flash of light, piercing its target and then skewering a couple of nearby enemies like meat on a spit. The Embroidered Uniform Guard, who’d barely escaped with his life, gave me a slight nod.
“Thank y—”
He never raised his head again.
*Thwack!*
An arrow pierced his throat, straight through his Adam’s apple.
He collapsed with blood gurgling in his throat. Enemies trampled his body as they rushed in, swinging their weapons at anyone in reach.
All accompanied by a calm voice that had no place in a situation like this—which made it all the more chilling.
“Heaven above, earth below.”
“All demons bow in reverence.”
Why did they remind me of the deranged fanatics I’d fought right before coming to Murim?
“Fucking lunatics...”

Short cries of dismay rang out here and there. The Embroidered Uniform Guards had continued fighting calmly despite the sudden betrayal of their allies, as if to prove the weight of the golden armor they wore. But even they looked afraid as they watched the traitors, who had become entirely different people.
Or maybe they feared the martial prowess of someone they couldn’t hope to face.
*Splash.*
A leather shoe sank into a pool of blood as its owner stepped forward.
One of the Embroidered Uniform Guards had backed away without realizing it. A groan slipped through his lips.
“Ma Sanbao...”
That’s right. It was him.
Ma Sanbao, the East Depot’s Brush-Holding Eunuch.
Its second-in-command and de facto leader.
Or rather, that was the identity he’d used to deceive the world. Now he moved toward me.
So fast that “approaching” hardly did it justice—he moved like a flash of light.
*Whoosh! BOOM!*
His blows rained down like lightning from above. Every time I blocked one, my hands went numb.
My breathing had grown rougher than before, throwing off movements that should have flowed like water.
*Huff. Huff.*
As I panted, I wondered whether I was struggling this badly because of my condition—or because my opponent was simply that formidable.
I didn’t have long to wonder.
*Shhk!*
The flexible sword curved like a living snake and grazed the bridge of my nose.
Hot blood ran from the cut. I retreated through the burning pain, and a low laugh reached my ear.
“What happened to all that momentum you had at the start, hmm?”
Instead of answering, I turned my head. A dagger sprang from Ma Sanbao’s voluminous sleeve and pierced the empty space beside me like a streak of light.
*Thwack!*
Another life ended with a sickening sound.
Ma Sanbao went on as if nothing had happened.
“That’s a shame. If you hadn’t dodged, that young Embroidered Uniform Guard would still be breathing.”
I looked at Ma Sanbao, who was taunting me, and wondered:
*If I hadn’t dodged, would the guard have survived?*
*Could he have made it through this battle and returned to his family someday?*
*I didn’t know. I didn’t know anything.*
The pointless guilt made me feel like shit, even though someone else was the one who owed the dead guard an apology.

I wanted to turn around. I wanted to look the Emperor and So Gyo in the eye—the two who had thrown me, Jeok Cheongang, and even their own subordinates into this battlefield, only to stand by and watch. I wanted to ask them why they’d held this damn banquet. Why they weren’t stepping in when they had the power to turn the tide.
“Why the hell?!”
I couldn’t hold back the shout any longer. But it wasn’t the Emperor or So Gyo who answered.
It was Ma Sanbao.
“Do you still not understand why they’re standing by and doing nothing?”
He let out a derisive laugh and continued.
“Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung. The Emperor used you too, in the end. Just as we tried to use you and the Fire King to get rid of So Gyo.”
“Borrow another’s blade to kill. There’s no better way to keep blood off your hands. Especially when the blades are as fine as the Fire King and the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.”
I wanted to tell him to shut his damn mouth.
But no matter how badly I wanted to deny it, I couldn’t speak.
It was all too plausible.
If the Emperor was anything like the man I’d experienced firsthand...
And with that woman, So Gyo, still a complete mystery...
“You and your master have only one role left. Fight for your lives until, in the end, you die.”
*Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!*
The flexible sword became dozens of blades, whistling toward me from every direction.
A sword technique of extreme speed, pushed to its very limit.
But however densely the afterimages surrounded me, only one blade was real.
*Clang!*
A clash far too loud to have come from two weapons meeting sent me sliding back.
Ma Sanbao kept swinging the flexible sword, giving me no pause. His voice came from beyond it.
“The Great Nation, the Emperor—it’s always been like this. To the rulers who hold this vast land, people like you and me, people of Murim, aren’t subjects to govern.”
*Whoosh-whoosh! Slice!*
The pressure behind his sword cut through my skin. Thin sprays of blood scattered into the air.

“That’s why I followed my master and pledged my loyalty to that person. It’s why you’ll die here today. The Emperor only wants to protect Prince Shangshan. He won’t play the cards he’s kept hidden just to save a pack of martial-world ruffians.”
“What?”
A realization flashed through my mind, and my eyes widened.
Even though there was considerable distance between us, I suddenly thought of someone fighting a thunderous battle alongside Jeok Cheongang far away.
*Could it be?*
No. There was no *could* about it.
Ma Sanbao had said it himself. This wasn’t a guess. It was a certainty.
*Krrrrang!*
Their different Forces collided, spitting sparks.

My spear had once been a single weapon. Ma Sanbao’s fierce assault had broken it into two short spears. I crossed them to block his flexible sword and felt a chill coming off the blade, stopped inches from my face.
“Cang Gong. Were you his disciple?”
“Cang Gong? How dare you call him a servant of that sinister, weak Emperor?”
Ma Sanbao’s lips twisted.
“Eastern Heaven Demon Lord. That is the new name the great and all-powerful Lord of Heaven bestowed on his loyal servant.”
“And that Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s disciple will bring you to your knees.”
At that moment—
*Whirr.*
The springy blade of the flexible sword bent.
It slipped over the spear shaft blocking its way like a living snake and flashed toward me. I swung my crossed short spears upward with all my strength.
*Clang!*
The flexible sword veered away from my chest.
But I’d only survived a dangerous moment. The attack wasn’t over.
*Wham!*
*Hk!*
My breath caught, and my vision flashed.
A fist struck my exposed chest. I staggered back more than ten steps, giving Ma Sanbao an opening he couldn’t afford to miss.
*Tap.*
One step.
At the same time, Ma Sanbao’s figure vanished like an illusion.
But even with my battered body and dulled senses, I reacted in time.
*Left!*
The instant I was sure, I flung out one hand.
Broken in two, the spear had lost the advantage of its long reach. But the shortened shaft was the perfect length and speed for a throw. I sent it flying with all my strength.
*Whoooosh!*
A single fierce whistle ripped through the air.
Then came a tremendous impact.
*BOOM!*
Dust billowed from the ground.
And then—
*Shhhhk!*
Space split open.
The flexible sword had knocked my short spear aside. Now it came through the dust, blazing with Force and cutting the cloud apart.
Ma Sanbao’s taunting Sound Transmission reached me with it.
—Don’t worry. I’ll only cut you enough to leave you barely alive.
That was his mistake.
The world slowed. I could see every one of the dozens of sword-images raining down through the air.
*Cut me? And only enough to leave me alive?*
What a joke.
He was talking like that while his opponent was still standing on two perfectly good legs.
Win a life-and-death duel, and you could spit on your opponent. Boast about your strength. Laugh in his face.
But...
*You do that after it’s over.*
My body was heavy as waterlogged cotton, and the internal energy that usually surged through me like a wave was coming in broken strands.
It didn’t matter.
My eyes hadn’t wavered. Neither had the hand gripping my one remaining short spear.
*I see it.*
*Shwoosh!*
The spear tip pierced a single precise point. Dozens of sword-images vanished as it struck the real blade.
*BOOM!*
The impact sent the figure flying, unable to withstand the force of the collision.
Not me.
Ma Sanbao.
*Crunch.*
He planted a foot hard enough to tear up the ground and barely managed to steady himself. His eyes widened as he stared at me.
*Tap.*
I was already right in front of him.
“You bastard!”
Ma Sanbao cried out, his flexible sword cutting through the air at a speed worthy of being called extreme. It scattered Force like a glacier—colder and more merciless still.
*Shwoooosh!*
Facing that force, which seemed capable of freezing everything it touched, I drew up every last bit of internal energy in my body.
*Fwoosh.*
Wet firewood caught flame.
I poured the Scorching Yang Qi that surged like fire through my acupoints, as unstable as twisted railway tracks, into my hand and grabbed the blade just as it began to pierce my side.
*Krrk, KRAAAASH!*
Power collided with power.
Agony shot through both hands.
This wasn’t Empty-Hand Seizes the Blade, catching a weapon between bare fingers with precise timing and speed.
This was just a brute-force grab.
“You crazy—!”
No martial artist could blame Ma Sanbao for saying that.
This really was insane.
You might get away with it against someone at least a level below you. Against a master of similar skill—especially one with greater internal energy—you’d lose both arms in an instant.
But...
*It’s different when the lunatic grabbing the blade has been busting his ass to raise his Muscles and Bones through the System.*
If my other stats were blue-chip stocks, Muscles and Bones were a savings account I’d kept adding to with every level and every training session.
So what about now, more than a year after I’d gotten the System?
*What level am I again?*
I smiled.
I endured the horrible pain as my palm turned into a shredded mess, and looked into Ma Sanbao’s eyes, bulging as if they were about to burst.
Then I gave his words back to him, changing just a few.
“Don’t worry. I’ll stab you just enough to kill you.”
Ma Sanbao tried to shout, but no sound came out.
*Krrk!*
The short spear in my hand pierced his throat just as his lips began to part.
“Ghk. Kgh.”
Blood gurgled in his throat. The light faded from his eyes as he stared at me.

A groan slipped through his lips.

That’s right.
It was him.
Ma Sanbao, the East Depot’s Brush-Holding Eunuch.
Its second-in-command and de facto leader.

Now he moved toward me.

*Whoosh!

His blows rained down like lightning from above.
Every time I blocked one, my hands went numb.
My breathing had grown rougher than before, throwing off movements that should have flowed like water.
*Huff.

I didn’t have long to wonder.

The flexible sword curved like a living snake and grazed the bridge of my nose.
Hot blood ran from the cut.
I retreated through the burning pain, and a low laugh reached my ear.
“What happened to all that momentum you had at the start, hmm?”
Instead of answering, I turned my head.
A dagger sprang from Ma Sanbao’s voluminous sleeve and pierced the empty space beside me like a streak of light.
*Thwack!*
Another life ended with a sickening sound.
Ma Sanbao went on as if nothing had happened.
“That’s a shame.
If you hadn’t dodged, that young Embroidered Uniform Guard would still be breathing.”
I looked at Ma Sanbao, who was taunting me, and wondered:
*If I hadn’t dodged, would the guard have survived?*
*Could he have made it through this battle and returned to his family someday?*
*I didn’t know.
I didn’t know anything.*
The pointless guilt made me feel like shit, even though someone else was the one who owed the dead guard an apology.
I wanted to turn around.
I wanted to look the Emperor and So Gyo in the eye—the two who had thrown me, Jeok Cheongang, and even their own subordinates into this battlefield, only to stand by and watch.
I wanted to ask them why they’d held this damn banquet.
Why they weren’t stepping in when they had the power to turn the tide.
“Why the hell?!”
I couldn’t hold back the shout any longer.
But it wasn’t the Emperor or So Gyo who answered.
It was Ma Sanbao.
“Do you still not understand why they’re standing by and doing nothing?”
He let out a derisive laugh and continued.
“Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung.
The Emperor used you too, in the end.
Just as we tried to use you and the Fire King to get rid of So Gyo.”
“Borrow another’s blade to kill.
There’s no better way to keep blood off your hands.
Especially when the blades are as fine as the Fire King and the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.”
I wanted to tell him to shut his damn mouth.
But no matter how badly I wanted to deny it, I couldn’t speak.
It was all too plausible.
If the Emperor was anything like the man I’d experienced firsthand...
And with that woman, So Gyo, still a complete mystery...

A sword technique of extreme speed, pushed to its very limit.

chapters.title: Chapter 907
paragraphs: I won’t say the fight with Ma Sanbao was fiercer or harder than any I’d ever fought.
There had been plenty of stronger opponents in the hellish battlefields I’d fought my way through. Even now, I could name several who’d been far worse than him.
But one thing was certain: today, Ma Sanbao had been stronger than me.
*No. More precisely, I was weaker than usual.*
The System was practically sealed, and my body, wrecked by the aftereffects of One Annihilation, wouldn’t move the way I wanted it to.
Even so, I was the one still standing.
In this merciless world ruled by the law of the jungle, Ma Sanbao had made a small but fatal mistake.
He’d mistaken himself for someone a step above me.
“If you wanted to take me alive... you should’ve come at me ready to kill me from the start.”
I looked into Ma Sanbao’s empty eyes as I whispered, then drove the short spear deeper through his throat.
*Crunch. Crack.*
Bone fragments burst through his skin with a sickening sound.
I didn’t let go until the spear had severed his carotid artery and followed his collarbone down toward his heart. Freed from my grip at last, Ma Sanbao’s body slowly toppled.
The spear remained buried deep inside him like a tree root.
*Thud. Splash.*
There was no System message telling me I’d defeated an enemy. No clear, familiar chime.
But this was enough.
*Finally. One down.*
Panting, I stared at the corpse lying motionless in a pool of blood, then let out a shout charged with internal energy.
“Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan has killed Ma Sanbao, Brush-Holding Eunuch of the East Depot!”
Before anyone could grasp what that meant, I plunged back into the battlefield, where swords and spears were flying.
*Whoosh! Crunch!*
Short, simple movements. The bare minimum of internal energy.
I dodged, struck, and smashed.
*Crack!*
I crushed the face of a man muttering those eight words like a mantra—“Heaven above, earth below. All demons bow in reverence.” I was sick of hearing them.
*Whsssh!*
As his body crumpled, its features mangled beyond recognition, blades flew at me from either side. I jerked my head out of their path.
*Clang!*
The two blades missed me by a hand’s breadth and struck each other. Ignoring the vibration ringing in my ears, I thrust out my torn hand.
*Boom!*
Hot, compressed air burst outward.
I’d put only three-tenths of my internal energy into the Flame Divine Palm. Even so, the force and heat of that strike were enough to kill most Peak masters on the spot.
The man flew backward, spraying dark red blood.
Whether that nameless enemy lived or died was no longer my concern. What he’d left behind was another matter.
*Tap.*
His sword had already slipped from his hand. I caught the hilt and swung it in one smooth motion.
*Shhhh!*
Space split open. Flames wrapped around the blade, heating the air and burning flesh and bone.
Simple and swift. Too powerful to stop.
And at the end of it came my enemies’ blood and screams.
*Fwoosh!*
“Gaaah!”

I pushed forward, drenched in blood spraying like a fountain. I dodged the countless blades crashing in from every direction, knocked them aside, then sent them flying right back where they came from.
When the sword broke, I used a spear. When the spear snapped, an ax or a dagger.
And if I had none of those, I used arms and legs harder than steel.
*Crunch!*
*Boom!*
I broke the bones and crushed the flesh of every enemy in my way.
There was no need to invoke some grand concept like all streams returning to the sea.
Every weapon in the world had been made to fight more efficiently. Martial arts existed for the same reason.
Stab. Slash. Strike.
To me, martial arts were connections between countless points and lines.
When your life was on the line, you couldn’t afford to rule out any means.
If a weapon could kill an enemy as quickly and surely as possible, its shape didn’t matter.
Just like now.
*Cr-rack!*
A corpse collapsed, its neck bent at an unnatural angle.
The enemies kept blocking my way, no matter how many I killed. Their lips never stopped murmuring those mantra-like words, but I could see the emotion in their eyes.
*Fear.*
*Huff. Huff.*
I fought to keep my ragged breathing quiet. Every muscle in my body throbbed as if I’d been electrocuted, and the hand that had grabbed Ma Sanbao’s sword could barely feel pain anymore.
After pulling something that crazy, I was probably in terrible shape.
But I couldn’t show even the slightest weakness.
Wolves hunted in packs, but no matter how hungry they were, they couldn’t bare their teeth at a lion that roared and charged them.
They only tried to sink their teeth into a lion’s nape when it started backing away.
*Splash.*
My heavy step sent the blood pooled around my ankles rippling.
Like the blood still seeping from the countless wounds carved into my body, the blood reflecting the night sky was dark red.
*Can I do this?*
A wave of exhaustion hit me.
I’d killed over a hundred of them by my rough count, yet enemies still filled my view.
The Great Nation’s—no, Dark Heaven’s—elite. They ranged from Supreme First Rate to the upper reaches of Peak.

Their individual prowess aside, I had to defeat every last one of those fanatics who worshiped the Lord of Heaven before I could reach Jeok Cheongang, who was still fighting a thunderous battle that seemed like it would never end.
*Goddammit.*
I didn’t know.
We were gaining the upper hand without the Emperor’s help, so why did unease still gnaw at me?
Why did that cloud-choked night sky look so ominous?
No. I knew.
*This isn’t all of it.*
I couldn’t see them anywhere, no matter how I looked: the assassins who were supposed to protect the Emperor, or the twin Supreme Peak masters who had guarded Qianqing Palace.
Even the number of Embroidered Uniform Guards in the Grand Banquet Hall was only half what I knew it should be.
*And the same goes for Cang Gong.*
The Emperor and Cang Gong.
The two men had crossed a point of no return, yet neither had revealed all his forces. They had to be concealing their moves, waiting for the other to show his hand first.
I wouldn’t have been surprised if the entire Imperial Capital had split in two by now and was fighting a bloody battle.
*Fuck.*
What a shitty mess.
Even so, I had to fight.
I had to survive.
The Dark Heaven dogs charging beneath that rain of arrows weren’t the only ones I had to survive. There were also the Emperor and So Gyo, and I didn’t even know whether they were enemies or allies.
*What the hell are you planning?*
I turned toward the high platform in the distance.
Baek Yeon and So Gyo stood on either side of the Emperor. With those two Supreme Peak masters, either of whom could turn the battle around in an instant, he watched the fighting.
I could also see Aehyang surrounded by a handful of palace attendants, and the young king kneeling for some reason.
My gaze lingered on them for a moment. Only then did the countless whistles crossing the sky reach my ears.
*Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!*
A deep shadow fell over my head.
Hundreds of arrowheads flashed as they fell, all aimed at me alone. At the same moment, a red alarm bell rang violently inside my head.
*Shit.*
I knew before I moved.
Dodging them all would be next to impossible.
I was exhausted. My body and senses had grown sluggish, and I stood isolated in an open space with nowhere to evade the countless arrows fired by First Rate masters using internal energy.
*Use as little strength as I can. Avoid anything fatal.*
I gritted my teeth and pulled an abandoned spear from the ground. With my other hand, I reached toward the sky.
*Whummm.*
The air around me trembled.
I’d avoided using my Middle Dantian during the fight unless the danger was extreme, conserving my stamina. Now wasn’t the time to weigh whether it would be bitter or sweet.
Bitter or not, I had to swallow it.
I had to bear it myself.
There was no way in hell I was going to fall here, of all places.
Just as I clenched my fist, ready to meet the arrows hurtling toward me with a ferocious whistle that seemed to tear through my ears—
“Turtle Shell! Defend!”
At a shout from someone whose voice sounded familiar, a group swept in with blinding speed and surrounded me.
They held up massive shields.
*Bam-bam-bam!*
Sparks lit up the darkness. Broken arrow fragments scattered in every direction. Moments later, a second rain of arrows came, and dozens of crescent-bladed polearms flashed toward it.
“Slash!”
*Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh! Slice!*
Blade Force swept across the sky in brilliant half-moons.
The powerful energy formed a kind of barrier, slicing apart every arrow that flew toward them. The scattered fragments couldn’t pierce the gaps in their golden armor.
*Clatter. Thud-thud-thud!*
Countless fragments fell, their force spent.
I watched in silence, then spoke to the familiar face beneath a helmet pulled low.
“Should I thank you for that?”
Jeong Hogun, Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, answered evenly.
“I didn’t know you knew how to say thank you.”
“I don’t say it very often.”
“I thought not. I wasn’t expecting it.”
“What about you?”
“When I owe someone, I thank them. Like now.”
*Clank.*
Jeong Hogun struck his golden armor in a military salute. When he spoke again, his tone had changed.
“Thank you for helping His Majesty. And us.”
“I’m sure you have plenty to ask me, and plenty you want to say. But I’d like you to save it until after this is over.”
Goddammit.
If he came out with something like that before I could even open my mouth, there was nothing left to say.
I clicked my tongue and watched the enemies pressing in from all sides.
“Hey. One question.”
“Anything.”
“That guy over there playing peeping Tom—is he on our side?”
Jeong Hogun flinched at “peeping Tom,” then nodded.
“At least His Majesty is. We’re on your side.”
*At least?*
I understood immediately why he’d added those words.
*So not So Gyo. No—more precisely, he doesn’t know, either.*
It had to be that. Ma Sanbao hadn’t seemed to know, and neither had Cang Gong.
Who that mysterious woman was, or what she had in mind.
An unknown like that meant danger.
*...Shit. Good thing I left the kids behind.*
I muttered to myself and raised the ownerless spear I’d picked up moments ago, aiming it at the enemies surging toward us.
I thought of the Fire Dragon Pavilion members, who should be somewhere safe, waiting for Murim Alliance reinforcements that weren’t coming.
They’d probably kick up a fuss later, repeating “Captain” like parrots. But if they’d stayed here, it wouldn’t have been surprising if they were already dead—
“Captaiiin!”
“Captaaaain!”
What the fuck?
I turned around, feeling as though I’d been possessed by a ghost, and spotted familiar faces appearing in the distance.
“Captaaaaaain!”
More precisely, I saw Hyuk Mujin at the head of the Fire Dragon Pavilion members, hollering at the top of his lungs.
*Rumble-rumble-rumble!*
And countless black figures trailing behind him like a tail.

Splash.*
There was no System message telling me I’d defeated an enemy.
No clear, familiar chime.
But this was enough.
*Finally.
One down.*
Panting, I stared at the corpse lying motionless in a pool of blood, then let out a shout charged with internal energy.
“Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan has killed Ma Sanbao, Brush-Holding Eunuch of the East Depot!”
Before anyone could grasp what that meant, I plunged back into the battlefield, where swords and spears were flying.
*Whoosh!
Crunch!*
Short, simple movements.
The bare minimum of internal energy.
I dodged, struck, and smashed.
*Crack!*
I crushed the face of a man muttering those eight words like a mantra—“Heaven above, earth below.
All demons bow in reverence.” I was sick of hearing them.
*Whsssh!*
As his body crumpled, its features mangled beyond recognition, blades flew at me from either side.
I jerked my head out of their path.
*Clang!*
The two blades missed me by a hand’s breadth and struck each other.
Ignoring the vibration ringing in my ears, I thrust out my torn hand.
*Boom!*
Hot, compressed air burst outward.
I’d put only three-tenths of my internal energy into the Flame Divine Palm.
Even so, the force and heat of that strike were enough to kill most Peak masters on the spot.
The man flew backward, spraying dark red blood.
Whether that nameless enemy lived or died was no longer my concern.
What he’d left behind was another matter.
*Tap.*
His sword had already slipped from his hand.
I caught the hilt and swung it in one smooth motion.
*Shhhh!*
Space split open.
Flames wrapped around the blade, heating the air and burning flesh and bone.
Simple and swift.
Too powerful to stop.
And at the end of it came my enemies’ blood and screams.
*Fwoosh!*
“Gaaah!”
I pushed forward, drenched in blood spraying like a fountain.
I dodged the countless blades crashing in from every direction, knocked them aside, then sent them flying right back where they came from.
When the sword broke, I used a spear.
When the spear snapped, an ax or a dagger.
And if I had none of those, I used arms and legs harder than steel.
*Crunch!*
*Boom!*
I broke the bones and crushed the flesh of every enemy in my way.
There was no need to invoke some grand concept like all streams returning to the sea.
Every weapon in the world had been made to fight more efficiently.
Martial arts existed for the same reason.
Stab.
Slash.
Strike.
To me, martial arts were connections between countless points and lines.
When your life was on the line, you couldn’t afford to rule out any means.
If a weapon could kill an enemy as quickly and surely as possible, its shape didn’t matter.
Just like now.
*Cr-rack!*
A corpse collapsed, its neck bent at an unnatural angle.
The enemies kept blocking my way, no matter how many I killed.
Their lips never stopped murmuring those mantra-like words, but I could see the emotion in their eyes.
*Fear.*
*Huff.
Huff.*
I fought to keep my ragged breathing quiet.
Every muscle in my body throbbed as if I’d been electrocuted, and the hand that had grabbed Ma Sanbao’s sword could barely feel pain anymore.
After pulling something that crazy, I was probably in terrible shape.
But I couldn’t show even the slightest weakness.
Wolves hunted in packs, but no matter how hungry they were, they couldn’t bare their teeth at a lion that roared and charged them.
They only tried to sink their teeth into a lion’s nape when it started backing away.
*Splash.*
My heavy step sent the blood pooled around my ankles rippling.
Like the blood still seeping from the countless wounds carved into my body, the blood reflecting the night sky was dark red.
*Can I do this?*
A wave of exhaustion hit me.
I’d killed over a hundred of them by my rough count, yet enemies still filled my view.
The Great Nation’s—no, Dark Heaven’s—elite.
They ranged from Supreme First Rate to the upper reaches of Peak.

Their individual prowess aside, I had to defeat every last one of those fanatics who worshiped the Lord of Heaven before I could reach Jeok Cheongang, who was still fighting a thunderous battle that seemed like it would never end.
*Goddammit.*
I didn’t know.
We were gaining the upper hand without the Emperor’s help, so why did unease still gnaw at me?
Why did that cloud-choked night sky look so ominous?
No.
I knew.
*This isn’t all of it.*
I couldn’t see them anywhere, no matter how I looked: the assassins who were supposed to protect the Emperor, or the twin Supreme Peak masters who had guarded Qianqing Palace.
Even the number of Embroidered Uniform Guards in the Grand Banquet Hall was only half what I knew it should be.
*And the same goes for Cang Gong.*
The Emperor and Cang Gong.
The two men had crossed a point of no return, yet neither had revealed all his forces.
They had to be concealing their moves, waiting for the other to show his hand first.
I wouldn’t have been surprised if the entire Imperial Capital had split in two by now and was fighting a bloody battle.
*Fuck.*
What a shitty mess.
Even so, I had to fight.
I had to survive.
The Dark Heaven dogs charging beneath that rain of arrows weren’t the only ones I had to survive.
There were also the Emperor and So Gyo, and I didn’t even know whether they were enemies or allies.
*What the hell are you planning?*
I turned toward the high platform in the distance.
Baek Yeon and So Gyo stood on either side of the Emperor.
With those two Supreme Peak masters, either of whom could turn the battle around in an instant, he watched the fighting.
I could also see Aehyang surrounded by a handful of palace attendants, and the young king kneeling for some reason.
My gaze lingered on them for a moment.
Only then did the countless whistles crossing the sky reach my ears.
*Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!*
A deep shadow fell over my head.
Hundreds of arrowheads flashed as they fell, all aimed at me alone.
At the same moment, a red alarm bell rang violently inside my head.
*Shit.*
I knew before I moved.
Dodging them all would be next to impossible.
I was exhausted.
My body and senses had grown sluggish, and I stood isolated in an open space with nowhere to evade the countless arrows fired by First Rate masters using internal energy.
*Use as little strength as I can.
Avoid anything fatal.*
I gritted my teeth and pulled an abandoned spear from the ground.
With my other hand, I reached toward the sky.
*Whummm.*
The air around me trembled.
I’d avoided using my Middle Dantian during the fight unless the danger was extreme, conserving my stamina.
Now wasn’t the time to weigh whether it would be bitter or sweet.
Bitter or not, I had to swallow it.
I had to bear it myself.
There was no way in hell I was going to fall here, of all places.
Just as I clenched my fist, ready to meet the arrows hurtling toward me with a ferocious whistle that seemed to tear through my ears—
“Turtle Shell!
Defend!”
At a shout from someone whose voice sounded familiar, a group swept in with blinding speed and surrounded me.
They held up massive shields.
*Bam-bam-bam!*
Sparks lit up the darkness.
Broken arrow fragments scattered in every direction.
Moments later, a second rain of arrows came, and dozens of crescent-bladed polearms flashed toward it.
“Slash!”
*Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
Slice!*
Blade Force swept across the sky in brilliant half-moons.
The powerful energy formed a kind of barrier, slicing apart every arrow that flew toward them.
The scattered fragments couldn’t pierce the gaps in their golden armor.
*Clatter.
Thud-thud-thud!*
Countless fragments fell, their force spent.
I watched in silence, then spoke to the familiar face beneath a helmet pulled low.
“Should I thank you for that?”
Jeong Hogun, Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, answered evenly.
“I didn’t know you knew how to say thank you.”
“I don’t say it very often.”
“I thought not.
I wasn’t expecting it.”
“What about you?”
“When I owe someone, I thank them.
Like now.”
*Clank.*
Jeong Hogun struck his golden armor in a military salute.
When he spoke again, his tone had changed.
“Thank you for helping His Majesty.
And us.”
“I’m sure you have plenty to ask me, and plenty you want to say.
But I’d like you to save it until after this is over.”
Goddammit.
If he came out with something like that before I could even open my mouth, there was nothing left to say.
I clicked my tongue and watched the enemies pressing in from all sides.
“Hey.
One question.”
“Anything.”
“That guy over there playing peeping Tom—is he on our side?”
Jeong Hogun flinched at “peeping Tom,” then nodded.
“At least His Majesty is.
We’re on your side.”
*At least?*
I understood immediately why he’d added those words.
*So not So Gyo.
No—more precisely, he doesn’t know, either.*
It had to be that.
Ma Sanbao hadn’t seemed to know, and neither had Cang Gong.
Who that mysterious woman was, or what she had in mind.
An unknown like that meant danger.
*...Shit.
Good thing I left the kids behind.*
I muttered to myself and raised the ownerless spear I’d picked up moments ago, aiming it at the enemies surging toward us.
I thought of the Fire Dragon Pavilion members, who should be somewhere safe, waiting for Murim Alliance reinforcements that weren’t coming.
They’d probably kick up a fuss later, repeating “Captain” like parrots.
But if they’d stayed here, it wouldn’t have been surprising if they were already dead—
“Captaiiin!”
“Captaaaain!”
What the fuck?
I turned around, feeling as though I’d been possessed by a ghost, and spotted familiar faces appearing in the distance.
“Captaaaaaain!”
More precisely, I saw Hyuk Mujin at the head of the Fire Dragon Pavilion members, hollering at the top of his lungs.
*Rumble-rumble-rumble!*
And countless black figures trailing behind him like a tail.

chapters.title: Chapter 908
paragraphs: For a moment, every thought in my head stopped.
*What the hell is this?*
I stared, mouth open, at the scene in the distance.
The Fire Dragon Pavilion members were running toward me, panic written all over their faces. A group of black-clad figures was racing after them.
*Rumble, rumble, rumble!*

The ground shook. Even the figures I could see numbered well over a thousand, all dressed in black from head to toe. As they drew closer, their chilling aura grew clearer. It could mean only one thing.
*Enemies!*
The instant I reached that conclusion, a red warning light flashed in my mind.
*Shit.*
I had no idea what had happened, but what I needed to do was clear.
The unknown figures had brought the battlefield to a momentary lull. I shouted at the Embroidered Uniform Guards.
“Quit standing there and pick up your weapons!”
I didn’t expect them to obey me just because I’d given an order. But beside me stood a man of considerable rank—a Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
“Rally! Rally immediately!”
As Jeong Hogun’s shout roused the battlefield, I channeled my internal energy and kicked off the ground.
*Boom!*
Flamefire Path.

Flames burst from my toes, scorching the air. Riding the shock wave, I took one step, then another. The twenty-odd *jang* between me and the stone wall vanished, and the figures atop it came into view.
The Imperial Guards.

Along with the Embroidered Uniform Guard, they were one of the Great Nation’s elite forces, charged with protecting the Imperial Capital. They were also traitors who’d betrayed the Emperor and taken refuge in the shadow of the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, who had lived behind the guise of Cang Gong.

From behind the high stone wall, they had been firing arrows without pause. Their bows were now aimed at the Fire Dragon Pavilion members who had appeared behind them alongside the black-clad figures.
At least, they were until I arrived.
“General, your orders!”
At the urgent call of someone who looked like a junior officer, a middle-aged man in ornate armor swung the baton in his hand without hesitation.
He swung it at me as I closed the dozens of *jang* between us in an instant.
“Loose!”
*Thwang-thwang-thwang! Fwoooosh!*
Nearly a thousand archers turned and released their taut bowstrings. Countless silver arrowheads, imbued with internal energy, blanketed the sky as they rained down on me.
It was a near-perfect volley, powerful enough that even a Supreme Peak master couldn’t ignore it.
But...
*Not if they can’t hit me.*
*Boom!*
Another burst of Flamefire Path exploded from my toes, and I shot forward like a cannonball.
A sudden burst of speed. A swerve.
*Thup-thup-thup-thup!*
Arrows whistled past behind me with a sound that made my skin crawl. I didn’t need to look back to know that the spot where I’d stood a moment ago was bristling with them.
Nor did I think the Imperial Guards, one of the Great Nation’s elite forces, would stop there.
“What the—!”
“Don’t lose your nerve! Loose!”
Their surprise at my speed lasted only a moment. Thoroughly trained, the Imperial Guards nocked new arrows and fired in one swift, fluid motion.
*Fwoooosh!*
Once.
*Thup-thup-thup!*
Then again.
“Fire! I said fire!”
“Begin staggered fire!”
*Thwang-thwang!*
I narrowly evaded the fourth rain of arrows, loosed in two successive waves.
*Bang!*
Then I kicked off the ground and shot into the air. The Imperial Guards were nocking their fifth volley—the last they would get to fire—when they cried out.
“H-He’s coming!”
“Loose! Loose!”
It all happened in an instant: four volleys, and my passage through that dense storm of arrows to the top of the stone wall.
In the world that had slowed around me, a few of the quickest Imperial Guards obeyed the order. Their arrows cut through the air toward me.
Slowly. So slowly that I could hear the wind flowing along each advancing arrowhead.
*Whoosh.*

I reached toward the dozens of arrows flashing in the darkness, each imbued with internal energy. At the same time, I awakened the pulse I alone could feel at the center of my chest, at the point called the Jade Hall.
*Stop.*
At that instant—
*Whoooosh!*
An invisible power, utterly unlike internal energy, spread in every direction at my will. It erased the wind, stilled the air, and caught the dozens of arrows moving through it.
*Rrrrrumble.*
The air trembled. Time returned to its normal pace.
But the Imperial Guards looking up at me, standing in midair, remained frozen in shock.
“Th-This is insane...”
Someone’s groan broke the heavy silence. Reflected in their wide, staring eyes were dozens of arrows suspended as though caught by an invisible hand, with me at their center.
“A m-monster.”
“How... How is this possible?”
Shock. Fear. The questions of men who had seen something they couldn’t comprehend.
And then came the desperate resistance of the few who hadn’t given up.
“What are you waiting for? Shoot him!”
“B-But...”
“All Imperial Guards! Follow the General’s orders and take down that heinous—!”
I shot my hand out like a bolt of lightning toward the few officers screaming at their men.
Or, to be exact, I scattered the arrows I’d been holding with the power of my Middle Dantian.
*Whoosh! Thup-thup-thup!*
“G-Gah!”
“Gaaah!”
Screams followed the arrows’ fierce whistle.
True to their reputation as Imperial Guards, each of them was a master of no small skill. But they couldn’t dodge the arrows I sent flying as if I were controlling them.
Except one.
*Clang-clang!*
Arrows flew aside in a flash of swordlight.

The middle-aged man cut down the attacks converging on him from every direction in a single sweep. His Force shone as brilliantly as the armor that set him apart from the other Imperial Guards. A thought crossed my mind, and I said it aloud.
“One of the Twelve Palaces of the Zodiac?”
The Twelve Palaces of the Zodiac: the collective title for the twelve Supreme Peak masters who represented the imperial court.
“Have you ever heard of the Twelve Palaces of the Zodiac?”
“Sure. Aren’t they the names of constellations?”
“It’s also what they call the twelve Supreme Peak masters who represent the Imperial Capital. And half of them are on our side.”
Ma Sanbao had told me that himself.
The middle-aged man fixed me with a grave look and tightened his grip on his great saber.
“Do you know me?”
“I know you well.”
I nodded and went on.
“You’re the treacherous piece of shit who betrayed the Emperor and sided with Dark Heaven. The asshole who wanted to turn me and my people into pincushions. And the asshole who’s about to die.”
“That about covers it. If you need to add anything, spit it out yourself.”
“...No. That’s enough. Except for one thing.”
His eyes gleamed as he added quietly, “I’m not the one who’s going to die.”
At that moment—
*Whoosh!*
His figure blurred.
Shifting Form and Position: a supreme movement technique available only to those who had reached the highest realms.
He kicked off the stone wall and sprang into the air. His great saber, longer and larger than most grown men, flashed across the space between us.
Its speed and power were worthy of a superhuman. Terrifying energy poured from the Force wrapped around the blade.
*Strong.*
I could tell at a glance how powerful this nameless man was. I could imagine the grueling training it had taken to reach his realm and become commander of the Imperial Guards.
But that was precisely why his saber would never touch me.
If you could take in an entire mountain range at a glance, you had to be looking down from higher up.
*Whoooosh!*
One step was enough.
The great saber tore through distorted space, but it couldn’t match my speed as I moved through the air as if it were solid ground. Only the strands of Force it sent flying barely grazed me.
*Sizzle.*
Pain like a burn.
The pressure split the skin exposed beneath my tattered clothes. Drops of my blood scattered through the air and mingled with someone else’s.
*Grrk. Cough.*
The middle-aged man’s body shuddered with a wet, rattling sound. Something that hadn’t been there a moment ago protruded from his thick, bull-like neck.
Something that glinted coldly in the dark.
“Grrk. Wh-What is this?”
He could barely maintain Stepping on Empty Air. Still, he felt for the arrowhead, as though he couldn’t believe it was there. I watched him calmly.
“I’ve received so many unexpected gifts that I was starting to feel bad. Here, you can have one back.”
“Seizing an Object Through Empty Space?”
“Similar, but different.”
*Tap.*
I touched the center of his swaying chest with a finger.
“Much harder, though. And more certain.”
“...The Middle Dantian. It’s the Middle Dantian.”
*Cough.*
He spat out a mouthful of blood and looked at me, his eyes trembling. Then, with his last strength, he struggled to raise the great saber he still held.
His voice faded as he spoke.
“I... I am the Golden Ox Palace of the Twelve Palaces of the Zodiac, the Chief Commander of the Imperial Guards, and one who devotes his life to the great and almighty Lord of Heaven...”
He never finished.
*Slip.*
Did the saber slide from his hand first? Or did his body tip as death closed in?
I didn’t know which struck the ground first. I didn’t care.
Man and weapon fell together. As a dull thud rose from below, I stepped onto the stone wall.
Right into the middle of the Imperial Guards, who stood frozen like statues.
*Hff.*
Someone drew a sharp breath. I could feel countless emotions swirling among the guards who filled the stone wall.
Fear and anger, shock. And, last of all, confusion at not knowing what to do.
That confusion could mean only one thing.
*Not all of them are Dark Heaven’s lackeys.*

There were thousands of traitors on this battlefield alone. No matter how long the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had lived in the imperial court as Cang Gong, they couldn’t all have been raised as Dark Heaven’s dogs from the start.
The Great Nation’s imperial court wasn’t so easily fooled.
*They were won over. Coerced. Or given orders they couldn’t refuse.*
That was probably how Dark Heaven had brought them into line. Now I had their carrots and sticks in my hands.
“There’s one thing I can promise you, at least.”
I spoke up abruptly, then addressed all the Imperial Guards.
“If you side with the imperial court now, I’ll make sure you don’t end up as traitors, one way or another.”
As soon as I finished speaking, I reached out toward an Imperial Guard officer approaching from a blind spot, his killing intent unmistakable.
*Whoosh. Thud.*
A whistle cut through the air. One more corpse was added to the count.
I pointed at the body lying there, a Finger Qi hole through its brow, and added calmly,
“Anyone who doesn’t like my offer, raise your hand.”
No one raised a hand. I jumped down from the stone wall.
Of course, I didn’t forget one last thing I absolutely had to say.
“Oh, and if there’s someone you know is a real bastard, cut him down right now.”
“E-Excuse me?”
“Kill him. Do it yourselves.”
That’s right.
From here on out, kill each other.
I left the Imperial Guards glancing at one another and ran toward the Fire Dragon Pavilion members fleeing the unknown black-clad figures.
To meet them.
To save them.
*Whoooosh!*

Still, he felt for the arrowhead, as though he couldn’t believe it was there.
I watched him calmly.
“I’ve received so many unexpected gifts that I was starting to feel bad.
Here, you can have one back.”
“Seizing an Object Through Empty Space?”
“Similar, but different.”
*Tap.*
I touched the center of his swaying chest with a finger.
“Much harder, though.
And more certain.”
“...The Middle Dantian.
It’s the Middle Dantian.”
*Cough.*
He spat out a mouthful of blood and looked at me, his eyes trembling.
Then, with his last strength, he struggled to raise the great saber he still held.
His voice faded as he spoke.
I am the Golden Ox Palace of the Twelve Palaces of the Zodiac, the Chief Commander of the Imperial Guards, and one who devotes his life to the great and almighty Lord of Heaven...”
He never finished.
*Slip.*
Did the saber slide from his hand first?
Or did his body tip as death closed in?
I didn’t know which struck the ground first.
I didn’t care.
Man and weapon fell together.
As a dull thud rose from below, I stepped onto the stone wall.
Right into the middle of the Imperial Guards, who stood frozen like statues.
*Hff.*
Someone drew a sharp breath.
I could feel countless emotions swirling among the guards who filled the stone wall.
Fear and anger, shock.
And, last of all, confusion at not knowing what to do.
That confusion could mean only one thing.
*Not all of them are Dark Heaven’s lackeys.*
There were thousands of traitors on this battlefield alone.
No matter how long the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had lived in the imperial court as Cang Gong, they couldn’t all have been raised as Dark Heaven’s dogs from the start.
The Great Nation’s imperial court wasn’t so easily fooled.
*They were won over.
Coerced.
Or given orders they couldn’t refuse.*
That was probably how Dark Heaven had brought them into line.
Now I had their carrots and sticks in my hands.
“There’s one thing I can promise you, at least.”
I spoke up abruptly, then addressed all the Imperial Guards.
“If you side with the imperial court now, I’ll make sure you don’t end up as traitors, one way or another.”
As soon as I finished speaking, I reached out toward an Imperial Guard officer approaching from a blind spot, his killing intent unmistakable.
*Whoosh.
Thud.*
A whistle cut through the air.
One more corpse was added to the count.
I pointed at the body lying there, a Finger Qi hole through its brow, and added calmly,
“Anyone who doesn’t like my offer, raise your hand.”
No one raised a hand.
I jumped down from the stone wall.
Of course, I didn’t forget one last thing I absolutely had to say.
“Oh, and if there’s someone you know is a real bastard, cut him down right now.”
“E-Excuse me?”
“Kill him.
Do it yourselves.”
That’s right.
From here on out, kill each other.
I left the Imperial Guards glancing at one another and ran toward the Fire Dragon Pavilion members fleeing the unknown black-clad figures.
To meet them.
To save them.
*Whoooosh!*

chapters.title: Chapter 909
paragraphs: “Hah... Hah...”
Hyuk Mujin was gasping for breath. His arms and legs, moving nonstop while he was on edge, creaked like they belonged to someone else. His heart felt ready to burst at any second.
*How did it come to this?*
Even as he ran for his life, Hyuk Mujin wondered when and where everything had started going wrong.
But as always, one question led to another, with no end in sight. At the end of it all, only one self-mocking thought remained.
*Fuck. Was being born the mistake?*
Hyuk Mujin felt so wronged and miserable he could have cried.
Why the hell had a textile-shop owner’s son insisted on becoming a martial artist? He could’ve quietly taken over the family business.
If he hadn’t read all those trashy books starring extraordinary martial artists as heroes, he might be like everyone else by now, with a family and two or three kids he adored.
At the very least, he wouldn’t be getting chased by a bunch of weirdos who’d appeared out of nowhere.
*Thud-thud-thud-thud!*
The pursuers’ heavy footsteps rang out behind him. A chill ran down Mujin’s spine.
*Shit. If they catch me, I’m done for.*
He didn’t know who they were or where they’d been hiding before they suddenly appeared, but one thing was certain.
*Those bastards are like monsters. No—they’re monsters.*
It wasn’t just a judgment of their martial arts.
The chill, the primal fear he’d felt from the moment he first spotted the black-clad figures, had only grown stronger with time.
*What the hell... are they?*
His mind was full of questions he couldn’t answer.
And his body, already pushed to its limit, was slipping out of his control a little at a time without him even realizing it.
*Slip.*
His legs suddenly gave out.
Still moving too fast to catch himself, Mujin pitched forward. His eyes flew wide—
“Hyuuuuuk!”
*Grab!*
A thunderous shout rang out as a powerful hand seized his collar. Mujin, who had nearly slammed face-first into the ground, tried to calm his pounding heart and looked up.
*Thump. Thump!*
He saw the face of the giant—no, Taishan—running with Mujin tucked under his arm like a piece of luggage.
“Hyuk. You okay?”
Mujin barely managed to squeeze out a reply.
“No. Not even a little.”
“Yeah. You look that way.”
“...If you know, why ask? Are you messing with me?”
“Hyuk. Is that how you treat the person who saved your life?”
“No. Thanks, then.”
“If you’re thankful, pay me back with a hundred bowls of five-spice pork later.”
“I’ll buy you two hundred bowls, not just a hundred. For now, let’s stay alive. Alive.”
“Two hundred bowls?”
Taishan furrowed his brow and slowed down, muttering to himself.
“How much is two hundred bowls?”
Namho and the Divine Physician, perched on Taishan’s broad shoulders, and Mujin, now tucked under his arm, all screamed at once.
“What kind of lunatic does that? Why the hell are you slowing down all of a sudden?”
“Young Hero Taishan! This is no time for that!”
“What are you doing, you crazy bastard?”
But even amid their frantic protests, Taishan’s brow remained furrowed as he wrestled with the problem.
“I don’t understand. How much is the number two hundred?”
“Goddamn it...”
Namho groaned toward the heavens, then turned to look behind them.
The others bringing up the rear—and the black-clad figures right on their heels—were rapidly drawing closer.
“Just answer him! Looks like he’ll need an answer even if his head gets smashed in! Hurry!”
At the Divine Physician’s desperate plea, Namho shouted, his face pale.
“A hundred bowls! If you have a hundred bowls twice, how many is that?”
“Hmm. A hundred bowls twice is... Ah. Taishan understands now.”
At last, Taishan found his answer. He spoke with a triumphant look.
“A hundred and two.”
“You fucking bastard!”
“You goddamn idiot!”
“Ah, Master...”
Wails erupted all around them.

Namho, driven to the edge of his patience, brought his elbow down on Taishan’s thick skull. Mujin let out a sobbing scream. The Divine Physician thought of his absent master and fingered the large acupuncture needle inside his sleeve, wanting, for the first time, to kill someone.
But unlike the others, Taishan’s face shone like the midday sun. He’d worked out for himself how much two hundred bowls was.
“Two hundred bowls. A lot. Anyway, it’s a whole lot!”
Even a hundred bowls would be enough to eat until his stomach burst. And two hundred bowls!
Truthfully, he didn’t know the exact difference between two hundred and a hundred and two. But Taishan decided not to worry about such trivial details.
Then, grinning broadly, he waved both hands at someone who hadn’t heard the good news yet.
“Pavilion Master! Pavilion Master! Taishan gets to eat five-spice pork! Hyuk said he’ll feed me till I burst—a hundred and two? Two hundred? Anyway, till I burst!”
“Don’t worry about your stomach bursting. Before that, I swear to Heaven I’ll burst your head myself—Wait, what did you just say?”
Namho, who’d been hammering away at Taishan’s crown with all the persistence of the Foolish Old Man moving mountains, widened his eyes and looked up.
And saw him.
Namho saw him. So did the Divine Physician, Hyuk Mujin, and every Fire Dragon Pavilion member following behind.
*Whoooosh!*
Someone was rushing toward them with a fierce whistle of air. Familiar flames burst from his toes.
“Captaiiin!”
Mujin finally let out the tears he’d been holding back.
Life has a way of throwing things at you that make no sense.

For people who’d lived before the Great Cataclysm, it must have been the monsters and Hunters that seemed to drop out of the sky one day. For me, it was the world I’d come to know through the capsule.
The situation in front of me wasn’t quite on that level, but it was still plenty confusing.
“Five-spice pork! A hundred and two! Two hundred!”
Taishan, his face alight with near-maniacal joy.
“Kill this bastard right now! You’re more than capable of cracking this fucking idiot’s head open!”
Namho, radiating so much rage that *mania* didn’t begin to cover it.
“Waaah! Captain! Why’d you take so long?”
Hyuk Mujin, sobbing with the relief of someone who’d died and come back to life.
“Ah, Master... This unworthy Disciple had a wicked thought.”
And finally, the Divine Physician, muttering with such a serene, transcendent expression that he looked ready to send even the Buddha flying with a Palm Strike of the Tathagata.
What the fuck?
I had no idea what was going on.
I stared at them, speechless for a moment, then gave up trying to understand.
Though it would be more accurate to say I didn’t have time to make sense of it.
*Pat-pat!*
“Pavilion Master! No, Young Master Jin! No, Benefactor!”
Ju Hwaran came running toward me, somehow managing to address me by three different titles in the space of a breath. Her clothes were a mess.
Behind her, Song Ilseom and Sama Pyo swung their weapons like mad to keep their pursuers at bay.
*Clang!*
*Slice!*
Sword Energy flashed in the darkness, and what looked like blood sprayed through the air.
The wind carried an unbearable stench with it.
*What’s that smell?*
Even from this distance, it made me frown and turned my stomach.
But I had no time to work out what it was. As the three drew closer, narrowly staying ahead of their pursuers, I moved my lips.
—When I give the signal, everyone get down.
I sent the Sound Transmission to each of them and gathered every last bit of internal energy in my body.
*Shhhh...*
I drew heat from deep within myself and sent it through every limb and acupoint.
My acupoints, still not fully healed, screamed. I felt the wounds I’d sustained in the fight, large and small, tearing wider. But there was no other way.
*I have to do it.*
*Whummm.*
The iron spear I’d taken from some nameless Imperial Guard just before jumping down from the stone wall trembled, filled with Scorching Yang Qi.
The spearhead glowed red. Blue-white flames spread over it, nothing like they once had been, but still too powerful to ignore.
And at last—
*Fwoosh.*
Hellfire surged around the spearhead, burning the air and devouring the darkness. It swelled toward the figures approaching in silence, without a scream or a shout.
Like a beast poised to charge a flock of sheep.
Hotter and more ferocious than anything else in the world.
—Now.
I sent the signal to the three and swung the spear with all my strength, as though to cut the world in two.
Like a dragon’s tail stretching out without end.
*The first form of the Blazing Flame Divine Spear.*
**Fire Dragon’s Single Tail.**
*Fwoooosh!*
In that moment, all around us lit up as brightly as day.
Blue-white flames leaped from the spearhead and surged forward, burning and melting the ornaments scattered throughout the imperial palace.
They passed over the heads of the three, who’d heard my Sound Transmission and dropped down half a beat before the final moment.
Then they engulfed the vision of the black-clad figures close on their heels.
*Kwaaaaaa!*
*Rumble-rumble-rumble!*
A tremendous explosion and roar. Then the earth shook.
Light flashed, and the swelling flames fell like rain, covering a radius of several dozen *jang*.
It was a sight worthy of the name *fire demon*.
And through the acrid smoke of that blazing inferno, where not even a scream could be heard, three people came running.
*Pat-pat!*
Ju Hwaran. Song Ilseom. Sama Pyo.
I spotted their familiar faces and gave a faint smile.
Or maybe it was my vision that was growing faint, tilting a little more with every passing moment.
*Thump.*
Making it look as natural as possible, and without anyone noticing, I straightened the spear and used it to support myself. Then I suppressed my labored breathing.
*...Damn it.*
Weakness crawled up my body like a living snake.
My internal energy, abundant despite its instability, had run dry. My body, which should’ve been resting, cried out in pain from the strain I’d put it through.
And on top of that came mental exhaustion I could barely bear.
*I should’ve held back with the Middle Dantian as much as possible...*
I knew well enough there was no point regretting it now.
If I’d held back more, I wouldn’t be in this state. But there was no guarantee things would’ve gone any better.
For now, I could only be satisfied that I’d saved the Fire Dragon Pavilion members, who’d come back here for some reason, from the danger right in front of them.
“Benefactor!”
Ju Hwaran, now right in front of me, shouted with alarm written across her face.
Song Ilseom and Sama Pyo came up on either side of her and spoke, their expressions strained.
“We all have to run.”
“Right now!”
Their reaction was only natural.

My all-out strike had swept through the front ranks, but at a glance, more than a thousand enemies remained. I couldn’t judge their individual strength precisely, but none of them would be easy to deal with.
Then the smoke began to clear. As the scene behind it slowly came into view, I finally understood.
Why they were so desperate.
And why Ma Sanbao had been so confident the rebellion would succeed.
“That’s...”
A faint groan escaped my parted lips.

chapters.title: Chapter 910
paragraphs: They say even a dog at a village school can recite poetry after three years. Spend a few years working as a Hunter, and you stop batting an eye at most things.
The awful stench coming off a monster’s body? That’s nothing.
If you see blood spraying like a fountain and someone’s limbs getting chopped off—not in a game or a movie, but in real life—
And if that someone is you or one of your companions... well, there’s no need to say more.

First comes the fear of death, before you even set foot on a battlefield. Then you watch brutal scenes day in and day out until every nerve and sense begins to go numb. Only then do you become a Hunter in the truest sense.
That was how it happened for me.
But even I, with a fair amount of hard-earned experience under my belt, couldn’t hold back the nausea rising from the pit of my stomach right now.
“That’s...”
*What the hell is that?*
I couldn’t bring myself to say the rest aloud. I had to clamp my mouth shut just to settle my churning stomach.
And I wasn’t the only one.
“Ugh.”
Ju Hwaran was the first to bend over, her face pale as she covered her mouth.

As heir to the Yongbong Escort Bureau, she’d had far more experience than other young prodigies her age. But compared to the rest of us, she still lacked real combat experience. Her reaction was only natural.
No, the fact that she hadn’t thrown up was impressive.
Everyone here—including me, who’d fought my way through all kinds of hellish situations—was barely holding back a gag, our faces twisted.
“What... What is this?”
The Divine Physician muttered in a strained voice.
The old physician’s eyes trembled with undisguised shock and the fear of someone who’d glimpsed something beyond comprehension.
Along with a sight before us that was impossible to believe.
*Sizzle. Hissss.*
Less than a dozen *jang* away, flesh burned with a sound we could hear. A horrible stench filled my nose.
Amid the remnants of the flames and the blackened ashes, shapes staggered to their feet.
“Grrr... Gaaah.”
Their voices were neither screams nor words.
The black-clad figures—no, the *things*—let out strange, unrecognizable cries through melted lips and stumbled forward.
As though they couldn’t feel the slightest pain.
As though they didn’t even know what state their bodies were in.
*Crack. Crumble.*
Arms, legs, and other parts blackened by the Scorching Yang Qi that had swept through them broke apart and scattered as ash.
One of the things that lost its balance and fell tilted its head.
It looked as though it were asking why its body wouldn’t move. A shiver ran down my spine.
*They’re moving? Even after taking a blow like that?*
Of course, not all of them had been caught in my attack.
But the hundred or so black-clad figures at the very front had taken the flames pouring from my spearhead full on.
That terrible heat. That devastating strike made of Scorching Yang Qi.
I’d seen it with my own eyes, and everyone here knew what they’d seen.
That was why it was so hard to believe.
*That should’ve killed them outright. No—there’s no way they should’ve survived.*
My body might not have been in good shape, but I’d given it everything I had.
I’d poured most of my remaining internal energy into the strike. I’d been certain it would kill at least one in ten of them.
But I’d been wrong.
Before my eyes, nearly half of the hundred figures at the front were getting back up, trampling the ashes of what had once been their comrades.
And they looked nothing like creatures with any life left in them.
“...This is insane. What am I looking at?”
Namho had lived through the horrors of the Great Faction War. His groan spoke for everyone here—except me.
Or, to be more precise, at that moment I was seeing something else the others didn’t know.
*How is this possible?*
Death was fair to everyone.
A Supreme Peak master could be cut down by a weapon just like a Third Rate knife-fighter. Once your skin melted and your insides burned like theirs, you didn’t get back up.
But they had survived.
They showed no sign of screaming, no agitation—not even the pain they should have felt.
*This is...*
That was when a word I desperately didn’t want to believe came to me. It struck like lightning, then slipped through my parted lips.
“Undead...”
Not dead, but not alive either.
Supernatural beings who went on existing past death instead of finding rest. Monsters that should never have appeared in this world.
There was only one answer, and I knew what I had to do.
“Eom Dae-du? What does that mea—”
“Run.”
“What?”
I looked at Hyuk Mujin, whose eyes had gone wide, and spoke to him and everyone else in a low, tight voice.
“If you want to live, run. Right now.”
The next moment—
*Rumble!*
Through the ringing air, the smoke still hanging thick around us, and the blazing piles of ash, an army of the dead walked out and began to advance as one.
“Grrraaaaa!”
Their cries carried the chill of death.
For as long as anyone could remember, the Murim had fascinated the continent’s gossips.
And why wouldn’t it?
Another world, with borders and laws of its own—or rather, none at all.
A place where outlaws lived beyond the bounds of nation and citizen.

It teemed with righteous heroes, fiends, and people who, depending on the moment, might be neither. A mountain of sabers and a forest of swords, where even the greatest master could meet his death at any time.
So those who belonged to the Murim were scorned and admired in equal measure. And the gossips, who loved nothing more than a story, gathered everything they saw and heard and ranked its people.
That was how a book with the ridiculous title *Murim Ranking Record* came into being.
But no matter how many connections those gossips had or how keenly they listened, there was a limit to what they could know.
Who was stronger than whom?
Everyone named in the *Murim Ranking Record* was a formidable master. The closer you got to its last page, the more often you encountered those called superhuman.
Supreme Peak masters of the orthodox faction, the unorthodox faction, the Demonic Cult, or somewhere between orthodox and unorthodox.

Among them were wandering martial artists who roamed the Murim alone like lone wolves, heirs to mysterious and little-known sects, leaders of great powers, and people called Cult Leaders. Most of them shared one thing in common.
Nonaggression. A ban on fighting.
They didn’t confront one another lightly, much less come to blows.
That was only natural when every one of them was a giant capable of moving the Murim. For the gossips, though, it was a disappointment.
If a life-and-death duel broke out between Supreme Peak masters, they’d learn for certain who outranked whom—and gain a rare story they could dine out on for the rest of their lives.
But conflict in the Murim didn’t erupt so easily. For a long time, the last page of the *Murim Ranking Record*, where the greatest warriors’ names were written, went unchanged.
Until the storm of the Great Faction War swept through some fifty years ago.
As if to mock those long years of peace, things no one could have imagined began to change.
One revered master died, then another, and another.
News arrived with every sunrise and sunset. The gossips nearly wore their brushes down recording it all.
But just as surely as the sun rose and set, new names appeared.
“Have a look at this. I think we’ve been given bad information.”
“Bad information? That can’t be right.”
“Read it. It says a thousand Demonic Cult members were wiped out in Anhui. I can’t see how it could be true.”
“A thousand? That’s quite a force. But why doubt it? Looks like the Murim Alliance finally dealt them a proper blow.”
“It wasn’t the Murim Alliance.”
“What?”
“It says it was all done by one person. He wiped out a thousand Demonic Cult members alone, without anyone’s help. Not a single one was spared.”
“...What?”

The name Jeok Cheongang was first made known that way. A few years later, he acquired the title Fire King. By the end of the Great Faction War, which had shaken the world of the Murim, his name had made it to the last page of the *Murim Ranking Record*.
The Martial God and the Three Saints.
And among the ten Supreme Peak masters who followed them, he was the fiercest and strongest of the kings: the King of Kings.
Fire King Jeok Cheongang.
The man himself wasn’t proud of it in the slightest.
“*Murim Ranking Record*? The world’s gone mad. Do they give firewood grand names like that these days?”
The monk who’d brought him the news smiled at Jeok Cheongang’s indifference and sipped his suspiciously warm grain tea.
“Is that so? When I looked it over, I found it surprisingly accurate for firewood.”
“That’s just fools talking nonsense. Are orthodox martial artists the only ones in the world? There are plenty of strong fighters among those who practice demonic and heterodox arts.”
“Even so, in the orthodox Murim, you’re fourth. After the Martial God and the Three Saints. Quite impressive.”
“Enough of that nonsense. Pour this old man a drink. What did you brew it with this time?”
“Amitabha. You mustn’t say such things. This is grain tea, not alcohol.”
“Grain tea, my ass. You sound like you’re kicking the Buddha in the ribs.”
“Watch your mouth. Do you want to suffer in tongue-pulling hell someday?”
“Fine, fine. Give me a cup before I break that Green Jade Buddha Staff you’re holding. I don’t want to set fire to the Shaolin Temple at my age.”
“Ha ha! What a joke. Still, I’d wager that within ten years, you’ll overturn the order of this *Murim Ranking Record*.”
“Hmm. I probably will. I’m old enough that I could be dead within ten years.”
“...Amitabha. You say the most ill-omened things without a second thought.”

“I’ve lived long enough. I don’t know when we’ll meet again, but if you haven’t heard from me in ten years, come to Mount Jiuhua and cremate my body. Scatter my ashes from the highest peak, if you would.”
“Hm. You’re more extravagant than you look. Asking the Abbot of Shaolin to come chant sutras for you.”
“I don’t need sutras or a fortunate rebirth in paradise. That’s how I’ve lived.”
“Then shall we make a wager?”
“A wager? On what?”
“Whether you’ll surpass even the Three Saints in ten years, or die as you say. I’m betting on the former.”
“Trust me. And in ten years, let’s meet here and have another drink.”
That had been a long time ago.

The ten years they’d spoken of had passed three times over. Jeok Cheongang had seen off an unworthy Disciple he’d taken in by mistake, and even the friend who’d sat across from him sharing drinks had returned to the earth.
Yet now, a memory he’d long forgotten came back to him.
The words Hong Dao, the Dharma King, had spoken with a serious face, though he was usually so quick to smile.
*You’ll surpass the Three Saints.*
*Boom!*
His departed friend’s faint voice didn’t fade beneath the blast of air from a powerful Palm Force.
If anything, Jeok Cheongang heard it more clearly.
*Trust me.*
*Shh-shh-shh-shing!*
Wind sharp as blades whipped around him. But the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s fierce attack—the pale-skinned old man’s—didn’t touch a single part of Jeok Cheongang’s body.
To him, that felt entirely natural.
*Ah.*
Elation welled up from deep in his chest.
He had lived a hundred and several decades. All his life, he’d inflicted pain, suffered pain, and, for the first time, shared that pain with someone.
His advanced age. The Heart Demon that had filled his mind.
*I thought this realm, which I reached by a stroke of fortune, was the furthest I could go.*
Now he knew.
He had been wrong. His departed friend had been right.
*Though I haven’t surpassed them yet...*
“I’ll try.”
As the words scattered from the tip of his tongue, a faint smile formed on Jeok Cheongang’s lips.
At that moment—
*Fwoosh.*
A massive blaze unlike anything seen before struck the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord in the chest.
