chapters.title: Chapter 911
paragraphs: He could feel it.
His body and mind were light enough to take flight.
Power welled up from deep within him, and the joy of having taken even a small step into a higher realm swept through Jeok Cheongang.
That sudden, modest insight was blooming into a greater, fiercer blaze.
Just as it was now.
*Fwoosh.*
A dazzling white flame flashed through the darkness, devouring and tearing its way forward.
Toward the enemy before him. Its heat filled the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s gray eyes.
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes widened as a fist came crashing toward him, erasing the space between them.
*What is this?*
He knew instinctively.
The power in that fist was unlike anything in the countless attacks he had clashed with or evaded until now.
The great martial artist known as the Fire King had taken another step forward.
And for the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, that meant only one thing.
*I can’t dodge it.*
At that moment—
*Kwaaaang!*
The earth shook beneath a roar that seemed to split the sky.
A terrifying tremor and the force of the impact swept outward. Through smoke and steam heavy with dreadful heat, a figure was hurled away.
*Whooosh!*
As the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s view spun amid the fierce rush of air, Jeok Cheongang stepped toward him. The impact had sent the Demon Lord flying like a cannonball.
*Crack—boom!*
He moved faster than sound.
Shooting forward like a streak of flame, Jeok Cheongang reached out.
The Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist, brought to full mastery—or perhaps now beyond it—washed the space in white.
*Bang!*
The first strike broke the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s sword.
*Boom!*
The second barely grazed him and melted the ground.
*Kaaa-bang!*
The final, third strike slammed into the staggering Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s chest once more.
It shattered even the formidable Body-Protecting Qi that enveloped him.
*Krrrunch!*
The hard bluestone paving the grand banquet hall crumbled like tofu.
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord hurtled away, his body smashing through more than ten *jang* of ground. Those who grasped what had happened in that instant moved at once.
“Kill him! Kill him!”
“The Demon Lord is in danger!”
“Stop him!”
Shouts rang out from every direction. Blades flashed.
But nothing could stop Jeok Cheongang now.
“Who dares—”
*Crack!*
“—stand in this old man’s way?”
*Boom!*
No one reached Jeok Cheongang. No one could.
Blades gleaming with Sword Energy melted in the flames of the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist, while the Flame Divine Palm shot across the distance and swept through the approaching enemies.
“Urk—cough!”
“Aaargh!”
Those who mustered the courage to charge him head-on were the lucky ones.
Anyone who so much as touched the flames howled as they felt their own body burn alive.
Their screams became their last words.
*Rustle. Thud.*
After a brief but horrific agony, the dead sprawled like rotting trees.
Above the traitors’ bodies, fused to their melted golden armor, flashed armor that had yet to lose its shine.
“Execute the traitors!”
“Long live His Majesty the Emperor!”
*Shh-shh-shing! Slash!*
Jeong Hogun cut down an enemy frozen by the unbelievable display of Jeok Cheongang’s power. Behind him, the Embroidered Uniform Guard charged over the traitors like a wave.
*Clang-clang!*
*Thwack!*
Weapons met, spitting sparks, and blood sprayed in every direction.
At the center of it all, the giant known as the Fire King pressed forward as he always had, smashing and burning everything in his path.
To end this fight.
To reach the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, who was staggering to his feet behind the countless moths still rushing at Jeok Cheongang.
*Boom!*
Scorching Yang Qi, hot as lava, swallowed dozens of enemies.
The bluestone had lost its smooth sheen and melted into a ruin. Corpses burned like firewood amid the embers that remained.
As Jeok Cheongang approached, forging a path of fire no one dared block, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord spoke in a voice mixed with a sigh and admiration.
“You attained... cough. You attained enlightenment?”
Jeok Cheongang stopped a few steps away and stared at him without a word.
The Demon Lord was in a terrible state.
His beard, once white as an immortal’s, was soaked with blood. One arm and one leg were broken. His clothes had already turned to ash, leaving his chest exposed and blackened with burns.
Not even Hua Tuo—or a Great Firmament Immortal—could have guaranteed his survival.
Yet the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord kept giving short, dry coughs and speaking, as though it might ease the terrible pain for even a moment.
“The Three Saints are a thing of the past now. A fourth star has risen right here, today.”
Jeok Cheongang answered in a low voice.
“Call it whatever you want. I don’t care about things like that. But...”
*Step.*
He began walking again. White hellfire rippled over his body, ready to bring this brief, ill-fated encounter to an end.
“You know one thing, at least. The third Demon Lord is about to die.”
Jeok Cheongang’s gaze on the unsteady Eastern Heaven Demon Lord was cold and clear, unlike the energy he wielded.
He would take no chances. He would make certain of the man’s death.
The members of Dark Heaven had demonstrated unbelievable abilities time and again, defying the laws of the world Jeok Cheongang had believed in for more than a hundred years.
But those encounters had been trial and error, not failure.
They had been steps toward something broader and higher.
Each time Jeok Cheongang survived an unpredictable turn of events, he gained experience and insight. Little by little, he grew stronger.
The old monster of Mount Jiuhua was still growing.
Just as his Disciple was.
Just as his close friend, now dead, had once promised he would.
“A certain bald monk said long ago that this old man would surpass the Three Saints before long.”
*Step.*
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord watched Jeok Cheongang approach with careful steps and smiled faintly.
“That monk was right.”
“Yes, he was. Thinking back on it now, I wonder if that monk had some trick for reading the heavenly patterns... but I’ll never be able to find out. Do you know why?”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord didn’t answer. At the mention of reading the heavenly patterns, he had realized which bald monk Jeok Cheongang meant.
And Jeok Cheongang expected no answer.
“He’s dead. Killed by you people of Dark Heaven.”
“...Hong Dao, the Dharma King.”
“If I’d been at Mount Jiuhua, I wouldn’t have been this angry. There would’ve been nothing I could do about it.”
But he hadn’t been at Mount Jiuhua.
Hong Dao, the Dharma King and Jeok Cheongang’s friend, had died at the Blood Lord’s hands within the grounds of Shaolin Temple.
A place Jeok Cheongang could have reached in mere moments.
“That’s how the monk died. By the time I got there, it was too late.”
Jeok Cheongang had once been afraid.

Afraid that the damned infirmities of old age would return one day and erase even the last image of his dying friend. That they would make him forget the vow he had made while biting his lip until it bled.
“That day, I made a vow.”
*Step.*
He took another step and went on.
“I swore I’d kill every last bastard bearing the name of Dark Heaven.”
*Rumble, rumble.*
The ground shook. The air boiled.
Energy hot enough to erase the very air—worthy of being called Extreme Yang, no, Extreme Flame—flowed from Jeok Cheongang’s entire body like lava.
It looked ready to swallow the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord at any moment.
“And today, I’ll send one more to the afterlife with my own hands.”
Five steps.
That was the distance between them, far too little to stand between either man and death.
“Save your last words for Yama.”
At that moment—
*Fap.*
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord pushed off with his foot. His body vanished. Nothing in his speed or movement suggested the man who, moments ago, had seemed to be waiting for death.
*Shh-shing!*
Jeok Cheongang reacted to the sound cutting past his ears.
Two rushes of air overlapped. No—three.
“Hah!”
*Paaang!*
The azure dragon’s roar shook the battlefield, the internal energy carried in Jeok Cheongang’s shout bursting the compressed air.
At the same time, two streaks of light shot toward Jeok Cheongang’s back as if guided by an invisible hand—then were knocked away.

They were the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s two swords, pulled toward him by the power of his Middle Dantian. Jeok Cheongang drew up energy from throughout his body, gathered it in both hands, and swung upward as though scooping from below.
Toward the sky above him. Toward the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, falling like a meteor.
*Whoom.*
Two currents of white energy, unmistakably alike yet astonishingly different, rushed toward each other.
To the two men, they moved slower than an ant. To everyone else, they moved too fast to see.
And the moment the two monsters struck with both palms, each using all his strength—
*Kaaaang!*
*Rumble, rumble, rumble!*

A blinding flash filled everyone’s vision. A vast, terrifying force unlike anything before it burst outward, spreading in every direction. It swelled until it swallowed the sprawling grand banquet hall, already turned into a battlefield.
*Whooosh.*
The darkness disappeared. So did the unsteady torchlight, the people driving blue blades into their enemies, and the angry shouts they had been roaring.
No—more precisely, the flash and roar had blinded and deafened everyone for an instant.
A white world where nothing could be seen or heard.
Those trapped within it forgot friend and foe alike, frozen in confusion. Only a tiny handful were exceptions.
*Papapat!*
Jeok Cheongang and the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord charged at each other without pause.
Moving faster than sound, they deflected each other’s attacks, countered, and charged again.
To the rest of the world, it all lasted but an instant. To these superhumans, who had cast off the limits of humanity, it was different.
In time that seemed to have stopped, they fought hundreds of exchanges and faced dozens of close calls, until at last they reached the end of their seemingly endless life-and-death duel.
*Thwack!*
Bone and flesh crushed, and one figure staggered.
But the fist piercing his chest and protruding from his back, wreathed in white flame, would not even let him fall.
“Truly... truly remarkable...”
His voice trailed off, drained of strength.
In Jeok Cheongang’s deeply sunken eyes, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s shattered arms hung limp.
“If Yama asks why you died...”
*Shunk.*
Jeok Cheongang slowly pulled his fist free. Only then did the Demon Lord’s body begin to crumple.
“...Tell him a friend of that bald monk sent you.”
*Thud.*
Jeok Cheongang silently looked down at the fallen Eastern Heaven Demon Lord. Not a trace of life remained in the corpse.

sentences.text: He could feel it.
His body and mind were light enough to take flight.
Power welled up from deep within him, and the joy of having taken even a small step into a higher realm swept through Jeok Cheongang.
That sudden, modest insight was blooming into a greater, fiercer blaze.
Just as it was now.
*Fwoosh.*
A dazzling white flame flashed through the darkness, devouring and tearing its way forward.
Toward the enemy before him.
Its heat filled the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s gray eyes.
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes widened as a fist came crashing toward him, erasing the space between them.
*What is this?*
He knew instinctively.
The power in that fist was unlike anything in the countless attacks he had clashed with or evaded until now.
The great martial artist known as the Fire King had taken another step forward.
And for the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, that meant only one thing.
*I can’t dodge it.*
At that moment—
*Kwaaaang!*
The earth shook beneath a roar that seemed to split the sky.
A terrifying tremor and the force of the impact swept outward.
Through smoke and steam heavy with dreadful heat, a figure was hurled away.
*Whooosh!*
As the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s view spun amid the fierce rush of air, Jeok Cheongang stepped toward him.
The impact had sent the Demon Lord flying like a cannonball.
*Crack—boom!*
He moved faster than sound.
Shooting forward like a streak of flame, Jeok Cheongang reached out.
The Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist, brought to full mastery—or perhaps now beyond it—washed the space in white.
*Bang!*
The first strike broke the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s sword.
*Boom!*
The second barely grazed him and melted the ground.
*Kaaa-bang!*
The final, third strike slammed into the staggering Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s chest once more.
It shattered even the formidable Body-Protecting Qi that enveloped him.
*Krrrunch!*
The hard bluestone paving the grand banquet hall crumbled like tofu.
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord hurtled away, his body smashing through more than ten *jang* of ground.
Those who grasped what had happened in that instant moved at once.
“Kill him!
Kill him!”
“The Demon Lord is in danger!”
“Stop him!”
Shouts rang out from every direction.
Blades flashed.
But nothing could stop Jeok Cheongang now.
“Who dares—”
*Crack!*
“—stand in this old man’s way?”
*Boom!*
No one reached Jeok Cheongang.
No one could.
Blades gleaming with Sword Energy melted in the flames of the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist, while the Flame Divine Palm shot across the distance and swept through the approaching enemies.
“Urk—cough!”
“Aaargh!”
Those who mustered the courage to charge him head-on were the lucky ones.
Anyone who so much as touched the flames howled as they felt their own body burn alive.
Their screams became their last words.
*Rustle.
Thud.*
After a brief but horrific agony, the dead sprawled like rotting trees.
Above the traitors’ bodies, fused to their melted golden armor, flashed armor that had yet to lose its shine.
“Execute the traitors!”
“Long live His Majesty the Emperor!”
*Shh-shh-shing!
Slash!*
Jeong Hogun cut down an enemy frozen by the unbelievable display of Jeok Cheongang’s power.
Behind him, the Embroidered Uniform Guard charged over the traitors like a wave.
*Clang-clang!*
*Thwack!*
Weapons met, spitting sparks, and blood sprayed in every direction.
At the center of it all, the giant known as the Fire King pressed forward as he always had, smashing and burning everything in his path.
To end this fight.
To reach the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, who was staggering to his feet behind the countless moths still rushing at Jeok Cheongang.
*Boom!*
Scorching Yang Qi, hot as lava, swallowed dozens of enemies.
The bluestone had lost its smooth sheen and melted into a ruin.
Corpses burned like firewood amid the embers that remained.
As Jeok Cheongang approached, forging a path of fire no one dared block, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord spoke in a voice mixed with a sigh and admiration.
“You attained... cough.
You attained enlightenment?”
Jeok Cheongang stopped a few steps away and stared at him without a word.
The Demon Lord was in a terrible state.
His beard, once white as an immortal’s, was soaked with blood.
One arm and one leg were broken.
His clothes had already turned to ash, leaving his chest exposed and blackened with burns.
Not even Hua Tuo—or a Great Firmament Immortal—could have guaranteed his survival.
Yet the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord kept giving short, dry coughs and speaking, as though it might ease the terrible pain for even a moment.
“The Three Saints are a thing of the past now.
A fourth star has risen right here, today.”
Jeok Cheongang answered in a low voice.
“Call it whatever you want.
I don’t care about things like that.
But...”
*Step.*
He began walking again.
White hellfire rippled over his body, ready to bring this brief, ill-fated encounter to an end.
“You know one thing, at least.
The third Demon Lord is about to die.”
Jeok Cheongang’s gaze on the unsteady Eastern Heaven Demon Lord was cold and clear, unlike the energy he wielded.
He would take no chances.
He would make certain of the man’s death.
The members of Dark Heaven had demonstrated unbelievable abilities time and again, defying the laws of the world Jeok Cheongang had believed in for more than a hundred years.
But those encounters had been trial and error, not failure.
They had been steps toward something broader and higher.
Each time Jeok Cheongang survived an unpredictable turn of events, he gained experience and insight.
Little by little, he grew stronger.
The old monster of Mount Jiuhua was still growing.
Just as his Disciple was.
Just as his close friend, now dead, had once promised he would.
“A certain bald monk said long ago that this old man would surpass the Three Saints before long.”
*Step.*
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord watched Jeok Cheongang approach with careful steps and smiled faintly.
“That monk was right.”
“Yes, he was.
Thinking back on it now, I wonder if that monk had some trick for reading the heavenly patterns... but I’ll never be able to find out.
Do you know why?”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord didn’t answer.
At the mention of reading the heavenly patterns, he had realized which bald monk Jeok Cheongang meant.
And Jeok Cheongang expected no answer.
“He’s dead.
Killed by you people of Dark Heaven.”
“...Hong Dao, the Dharma King.”
“If I’d been at Mount Jiuhua, I wouldn’t have been this angry.
There would’ve been nothing I could do about it.”
But he hadn’t been at Mount Jiuhua.
Hong Dao, the Dharma King and Jeok Cheongang’s friend, had died at the Blood Lord’s hands within the grounds of Shaolin Temple.
A place Jeok Cheongang could have reached in mere moments.
“That’s how the monk died.
By the time I got there, it was too late.”
Jeok Cheongang had once been afraid.
Afraid that the damned infirmities of old age would return one day and erase even the last image of his dying friend.
That they would make him forget the vow he had made while biting his lip until it bled.
“That day, I made a vow.”
*Step.*
He took another step and went on.
“I swore I’d kill every last bastard bearing the name of Dark Heaven.”
*Rumble, rumble.*
The ground shook.
The air boiled.
Energy hot enough to erase the very air—worthy of being called Extreme Yang, no, Extreme Flame—flowed from Jeok Cheongang’s entire body like lava.
It looked ready to swallow the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord at any moment.
“And today, I’ll send one more to the afterlife with my own hands.”
Five steps.
That was the distance between them, far too little to stand between either man and death.

*Fap.*
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord pushed off with his foot.
His body vanished.
Nothing in his speed or movement suggested the man who, moments ago, had seemed to be waiting for death.
*Shh-shing!*
Jeok Cheongang reacted to the sound cutting past his ears.
Two rushes of air overlapped.
No—three.

chapters.title: Chapter 912
paragraphs: Everything happened in a flash.
Jeok Cheongang sensed the sinister energy flying at him from behind. Alarm bells rang in his mind, and he twisted away.
But even instinct, faster than reason, couldn’t help him fully evade the strike.
*Crunch.*
Hot. And cold at the same time.
The two opposing pains began in his side and spread through his body like wildfire, bringing with them a question he could not answer.
Jeok Cheongang looked down, his eyes trembling, at something buried halfway in his side.
It had crushed flesh and bone, severing the vital points and internal energy within him strand by strand. It was a white hand.
Pale as a corpse’s—or rather, the hand of someone who should have been lying dead.
“How could you... how could you...”
Jeok Cheongang lifted his head, forcing the words out. Before him was a face he should never have seen again.
“You were clearly... dead.”
The owner of the hand, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, replied.
“Yes, I was.”
Then he added, his voice calm as if nothing had happened, his expression showing not a trace of pain:
“But who in this world can lose his one and only life twice?”
“...What?”
Jeok Cheongang stared at him, eyes wide, unable to make sense of it. Instead of an answer, icy energy burrowed into his body.
*Danger!*
It happened almost at the same time.
Powerful Palm Force drove deep inside him, and Jeok Cheongang twisted away in a flash.
But caught off guard by the first blow, he couldn’t evade this one completely.
*Boom!*
Jeok Cheongang bit his lip as his vision dimmed for an instant.
*Kh.*
The pain was intense.
He felt the Body-Protecting Qi around him scatter like smoke, and his body shot backward.
*Whoooosh!*
His vision blurred. The sky and earth flipped over and over.
Someone screamed. Fragments of whatever his hurtling body had struck flew in every direction.
A blow like that would have taken even a Supreme Peak master out of the fight.
But he was the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
*Crack! Bang!*
He twisted in midair, righted himself, and landed on his feet.
Jeok Cheongang carved a deep furrow several *jang* long into the ground, absorbing the remaining force. Then his body suddenly staggered.
*Hack.*
Dark red blood spilled from between his lips.
Unable to hold back the congested blood that had risen with his internal injuries, Jeok Cheongang spat it out. That was when a faint whistle reached his ears.
*Whoosh.*
He couldn’t see it. But he could feel it.
A strike plunging toward his head. The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord reaching out with a hand that shone an icy, glacial white.
Picturing the scene half a beat before it happened, Jeok Cheongang pushed off the ground.
*Shwaaack! Boom!*
In that sliver of an instant, the strike narrowly missed him. It cleaved through the ground like tofu, then exploded, leaving a huge crater.
A few Embroidered Uniform Guards nearby were unlucky enough to be swallowed up by it.
But the predator’s pursuit didn’t end when it missed its prey.
*Swish.*
The movement was as smooth as a snake’s.
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord rose from the crater and stepped toward the retreating Jeok Cheongang.
*Papap!*
In an instant, he closed the distance between them. A dazzling, icy white light burst from his fingertips.
*Fwoosh.*
Jeok Cheongang watched that brilliant, dreadful light swell and swallow the darkness. He gritted his teeth.
*Crack.*
A faint pain, then the taste of blood in his mouth.
At last his blurred vision came into focus. His dulled senses returned, making the pain from his internal injuries sharper, but he paid it no mind. He drew up the internal energy throughout his body.
*Wooooong.*
The air, chilled moments ago, grew hot. His torn meridians screamed.
The fire dragon inside him writhed violently, barely under his control.
As if it would burn even its master’s body.
As if it would devour everything and reduce it to ashes.
And yet—
“I don’t know what strange power brought you back to life.”
Jeok Cheongang met the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s gaze without a flicker of hesitation. His voice burned like lava as he went on.
“But I’ll put an end to that stubborn life of yours.”
Even if he had to do it dozens, hundreds of times.
His closed lips held back the words he left unsaid. They could not hold back the several *jiazi* of Scorching Yang Qi surging through his body, setting every limb and meridian ablaze.
*KWAOOOOO!*
Amid a roar like a dragon’s, light-flames and white light shot toward each other. At last, they collided.
At the center of that space, warped by an energy beyond anything seen before, they swallowed even Jeong Hogun’s scream-like order to retreat.
*Fwoosh.*
And in the blinding flash that filled his vision, Jeok Cheongang heard a voice.
“Old Master!”
The next moment—
*Rumble, rumble, rumble!*
The entire world—the sky and the earth—shook.
There are moments when it feels as if the world has stopped.
When the shock and roar shaking everything around you numb every sense.
That was how it felt to me right then.
If the sun fell from the sky and landed right in front of you, would it feel like this?
Blinded and deafened by the flash and roar, all I could do was protect the people nearby as best I could from the enormous force about to hit us.
“Get down, ri—!”
I had no idea whether my frantic shout reached the Fire Dragon Pavilion members, or whether they’d dropped to the ground when they heard it.
I knew only one thing for certain: if they’d hesitated for even a moment, not one of them would still be on their feet.
*KWAaaaaa!*
*Rrrrcrack!*
The raging gale shoved me back. The ground heaved like a volcanic field, and bluestone broke into dozens, hundreds of fragments that flew in every direction like hidden weapons.
The corpses of those already dead went with them, along with the countless weapons that had lain scattered around like their gravestones.
*Sh-sh-sh-shik! Thud!*
“Aaargh!”
Someone’s blood and screams scattered on the wind.
But I drove both feet deep into the ground and took the shock wave with my whole body.
Squeezing out what little internal energy I had left, I knocked aside or cut down everything flying toward us.
*Pit-pit!*
Even when small, thin fragments of blades and bluestone swept in with the gale and grazed me all over, I didn’t care.
*If I dodge, the others will get hurt.*
If someone had to be hurt, it was a hundred, a thousand times better for that someone to be me.
*Old Master must have felt the same way.*
I’d seen him clearly at the last moment.
He’d heard my shout and suddenly shifted to block the direction we were heading.
*KWAaaaaa...*
How much time passed?
After what felt like an eternity, the roar and the shock began to fade.
One by one, the things the wind had hurled into the air fell back down. Sounds that had gone muffled for a moment began to reach my ears again.
“Ungh...”
“P-please. Save me...”
The groans of people from both sides, fallen in a tangled heap. Someone begging for their life.
And finally, familiar voices behind me.
“Is everyone—everyone all right?”
“Cough. I’m fine.”
“Taishan gritted his teeth and held on by thinking about two hundred plates of five-spice pork.”
“I’m really sorry to ask at a time like this, but can someone break that bastard’s teeth?”
I wanted to answer Namho, but my strength had given out. Even that was difficult.
I staggered, and two people hurried over to grab my arms.
“Benefactor—no, Young Master Jin—no, Pavilion Master.”
“Captain, are you all right?”
I told Ju Hwaran to pick one form of address and stick to it. Then I gave Hyuk Mujin a long look that meant, *Do I look all right to you?*
Only then did I see the undead army climbing over the stone wall several dozen *jang* away.
The Imperial Guards, who had changed sides to avoid being branded traitors, were now falling in droves as the monsters that had appeared out of nowhere tore into them.
*Damn it. Maybe I should’ve lured them here after all.*
I couldn’t help wondering whether we might have done some damage to them if I had. But there was no telling how it would have turned out.
Those things were undead, plain and simple.
Monsters that got back up even with their arms and legs torn off or their chests pierced.
But the word *monster* wasn’t reserved for things with grotesque appearances or strange powers.
People used it for anything that defied common sense.
And the man known as the Fire King belonged in that category, too.
*Papap!*
I pushed Hyuk Mujin aside when he tried to stop me and hurried toward Jeok Cheongang as fast as I could.
No—I tried to.
If not for the one thing Jeok Cheongang said next.
“Stand back.”
His voice was deeper than usual.
His entire body was covered in blood and soot, but he kept his eyes fixed ahead without even glancing at me, though I stood a few steps behind him.
At the lone figure standing beyond the slowly settling dust cloud.
And right then—
*Fwoosh.*
A breeze blew from somewhere, sweeping away the dust cloud. Beyond it, the figure came into view, walking slowly over countless corpses and pools of blood.
I caught my breath without meaning to. Only then did I understand.
Why Jeok Cheongang had told me to stand back.
And why I hadn’t sensed even the slightest sign of life from someone who, for a moment, had been right beside us.
“Impressive, Fire King Jeok Cheongang. Truly impressive.”
*Squish.*
With each step, blood that had pooled to his ankles sprayed in every direction.
Arms and legs that had belonged to someone unknown bobbed in the blood as it pushed them along.
Yet none of it was as chilling as *that thing*.
“I very nearly died, you know.”
*Crackle. Sizzle.*
The flames were still burning his face. Beneath it, the only part that had kept its shape—his lips—curved into a gentle smile.
Cang Gong—the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord—or rather, the man who could no longer be called human, was smiling.
Melted skin left the bones beneath it plainly exposed.
In a state that would have killed anyone made of flesh and blood several times over, he looked at Jeok Cheongang, then at me, frozen behind Jeok Cheongang’s shoulder.
And then he spoke.
“You two seem very close, master and disciple. Don’t you think?”
At that moment, a voice I’d thought I would never hear again reached my ears.
“Yes, Master.”
“You’re late.”
“Forgive me. Your unworthy Disciple’s training wasn’t sufficient.”
Another figure staggered to his feet as he answered.
Ma Sanbao pulled out the short spear I’d driven deep into his body and came toward us. Jeok Cheongang muttered:
“Master?”
“Why? Is that strange?”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord stepped forward and continued:
“I once had a sect, too. A Master who became a parent to me, and countless Senior and Junior Brothers who became my family.”
“...You bastard. Don’t tell me...”
“But they all died. They bled and fell defending their sect’s home against an oppression that made no sense.”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord slowly turned his head. At the end of his empty gaze sat the Emperor, on a tall, ornate throne.
No—what lay there was a past long gone.
“Under the pretext of moving the capital, I had to lose them all.”
At that moment, I realized who he really was. Before he became the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord of Dark Heaven, before he became Cang Gong of the East Depot, where had he belonged?
Jeok Cheongang realized it, too.
“...The Maoshan Sect.”
The words slipped from his lips like a groan.
*Crick. Crrrick.*
At last, the army of the dead breached the stone wall and poured into the grand banquet hall.

I had no idea whether my frantic shout reached the Fire Dragon Pavilion members, or whether they’d dropped to the ground when they heard it.
I knew only one thing for certain: if they’d hesitated for even a moment, not one of them would still be on their feet.
*KWAaaaaa!*
*Rrrrcrack!*
The raging gale shoved me back.
The ground heaved like a volcanic field, and bluestone broke into dozens, hundreds of fragments that flew in every direction like hidden weapons.
The corpses of those already dead went with them, along with the countless weapons that had lain scattered around like their gravestones.
*Sh-sh-sh-shik!
Thud!*
“Aaargh!”
Someone’s blood and screams scattered on the wind.
But I drove both feet deep into the ground and took the shock wave with my whole body.
Squeezing out what little internal energy I had left, I knocked aside or cut down everything flying toward us.
*Pit-pit!*
Even when small, thin fragments of blades and bluestone swept in with the gale and grazed me all over, I didn’t care.
*If I dodge, the others will get hurt.*
If someone had to be hurt, it was a hundred, a thousand times better for that someone to be me.
*Old Master must have felt the same way.*
I’d seen him clearly at the last moment.
He’d heard my shout and suddenly shifted to block the direction we were heading.
*KWAaaaaa...*
How much time passed?
After what felt like an eternity, the roar and the shock began to fade.
One by one, the things the wind had hurled into the air fell back down.
Sounds that had gone muffled for a moment began to reach my ears again.
“Ungh...”
“P-please.
Save me...”
The groans of people from both sides, fallen in a tangled heap.
Someone begging for their life.
And finally, familiar voices behind me.
“Is everyone—everyone all right?”
“Cough.
I’m fine.”
“Taishan gritted his teeth and held on by thinking about two hundred plates of five-spice pork.”
“I’m really sorry to ask at a time like this, but can someone break that bastard’s teeth?”
I wanted to answer Namho, but my strength had given out.
Even that was difficult.
I staggered, and two people hurried over to grab my arms.
“Benefactor—no, Young Master Jin—no, Pavilion Master.”
“Captain, are you all right?”
I told Ju Hwaran to pick one form of address and stick to it.
Then I gave Hyuk Mujin a long look that meant, *Do I look all right to you?*
Only then did I see the undead army climbing over the stone wall several dozen *jang* away.
The Imperial Guards, who had changed sides to avoid being branded traitors, were now falling in droves as the monsters that had appeared out of nowhere tore into them.
*Damn it.
Maybe I should’ve lured them here after all.*
I couldn’t help wondering whether we might have done some damage to them if I had.
But there was no telling how it would have turned out.
Those things were undead, plain and simple.
Monsters that got back up even with their arms and legs torn off or their chests pierced.
But the word *monster* wasn’t reserved for things with grotesque appearances or strange powers.
People used it for anything that defied common sense.
And the man known as the Fire King belonged in that category, too.
*Papap!*
I pushed Hyuk Mujin aside when he tried to stop me and hurried toward Jeok Cheongang as fast as I could.
No—I tried to.
If not for the one thing Jeok Cheongang said next.
“Stand back.”
His voice was deeper than usual.
His entire body was covered in blood and soot, but he kept his eyes fixed ahead without even glancing at me, though I stood a few steps behind him.
At the lone figure standing beyond the slowly settling dust cloud.
And right then—
*Fwoosh.*
A breeze blew from somewhere, sweeping away the dust cloud.
Beyond it, the figure came into view, walking slowly over countless corpses and pools of blood.
I caught my breath without meaning to.
Only then did I understand.
Why Jeok Cheongang had told me to stand back.
And why I hadn’t sensed even the slightest sign of life from someone who, for a moment, had been right beside us.
“Impressive, Fire King Jeok Cheongang.
Truly impressive.”
*Squish.*
With each step, blood that had pooled to his ankles sprayed in every direction.
Arms and legs that had belonged to someone unknown bobbed in the blood as it pushed them along.
Yet none of it was as chilling as *that thing*.
“I very nearly died, you know.”
*Crackle.
Sizzle.*
The flames were still burning his face.
Beneath it, the only part that had kept its shape—his lips—curved into a gentle smile.
Cang Gong—the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord—or rather, the man who could no longer be called human, was smiling.
Melted skin left the bones beneath it plainly exposed.
In a state that would have killed anyone made of flesh and blood several times over, he looked at Jeok Cheongang, then at me, frozen behind Jeok Cheongang’s shoulder.
And then he spoke.
“You two seem very close, master and disciple.
Don’t you think?”
At that moment, a voice I’d thought I would never hear again reached my ears.
“Yes, Master.”
“You’re late.”
“Forgive me.
Your unworthy Disciple’s training wasn’t sufficient.”
Another figure staggered to his feet as he answered.
Ma Sanbao pulled out the short spear I’d driven deep into his body and came toward us.
Jeok Cheongang muttered:
“Master?”
“Why?
Is that strange?”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord stepped forward and continued:
“I once had a sect, too.
A Master who became a parent to me, and countless Senior and Junior Brothers who became my family.”
“...You bastard.
Don’t tell me...”
“But they all died.
They bled and fell defending their sect’s home against an oppression that made no sense.”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord slowly turned his head.
At the end of his empty gaze sat the Emperor, on a tall, ornate throne.
No—what lay there was a past long gone.
“Under the pretext of moving the capital, I had to lose them all.”
At that moment, I realized who he really was.
Before he became the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord of Dark Heaven, before he became Cang Gong of the East Depot, where had he belonged?
Jeok Cheongang realized it, too.
“...The Maoshan Sect.”
The words slipped from his lips like a groan.
*Crick.
Crrrick.*
At last, the army of the dead breached the stone wall and poured into the grand banquet hall.

chapters.title: Chapter 913
paragraphs: A sea of corpses and blood.
There was no other way to describe it.
Everywhere the eye could see, corpses lay strewn about and blood ran in overflowing streams.

This vast space had been built for imperial celebrations. Today, it was a battlefield where countless people killed and died. The Embroidered Uniform Guard under Jeong Hogun had finally put down most of the traitors, but they had no chance to savor their victory.
Instead, they stood back-to-back, afraid.
Their battle wasn’t over.
Now they faced monsters far beyond the bounds of common sense.
*Grrk. Grrrr.*
A terrible stench smothered even the thick smell of blood.
Jeok Cheongang stood back-to-back with Jin Taekyung, watching the creatures surround them and let out cries no one could understand. Then he spoke.
“Let me ask you one thing.”
“You can ask me as many things as you want for three days straight.”
Jin Taekyung spat out the blood pooling in his mouth, picked up a spear and sword lying on the ground, and added:
“If those bastards are willing to wait that long, of course.”
Of course, Jin Taekyung knew there was no chance of that happening.
*Everyone’s thinking the same thing.*

The faces of the Fire Dragon Pavilion members and the Embroidered Uniform Guards, now standing back-to-back in a circle, showed the same feelings swirling inside him. And then Jeok Cheongang’s subdued voice came from behind him, tense in a way he couldn’t hide.
“The realm of immortals... Your homeland. Does it have things like those?”
Jin Taekyung answered without hesitation.
“Of course. Tons of them.”
“Tons? Just how many?”
“Uh, Old Master, how many meals do you think Taishan’s eaten in his life?”
“An awful lot, I’d imagine. Too many to count.”
“I think so, too. Now imagine at least dozens—no, hundreds of times that many.”
Understanding dawned, and Jeok Cheongang sighed.
“Fuck, that’s a lot.”
“Yeah. A fucking lot. Some lunatic must’ve accounted for different tastes, too, because there are all kinds.”
“Damn it. That’s no realm of immortals. It’s the Demon Realm.”
“Oh, that’s a separate place. I think I told you about it before.”
“...For fuck’s sake. What kind of world is that?”
“What kind? A shitty one. But you know what?”
“What?”
“This place seems to be getting just as shitty as my homeland.”
Jeok Cheongang was silent for a moment after Jin Taekyung answered. Then he spoke.
“Yes,” he said at last. “I think so, too. I suppose I’ve lived too long, to see a miserable sight like this.”
“Why say you’ve lived too long? Don’t jinx it.”
“Enough with the pointless worrying. I plan to live another fifty years.”
“That’s much better. Yeah. You’d better.”
Jin Taekyung tried to sound cheerful, but a great weight had settled in his chest.
*Damn it.*
He silently surveyed the area. Familiar and unfamiliar faces alike filled his vision.
On every face, the whirlpool of complicated emotions they were feeling showed plainly.
Tension. Shock. Fear.
And a handful of courage, drawn with difficulty from beneath it all.
*How many of them will make it out alive?*
Jin Taekyung forced himself to erase the ominous question that had suddenly crossed his mind. Right now, keeping his attention on the enemy was all he could manage.
“I have waited a very long time for this day.”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord stood tall at the head and center of the army of the dead encircling the battlefield. He spoke slowly.
To everyone there.
No—to the Emperor.
“Today, in this very place, the Great Nation will cease to exist.”
At that moment—
*Shhhhh.*
An inexplicable chill spread through the air.
Pale energy flowed from the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s entire body, seeping like smoke across the battlefield.
No. It was swallowing the battlefield whole.
A bell in his hand rang, and the energy moved to its rhythm.
*Jingle.*
The eerie chime rang clear, yet it reached the mind rather than the ears. It was more like a wave of energy than an ordinary sound.
Most people lacked the martial arts realm to make sense of it.
But that same wave was raising those who no longer lived.
By the time Jin Taekyung realized what was happening, he was already too late.
*Thump.*
“Old Master!”
“Stop.”
Jeok Cheongang grabbed Jin Taekyung by the shoulder as he was about to shoot toward the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, and continued in a sunken voice:
“It’s already too late.”
Jin Taekyung’s eyes widened. The change that followed showed him what Jeok Cheongang meant.
*Crick. Crrick.*
The ground trembled. As the vibrations grew stronger, the pools of blood rippled and the air turned cold.
*No. That’s not it.*
Jin Taekyung swallowed a gasp. His trembling gaze fixed on the nameless corpse at his feet, which had begun to stir.
*It isn’t the ground... It’s the corpses.*
The thousands of corpses covering the battlefield were waking.
Returning to the world of the living, where they no longer belonged. Becoming something other than human.
“W-what is this?”
“Strike before they—before those monsters get up! Hurry!”
*Thwack! Slice!*
The air grew colder, and fear spread with it.
Spears and swords struck the corpses in a frenzy, but they would not stay down.
Amid the chaos, Jeok Cheongang remembered the legends of the Maoshan Sect, erased from Murim long ago. He looked at his Disciple.
“What do you call things like this where you live?”
*Crunch!*
Jin Taekyung stamped on the corpse beneath his foot and answered through gritted teeth.
“Undead.”
*Grrr...*
A corpse with its throat split open lifted its head from a pool of blood. Jin Taekyung had crushed its spine, yet it still struggled to rise.
“They’re monsters that aren’t dead, but aren’t alive, either.”
Jeok Cheongang nodded.
The pronunciation was unfamiliar, but the meaning was similar.
Among all the sects and martial families under Heaven, only the Maoshan Sect had preserved tales of such monsters. *Undead* described them perfectly.
*Monsters that aren’t dead, but aren’t alive, either.*
When Jeok Cheongang had first heard those tales, he had dismissed them as nonsense invented by idle gossips.
It was simply impossible.
It defied the natural order ordained by Heaven—an utterly bizarre legend.
But now, that was no longer the case.
The unbelievable legend was before his eyes.
“...Jiangshi.”
Jeok Cheongang murmured the word like a groan and reached toward the corpse twitching as it rose.
*Fwoosh. Boom!*

Despite his serious Internal Injury, his light-flames burst forth without dimming in the slightest. They ate through the flesh of the thing that had returned from beyond the river of death, burning its bones and organs.
*Psssh. Splash.*
Jeok Cheongang stamped on the remains as they crumbled to ash and dissolved into the pool of blood. Then he turned to his Disciple.
“What under Heaven could survive the Fire Gate Clan’s flames?”
“Burn them without end. If they won’t die, burn them to ash until they do. Just as our sect’s ancestors did.”
Jin Taekyung stared at Jeok Cheongang with wide eyes, then replied with a deliberately serious expression:
“How did you know? That’s exactly what I’m best at.”
Master and Disciple smiled at each other at the same time.
Then they charged the corpses surging in from every direction.
One streak of flame. No—two.
The eerie bell kept ringing.
*Jingle. Jingle.*
*KWAAAAH!*
It was a clash between the dead and the living, like watching a boulder fall toward an egg.
*GRAAAH!*
Undead. Jiangshi.
Or perhaps something else entirely. The corpses shot toward the surviving humans from every direction, sharp and fast as spikes.
They weren’t stiff or slow like jiangshi, nor were they weak like undead.
That was what made them so formidable.
*Crunch!*
“Hold the line!”
“For His Majesty the Emperor—!”
*Clang! Slice!*
Their cries of loyalty vanished beneath the din.
Thousands of corpses crashed into the humans’ shieldlike circle. They moved as nimbly as they had in life, and their souls, caught by the sound of the bell, no longer feared injury or death.
*Crunch!*
“Aaagh!”
Crimson blood spurted like a fountain. Every scream wrenched from someone’s lungs belonged to the living.
Sword Energy severed arms, cut through legs, and pierced chests. Still the dead rose and advanced, breaking down the human formation little by little.
They followed the bell as it rang faster and sharper, carrying out their master’s command.
*Jingle, jingle.*
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord walked forward slowly. Hundreds of the dead followed him, Ma Sanbao among them. At the end of their path rose a high dais.
No—the Emperor stood there.
“When the long and fierce age of warring heroes was drawing to a close, I was only thirteen.”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord spoke in a singsong voice. His gray gaze drifted to the young king trembling beside the Emperor.
A boy barely in his early teens.
Even he, an old man and a monster who had ceased to be human, had once been called a boy.
“I was a sinner from the moment I was born. A sinner guilty of being born in an age of chaos—a sin that could never be washed away.”
The day his father, an ordinary farmer, and his two older brothers, both still in their teens, were dragged off to the battlefield, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord learned something for the first time.
Misfortune did not come only to those who had sinned.
Having no wealth, no strength, and no spear or sword with which to fight back was itself a crime.

“And yet the rulers who sent innocent people before spears and swords were not sinners. They were Heaven itself. Thousands, tens of thousands, died on battlefields of their making while they filled their bellies with rice and meat.”
The last blaze of that age of chaos was spectacular. Men who proclaimed themselves kings and Sons of Heaven fought hardest at the edge of the precipice.
Among the countless lives reduced to ash in that blaze were the young Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s father and two older brothers.
And his mother, raped and killed after she resisted the soldiers who came to conscript her thirteen-year-old son.
From that day on, the boy did not cry.
Even a year later, after the final victor—who had ended the age of chaos with the sharpest and strongest spears and swords—ascended the throne.
Not when a Daoist recognized the wandering boy’s aptitude, took him as a Disciple, and brought him into his sect.
There, he met his Master and came to know his Senior and Junior Brothers.
At the Maoshan Sect, he found laughter instead of tears. Happiness.
And within a few years, that happiness ended.
“Did you know?”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord stopped walking. Then he asked his enemy’s descendant, who was looking down at him from hundreds of steps above:
“What your grandfather, Taizu, did to us?”
*Jingle.*

chapters.title: Chapter 914
paragraphs: *Jingle.*
At the clear chime, which seemed to ring inside his head, the Emperor was suddenly seized by a splitting headache.
The Maoshan Sect.
The name remained in his memory, however faintly.
He and every other prince had studied the art of ruling. They were expected to know the history of the Great Nation and the imperial family inside and out.
That history included the Maoshan Sect—or, more precisely, the event known as the “Maoshan Rebellion.”
**Third year of Pyeongjeong.** When His Majesty Taizu declared Nanjing in Jiangsu the Imperial Capital, the treasonous Maoshan rebels opposed the decision, rallied their forces, and rose against him.
The court historians had given the event only a brief mention, but its repercussions had been considerable.

It was an open revolt against the first Emperor, who had emerged from the long, fierce age of warring heroes as the continent’s final victor and established himself as an absolute ruler with boundless power.
*That was why he’d been more merciless than ever.*
Taizu, founder of the unified dynasty, was as cruel as he was great.

The day the imperial court received word that the Maoshan Sect, facing the loss of its ancestral home after generations of inhabiting it, had gathered its forces to oppose the relocation of the capital, Taizu immediately ordered his troops to march.
Three days later, it had disappeared from the world.

The mountain they had risked their lives to protect was engulfed in flames. Everything connected to the three characters that spelled *Maoshan Sect* was hacked apart by wave after wave of soldiers and thrown onto the pyres.
Humans and livestock alike.
The living and the dead alike.
But...
*The records were wrong. Someone survived.*
The Emperor endured the pain stabbing through his skull and looked down the seemingly endless flight of stairs.

There stood the Maoshan Sect’s last surviving root, gazing back at him. He had endured through the ages for this day alone, his eyes burning with the hatred of a man who had never once forgotten his grudge.
“I’ve always wondered why you wanted to destroy the imperial family and the Great Nation.”
The Emperor slowly rose from his throne. The hem of his long, ornate dragon robe brushed the ground.
*Swish.*
He walked forward at an unhurried pace. Baek Yeon, standing beside him, blocked his path with a rigid expression, but the Emperor did not stop.
*Step. Step.*
One step. Then another.
The Emperor descended the stairs carpeted in crimson silk. The two men who had once been bound as ruler and subject drew closer to each other.
Then the Emperor stopped halfway down, and a quiet voice slipped through his cracked lips.
“So you betrayed the late Emperor—my father?”
“Betrayed?”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord laughed aloud at the abrupt question, though his monstrous face was twisted into anything but a smile.
“Who betrayed whom? I never gave you bastards my loyalty for even a single moment.”
He had waited a very long time for this day.
How many nights had he lain awake, reliving his sense of betrayal and his thirst for revenge?
How many buckets of blood had he spilled mastering the martial arts manuals his Master had entrusted to him as the sect faced destruction?

The boy had chosen to become a eunuch as the surest way to bring down the impregnable fortress of the Great Nation. Then, one day after he had grown into a young man, an unwelcome visitor appeared with an offer.
“I bring you the words of the almighty and great Lord of Heaven.”
And that day, the young man joined the demonic army.
“Do you still not understand?”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord stared at the Emperor with cold, gray eyes.
“You’re not the ones who were betrayed.”

His father had often said that an age of peace and prosperity would come someday. His two older brothers had been dragged off to the battlefield as though they were captives, yet they had promised to return alive.
And their mother, who had lost her husband and two sons, had believed that at least her youngest boy—far too young to be on his own—would survive.
But she had been wrong.
Every last one of their hopes had been betrayed.
The boy had lost his entire family and barely survived a battlefield he’d been forced onto. Then the second happiness that had found him, almost like a miracle, was stolen away as well.
“You betrayed me first.”
All of them.
“No—the whole world.”
*Jingle.*
“You betrayed it.”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s voice and gaze, both cold until now, seethed like molten lava.
As he saw it, he was the one who had been betrayed first. The common people had been betrayed. The whole world had been betrayed.

He had lost his family to the struggles of men dreaming of becoming kings and ministers. His Master and fellow disciples, who had become another family to him, had been hacked apart by countless spears and swords.
And there had been only one reason.
They had tried to protect the home passed down to them through generations, defying Taizu’s decree that no martial artists could live near the Imperial Capital.
That was all.
“That is why you must die.”
In the most miserable, most horrific way possible.
“For that one wish alone, I have endured and waited all this time.”
It had taken many years for the boy to become a young man, the young man to become middle-aged, and finally for his hair to turn white. But those years had not been wasted.
The mask of Cang Gong that the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord wore was magnificent and powerful.
The East Depot’s intelligence network stretched across the world, and few among the civil and military officials who upheld the Great Nation had no connection to him.
As both the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord and Cang Gong, he was second in power only to the Emperor.
He might not have worn a dragon robe, but he was another absolute ruler—second to one, above all others. Most of the court lay in his grasp.
Even the imperial family.
“I—or rather, we are...”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s voice boiled as he spoke to the Emperor looking down at him.
“The Great Nation.”
The air around them froze. At the same time, the worn bell in the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s hand began to tremble wildly.
*Jingle. Jingle. Jingle.*
Sound like the wailing of ghosts spread in every direction.
Louder. Farther.
It crossed the vast banquet hall and reached the stone walls covered in the bodies of the Imperial Guards.
It was loud enough to raise those who already lay there in a pitiful state from the dead.
*GRAAAH!*
A roar that chilled the spine alone shook the night air. The monsters, now more ferocious and powerful, advanced in response to the sound waves ringing through their minds.
Toward the towering stairs. Toward the Emperor standing at their center.
And at the head of that surging wave of the dead was the man who had waited for this day alone.
“Now, let’s see it through to the end.”
He muttered the words as though making a vow to himself, then took a step.
No—he was about to shoot forward and tear the Emperor to pieces.
Then a voice pierced his ear.
“Stop.”
“I know what you’re trying to do, but you’d better leave it at that.”
*Hummm.*
The air shuddered.
There was clearly only one speaker, yet the voice came from several directions.
Six-Harmonies Voice Transmission—a technique even a Supreme Peak master would scarcely dare attempt.
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord felt the terrifying internal energy behind it and bit down on his lip.
He remembered his bitter defeat more than a decade ago and fixed his gaze on the woman looking down at him from just behind the Emperor’s shoulder.
*So Gyo.*

On the surface, she looked like nothing more than a beautiful, graceful woman. But he had suffered a crushing defeat once before because of her intervention. He knew exactly how much power was contained in that slender body.
He knew how much he himself had grown in the years since, too.
But there was one thing he still had no way of knowing.
“Who the hell are you, woman?”
So Gyo’s image was reflected in his darkened eyes.
An unknown superhuman whose identity had eluded even the intelligence networks of Dark Heaven and the East Depot.
The greatest enemy of his life, who had appeared without warning one day and left wounds on his body and soul that would never heal.
The grave Internal Injury she had inflicted on him had never healed, forcing him to turn himself into a jiangshi. Even now, he could not be sure who So Gyo was.
“Answer me. Who are you?”

If she were an agent of the orthodox faction, she would not have stood by while matters reached this point. If she were a master secretly raised by the imperial family, she should have appeared to stop him long ago.
But So Gyo was neither.
Gripping a weapon resembling a curved saber in each hand, she looked straight at him, her gaze untroubled.
She had cast off the black clothing that had once covered her from head to toe and freely released the immense power she had kept confined within her body.
*Fwoooosh.*
It was unmistakable. Overwhelming.
An unprecedented energy took visible form, rising in fine strands from all over So Gyo’s body. Her calm voice, at odds with the situation, rang out from all six directions.
“Well, I have my own circumstances, just like you do. I’m not sure I should tell you for free...”
*Step.*
She walked forward slowly, and her gaze turned cold.
“If you bite down on a sword and kill yourself right now, I might think about telling you.”
“Oh. Would that not kill you anymore?”
*Crack.*
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord clenched his teeth without realizing it. But having stopped, he found it difficult to take another step.
*Why?*
By now, he had achieved Great Completion in all of his sect’s supreme techniques.
The Maoshan Sect’s arts might have focused on sorcery, including the art of controlling jiangshi, but he had made even death his own and become a superhuman in a different sense.
And yet...
*She’s dangerous.*
He knew it instinctively. If he moved carelessly now, So Gyo would get the better of him.
Even though he could no longer die or feel pain, his Qi Sense kept sending him warning after warning.
“Master.”
His Disciple Ma Sanbao’s low voice reached his ear, but the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord did not move. He stared at So Gyo without a word.
The aura he felt from her now was on a level with the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
Considering the full strength at his disposal, he still had a good chance of winning, even with the Emperor, Baek Yeon, and the Emperor’s hidden guards against him.

Strictly speaking, he judged his own martial prowess to be half a step below the Fire King’s or So Gyo’s. But he and every soldier under his command possessed such horrifying tenacity that they could keep attacking as though each strike were meant to take their own lives along with the enemy’s.
Even if their arms and legs were cut off, even if their chests were pierced, they would not stop.
Not until every living person had fallen.
Not until their enemies’ bodies and the blood flowing through them had gone cold as ice.
*If I capture the Emperor and Prince Shangshan—or kill that woman—this will all be over.*

The battle to the death was not taking place in this hall alone. By now, the armies of the Great Nation, divided into two, would be fighting a bloody battle around the imperial capital, and his side would win.
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord opened his tightly shut mouth.
“Go.”
*Jingle.*
The worn bell, a divine artifact of the Maoshan Sect, gave a strange chime.
*Rumble!*
More than a thousand of the dead—the Great Nation’s elite soldiers, once known as the Imperial Guards—charged across the banquet hall.
*GRAAAAH!*
As the shrieking army surged forward like a wave, two streaks of light burst toward it.
*Shwaaah!*
Brilliant light flashed.
At the same time, the overwhelming Force unleashed by Baek Yeon and So Gyo, the two superhumans who had stepped in front of the Emperor, crushed and smashed the flesh and bones of the dead.
*CRUNCH!*
The vanguard was pulverized in an instant. But the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord knew what the two of them could do and was not the least bit surprised.
*I expected this.*
Humans were made of flesh and blood, and all were fated to die.
Even those called superhuman had limits. Their limits might be far beyond those of ordinary people, but they were human limits all the same.
*I’ll wait for an opening and kill them in one strike.*

The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord moved forward, his gaze dark. With his Disciple Ma Sanbao on one side and a master of the Twelve Palaces of the Zodiac, returned from the dead, on the other, he climbed the stairs now covered in rotten blood and shattered corpses.
*Splash.*
And at that very moment—
“Are you busy right now?”
The voice came from some distance behind him.
Only then did he realize that the howls of his followers, which had been ringing out far away, were beginning to die down.
Perhaps the limits he had assigned to superhumans were higher than he thought.
*Swish.*
He turned, his face rigid, and saw two men he had not expected to meet again so soon.
“Hey, ugly-ass big bro. If you’re not too busy, make some time for me.”
“Indeed. This old man will take very good care of you.”
Jeok Cheongang and Jin Taekyung stood there looking like men drenched in blood. They bared their white teeth and grinned.
They looked so much alike.

chapters.title: Chapter 915
paragraphs: “You got here fast. Much faster than I expected.”
After a brief silence, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord spoke again, his gaze dark.
“Which means you’ll die all the sooner.”
His cold gray eyes moved between Jeok Cheongang and me—or, more precisely, over the wounds covering us from head to toe.
*Damn. He’s sharp as hell.*
The smile I’d forced onto my face faded. I tried to ignore the pain coming from every part of my body and lowered my stance.
Jiangshi. Or undead.
I couldn’t even decide what to call those things, let alone remember how many I’d taken down. I’d fought the monsters pouring in without end, then fought some more.
I swung anything I could get my hands on. When there was nothing to swing, I smashed them with my fists and feet.
If they’d been ordinary humans, it wouldn’t have been this hard.
But they weren’t.
Attacks that should have killed a person in one blow had to be delivered at least three or four times before one of these things could no longer fight.
*It would’ve been a lot easier if I’d had enough internal energy...*

Jeok Cheongang and I had both used up a considerable amount in the fighting. The Extreme Yang Scorching Yang Qi accumulated through the Fire Gate Clan’s secret cultivation technique was the natural opposite of the death energy within the corpses, but we couldn’t draw on it without limit.
Especially with an enemy as powerful as the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord still ahead of us.
“You both look exhausted. Why don’t you turn back now, while you still can?”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord glanced over our shoulders.
“Before everyone you left behind is dead.”
*Clench.*
My grip tightened around the spear before I realized it. He’d struck a nerve because he was right.

Jeok Cheongang and I had broken through one section of the encirclement to reach him, but plenty of monsters remained behind us. The Embroidered Uniform Guard led by Jeong Hogun and the Fire Dragon Pavilion members were fighting with everything they had.
They numbered far less than half the enemy. And the enemy were genuine monsters that neither tired nor died easily.
Even so, we’d had to leave them behind. We’d judged this our only chance.
*This battle won’t end unless we take out the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord.*
He’d raised the dead twice already. Nothing said he couldn’t do it a third or fourth time.
And if that happened...
*We’d die. All of us.*

As time passed, our allies would die and the enemy would multiply. Reinforcements wouldn’t change that, even if they arrived—and I didn’t know when they might come, or whether the Emperor had prepared any at all.
*But if we take out their leader, that changes things.*
I’d lived as a Hunter before I ever became a Murim martial artist. I knew the fastest, most effective way to bring down an undead army was to eliminate the Lich who’d raised it.
The problem was time.
Fifteen minutes at most.
We had to take him down within that time. Any longer, and the gap Jeok Cheongang and I had left would be filled with our allies’ corpses.

The result would be the same if the other front, where So Gyo and Baek Yeon were holding the line, collapsed. Defeating the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord before the balance between those two fronts tipped was the only way out.
But...
*Can we do it? In that little time?*
I couldn’t shake the sudden doubt. I didn’t know if we’d made the right choice.

Maybe the best we could do was save Prince Shangshan and the Fire Dragon Pavilion members and escape this damn imperial palace. Maybe surviving—even if that was all we managed—was the right answer. The thought pierced me like an awl.
*GRAAAH!*
*Clang! Cough!*
The roars behind me that I’d tried to ignore came through clearly now, along with people’s screams and the clash of blades. The sounds kept tearing through my thoughts.
*Damn it.*
I swallowed the curse rising to my lips and gripped the spear shaft until my hand felt ready to burst.
—You can do it.
—Trust me.
Jeok Cheongang’s Sound Transmission came as if he’d seen straight through my thoughts. To my surprise, my wavering heart grew calm.
That’s right.
I can do this. No—I have to.
With the Old Master, with Jeok Cheongang, it’s possible. Because I’m not alone. It’s *us*.
Even if we’re facing three Supreme Peak masters. Even if every one of them is a monster who’s left humanity far behind.
I have to fight.
I have to take them down.
—Now!
At his forceful command, Jeok Cheongang and I stepped forward together.
*Whoosh.*
The distance vanished in an instant. As though we’d agreed on it long ago, we thrust out our palms.
*Fwoosh! KABOOM!*
A raging blaze devoured the air.
*KABOOM!*
It was unbearably hot. And terrifying.
As the fighting became a three-way battle, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord leaped clear of the flames. The situation brought a three-legged cauldron to mind.
*Break even one leg, and the whole thing loses its balance.*
The battle as a whole was certainly going his way.

So Gyo, the one he had to be most wary of, was tied down fighting well over a thousand monsters alongside Baek Yeon. The best the Embroidered Uniform Guard led by Jeong Hogun and the Fire Dragon Pavilion members could do was hold on.
But even among the three legs of a cauldron that would topple if any one of them broke, there was a most important leg.
That leg was the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord himself.
*That’s why they pushed themselves so hard to break through the encirclement.*
*Boom!*
The first blow missed him. He evaded the second just as easily, calmly watching the two men charge.
They’d grasped the heart of the matter at once. Amid the chaos of fallen enemies and comrades rising again, they’d found his weakness.
But which of them had made the call—the Master or the Disciple?
Jeok Cheongang?
Or Jin Taekyung?
*If it was the former, I’d expect nothing less of the Fire King. But if it was the latter... I see why that person wants him so badly.*
Martial prowess far beyond his years. Composure that held in any situation, and the bold judgment to see straight to the heart of a battle.
The Great Nation’s military, nearly a million strong, had plenty of fierce generals. Truly great commanders were rare.
Jin Taekyung had both qualities, though he was barely past twenty.
*Does that person mean to have the boy fill the places left by the departed?*

In the past few months, the Western Heaven Demon Lord and the Southern Heaven Demon Empress had died. Other powerful figures remained, himself among them, but the strength lost with those two had to be replaced somehow.
For his revenge. For the great undertaking still ahead.
And to the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, Jin Taekyung looked more than capable of filling the gap they’d left.
His Master, of course, could not be allowed to live.
*Jingle.*
The bell rang as the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord flowed away from another attack.
Golden Ox Palace responded at once. He had been commander-in-chief of the Imperial Guards and a Supreme Peak master of the Twelve Palaces of the Zodiac.
*Whoosh!*
A greatsword larger than most grown men cut through the air.
Jeok Cheongang, who had been pressing the retreating Eastern Heaven Demon Lord without pause, roared:
“How dare a bastard like you!”
At that moment—
*Fwoosh! KABOOM!*
The Force coating the greatsword, stronger than it had been in life, met the heat of the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
No. The flames swallowed it.
*Crack. KABOOM!*
A faint sound, like something splitting apart.

Unable to withstand the tremendous power, the Force shattered along with the greatsword. The flames melted the dozens of fragments even as they hurled them back at the wielder who had dared challenge the Fire King.
*Papat! Thud!*
More than ten blood-streaked shards drove into him like flashes of light, shattering flesh and bone as they lodged inside.
The impact shook Golden Ox Palace’s body. The blood left within him gushed out like a fountain.
*Splaaat!*
Any physician in the land would have taken one look at his wounds and pronounced him dead on the spot.

—Kill the Fire King.

His master’s command had been driven deep into his emptied mind. Engraved there by the bell, that single mission lent strength to his staggering corpse and sent him charging forward, heedless of pain he could no longer remember.
Just as it did now.
*GRAAAH!*

With his whites showing and a roar that made anyone who heard it feel fear, the commander of the Imperial Guards, once called Golden Ox Palace, shot forward. His broken golden armor gleamed, proof of the fame he’d earned in life.
*Whoosh!*
The wind buckled. The space between them vanished.
Even when the flames in his path melted his armor and flesh together, he didn’t stop. Like an enraged bull, true to the name Golden Ox Palace, he charged with all his might.
Toward one man.
The giant known as the Fire King.

*Tssss!*
Force surged over the handspan of blade that remained of his greatsword.

The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord.

*Damn it.*

Dodge?

*I’ll die. No question.*

The boy would live.
*Fwoosh.*

*I’ll kill you. I’ll kill you until you die.*

*KABOOM!*

“Old Master!”
*Thud!*
Hot blood fell.

Much faster than I expected.”

“Which means you’ll die all the sooner.”
His cold gray eyes moved between Jeok Cheongang and me—or, more precisely, over the wounds covering us from head to toe.
*Damn.
He’s sharp as hell.*
The smile I’d forced onto my face faded.
I tried to ignore the pain coming from every part of my body and lowered my stance.
Jiangshi.
Or undead.
I couldn’t even decide what to call those things, let alone remember how many I’d taken down.
I’d fought the monsters pouring in without end, then fought some more.
I swung anything I could get my hands on.
When there was nothing to swing, I smashed them with my fists and feet.
If they’d been ordinary humans, it wouldn’t have been this hard.
But they weren’t.
Attacks that should have killed a person in one blow had to be delivered at least three or four times before one of these things could no longer fight.
*It would’ve been a lot easier if I’d had enough internal energy...*
Jeok Cheongang and I had both used up a considerable amount in the fighting.

The Extreme Yang Scorching Yang Qi accumulated through the Fire Gate Clan’s secret cultivation technique was the natural opposite of the death energy within the corpses, but we couldn’t draw on it without limit.
Especially with an enemy as powerful as the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord still ahead of us.
“You both look exhausted.
Why don’t you turn back now, while you still can?”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord glanced over our shoulders.
“Before everyone you left behind is dead.”
*Clench.*
My grip tightened around the spear before I realized it.
He’d struck a nerve because he was right.
Jeok Cheongang and I had broken through one section of the encirclement to reach him, but plenty of monsters remained behind us.
The Embroidered Uniform Guard led by Jeong Hogun and the Fire Dragon Pavilion members were fighting with everything they had.
They numbered far less than half the enemy.
And the enemy were genuine monsters that neither tired nor died easily.
Even so, we’d had to leave them behind.
We’d judged this our only chance.
*This battle won’t end unless we take out the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord.*
He’d raised the dead twice already.
Nothing said he couldn’t do it a third or fourth time.
And if that happened...
*We’d die.
All of us.*
As time passed, our allies would die and the enemy would multiply.
Reinforcements wouldn’t change that, even if they arrived—and I didn’t know when they might come, or whether the Emperor had prepared any at all.
*But if we take out their leader, that changes things.*
I’d lived as a Hunter before I ever became a Murim martial artist.
I knew the fastest, most effective way to bring down an undead army was to eliminate the Lich who’d raised it.
The problem was time.
Fifteen minutes at most.
We had to take him down within that time.
Any longer, and the gap Jeok Cheongang and I had left would be filled with our allies’ corpses.
The result would be the same if the other front, where So Gyo and Baek Yeon were holding the line, collapsed.
Defeating the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord before the balance between those two fronts tipped was the only way out.
But...
*Can we do it?
In that little time?*
I couldn’t shake the sudden doubt.
I didn’t know if we’d made the right choice.
Maybe the best we could do was save Prince Shangshan and the Fire Dragon Pavilion members and escape this damn imperial palace.
Maybe surviving—even if that was all we managed—was the right answer.
The thought pierced me like an awl.
*GRAAAH!*
*Clang!
Cough!*
The roars behind me that I’d tried to ignore came through clearly now, along with people’s screams and the clash of blades.
The sounds kept tearing through my thoughts.
*Damn it.*
I swallowed the curse rising to my lips and gripped the spear shaft until my hand felt ready to burst.
—You can do it.
—Trust me.
Jeok Cheongang’s Sound Transmission came as if he’d seen straight through my thoughts.
To my surprise, my wavering heart grew calm.
That’s right.
I can do this.
No—I have to.
With the Old Master, with Jeok Cheongang, it’s possible.
Because I’m not alone.
It’s *us*.
Even if we’re facing three Supreme Peak masters.
Even if every one of them is a monster who’s left humanity far behind.
I have to fight.
I have to take them down.
—Now!
At his forceful command, Jeok Cheongang and I stepped forward together.
*Whoosh.*
The distance vanished in an instant.
As though we’d agreed on it long ago, we thrust out our palms.
*Fwoosh!
KABOOM!*
A raging blaze devoured the air.
*KABOOM!*
It was unbearably hot.
