chapters.title: Chapter 916
paragraphs: It happened in an instant.
In a sliver of time split and split again, it all began and ended like a passing flash of light.
*Thnk!*
Jeok Cheongang heard it clearly. He saw it, too.
A chilling sound of something being pierced reached his ears. At the same moment, something sticky splashed across his vision, staining it red.
*Drip. Splaaash.*
The world before him stopped.
Everything was red. The blood covering his face was hot.
And... it hurt.
More than anything ever had.
*Why?*
The hollow question that rose in his mind faded away.
No—perhaps it was Jeok Cheongang’s consciousness that was fading.
His mind struggled to grasp a sight that should never have happened. Pain and emotion boiled up from his chest, driving him into a confusion and rage unlike anything he had ever known.
*Slide.*
He was falling. Tilting.
In the slowed world, a familiar figure was slowly flung away, his back to Jeok Cheongang as scarlet blood sprayed from him. The sight burned itself into Jeok Cheongang’s wide-open eyes like a brand.
The Fire King Jeok Cheongang understood. He accepted it.
Everything unbelievable unfolding before his eyes was real.
He understood what the second Disciple he had taken in late in life meant to him.
And that he was not the only one who felt this way.
*Thump.*
His hand reached out through time as it flowed slowly, supporting that familiar back.
It was firm and warm.
Like the heart of the Disciple who had thrown himself forward with all his might to save his Master. Like the blood spilling from his torn-open chest.
*You foolish, foolish boy.*
Jeok Cheongang had lived for well over a hundred years. Across the vast land, he had seen countless kinds of people, watched them rise and fall, and found the path he meant to walk among them.
He had walked it one step at a time, always decisive, never hesitant.
But even he did not know what to say now.
What could he say to the fearless fool who had thrown himself into Force in his Master’s place? To the unfilial Disciple who dared to leave before his Master?
There was only one thing he knew he had to do.
He could not let the moment his Disciple had bought with his life go to waste. And he had to trust in the boy’s stubborn vitality—the boy who had survived every kind of hell as if by miracle.
*You have to survive. No matter what.*
With that plea the boy could not hear, the old Master made the flames still burning in both hands flare fiercer.
*Tssss.*
The air burned. Moisture evaporated.
And within it, time began to move again.
At the end of that moment—
*Fwoooosh!*
A vast blaze swallowed even death.
*Hummm.*
Everyone saw it.
No—they took it in with all five senses.
They watched space warp in the terrible heat. Pain filled their muffled ears, and they trembled at the sudden terror borne on the scorching air and wind.
There was not a single exception.
The living and the dead alike.
Even the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, who had watched wide-eyed as So Gyo tirelessly cut down the charging monsters and Jin Taekyung fell spraying blood, felt a chill seize his spine.
No. It was heat, as though his insides were melting.
*This...*
He understood instinctively. This strike held something that internal energy alone could not explain.
The old Master’s grief and rage had drawn out a power even he had not known lay dormant within him.
*I’ll die.*
The fear of death awoke—a fear the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had forgotten, one he had believed he would never feel again.
Killing intent, deeper and more terrible than what he had felt facing So Gyo over a decade ago, surged toward him.
Toward him and everyone else.
“Ru—”
And in that instant—
*KABOOOOOM!*
A tremendous roar swallowed his cry, and a pillar of white-hot fire shot forth.
*CRACK! RRRRUMBLE!*
The fire dragon thrashed, melting the ground and burning everything in its path.

Surging forward like a wave, it filled their vision and greedily devoured everything its enormous body touched. It burned and vaporized it all, as if determined not to leave a single drop of moisture behind.
Blades lying where their owners had dropped them. Impossibly hard bluestone. Even the soil and rock beneath it.
Even bodies that had once transcended death.
*KABOOOOOM!*
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord saw it clearly. He heard it without a doubt.
Golden Ox Palace, reborn as one of his followers—a Supreme Peak master formidable enough in life to be counted among the Twelve Palaces of the Zodiac—was engulfed in white flames.
And he heard his dying scream.
*GRAAAAH!*
Impossible. How could someone who no longer felt pain scream like that?
How could he writhe so desperately?
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord stared in shock. At the same time, he felt the Extreme Yang heat, fierce enough to burn away even his soul.
At its center, he saw one man’s eyes glowing red.
“You shouldn’t have touched my Disciple.”
The Fire King Jeok Cheongang.
*ROOOOAR!*
The fire dragon roared loudly enough to shake the entire Imperial Capital. Hearing it, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord prepared to die and drew up every last scrap of strength he had.

He blamed the subordinate who had been so damned faithful to his orders that he couldn’t stop, and blamed himself for bringing about the touch upon the reverse scale of the dragon called the Fire King.
But...
*It isn’t over yet.*
Not his life. Not the revenge he had pursued for more than half a century.
*Fwoooosh.*
The deathly energy of the dead closed around the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s body. The flames breathed out by an old, weary dragon crashed over it.
*KABOOOOOM!*
I don’t know.
How much time had passed. How much time I had left if I was going to die here.
My senses had dulled and my vision was blurred. Neither told me much.
The ground shook as if there’d been an earthquake. A roar kept pounding against my muffled ears.
And then there was the heat.
It was hot. My body lay sprawled beyond my control, but I could feel that heat more clearly than anything else.
*Old Master’s really pissed.*
I wanted to cackle, but what slipped between my trembling lips was sticky, and it wasn’t laughter.
*Cough.*
Blood. Dark red blood with little clots in it.
I felt around my mouth, touched something soft and squishy, and paused to wonder.
Was that my lip? Or a piece of my insides?
*...Damn it. I know which.*
I let out a small sigh.
It was sad that I could even say this, but it wasn’t the first time.
One strange, almost galling thing was that I’d never been this badly injured back when I was an F-rank Hunter.
*Of course, getting stronger is the only reason I’m still alive.*
I scraped together enough strength to lift my head. Dust and ash filled the air. With the aftermath still hanging over everything, all I could see was my own body.
Wounds covered me from head to toe.
And my chest... Force had torn through it, leaving flesh and bone horribly exposed.
*Cough. Cough.*
I coughed up blood again. This time it was darker still.
Proof that the sword strike I’d taken earlier had reached more than my flesh and bones. It had hit my internal organs, too.
*That was insane.*
Yeah. It had definitely been insane.
Something I wouldn’t have done if I’d been thinking straight. No—even a reasonably crazy bastard wouldn’t have dared try it.
But I did.
I had to.
*How was I supposed to just watch?*
If I hadn’t thrown myself in at the last moment, even turning my back on Ma Sanbao, Jeok Cheongang would be lying here instead of me.

The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord wasn’t just a sorcerer who commanded the dead. He was an incredibly skilled fighter, and even Jeok Cheongang couldn’t have taken him and another Supreme Peak master at the same time.
Part of me had hoped it might work, though.
To the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, I wasn’t just an enemy he had to bring down. I was someone the Lord of Heaven wanted.
*So much for taking me alive. He just went and stabbed me.*
I laughed, coughing up bloody foam.
I’d gambled my life and lost spectacularly.
Now here I was, sprawled like a corpse, feeling my senses slip away one by one as I waited to die.
But I could laugh because I was the only one who’d lost this gamble.
My life alone wouldn’t decide the outcome of the much bigger gamble playing out on this battlefield.
Some would lose and pay with their lives. Others would win and survive.
I was one of the former. That was all.
Regrets?
I’d be lying if I said I had none.
But I knew the state of my body better than anyone. No—maybe what I felt was just human instinct.
Death.
I could see it.
The thing that had already taken a father from my family—the unwelcome visitor I’d narrowly avoided through every danger I’d faced—had finally come for me.
Even now, through my fading vision, a black shape seemed to waver amid the falling ash and dust.
*Don’t come.*
I tried to squeeze out a voice with all my strength, but all that came from between my lips was a little blood and a ragged breath.
I didn’t give up.
Clinging to a consciousness that seemed ready to go out at any moment, I swallowed the blood pooling in my mouth and forced myself to stay alert.
I was afraid. Of death.
Afraid of leaving everyone like this.
There was still so much I had to do. So many things I wanted to do with the people I loved and who loved me.
But, but why?
Why was that shadow coming closer to me?
Why wouldn’t it stop walking, even now?
I wasn’t ready yet. I didn’t want to die like this.
*Just a little longer. Even for the briefest moment.*
Gasping for breath, I begged it to wait.
Even if it took me after that, I wanted time to say goodbye. I prayed desperately to see, just once more, the faces of the people whose lives had become bound to mine. My family.
I prayed to a god I had never seen.
No.
To the System.
“Please...”
And in the moment those words escaped me, wrung from the last of my strength—
*Ding.*
A clear chime that only I could hear rang out across the whole world.

Golden Ox Palace, reborn as one of his followers—a Supreme Peak master formidable enough in life to be counted among the Twelve Palaces of the Zodiac—was engulfed in white flames.
And he heard his dying scream.
*GRAAAAH!*
Impossible.
How could someone who no longer felt pain scream like that?
How could he writhe so desperately?
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord stared in shock.
At the same time, he felt the Extreme Yang heat, fierce enough to burn away even his soul.
At its center, he saw one man’s eyes glowing red.
“You shouldn’t have touched my Disciple.”
The Fire King Jeok Cheongang.
*ROOOOAR!*
The fire dragon roared loudly enough to shake the entire Imperial Capital.
Hearing it, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord prepared to die and drew up every last scrap of strength he had.

He blamed the subordinate who had been so damned faithful to his orders that he couldn’t stop, and blamed himself for bringing about the touch upon the reverse scale of the dragon called the Fire King.
But...
*It isn’t over yet.*
Not his life.
Not the revenge he had pursued for more than half a century.
*Fwoooosh.*
The deathly energy of the dead closed around the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s body.
The flames breathed out by an old, weary dragon crashed over it.
*KABOOOOOM!*
I don’t know.
How much time had passed.
How much time I had left if I was going to die here.
My senses had dulled and my vision was blurred.
Neither told me much.
The ground shook as if there’d been an earthquake.
A roar kept pounding against my muffled ears.
And then there was the heat.
It was hot.
My body lay sprawled beyond my control, but I could feel that heat more clearly than anything else.
*Old Master’s really pissed.*
I wanted to cackle, but what slipped between my trembling lips was sticky, and it wasn’t laughter.
*Cough.*
Blood.
Dark red blood with little clots in it.
I felt around my mouth, touched something soft and squishy, and paused to wonder.
Was that my lip?
Or a piece of my insides?
*...Damn it.
I know which.*
I let out a small sigh.
It was sad that I could even say this, but it wasn’t the first time.
One strange, almost galling thing was that I’d never been this badly injured back when I was an F-rank Hunter.
*Of course, getting stronger is the only reason I’m still alive.*
I scraped together enough strength to lift my head.
Dust and ash filled the air.
With the aftermath still hanging over everything, all I could see was my own body.
Wounds covered me from head to toe.
And my chest...
Force had torn through it, leaving flesh and bone horribly exposed.
*Cough.
Cough.*
I coughed up blood again.
This time it was darker still.
Proof that the sword strike I’d taken earlier had reached more than my flesh and bones.
It had hit my internal organs, too.
*That was insane.*
Yeah.
It had definitely been insane.
Something I wouldn’t have done if I’d been thinking straight.
No—even a reasonably crazy bastard wouldn’t have dared try it.
But I did.
I had to.
*How was I supposed to just watch?*
If I hadn’t thrown myself in at the last moment, even turning my back on Ma Sanbao, Jeok Cheongang would be lying here instead of me.
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord wasn’t just a sorcerer who commanded the dead.
He was an incredibly skilled fighter, and even Jeok Cheongang couldn’t have taken him and another Supreme Peak master at the same time.
Part of me had hoped it might work, though.
To the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, I wasn’t just an enemy he had to bring down.
I was someone the Lord of Heaven wanted.
*So much for taking me alive.
He just went and stabbed me.*
I laughed, coughing up bloody foam.
I’d gambled my life and lost spectacularly.
Now here I was, sprawled like a corpse, feeling my senses slip away one by one as I waited to die.
But I could laugh because I was the only one who’d lost this gamble.
My life alone wouldn’t decide the outcome of the much bigger gamble playing out on this battlefield.
Some would lose and pay with their lives.
Others would win and survive.
I was one of the former.
That was all.
Regrets?
I’d be lying if I said I had none.
But I knew the state of my body better than anyone.
No—maybe what I felt was just human instinct.
Death.
I could see it.
The thing that had already taken a father from my family—the unwelcome visitor I’d narrowly avoided through every danger I’d faced—had finally come for me.
Even now, through my fading vision, a black shape seemed to waver amid the falling ash and dust.
*Don’t come.*
I tried to squeeze out a voice with all my strength, but all that came from between my lips was a little blood and a ragged breath.
I didn’t give up.
Clinging to a consciousness that seemed ready to go out at any moment, I swallowed the blood pooling in my mouth and forced myself to stay alert.
I was afraid.
Of death.
Afraid of leaving everyone like this.
There was still so much I had to do.
So many things I wanted to do with the people I loved and who loved me.
But, but why?
Why was that shadow coming closer to me?
Why wouldn’t it stop walking, even now?
I wasn’t ready yet.
I didn’t want to die like this.
*Just a little longer.
Even for the briefest moment.*
Gasping for breath, I begged it to wait.
Even if it took me after that, I wanted time to say goodbye.
I prayed desperately to see, just once more, the faces of the people whose lives had become bound to mine.
My family.
I prayed to a god I had never seen.
No.
To the System.
“Please...”
And in the moment those words escaped me, wrung from the last of my strength—
*Ding.*
A clear chime that only I could hear rang out across the whole world.

chapters.title: Chapter 917
paragraphs: *Fwoosh.*
A fierce gale roared through the air. Layers of black ash that had piled up across the ground, along with embers that still hadn’t gone out, rode the wind and scattered in every direction.
From within the pale haze that blocked everyone’s view, a flame-wreathed fist cleaved through the air.
*BOOM! KABOOOOOM!*
Compressed air burst apart. White flames surged beyond the superheated air.
Nothing could stop that fire.
It was a dragon’s breath, its roar, its rage beyond measure.
The old dragon’s flames poured over the enemies who had dared touch his reverse scale, burning more fiercely than ever before.
Fiercely enough that someone who had become nearly immortal found himself thinking of *death* without realizing it.
*Ah.*
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord let out a quiet groan.
His gray eyes, filled now with fear and awe, remained fixed on the man advancing through the flames he ceaselessly unleashed.
Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King.
Him.
Only him.
Of the ten Kings who had never reached that lofty heaven, the foremost—the Emperor of Fire—was finally spreading the wings he had kept hidden and soaring upward.
Toward the three stars adorning the heaven called the Martial God.
All while pouring out his rage at the enemies who had touched what they should never have touched.
*Rumble.*
A tremendous impact hammered the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s entire body.

The death energy surrounding him without a single gap shuddered beneath a palm strike of unprecedented power. His legs, driven into the ground with ten thousand *geun* of force, carved deep furrows as they slid backward.
*BAM! BAM! KABOOM!*
One advanced.
The other could only retreat.
Jeok Cheongang was the former. The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord was the latter.
Like a sinner huddled beneath divine punishment, he dodged the thunderbolts that fell without pause.
*How? How in the world...?*
How could that exhausted body, already covered in wounds great and small, wield such strength?
How could he feel such rage?
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord swallowed the sigh rising to his lips.
Jeok Cheongang approached with an overwhelming aura, his anger so fierce the Demon Lord felt he could reach out and touch it. And he found that he understood.
He had felt the same.
*BAM!*
He had lost his family.
*BAM!*
He had lost his sect.
*BAM!*
When he thought he had lost everything, he discovered something still remained in a corner of his emptied heart.
*Rage.*
They said humans were human because they could feel joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure.
They said living beings could laugh, rage, grieve, and take pleasure in life.
But the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had lost three of those things.
With only rage remaining, he had finally given up being human and become a monster.
A monster called a vengeful spirit.
That was why, in one respect, he understood Jeok Cheongang—the heart of an old Master who had seen his Disciple on the brink of death.
He understood, too, the rage held within that mighty flame, which was trying to burn even the death energy he had summoned with all his might.
*KABOOOOOM!*
In that instant, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord felt it.
The death energy encircling him had finally reached its limit.
For this moment, Jeok Cheongang’s rage had surpassed his own.
*Crack.*
The sound announcing a rift reached the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s ears. The energy that had poured ceaselessly from deep within his body was scattering.

At the starting point of that rift was a fist wreathed in pure white flames—and a pair of eyes pouring out stream after stream of fire and an even greater heat, flames that would bring down his last line of defense.
“Understand this clearly.”
Jeok Cheongang’s gaze seemed hot enough to turn anyone it met to ash.
“Understand what you’ve touched.”
Yet his voice was as cold as the glaciers of the North Sea. It froze the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s spine and seeped into his soul.
It awakened the fear he had forgotten long ago, on the day he rose from death.
*Hah.*
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord trembled despite himself. A hollow laugh escaped him.
And suddenly, he understood.
*Perhaps the Three Saints... or even beyond.*
At least for this moment, nothing could stop the old dragon’s rage.
Nothing.
*CRASH!*
At last, the barrier split and shattered.
As everything surrounding him broke to pieces, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord thrust his fist toward the white flames flooding his vision.
*Whoosh!*
A movement faster than sound.
The dead clashed with the living.
In a world turned pure white, the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist advanced as if in slow motion and met the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s fist.
No.
It swept right through it.
*BAM!*
An instant of contact. A tremendous boom.
But the time their fists met was far too brief, and the balance of power had already tipped.
*Crack.*
Heat swallowed the scattered death energy and mangled his skin. It melted his acupoints and sinews, then shattered his bones.
The stronger body and regenerative powers the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had gained by giving up his human life were useless.
*KABOOOOOM!*
Jeok Cheongang’s fist was lava and lightning at once.
True to the name Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist, the flames he unleashed shot forward, reducing everything in their path to ash.
They swallowed the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s fist, then his entire arm.
*Fwoosh. BOOM!*
The flames erupted at their peak.
But no blood burst forth. There were no scraps of flesh, not even fragments of bone.
All of it had vaporized or turned to ash. It was gone beyond recovery unless time itself could be turned back.
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord knew it better than anyone.
So did Jeok Cheongang.
*Step.*
Jeok Cheongang took a single stride, and the space between them folded.
Thrown backward like a misfired cannonball, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord gritted his teeth and twisted his body.
*Crack. BAM!*
A fist grazed his side—if pulverizing a handspan of flesh and bone could be called a graze—and slammed into the ground.
At the same time, a tremendous boom split the sky, and a massive crater opened in the earth.
A chill ran through the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord. He felt as though every hair on his body stood on end.
If he could feel pain like an ordinary human, if he had fought Jeok Cheongang as he was now, how long would he have lasted?
How many times would he have died?
*This is...*
He had thought himself immortal. Unless the Martial God, who had vanished long ago, returned, he had been confident no one who came for him could bring him down.
He had been wrong.
*If I can’t dodge, I’ll die.*
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord wanted to live.
Even if he had died once already, he wanted this life to continue.
At the very least, he had to bring down the Imperial House, heir to that loathsome bloodline, and the Great Nation that was Taizu’s achievement and legacy.
He could not fall before his revenge was complete.
For his family and the members of his sect, who had met such horrific deaths.
And for himself—the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, who had chosen to become a monster for the sake of this day.
*Grind.*
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord clenched his teeth. With no blood left to spill, bits of flesh fell away instead.
*I cannot fall. Not ever.*
Even the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord himself couldn’t tell what it was.
Was it the rage that had carried him this far? His obsession with revenge?
Or the last surge of fighting spirit from a martial artist facing the greatest enemy of his life?
Only one thing was certain.
Just as Jeok Cheongang had before him, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had surpassed his former limits.
*Whoosh!*
In the blink of an eye, Finger Qi streaked across the space between them like lightning and pierced Jeok Cheongang’s neck.
No—it only looked as though it had pierced him.
Jeok Cheongang had been charging at him like a streak of flame. For an instant, it seemed he would fall with blood spraying from his pierced neck—then his figure dissolved like a heat haze.
*Shifting Form and Position.*
At the instant those four characters flashed through the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s mind, he spun around and swung the bell clutched in his only remaining arm.
*Whoosh!*
The bell slashed downward with a fierce whistle, gleaming with death energy.
A single blow. If even one strike landed cleanly, no one could come away unscathed.
That was how battles between Supreme Peak masters called superhuman were fought.
And the Fire King and the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord were monsters whose martial prowess could not be fully expressed even by the words *Supreme Peak*.
But—
*Crack.*
That strike was not enough against someone who, for this moment at least, had reached a new realm. One he might never reach again, even if he lived past today.
*Was that all you had?*
Jeok Cheongang had neither spoken aloud nor used Sound Transmission.

But the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord heard it clearly. He saw it, too: the unspoken words in Jeok Cheongang’s blazing gaze and tightly closed mouth as he stared at him, one flame-wreathed hand gripping the bell.
At the same time, he saw his own arm engulfed in flames in the next instant.
*Fwoosh! KABOOOOOM!*
A wildfire on a mountainside might burn for days. The Scorching Yang Qi summoned by its master’s will did not.
Its dreadful heat flared in an instant and faded just as quickly, melting away the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s last arm without a trace.
But the enraged Master’s punishment did not end there.
*CRACK!*
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s vision shook.
As his arm vanished, a fist smashed into his side. It crushed flesh and bone, then poured flames into his organs, long since rotted away.
*No!*
Each blow Jeok Cheongang landed brought death another step closer.
*SHWAAAA!*
Half the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s upper body had been scorched black by the previous attack. He didn’t resist the force throwing him backward.
Instead, he poured every bit of energy remaining into his still-intact legs.
He had lost both arms and the bell. He had to put as much distance between them as he could.
But as he kicked off the ground with all his strength, he felt a force of ten thousand *geun* seize his ankle.
*Crack.*
Flesh was crushed. Bone shattered.
And at the same time—
*Whoooosh!*
The world turned upside down. Through the rushing wind, the ground surged up to meet him.
*KABOOOOOM!*
A thunderous roar drowned out his ears, and the earth’s crust surged upward.
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord lay buried deep amid shattered dirt and rock, in earth that had hardened like granite. His eyelids trembled.
*This is...*
For well over half a century, he had worked in the shadows of the Imperial Palace and seen countless Supreme Peak masters.
So he knew.
This wasn’t a matter of speed or strength.
Jeok Cheongang now stood in a realm beyond his.
*Rumble.*
He felt not the slightest pain. That made the sensation all the clearer.
One of his two remaining legs had just been torn off.
And that meant only one thing.
*There’s nowhere left to retreat.*
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord gave a hollow laugh.
Was that the smile of a man finally accepting the death before him?
No.

It was the bitter laugh of someone who had waited so long for revenge, but had been forced to choose between that and his life—and who had decided to reveal the hidden sword he had meant to draw at the very end.
“—Come out, Heaven’s Slaughter.”
And just as a faint line of Sound Transmission, its meaning unclear, slipped between his moving lips—
*Shiver.*
The empty air wavered.

An assassin dropped through the drifting ash and embers. The old man, whose limp gave no hint of his speed, shot forward like a flash of light and slashed a dagger down at the crown of Jeok Cheongang’s head.
*Whoosh!*
The ambush was nearly perfect. No—it was perfect beyond dispute.
Just as it was about to succeed—
*SHWAAAA!*
A spear cut through space like a streak of flame.

The ambush was that perfect.
Even the Fire King Jeok Cheongang as he was now could not evade it. No—he was angrier than ever, his composure gone, which made evasion even less likely.
Even if he somehow blocked or dodged the strike and escaped death, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord judged that he could not escape severe injury.
The limping old man he had called Heaven’s Slaughter was one of the finest assassins in the Central Plains, comparable even to the Slaughter Saint.
*I kept that sword hidden for the Emperor.*
It was bitter, but there was nothing to be done.
The grand plan was already on the verge of falling apart. Survival came first now.

No matter how long it took or what means he had to use, he had to finish his revenge with his own hands. He could not die until he had watched with his own two eyes as the imperial family, heirs to that cursed bloodline, was wiped out—and offered a memorial rite for his Master and fellow disciples, who had met untimely deaths.
But if he was ever to resume that revenge, he first had to bring down the monster before him.
The Fire King Jeok Cheongang.
That monster rampaging like a fire demon sweeping across a boundless plain.
*Die.*
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord was certain Jeok Cheongang would die. At the same time, he desperately hoped he was right.
Just as the old man’s dagger—its blade dulled by a coating of ash and charged with Force—was about to cut Jeok Cheongang in two—
*SHWAAAAK! BOOM!*
A sound of something piercing the air rang out from somewhere and reached the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s ears. It drowned out every other sound as it tore furiously through the air.
His eyes flew wide. A blue-white flash had reached its destination before its sound did, filling his vision.
*What is that...?*
A spear of a common, unremarkable design—the sort one could find anywhere.
But the light upon it shone as brightly as the sun overhead, and its heat, hotter than the sun itself, burned even the air as it raced onward.
Toward Jeok Cheongang.
No—to be exact, toward the old man falling above his head.
At that moment, everyone’s movements stopped. The world they saw stopped with them.
Jeok Cheongang, who had only just noticed the assassin. The old man plunging down at him like a bolt of lightning. And the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, watching it all unfold.
*Shwoosh!*
They all watched the spearhead cut slowly through the air toward them. They felt the power within the blue-white flames coiling around it.
And at the same time, they understood.
Who owned that spear.
Where that horrifyingly intense Scorching Yang Qi came from.

Before the three-syllable name that had suddenly surfaced could even take shape in their minds, the spearhead had raced forward, erasing the space between them, and reached its destination in an instant.
At the last possible moment, the old man frantically turned his dagger to block the spearhead bearing down on him.
*Whoom—KABOOOOOM!*
Blue-white flames swelled as they met the Force surging from the dagger. A thunderous boom shook heaven and earth, and the shockwave lashed out in every direction.
*KRRRACK!*
The earth shuddered as if struck by an earthquake. Wind whipped about madly.
In that muffled world filled with nothing but ash, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord finally pieced together one man’s name and screamed it like a wail.
“Jin Taekyung!”
At that moment—
*Fwoooosh.*
The hazy world split apart.
A man drenched in blood from head to toe approached, moving more lightly and swiftly than ever. He bared his white teeth in a grin.
“Don’t say my name. I might get attached.”
Then he shrugged toward one man standing dazed and motionless at the feet of the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, who was sprawled there, stiff as a statue.
“Looks like this bastard still hasn’t come to his senses. Should I pull out his tongue while I’m at it?”
“Old Master?”
The Fire King Jeok Cheongang, his old Master, didn’t answer.
No—he couldn’t answer.
He gazed in silence at his Disciple, who had come back as he always did. Then he burst out laughing, so delighted that tears ran down his face.
At the same time, he felt all the anger and sorrow that had held his whole body in its grip come crashing down, and he grasped his Disciple’s arm tightly.
“Thank you.”
*Grip.*
“For coming back. For coming back like this.”
The corner of Jin Taekyung’s eye, caked with dried blood, trembled.
*Thank you. For coming back.*
A few words, but they were enough.
He felt the warmth of his Master’s hand on his arm and the sincerity in every syllable.
That feeling was more than enough.
There was no need for them to say anything more.
This brief reunion between the two men who carried on the Fire Gate Clan’s lineage would soon mean death for their enemies.
That was how the Fire Gate Clan had survived for three hundred years. It was also the way of these two, bound as Master and Disciple by an inexplicable connection.
*Smash and burn everything in our way.*
Whatever it is.
Without fail. No matter what.
*Step.*
Master and Disciple moved forward together. Beyond the unsettled dust and ash, sticky killing intent crept toward them and wrapped around them.
*Whoooosh!*
The limping old man, Heaven’s Slaughter, blended into the darkness and quietly waited for his moment.
Even as he watched his subordinates die less than a dozen *jang* away, there wasn’t a trace of agitation in his cold, sunken eyes.
*Whoosh. Slice!*
Before the blade dulled by ash could even reach its target, a head sprang into the air.
Anyone who saw those men crumpling like straw dummies would find it hard to believe that each was an elite assassin he had spent at least thirty years training.
*I thought I could take down even the Three Saints with those children.*
No—perhaps he really could have.
His ambush moments earlier had been that perfect. He could have erased the giant known as the Fire King Jeok Cheongang from this world himself.
If not for the unwelcome visitor who had appeared out of nowhere.
*Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung.*
Heaven’s Slaughter swallowed the groan that threatened to escape him.
It wasn’t only because his broken wrist throbbed. It had snapped when he deflected that spear, so full of power, at the last moment before his ambush succeeded.
*So the real monster wasn’t the Master...*
He had seen it clearly from the darkness.
Jin Taekyung falling with an injury beyond recovery. Coughing up blood mixed with pieces of his organs, with the shadow of death stirring at the edge of his life.
*And yet, how could he possibly...?*
Those who roam the martial world with death for a companion are martial artists. And among them, assassins stand closest to death.
Heaven’s Slaughter knew that better than anyone.
Since early childhood, when he had been trained as an assassin, he had killed people with his own hands in every way he could. The weight of those deeds had brought him to death’s threshold, too.
*If Dark Heaven hadn’t helped me, this old man would have turned to a handful of dirt long ago.*
Heaven’s Slaughter’s survival had been a miracle. But even that seemed insignificant beside what Jin Taekyung had just done.
There was no doubt. Force had pierced straight through Jin Taekyung’s chest.
It had split flesh and bone, destroyed his acupoints, and seeped into his organs, tearing them to shreds from within.
No one could recover from such an injury—not even under the care of a Great Firmament Immortal, or if Yama himself erased their name from the book of the dead.
And yet Jin Taekyung had come back alive.
Though he looked like a man drenched in blood, his exposed skin was smooth, and his perfectly formed Muscles and Bones—the reason he was known as having a Heavenly Martial Physique—were plain to see.
And that wasn’t all.
His formidable internal energy—several *jiazi*’s worth, an impossible amount for someone barely past twenty—had filled back up as if nothing had happened.
As if someone had filled an empty teacup with water.
As if it were only natural.
*This is... something I can’t explain.*
An ability beyond reason.
Heaven’s Slaughter’s sunken eyes trembled faintly.
Now, his composure—barely held together until this moment—had finally crumbled. He was truly torn between two choices.
Flight and duty.
And he wondered who would kill him: Dark Heaven or Jin Taekyung.
Several decades ago, when he had been gasping at death’s door, Dark Heaven had made him an offer he could not refuse. It had never been out of kindness.
A blade forged by Dark Heaven.
A human butcher who moved only at Dark Heaven’s command.
That was the new identity Heaven’s Slaughter had accepted in exchange for his life. A shackle he could never break, no matter how far he ran.
If he abandoned his mission and fled, punishment was all that awaited him.
Pain and death so terrible that even he, after a lifetime of killing, could not imagine them.
He could not hide. He could not escape.
That was Dark Heaven—or rather, the Lord of Heaven.
*Heh. Heheheh.*
Heaven’s Slaughter laughed without a sound.
What a fool he was, agonizing over a question whose answer had been decided from the start.
There had never been a choice to make. Only one path lay before him.
*Kill or be killed.*
Heaven’s Slaughter moved quietly through the darkness.

He silenced his breathing and erased his presence. Watching the elite assassins he had painstakingly raised with Dark Heaven’s help get slaughtered, he slowly approached Jeok Cheongang and Jin Taekyung.
*Just one. If I can take down either of them, I can survive—even if I fail the mission and flee.*
The grand plan had already gone awry.
But if he brought back something of equal value—if he brought back the Fire King Jeok Cheongang’s head—he might be given another chance.
A chance to pursue his own unfulfilled revenge. A chance to keep this stubborn life going.
And, to his great fortune, even the heavens, usually so indifferent, seemed to be on Heaven’s Slaughter’s side today.
*Whoosh! Whoosh! Slice!*
Another life vanished with a piercing sound. But unlike Jin Taekyung, who was rampaging as if possessed, Jeok Cheongang looked utterly exhausted to Heaven’s Slaughter.
*Patapat. Splurt!*

Hidden weapons came flying from every direction, grazing Jeok Cheongang’s body. Then, after killing with a single palm strike the assassin who had dropped down from above, the old dragon exhaled raggedly through his lips.
*Huff. Huff.*
His lips were dry and tinged pale blue. His body trembled faintly, even as he continued to unleash attacks of terrifying power.
At the sight of Jeok Cheongang, who seemed to have forgotten the fearsome martial prowess he had displayed only moments ago, Heaven’s Slaughter muttered to himself.
*He’s reached his limit.*
In a way, it was only natural.
Jeok Cheongang had already surpassed his limits against the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, and even before that, his body had been covered in wounds large and small.
That opening was Heaven’s Slaughter’s only chance.
*This strike will end it. No matter what.*
Heaven’s Slaughter calmed his mind. He erased even his killing intent—the energy anyone about to kill would carry.
No one harbors killing intent when slaughtering livestock instead of a human being.
He had spent his life as a butcher called an assassin. Now he shot straight forward with all his might.
And at that same moment, he understood.
Though he himself was still cloaked by his concealment technique, he saw Jin Taekyung staring straight at him. He felt that gaze pierce his entire body.
*He knew from the beginning...*
*Puhk.*
A blazing flame pierced his chest.

chapters.title: Chapter 919
paragraphs: There are two main ways a predator hunts its prey.
It can chase its prey down—or make the prey come to it.
The first is simple. The second is difficult.
But for all its difficulty, the second is more likely to succeed. Luring prey right up to you means you’ve made it lower its guard.
Or...
*You’ve made the prey mistake itself for the predator.*
One thing was certain.
The man struck by my spearhead as it flashed through the air belonged squarely in the latter category.
*Puhk!*
The gruesome sound of pierced flesh announced a successful hunt, and the air rippled.
Where only ash and dust had been swirling, an old man quivered like a fish skewered on a harpoon. I hadn’t even seen him appear.
“Wha—how...? Cough!”
*Drip. Drip.*
Blood spilled from his mouth, running down his chin before he could finish speaking.
I looked at his face, twisted with pain like a fiend’s, and answered calmly.
“I saw you. Clear as day.”
“That’s impossible. It can’t be.”
The old man gasped for breath. The assassins—now barely a dozen—rushed in from every direction to save their leader.
Like moths throwing themselves into a flame, knowing they would burn.
But the ending of this short story had already been decided.
From the moment I opened my eyes to the sound of a clear bell.
And from the moment Jeok Cheongang showed weakness to lure in prey that might flee at any moment.
*Boom!*
The heat of the Flame Divine Palm warped the air.
When the predator known as the Fire King swung his flame-cloaked claws, the moths fell without even a dying cry.
*Rustle. Thud.*
The last assassin, his upper body charred black, dropped to his knees.
There was no need to check. He was dead.
With his last hope extinguished right before his eyes, the old man’s voice sank into an oddly calm murmur.
“So you showed an opening to lure in your target. You have more of an assassin’s nature than I expected.”
I made a show of frowning.
“That sounds like a compliment, but somehow it feels like an insult. Every assassin I’ve ever met has been trash, except for one.”
“I suppose so.”
The old man gave a tiny, spasmodic nod and continued.
“Mungyeong. Is that bastard still the same?”
“What?”
My brow furrowed before I could stop it.
Mungyeong was the Slaughter Saint’s real name.
Fewer than five people in the entire world knew that.
Maybe even fewer.
Even counting me.
“How do you...”
“You’re asking how I know that name?”
The old man coughed up blood again. “How could I not? He told me himself.”
At that moment, I thought I knew who the old man was.
A few months ago, while I was in Sichuan, the Slaughter Saint had mentioned Salcheonmun in passing. It was one of the few things he’d revealed about his otherwise shrouded past.
“Salcheonmun.”
Once, it had been the most feared assassin sect in the world.
Then the dagger it had forged—the Slaughter Saint—brought about its destruction. Now it was a remnant of the past, forgotten by most.
At the name, the old man nodded and smiled faintly.
“Make sure you tell Mungyeong this.”
A fierce light flashed in the dying man’s eyes. Blood poured from his lips, and his voice was thick with killing intent.
“Tell him we—Salcheonmun—will come for him. No matter the sacrifice, no matter how many years pass. We will come.”
Hmm...
Judging by that, it definitely wasn’t a reunion for Salcheonmun’s twelfth class.
The kind of reasonable, beautiful ending where they meet up, polish off a few bottles of Jiannan Chun, call a designated driver, and ride home in a carriage wasn’t something the assassin world did.
Especially if the Slaughter Saint himself had brought about Salcheonmun’s destruction.
*First the Maoshan Sect, and now Salcheonmun.*
I’d thought something was off from the moment I first saw him.
The chain of gratitude and grudges went on and on, no matter how far I dug. I let out a small sigh.
“How thoughtful of you to give me advance notice. Don’t worry. I’ll pass on what you said word for word.”
I looked the old man straight in the eye and added, “I’ll tell him Gye Yabu of Salcheonmun said it.”
The old man’s eyes, which had seemed ready to close, flew open.
His calm acceptance of death vanished. His voice burst out with a spray of blood, full of undisguised shock.
“How—how do you know that?”
“I told you. I can see.”
“...What?”
Instead of answering, I jerked my chin toward the space above his head.
Floating in the empty air was a translucent roster that no one but me in this world could see.
**Lv. 140 Gye Yabu**
The difference was simple.
The old man—no, Gye Yabu—possessed concealment techniques bordering on the miraculous. I had the System, which was a miracle in its own right.
And that difference had made Gye Yabu the prey.
“Goodbye.”
With that farewell to end our brief encounter, I twisted the spear shaft in my grip.
*Crunch.*
White Flame, the weapon I had finally reclaimed, cut through bone and flesh like tofu and reached his heart.
The flames clinging to its transparent blade seeped inside.
*Boom.*
A small explosion made Gye Yabu stagger.
Dark-red blood poured from his seven apertures. He looked like a candle caught in a typhoon.
*Puhk! Splurt!*
I pulled out the spear and turned away. As I walked off, leaving his crumpling body behind, the bell I’d been waiting for rang in my ears.
*Ding.*

**System** You have defeated Lv. 140 Gye Yabu! You have gained a large amount of Fame! You have gained a large amount of EXP! If this becomes known, you will be pursued by Salcheonmun. Salcheonmun will not forget Gye Yabu’s death.
The System notification told me two things.
First, that Gye Yabu hadn’t been lying when he spoke before he died.
Second, I’d grown strong enough that killing a Level 140 enemy wasn’t enough to level me up—and that a warning about becoming Salcheonmun’s target didn’t bother me.
*Though it does feel a little ominous.*
I could just kill them coming or going.
I didn’t know how skilled Salcheonmun’s human butchers were, but I already had the Lord of Heaven’s undivided attention.
How much hotter could a jalapeño really get if you added a Cheongyang chili?
I’d just have to drink a nice, cold glass of milk first.
Living milk packed with EXP instead of calcium. Enough to put an end to this damnable fight.
“Sorry I’m a little late. Get bored waiting?”
*Step.*
I stepped into the path of someone crawling away, scrabbling with the only leg he had left intact.
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord confirmed it was me, then smiled through his twisted face.
“Yeah, you monster.”
Those who failed despaired.
They wept and sank into misery.
But the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord did not.
He neither despaired nor wept. He did not give up.
His revenge wasn’t over yet. Hope remained.
His grand plan had failed, but he was still alive.
*Even if a branch breaks, the tree doesn’t die.*
As long as its roots remained, the tree would not fall. Someday, it could grow thick branches and fresh leaves again.
Just as everything from the Maoshan Sect, destroyed by Taizu long ago, had passed down to him.
That was why he struggled.
With just one leg, his undying body squirmed as he tried to escape.
*Not yet. It’s not over yet.*
Golden Ox Palace was dead. Ma Sanbao had disappeared, and the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord didn’t know whether he was alive or dead.
And there was more.
He had lost the means to control the jiangshi, and the Salcheonmun assassins, including Gye Yabu, were dead.
But if that was all he had prepared for today, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord would never have begun this grand plan.
*I need time. Time.*
It had been half a century since he infiltrated the imperial court as a eunuch.
The shadow of Dark Heaven that the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had cast over the Great Nation was deeper and larger than anyone imagined.

There were commanders leading armies of tens of thousands, admirals commanding fleets, and political heavyweights who could wield enormous influence with a few words or a handful of hastily written lines.

The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had more than satisfied their greed. In return, they had sworn loyalty and willingly climbed aboard the same ship, bringing everything they possessed: strength, influence, authority.
The great rebellion meant to overturn the Great Nation was not confined to the grand banquet hall.
That was why the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord could still smile.
Why he could smile even as he faced a monster greater than himself.
“Sorry I’m a little late. Get bored waiting?”
*Step.*
The voice was light, as though greeting an old friend. But the footstep blocking his way was heavy and firm.
*Jin Taekyung.*
The face of one man crossed his mind, then appeared in the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s vision.
“Yeah, you monster.”
And at that moment—
*Crack!*
With a gruesome sound of crushed flesh, his only remaining leg was smashed to pieces.
Now deprived of all four limbs, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord calmly addressed another opponent through pain he could no longer feel.
“The world would be astonished to learn that the Fire King, famed for his rough ways, cares so deeply for his Disciple...”
*CRUNCH!*
A thunderous impact drowned out the rest of his words.
Then, as the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord was driven deep into the ground, a voice reached his ears, growling like a beast.
“Shut your mouth. Before I rip out your tongue.”
“My tongue? You’d rip out my tongue?”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord gave a short laugh.
“That’s not a bad idea. It would be a new experience for me, too.”
“You bastard!”
“My ears are ringing. Stop shouting and try it. Right now.”
“What are you waiting for? I said, rip out my tongue.”
But no answer came, no matter how often he urged him. The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s smile deepened.
“Right. You can’t. You won’t. If you rip out my tongue here and now, you’ll never get the answers you want.”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord already knew.
In a desperate fight for their lives, they might have killed him. But now that they had won, they could not.
He knew a great deal about Dark Heaven and the Lord of Heaven. One word from the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord could change the course of a Great War that would decide the future of the world.
A war that would put hundreds of thousands, perhaps millions, of lives at stake.
That was the last hope he clung to.
“Listen, Fire King.”
*Rumble. Rumble.*
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord felt faint vibrations through the ground, growing stronger by the moment, and burst into hearty laughter.
“It seems Heaven hasn’t abandoned me after all.”
At that moment—
*CRAAASH!*
With a roar that shook the earth, thousands of soldiers poured over the shattered outer wall.
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord laughed aloud.
No—he was about to.
*Gooooong.*
Until an enormous beam of light shot from somewhere, wrapped around them, and burst.
*KABOOM!*
Faced with that unbelievable power, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes flew wide.
At the same time, he screamed one person’s name.
“So Gyo...!”

sentences.text: There are two main ways a predator hunts its prey.
It can chase its prey down—or make the prey come to it.
The first is simple.
The second is difficult.
But for all its difficulty, the second is more likely to succeed.
Luring prey right up to you means you’ve made it lower its guard.
Or...
*You’ve made the prey mistake itself for the predator.*
One thing was certain.
The man struck by my spearhead as it flashed through the air belonged squarely in the latter category.
*Puhk!*
The gruesome sound of pierced flesh announced a successful hunt, and the air rippled.
Where only ash and dust had been swirling, an old man quivered like a fish skewered on a harpoon.
I hadn’t even seen him appear.
“Wha—how...?
Cough!”
*Drip.
Drip.*
Blood spilled from his mouth, running down his chin before he could finish speaking.
I looked at his face, twisted with pain like a fiend’s, and answered calmly.
“I saw you.
Clear as day.”
“That’s impossible.
It can’t be.”
The old man gasped for breath.
The assassins—now barely a dozen—rushed in from every direction to save their leader.
Like moths throwing themselves into a flame, knowing they would burn.
But the ending of this short story had already been decided.
From the moment I opened my eyes to the sound of a clear bell.
And from the moment Jeok Cheongang showed weakness to lure in prey that might flee at any moment.
*Boom!*
The heat of the Flame Divine Palm warped the air.
When the predator known as the Fire King swung his flame-cloaked claws, the moths fell without even a dying cry.
*Rustle.
Thud.*
The last assassin, his upper body charred black, dropped to his knees.
There was no need to check.
He was dead.
With his last hope extinguished right before his eyes, the old man’s voice sank into an oddly calm murmur.
“So you showed an opening to lure in your target.
You have more of an assassin’s nature than I expected.”
I made a show of frowning.
“That sounds like a compliment, but somehow it feels like an insult.
Every assassin I’ve ever met has been trash, except for one.”
“I suppose so.”
The old man gave a tiny, spasmodic nod and continued.
“Mungyeong.
Is that bastard still the same?”
“What?”
My brow furrowed before I could stop it.
Mungyeong was the Slaughter Saint’s real name.
Fewer than five people in the entire world knew that.
Maybe even fewer.
Even counting me.
“How do you...”
“You’re asking how I know that name?”
The old man coughed up blood again.
“How could I not?
He told me himself.”
At that moment, I thought I knew who the old man was.
A few months ago, while I was in Sichuan, the Slaughter Saint had mentioned Salcheonmun in passing.
It was one of the few things he’d revealed about his otherwise shrouded past.
“Salcheonmun.”
Once, it had been the most feared assassin sect in the world.
Then the dagger it had forged—the Slaughter Saint—brought about its destruction.
Now it was a remnant of the past, forgotten by most.
At the name, the old man nodded and smiled faintly.
“Make sure you tell Mungyeong this.”
A fierce light flashed in the dying man’s eyes.
Blood poured from his lips, and his voice was thick with killing intent.
“Tell him we—Salcheonmun—will come for him.
No matter the sacrifice, no matter how many years pass.
We will come.”
Hmm...
Judging by that, it definitely wasn’t a reunion for Salcheonmun’s twelfth class.
The kind of reasonable, beautiful ending where they meet up, polish off a few bottles of Jiannan Chun, call a designated driver, and ride home in a carriage wasn’t something the assassin world did.
Especially if the Slaughter Saint himself had brought about Salcheonmun’s destruction.
*First the Maoshan Sect, and now Salcheonmun.*
I’d thought something was off from the moment I first saw him.
The chain of gratitude and grudges went on and on, no matter how far I dug.
I let out a small sigh.
“How thoughtful of you to give me advance notice.
Don’t worry.
I’ll pass on what you said word for word.”
I looked the old man straight in the eye and added, “I’ll tell him Gye Yabu of Salcheonmun said it.”
The old man’s eyes, which had seemed ready to close, flew open.
His calm acceptance of death vanished.
His voice burst out with a spray of blood, full of undisguised shock.
“How—how do you know that?”
“I told you.
I can see.”
“...What?”
Instead of answering, I jerked my chin toward the space above his head.
Floating in the empty air was a translucent roster that no one but me in this world could see.
**Lv.
140 Gye Yabu**
The difference was simple.
The old man—no, Gye Yabu—possessed concealment techniques bordering on the miraculous.
I had the System, which was a miracle in its own right.
And that difference had made Gye Yabu the prey.
“Goodbye.”
With that farewell to end our brief encounter, I twisted the spear shaft in my grip.
*Crunch.*
White Flame, the weapon I had finally reclaimed, cut through bone and flesh like tofu and reached his heart.
The flames clinging to its transparent blade seeped inside.
*Boom.*
A small explosion made Gye Yabu stagger.
Dark-red blood poured from his seven apertures.
He looked like a candle caught in a typhoon.
*Puhk!
Splurt!*
I pulled out the spear and turned away.
As I walked off, leaving his crumpling body behind, the bell I’d been waiting for rang in my ears.
*Ding.*
**System** You have defeated Lv.
140 Gye Yabu!
You have gained a large amount of Fame!
You have gained a large amount of EXP!
If this becomes known, you will be pursued by Salcheonmun.
Salcheonmun will not forget Gye Yabu’s death.
The System notification told me two things.
First, that Gye Yabu hadn’t been lying when he spoke before he died.
Second, I’d grown strong enough that killing a Level 140 enemy wasn’t enough to level me up—and that a warning about becoming Salcheonmun’s target didn’t bother me.
*Though it does feel a little ominous.*
I could just kill them coming or going.
I didn’t know how skilled Salcheonmun’s human butchers were, but I already had the Lord of Heaven’s undivided attention.
How much hotter could a jalapeño really get if you added a Cheongyang chili?
I’d just have to drink a nice, cold glass of milk first.
Living milk packed with EXP instead of calcium.
Enough to put an end to this damnable fight.
“Sorry I’m a little late.
Get bored waiting?”
*Step.*
I stepped into the path of someone crawling away, scrabbling with the only leg he had left intact.
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord confirmed it was me, then smiled through his twisted face.

chapters.title: Chapter 920
paragraphs: It all happened in an instant.
At least, that was how it felt to the East Depot masters charging at the vanguard as they scrambled over the rubble of the collapsed outer wall.
*Fwoosh.*
What in the world was this?
How could anything be so fast—and so destructive?
A dazzling flash filled their vision. For a moment, they could only stare. It was the last thing they ever saw.
*KABOOM!*
A tremendous roar battered their ears. An irresistible force swept over their bodies, frozen like stone statues.
*Crunch! Fwoosh!*
The flash vanished as quickly as it had come. One of the East Depot eunuchs charging behind his comrades blinked.
When his vision finally cleared, he understood.
That flash had been Force fired by someone.
That terrifying energy had swept away dozens of his comrades—and taken one of his arms, too.
“A-ah. Ahh. Aaaaaah...”
His jaw trembled. A dazed moan slipped between his teeth as they clattered without pause.
They were dead. No—they’d been butchered.
His eyes took in what remained of the men who had once been his comrades: chunks of meat so mangled he could no longer tell who was who. His mind struggled to accept the sight.
Only then did pain reach him from his shoulder, left in shreds as though a beast had torn into it.
“GRAAAAH!”
A scream of agony poured from his gaping mouth.
But he wasn’t the only one caught in shock and pain.
“Ugh... Uuugh.”
“P-please, save...”
“Ugh—bleurgh!”
Some groaned as they clutched the stumps of their severed legs. Some pleaded desperately for help on the brink of death. Others bent over and vomited at the carnage before their eyes.
They trembled, terrified by the gruesome deaths they’d witnessed and helpless to do anything.
Those who realized what had happened a moment later were little better off.
“W-what is this...?”

Some of the Imperial Guards, long since recruited by the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord and drawn into the rebellion, and the East Depot eunuchs who had led them into the grand banquet hall were struck speechless.
One strike.
A single strike had killed or incapacitated more than fifty soldiers.
Each had charged at the vanguard without hesitation, and each was a formidable fighter, ranging from Supreme First Rate to Peak.
Compared to the full force of some three thousand, it wasn’t a major loss. But everyone had stopped because that one attack had swallowed dozens of Peak masters in its terrifying power.
No—it was the master behind that attack, whose might seemed almost demonic, who had stopped them.
Who was it?
The question pierced everyone’s mind.
The three thousand rebels who had surged into the grand banquet hall.
The Embroidered Uniform Guard and Fire Dragon Pavilion members fighting the dead, who refused to fall no matter how many times they were killed.
Even the dead, driven still further out of their minds when the bell was destroyed, stopped at some instinctive warning.
Then they turned their heads.
Toward the source of the flash.
At the end of countless gazes stood someone, trampling the twitching limbs of the dead.
*Whoosh.*
A breeze stirred the woman’s thick hair.
“So Gyo...!”
In the silence that had fallen over the hall, a cry like a scream rang out belatedly. The woman—no, So Gyo—lifted her head and looked toward the voice.
More precisely, toward the person standing there.
Jin Taekyung.
Her lips moved without a sound, and her dark blue eyes grew solemn.
The hundreds of steps leading up to the dais were already buried beneath countless bodies.
The thousand or so dead had been torn to shreds and finally died—or lay there writhing with their limbs severed.
As if hoping someone would put an end to their stubborn lives.
*Slice.*
A streak of light cut through the air.
The man who had split in two a dead man crawling up the steps on his one remaining arm lowered his sword and breathed hard.
*Huff. Huff.*
His entire body, soaked in blood and sweat, heaved.
His golden armor and sword, as intricate and splendid as works of art, felt heavier than ever.
No—perhaps it was the weight of the responsibility and guilt he had carried all this time.
And yet... he had no regrets.
He must not.
The Embroidered Uniform Guard who had turned to ash here today had also been prepared to die.
To pity them for a sacrifice they had chosen would be an insult worse than death.
Even if he was the most exalted man beneath the heavens, the one who stood above all others.
“Baek Yeon.”
The man—the Emperor—spoke, his voice rough with a metallic rasp.

He turned to the imperial court’s foremost military commander. Baek Yeon had done more than anyone to protect the late Emperor and the imperial family, and whenever the Emperor faltered, Baek Yeon’s harsh rebukes had lifted him back to his feet. He was more a comrade than a subject.
So the Emperor gave him a request, not an order.
“Sound the drum. The war drum.”
Baek Yeon’s eyes trembled.
Taking in the Emperor’s exhaustion, his fatigue more visible than ever, he bowed deeply and extended a palm toward the great drum that had announced the start of the banquet.
*Boom!*
The drumbeat, charged with profound internal energy, rang out without end.
It carried the heart of a warrior who had waited so long for this day. It carried the Emperor’s will.
Once.
Then once again.
The sound was immense enough for everyone in the grand banquet hall to hear. No—it rolled like a wave that might sweep across the entire Imperial Capital.
*Booooom!*
Even when the third drumbeat rang out, the three thousand rebels didn’t know what to do. They hesitated.
It had all unfolded so naturally.

So Gyo’s overwhelming display of martial power had abruptly swept through the vanguard, and the drumbeat resounded with a grandeur they couldn’t explain. For a moment, they had been overwhelmed before they even knew it.
Even the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord—the instigator and center of the rebellion, who should have been leading them from the front—lay in a horrific state at Jin Taekyung and Jeok Cheongang’s feet.
*What is this? What in the world is happening?*
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had been captured. Ma Sanbao was nowhere to be seen.
The Imperial Guards and East Depot leaders who had betrayed the imperial court and the Great Nation to join Dark Heaven looked at one another in confusion.
When they took the Outer Palace, they had thought it was all over.

Even when they had seized every gate leading into the imperial palace and defeated the remaining defenders, taking advantage of another allied force sweeping through the capital, they had been certain a new age was about to begin.
But the reality they had so eagerly come to meet was different. The battle should have been theirs already.
The flags that had flown so proudly when they first stormed into the grand banquet hall now fluttered as uneasily as their hearts.
And at that very moment—
*Boom. Boom.*
Another drumbeat reached their ears.
Every hair on their bodies stood on end. A chill ran down their spines.
The fourth drumbeat was no louder than the ones before it, nor did it have a deeper, more resonant ring.
Yet it made the rebels’ hearts sink for one reason alone.
Behind them.
The sound came not from Baek Yeon, visible in the distance, but from somewhere behind them.
And then it spread in every direction.
*Boom. Boom-boom.*
The countless drumbeats spread like flames across a wide plain. They were not echoes bouncing back from somewhere. They were not a trick of the ears.
They were the signal that this long and gruesome banquet was coming to an end—the footsteps of hunters closing in on prey caught at last in a trap.
*Rumble.*
How long had this been going on?
Where had such a vast army been hiding, and why had it waited until now?
*A trap!*
The realization struck like lightning through their skulls. At the same time, the rebels felt immense tremors drawing closer.
Then they saw them.
Hundreds of flags rising high on every side.
Following the fluttering flags, a dragon embroidered in golden thread writhed as though alive.
Shock, joy, and despair swept across the grand banquet hall.
Some were seized by an elation so intense their hearts felt ready to burst. Others clenched their teeth until they bled.
The three thousand rebels were the latter.
Thousands. Or tens of thousands.
No one could guess the exact number of their enemies, but one thing was certain: the forces tightening the encirclement would overwhelm them.
The rebels felt the killing intent bearing down on them.
They saw their faces reflected in the rippling pools of blood and imagined what was about to happen.
But they also thought of the only way out of this hopeless situation, surrounded on all sides.
The center of everything. Its beginning and its end.
The ruler who stood at the highest peak in all the vast world.
“The Emperor...”
The faint voice that slipped from someone’s lips swelled into a shout born of the desperate will to live.
“Capture the Emperor!”
The victor was king; the loser, a rebel.
Already driven to the edge of a cliff, they had no other choice.
A body without a head could not move.
Capturing the Emperor and his family to make the rebellion succeed was the only way forward.
“Whoever captures the Emperor and his family will become a marquis and enjoy wealth and glory for generations to come!”
At that moment—
*Rumble!*
Thousands of men and horses surged forward like a wave.
Toward the Emperor looking down at them from the high steps, his face worn with age.
They tried to drown out their fear of the woman standing before him with furious shouts.
“GRAAAAAH!”
“Charge! Don’t stop!”
Their cries, almost screams, mingled with countless footsteps and pounding hooves. The sound woke the deep night and spread through the thick darkness hanging on every side like a curtain.
Far away. Farther still.
Loud and clear.
Yet their desperate advance and shouts seemed unbearably slow and distant.
At least, they did to the young man and woman looking at each other in that moment.
He looked at her. She looked at him.
The hundred or so *jang* between them meant nothing now.
They both knew.
They knew they were looking at each other. They knew whose gaze had met theirs across the distance.
But only So Gyo had realized the other person’s true identity.
*So it was you.*
Swallowing a cryptic murmur, So Gyo silently looked down at the battlefield spread out beneath her.
It was vast. And it was horrific.

The grand banquet hall, stretching for hundreds of *jang* in either direction, was awash with blood. Ownerless weapons and severed limbs lay scattered across the ground. The wide-open eyes of the dead held no trace of life.
The music that had sounded for a brief while was gone. Only death remained in its place, and more people were surging in to pile death upon death.
*Whoosh.*
Amid the enemies’ thunderous shouts, a cold wind billowed her silky hair. It carried the smell of blood deep into her nose, thick as the crimson pools all around her.
Thick enough to draw fragments of the past up from where time had buried them.
Thick enough to revive the horrific memories she’d wanted to forget but never could.
Perhaps that was why she felt not the slightest joy, though she had found the answer—the key—she had sought for so long.
Perhaps that was why she knew it was time to end this long and gruesome banquet.
*Shhk.*
In the silence, So Gyo moved both hands. The two curved swords gripped in her blood-caked hands pointed toward sky and earth. Then she brought them together.
*Shrring. Clack.*
Steel forged by a craftsman’s countless rounds of quenching and hammering rang coldly. A hidden groove and the metal set within it joined the two weapons.
As if they had been one from the beginning.
As if they had once been something other than curved swords.
*Wooooong.*
Restored to its original form after long years, the weapon trembled in its owner’s hands. It resonated with the familiar energy flowing deep into it and shed tears of light.
*Zing.*
The air quivered.
A pure-white flash joined the two angled ends that had made the pieces look like curved swords.
Just as it had in the distant past.
Still bearing the splendor of an age when it had been divine punishment to some, salvation to others.
“It’s been a long time.”
So Gyo lifted her beloved weapon, her voice tender.
Then, as she had done tens of thousands of times before, she gripped the flash joining its ends and pulled hard.
*Fwoosh.*
A brilliant shaft of light took shape in midair, nocked against the shining bowstring.
The unbelievable sight stirred the old memories of someone watching from afar. It raised someone’s figure from a past buried in dust.
An old woman who had ruled the battlefield with a bow larger than any other, unleashing Force like lightning.
“The Bow Saint...!”
At that very moment—
*SHWAAAAAK!*
The shaft of light flew from So Gyo’s—or rather, the Bow Saint’s—fingertips and streaked across the grand banquet hall.
