But everyone had stopped because that one attack had swallowed dozens of Peak masters in its terrifying power.
No—it was the master behind that attack, whose might seemed almost demonic, who had stopped them.
Who was it?
The question pierced everyone’s mind.
The three thousand rebels who had surged into the grand banquet hall.
The Embroidered Uniform Guard and Fire Dragon Pavilion members fighting the dead, who refused to fall no matter how many times they were killed.
Even the dead, driven still further out of their minds when the bell was destroyed, stopped at some instinctive warning.
Then they turned their heads.
Toward the source of the flash.
At the end of countless gazes stood someone, trampling the twitching limbs of the dead.
*Whoosh.*
A breeze stirred the woman’s thick hair.
“So Gyo...!”
In the silence that had fallen over the hall, a cry like a scream rang out belatedly.
The woman—no, So Gyo—lifted her head and looked toward the voice.
More precisely, toward the person standing there.
Jin Taekyung.
Her lips moved without a sound, and her dark blue eyes grew solemn.
The hundreds of steps leading up to the dais were already buried beneath countless bodies.
The thousand or so dead had been torn to shreds and finally died—or lay there writhing with their limbs severed.
As if hoping someone would put an end to their stubborn lives.
*Slice.*
A streak of light cut through the air.
The man who had split in two a dead man crawling up the steps on his one remaining arm lowered his sword and breathed hard.
*Huff.
Huff.*
His entire body, soaked in blood and sweat, heaved.
His golden armor and sword, as intricate and splendid as works of art, felt heavier than ever.
No—perhaps it was the weight of the responsibility and guilt he had carried all this time.
And yet... he had no regrets.
He must not.
The Embroidered Uniform Guard who had turned to ash here today had also been prepared to die.
To pity them for a sacrifice they had chosen would be an insult worse than death.
Even if he was the most exalted man beneath the heavens, the one who stood above all others.
“Baek Yeon.”
The man—the Emperor—spoke, his voice rough with a metallic rasp.
He turned to the imperial court’s foremost military commander.
Baek Yeon had done more than anyone to protect the late Emperor and the imperial family, and whenever the Emperor faltered, Baek Yeon’s harsh rebukes had lifted him back to his feet.
He was more a comrade than a subject.
So the Emperor gave him a request, not an order.
“Sound the drum.
The war drum.”
Baek Yeon’s eyes trembled.
Taking in the Emperor’s exhaustion, his fatigue more visible than ever, he bowed deeply and extended a palm toward the great drum that had announced the start of the banquet.
*Boom!*
The drumbeat, charged with profound internal energy, rang out without end.
It carried the heart of a warrior who had waited so long for this day.
It carried the Emperor’s will.
Once.
Then once again.
The sound was immense enough for everyone in the grand banquet hall to hear.
No—it rolled like a wave that might sweep across the entire Imperial Capital.
*Booooom!*
Even when the third drumbeat rang out, the three thousand rebels didn’t know what to do.
They hesitated.
It had all unfolded so naturally.
So Gyo’s overwhelming display of martial power had abruptly swept through the vanguard, and the drumbeat resounded with a grandeur they couldn’t explain.
For a moment, they had been overwhelmed before they even knew it.
Even the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord—the instigator and center of the rebellion, who should have been leading them from the front—lay in a horrific state at Jin Taekyung and Jeok Cheongang’s feet.
*What is this?
What in the world is happening?*
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had been captured.
Ma Sanbao was nowhere to be seen.
The Imperial Guards and East Depot leaders who had betrayed the imperial court and the Great Nation to join Dark Heaven looked at one another in confusion.
When they took the Outer Palace, they had thought it was all over.

Even when they had seized every gate leading into the imperial palace and defeated the remaining defenders, taking advantage of another allied force sweeping through the capital, they had been certain a new age was about to begin.
But the reality they had so eagerly come to meet was different.
The battle should have been theirs already.
The flags that had flown so proudly when they first stormed into the grand banquet hall now fluttered as uneasily as their hearts.
And at that very moment—
*Boom.
Boom.*
Another drumbeat reached their ears.
Every hair on their bodies stood on end.
A chill ran down their spines.
The fourth drumbeat was no louder than the ones before it, nor did it have a deeper, more resonant ring.
Yet it made the rebels’ hearts sink for one reason alone.
Behind them.
The sound came not from Baek Yeon, visible in the distance, but from somewhere behind them.
And then it spread in every direction.
*Boom.
Boom-boom.*
The countless drumbeats spread like flames across a wide plain.
They were not echoes bouncing back from somewhere.
They were not a trick of the ears.
They were the signal that this long and gruesome banquet was coming to an end—the footsteps of hunters closing in on prey caught at last in a trap.
*Rumble.*
How long had this been going on?
Where had such a vast army been hiding, and why had it waited until now?
*A trap!*
The realization struck like lightning through their skulls.
At the same time, the rebels felt immense tremors drawing closer.
Then they saw them.
Hundreds of flags rising high on every side.
Following the fluttering flags, a dragon embroidered in golden thread writhed as though alive.
Shock, joy, and despair swept across the grand banquet hall.
Some were seized by an elation so intense their hearts felt ready to burst.
Others clenched their teeth until they bled.
The three thousand rebels were the latter.
Thousands.
Or tens of thousands.
No one could guess the exact number of their enemies, but one thing was certain: the forces tightening the encirclement would overwhelm them.
The rebels felt the killing intent bearing down on them.
They saw their faces reflected in the rippling pools of blood and imagined what was about to happen.
But they also thought of the only way out of this hopeless situation, surrounded on all sides.
The center of everything.
Its beginning and its end.
The ruler who stood at the highest peak in all the vast world.
“The Emperor...”
The faint voice that slipped from someone’s lips swelled into a shout born of the desperate will to live.
“Capture the Emperor!”
The victor was king; the loser, a rebel.
Already driven to the edge of a cliff, they had no other choice.
A body without a head could not move.
Capturing the Emperor and his family to make the rebellion succeed was the only way forward.
“Whoever captures the Emperor and his family will become a marquis and enjoy wealth and glory for generations to come!”
At that moment—
*Rumble!*
Thousands of men and horses surged forward like a wave.
Toward the Emperor looking down at them from the high steps, his face worn with age.
They tried to drown out their fear of the woman standing before him with furious shouts.
“GRAAAAAH!”
“Charge!
Don’t stop!”
Their cries, almost screams, mingled with countless footsteps and pounding hooves.
The sound woke the deep night and spread through the thick darkness hanging on every side like a curtain.
Far away.
Farther still.
Loud and clear.
Yet their desperate advance and shouts seemed unbearably slow and distant.
At least, they did to the young man and woman looking at each other in that moment.
He looked at her.
She looked at him.
The hundred or so *jang* between them meant nothing now.
They both knew.
They knew they were looking at each other.
They knew whose gaze had met theirs across the distance.
But only So Gyo had realized the other person’s true identity.
*So it was you.*
Swallowing a cryptic murmur, So Gyo silently looked down at the battlefield spread out beneath her.
It was vast.
And it was horrific.
The grand banquet hall, stretching for hundreds of *jang* in either direction, was awash with blood.
Ownerless weapons and severed limbs lay scattered across the ground.
The wide-open eyes of the dead held no trace of life.
The music that had sounded for a brief while was gone.
Only death remained in its place, and more people were surging in to pile death upon death.
*Whoosh.*
Amid the enemies’ thunderous shouts, a cold wind billowed her silky hair.
It carried the smell of blood deep into her nose, thick as the crimson pools all around her.
Thick enough to draw fragments of the past up from where time had buried them.
Thick enough to revive the horrific memories she’d wanted to forget but never could.
Perhaps that was why she felt not the slightest joy, though she had found the answer—the key—she had sought for so long.
Perhaps that was why she knew it was time to end this long and gruesome banquet.
*Shhk.*
In the silence, So Gyo moved both hands.
The two curved swords gripped in her blood-caked hands pointed toward sky and earth.
Then she brought them together.
*Shrring.
Clack.*
Steel forged by a craftsman’s countless rounds of quenching and hammering rang coldly.
A hidden groove and the metal set within it joined the two weapons.
As if they had been one from the beginning.
As if they had once been something other than curved swords.
*Wooooong.*
Restored to its original form after long years, the weapon trembled in its owner’s hands.
It resonated with the familiar energy flowing deep into it and shed tears of light.
*Zing.*
The air quivered.
A pure-white flash joined the two angled ends that had made the pieces look like curved swords.
Just as it had in the distant past.
Still bearing the splendor of an age when it had been divine punishment to some, salvation to others.
“It’s been a long time.”
So Gyo lifted her beloved weapon, her voice tender.
Then, as she had done tens of thousands of times before, she gripped the flash joining its ends and pulled hard.
*Fwoosh.*
A brilliant shaft of light took shape in midair, nocked against the shining bowstring.
The unbelievable sight stirred the old memories of someone watching from afar.
It raised someone’s figure from a past buried in dust.
An old woman who had ruled the battlefield with a bow larger than any other, unleashing Force like lightning.
“The Bow Saint...!”
At that very moment—
*SHWAAAAAK!*
The shaft of light flew from So Gyo’s—or rather, the Bow Saint’s—fingertips and streaked across the grand banquet hall.

chapters.title: Chapter 921
paragraphs: *Fwoosh!*
The moment they saw the streak of light hurtling toward them, the three thousand rebels charging as one instinctively understood.
Unavoidable death awaited them on the only path they had thought could save them.
“Dodge—!”
*KABOOOM!*

Someone’s scream was swallowed by the deafening roar. Amid the dust cloud that billowed up with the explosion, headless corpses and men and horses torn limb from limb shot into the air, spraying fountains of blood.
“GRAAAH!”
“S-spread out! Spread out at once and keep charging!”
“Don’t stop! If you stop, you die!”
Urgent commands rang out over countless screams.
Overcome by fear and confusion, the rebels forced strength into their trembling legs at the orders of their surviving leaders.
That was right.
If they stopped here, it was all over.
They had climbed onto the back of a rampaging tiger. Their fate was already sealed.
“AAAAAAH!”
“Charge! Chaaaarge!”
Bloodshot eyes wide in faces white as paper, the surviving rebels screamed in desperation and pressed forward.
Praying that the Force arrows liable to come flying from anywhere at any moment would spare them, at least.
Using the unlucky men at the front as shields.
*Please, please!*
They charged on with that desperate plea running endlessly through their clenched teeth. Then a dazzling streak of light appeared before them and blocked their path.
No. It swept them away.
*BOOM! CRUNCH!*
The earth shook. Rising dust soaked up blood and turned red.
Yet the gaze watching that horrific scene—and the hand that kept drawing the bowstring—remained terrifyingly calm.
*Four hundred paces.*
*Ziiing.*
The great bow shuddered. Its string and arrow, shining with their owner’s internal energy, unleashed speed and force no other archer could match.
Just as they did now.
*Thrum. Fwoosh!*
Another gale of light swept over the enemy, bringing the death—and the screams—that awaited them. Each arrow made of Force snuffed out dozens of lives like candles in the wind.
*Three hundred paces.*
Again.
*Two hundred paces.*
Again.
*KABOOM! KABOOM!*
The closer they came, the more corpses piled up. The men at the front had been replaced several times over, and those charging now howled like madmen.
Toward their only way out, which was also where they would die.
They pressed on as pawns on a vast game board until they met the dazzling light that would be the last thing they ever saw.
*Crunch!*
How many had died by the time they covered half the four hundred paces?
How many more would die crossing the two hundred that remained?
No one could answer the question that suddenly occurred to them.
Not those collapsing as they felt the life drain away. Not those forced to leave their fallen comrades behind and keep going.
Not even the leaders, who sent their men ahead while shouting for the charge.
“We’re almost there! Whoever captures the Emperor will be made a marquis and—!”
*Poom!*
A sharp crack cut off the shout.
In the blink of an eye, the commander flew from his saddle and landed in a pool of blood.
*Splash.*
“Ugh!”
“G-General of the Swift Cavalry!”
No one heard the rest of what he said, but looking at the General of the Swift Cavalry lying motionless in the blood, no one could help thinking of death.
He was unmistakably dead.
The powerful commander who had held military authority for so many years had died just like that.
Suddenly, miserably, and leaving one question behind.
*How?*
The leaders nearby were bewildered. The streak of light, far too powerful to seem like an arrow, had been nowhere in sight a moment ago.
*Then who...?*
As they turned to look for the unseen attacker, a low voice reached their ears.
“There’s something this old man wants to know. What do you call the bastards who started this goddamn mess?”
Someone else answered.
“What else? They’re fucking assholes.”
“Then what about the ones hanging back even now?”
“Hmm. Shitheads?”
“And if they’re both?”
“In a four-character idiom? Fucking dog-shitheads.”
“Fucking dog-shitheads, is it? That rolls right off the tongue.”
Not in front. Not behind. Not to either side.
The leaders, frozen like statues, slowly looked up.
Two people stood in midair above their heads.
A dreadful thought came to them: perhaps the sight before them and those voices would be the last things they ever saw and heard.
“W-wait. If you help us now, we can give you whatever you want...”
*Whoosh.*
A breeze blew. That was all.
It should have been all.
Then why were their minds growing hazy? There had been two people standing above them. Where had one gone?
“You fucking...”
A voice squeezed out between someone’s lips.
*Shhk.*
Deep within their bodies, death woke late and stretched. Faint red lines appeared where a spearhead had passed too quickly to see.
*Slip. Fwoooosh!*
Blood welled in small beads, then burst out. Heads, arms, and legs separated; bone and flesh came apart and slid away, defying their owners’ will.
The collapsing bodies fell behind the young man holding a spear untouched by blood—and poured down over his head.
*Thud-thud-thud!*
The young man standing beneath that red rain in the dark was Jin Taekyung. He finally gave them his answer.
“Help you? The best help you bastards can offer is to just fucking die. You fucking dog-shitheads.”
Those who had witnessed the horrific, unbelievable sight before their eyes were struck with shock—and despair, as they realized it was all over.

Every one of them wore splendid clothes. They were powerful figures who had pledged loyalty to Dark Heaven and the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, committing their families for generations to come. They had crossed a river they could never return from.
*It’s over. Completely.*
Jin Taekyung stood with his spearhead lowered and a calm expression, despite the hundreds of guards surrounding him. Jeok Cheongang still stood in the air.
Only then did the onlookers understand that their dreadful premonition had come true.
This vast rebellion was finished. So were the wealth and glory they had enjoyed for so long.
Their only consolation was that, instead of enduring brutal torture before being torn limb from limb by carts, they might receive a quick death from that martial-world ruffian.
Or so they thought.
Until Jeok Cheongang spoke.
“Leave the ones who look like the top dogs alive. I don’t know if they’re gold mines or spent ones, but we won’t know what’s in there unless we dig. Might as well take a few swings with the pickaxe.”
Their shock and resignation turned to fear in an instant. Before that instant was over, Jin Taekyung sent ten sharp cracks through the air toward them.
*Fwish-fwish-fwish!*
They weren’t given time to take out the poison pills they had kept hidden, just in case—or even a moment to draw the daggers at their waists and slash their own throats.
*Thud-thud-thud!*
They felt it.
Finger Qi crossing the distance in an instant and stiffening their entire bodies. The world slowly tilting as despair weighed down on their minds and bodies.
*Slip. Thump!*
They fell like waterlogged logs. Golden flags fluttering on every side filled their vision. Above the dragons writhing on the flags, countless arrowheads rained down across the dark sky.
*Shhhhhhh.*
A thousand repeating crossbowmen poured steel over the remaining rebels.
*Thud-thud-thud!*
The sounds of flesh being pierced announced the end of the blood-soaked banquet. Screams of pain joined them, mingling with the powerful, unceasing beat of drums.
Thick and sticky as blood.
*Boom. Boom. Booooom.*
Fifteen minutes.
That was how long it took for all three thousand rebels to be wiped out.
The Imperial Army swept into the grand banquet hall beneath a rain of arrows, bringing more than enough force to put an end to the long, horrific feast.
“Rebels, listen!”
“Rebels, listen!”
“Disarm and surrender at once!”
“Disarm and surrender at once!”
Shouts charged with powerful internal energy rang out one after another.
The twin officers urging them to surrender sounded so alike in voice and tone that they could have been one man. At the sight of them, the surviving rebels seemed to lose their last hope.
*Clunk. Clunk.*
*Clang.*
They loosened the joints of their bloodstained armor and dropped their cracked and broken weapons as if throwing them away.
No one knew who surrendered first, but the wave soon became a tide sweeping through the grand banquet hall.
“I surrender. I’ll surrender.”
“Please, just spare my life...”
Their eyes were vacant, their faces empty.
Some clutched the stump of a missing arm and begged for their lives. Others, backed to a cliff’s edge with nowhere left to retreat, made a choice they could never take back.
*Stab.*
“Kh... Urgh!”
A body pitched forward with a muffled death rattle.
The nameless rebel crumpled. His face held the despair of knowing it was over, and a trace of the peace he had found in escaping this hell.
“It’s over.”
At the faint words Jeok Cheongang murmured as if to himself, I forced myself to nod calmly.
Yeah. It was over.
The vast battle that had swallowed countless lives, both in plain sight and out of it, had finally ended.
But not everything was over.
The dead had gone somewhere far away, never to return. But the monster who was neither dead nor alive still remained here.
And we still had to deal with the living.
*Squish.*
A footstep landed in a pool of blood.
I watched her approach, my gaze cold and steady. Each light, graceful step left a sticky imprint of blood behind.
So Gyo.
No—the Bow Saint.
The woman who had kept everything about herself hidden.
At our first meeting, she had pretended to be the Emperor’s loyal servant. At our second, she had worn the mask of Dark Heaven. Only at our third had she finally revealed herself.
Now she was coming toward me.
With catlike steps that suited the name So Gyo, she crossed ground strewn with countless bodies. People who might still be alive if she had revealed her identity a little sooner.
*Fwoooosh.*
Blade-sharp qi rose from every part of my body. The Bow Saint stopped a few steps away and looked at me in silence, then suddenly spoke.
“So it was you.”
What did she mean?
I hesitated, unable to understand the meaning behind her words. A low voice sounded in my ear.
*—The one the Martial God spoke of. The chosen one.*
*...What?*

The woman who had kept everything about herself hidden.
At our first meeting, she had pretended to be the Emperor’s loyal servant.
At our second, she had worn the mask of Dark Heaven.
Only at our third had she finally revealed herself.
Now she was coming toward me.
With catlike steps that suited the name So Gyo, she crossed ground strewn with countless bodies.
People who might still be alive if she had revealed her identity a little sooner.
*Fwoooosh.*
Blade-sharp qi rose from every part of my body.
The Bow Saint stopped a few steps away and looked at me in silence, then suddenly spoke.
“So it was you.”
What did she mean?
I hesitated, unable to understand the meaning behind her words.
A low voice sounded in my ear.

The chosen one.*

chapters.title: Chapter 922
paragraphs: What made humans seem so special in a world teeming with life was their ability to think deeply and broadly.
Every human could do it.
They took in their current situation through their eyes and ears, thought about what to do or say to the person in front of them, and put together the right words.
At the same time, they predicted what those words and actions would bring about.
But their predictions weren’t always right.
When things took an unexpected turn, or the person they were talking to reacted in a way they hadn’t anticipated, they were thrown off.
Their racing thoughts came to a halt. They lost their words.
Just like me, right now.
“So it was you.”
So Gyo—no, the Bow Saint—stared at me. Her lips moved, and a voice only I could hear slipped between them.
*—The one the Martial God spoke of. The chosen one.*
*...What?*
The shock of learning that So Gyo was the giant known as the Bow Saint had completely disappeared.
That brief Sound Transmission hit me like a sledgehammer to the back of the head. I could only blink.
I’d expected an excuse, at least.
With me making no effort to hide my anger, I thought she’d say she hadn’t expected things to turn out this way. That she’d had no choice.
But she didn’t.
The Martial God.
And the chosen one.
I stood frozen like a statue, unable to make sense of those words or what they meant. Then the Bow Saint’s Sound Transmission continued.
*—Yes, you must be confused. I was, too, a long time ago.*
A long time ago? Just when was she talking about?
What had the Martial God, who had vanished into the distant past, told her?
But the question that flashed through my mind was cut short before it could even take shape.
*—It’s a long story I’ve kept to myself. But talking here and now wouldn’t be wise.*
I desperately wanted to press her for answers, but the Bow Saint’s Sound Transmission was enough to remind me of the situation I’d momentarily forgotten.
Right.
The bloodbath that had unfolded here today was over, but not everything was finished.
The curtain had fallen, but the curtain call remained.
The actors on this blood-soaked stage still had parts to play.
*I’ll get my answers after that.*
I nodded. The Bow Saint understood and quietly turned away, flicking a glance at the one person who’d stood beside us all along, watching in silence.
“That old hag hasn’t changed. No, she looks younger, but the look in her eyes is even more unpleasant.”
Jeok Cheongang muttered under his breath, then added, “Playing games through Sound Transmission with some young punk right in front of this old man, too.”
“What? You think I wouldn’t notice?”
I peeled a crust of dried blood off my cheek. “I figured you would. And even if you hadn’t, I would’ve told you myself.”
“You sure know how to talk.”
“So, did you hear everything?”
“Do you think the title Bow Saint belongs to Gaettong next door?”
“Then I’ll tell you. Every last word. I won’t leave out a single syllable.”
Jeok Cheongang studied me for a moment, then clicked his tongue.
“Forget it. There’s no rush, and she must have had her reasons. Anyway...”
*Pat. Pat.*
His solid palm tapped my shoulder. He turned his head sharply away, speaking in a gruff voice.
“Uh, well. What I’m trying to say is... hmm.”
“Yes?”
“No, what this old man means to say is... Hey, look at you. Are you laughing?”
A laugh must have slipped out without my realizing it.
But I didn’t rush to wipe the smile from my face like I used to.
I knew how he felt. And he’d understand how I felt, too.
*Thank you. For coming back to me.*
That was what Jeok Cheongang had said just a little while ago, when I’d been hovering between life and death, after I finally clawed my way back from death and recovered.
Now it was my turn to say it to him.
“Thank you. For always being by my side.”
I murmured it barely loud enough to hear, then looked up at the empty air as if something there had caught my attention.
It was a little embarrassing, and I wasn’t sure I could face his reaction.
But... well. Sometimes you want to say these things.
Even when you know each other so well that long explanations aren’t needed, sometimes you just want to tell someone how you feel.
And for all his immense martial prowess, Jeok Cheongang was remarkably bad at that.
“Ahem. What’s a hairy bastard like you doing saying something so revolting...”
He hesitated behind another unnecessary cough, then let out a quiet laugh. In the direction he pointed, a group was hurrying toward us.
“This old man’s a given. Save your thanks for them. They threw themselves into a deathtrap just to save you. They deserve at least that much praise, don’t they?”
I turned. Familiar faces were rushing toward me, drenched in blood from head to toe.
One, two, three... six.
They’d all survived. Not one of them was missing.
That was enough. More than enough.
*Ah.*
Was it the overwhelming relief? Or the exhaustion I’d forgotten?
All the strength went out of me at once. I staggered and began to fall.
No—I nearly fell.
Hands reached out from every side and caught me before I could.
*Grab.*
Jeok Cheongang, Hyuk Mujin, Ju Hwaran, Song Ilseom, Sama Pyo, Taishan, and the Divine Physician caught my arms and legs. They held me up as I started to topple.
They weren’t a burden to bear. They were pillars holding me steady.
Each of them had returned to this deathtrap hoping to help, even a little. Each had become my greatest reason to win this horrific battle.
“Damn it. I should be lending a hand at a moment like this, but this guy’s so tall I can’t reach him.”
At the mournful complaint from the old Hidden Shadow Pavilion agent perched on Taishan’s shoulder, everyone let out a quiet laugh.
Even me, though I’d been about to close my eyes and give in to the sleep demon.
*No. Not yet.*
I clenched my teeth and forced strength back into my failing body. Then I left their worried looks behind and started walking.
To bring this hellish night to an end.
To finish off the monster who had created a hellscape no painter could ever depict.
*Step. Step.*
I walked, and kept walking.
Past the dead and the rebels, bound tight in thick iron chains and struggling to break free.
Past dozens of flags rising high above me.
Until, at last, I saw the monster writhing alone at the Bow Saint’s feet. Across that vast space, there were no more cries of protest or screams.
“Eastern Heaven Demon Lord.”
At my call, the monster stopped moving.
The moment Jin Taekyung’s low voice reached his ears, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord felt all the strength leave his body.
Why?
He didn’t know.
Maybe it was because the man before him was Jin Taekyung—the one who had stood in his way at every turning point, every moment when the course of events might have changed.
Or maybe he’d been waiting for someone other than the Bow Saint, who had watched in silence all this time, to stop him.
To stop this meaningless struggle.
This hollow sense of defeat and fury, now that he could no longer achieve his goal.
“Yes, it’s you.”
A volcano cooled soon after spewing its lava. Now the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had cooled, too.
“You’re late. It’s rude to keep someone waiting this long.”
Jin Taekyung looked down at him in silence, then spoke.
“Well, I don’t think that applies to a monster like you who can’t even die.”
“A monster, is it? So that’s how you see me?”
“Yeah. And to be precise, I’m not exactly polite to people, either.”
“Ah. So you were born rude.”
“If you’d said that in front of my mom, she would’ve beaten you to death.”
“Didn’t you just say I couldn’t die?”
“Mom’s Divine Palm hits your soul. Not your body.”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord let out a hearty laugh before he could stop himself.
“I think I know what you mean. You have a point.”
Once, he’d had a mother, too.
She was gentle most of the time, but when he did something wrong, she’d scold him harshly and smack him on the back.
Even after all these years, he could faintly remember how it had hurt.
“Yes, I remember. I had times like that, too. My Master was usually gentle, but sometimes he’d take out the switch.”
Yet the more he recalled those happy memories, the more the smile on his lips faded.
“But... now I can’t remember.”
Once, those days had been the present.
They had been today, and yesterday.
But now, the only faces left in his memory were twisted hideously with pain. All he could see was them dead or dying.
“You bastards! Heaven will punish you!”
“Go! Hurry!”
It made no sense.

His mother’s piercing scream as the soldiers brutalized her while she fought to protect her only surviving child, and his Master’s final words—those memories were so vivid. So why were their smiling faces so faint?
Why were they blurred as if lost in fog?
*Crack.*
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord clenched his teeth so hard that his molars shattered.
But the pain that should have followed never came.
Only the result remained: they were broken.
Just as the people around him had died screaming.
Just as he had chosen to become a monster instead of a human being.
“Do you know something?”
His lips, wet with blood, moved. His eyes, fixed on Jin Taekyung, the Bow Saint, and the countless people who had gathered around him, flickered with cold flames.
“This is only the beginning.”
He spat out each syllable, filling it with anger.
He swallowed his resentment toward the world and his grief at knowing he could never be happy again.
“Even if you’ve protected the Imperial Capital, you can’t stop the fires spreading throughout the land.”
He had spent more than half a century in the imperial court. No one had gone without sheltering for a time beneath his vast shadow, and no one had escaped Dark Heaven’s reach.
Those frogs had left the great well of the Imperial Capital, each taking up an official post somewhere in the land. There they had put down new roots, grown branches, and borne fruit.
That was why the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord could smile.
He thought of the Great Nation soon to be engulfed by civil war and a raging fire. He thought of Dark Heaven’s forces advancing into the Central Plains with those flames before them.
“On that day, the Great Nation will fall.”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord threw his head back and laughed, looking at the Emperor standing before him and mocking the helplessness he would feel.

chapters.title: Chapter 923
paragraphs: How many people feel no fear in the face of death?
Very few.
No—none.

Of course, if you turned the whole world upside down and shook it out, you might find a few. But even among Murim warriors, whose guts are in a league of their own compared to ordinary people, I’d swear there wasn’t a madman like that.
After all, it’s only natural to fear death when you’ve lived a life of your own.
A battle-hardened veteran who’s survived countless brushes with death and a green kid who hasn’t even lost the down on his face are equals before it. Both are afraid.
All the more so if death comes with a full course of unspeakably horrific torture first.
But there are exceptions to everything.
Like the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, laughing at the top of his lungs before the Emperor.
“Ha! Hahahahaha!”
Sprawled on the ground without his limbs, he was a wretched sight.
Yet his laughter rang out like a victor’s.
The final death he’d put off once—perhaps dozens of times—was at last upon him. Still, I couldn’t find a trace of fear in him.
Was it simply because his body couldn’t feel pain?
*No.*
Even if he’d been an ordinary human instead of a monster, he would have laughed just the same.
He would have cursed the imperial family and the Great Nation that had taken everything from him, and gladly accepted torture and death.
After all those years, the only thing the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had left was his grievance.
Self-reproach and regret that he hadn’t completed his revenge with his own hands.
That was all.
The only truth, the only outcome. Nothing more, nothing less.
“It’s over. Completely.”
Jeok Cheongang’s mutter was clear enough.
No sweet words or kind gestures would get information out of the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord now.
Like a horse galloping across a wilderness without looking back, his path had been set long ago.
“I’ve seen eyes like that before. Don’t waste time. Kill him now, before he can cause any more trouble.”
He wasn’t speaking only to me. Jeok Cheongang was speaking to everyone here.
It was the greatest respect he could show the people who had fought beside him on the same battlefield—and a proposal addressed to one man.
The ruler of this vast continent.
The Emperor.
“Your Majesty.”
Jeong Hogun, a Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, stepped forward with a sword broken in half. Blood covered him from head to toe.
“Please, give your command.”
But the Emperor didn’t answer.
He stood with his lips pressed shut, gazing down at the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, exhaustion on his face. Some time passed before he spoke.
“What do you think?”
At first, I didn’t know who he was asking.
But as the Emperor’s gaze settled squarely on me, and the people around us erupted as if a dam had burst, I understood.
The Emperor was asking *me*, of all people, what should be done with the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord.
“Y-Your Majesty!”
“You mustn’t!”
“How could Your Majesty, the sovereign of all under Heaven, ask a mere subject—not even a minister of the court, but a lawless ruffian from the martial world—”
“Lawless ruffians from the martial world, you say.”
The Emperor repeated the words quietly and looked around. Officials in court robes had gathered on every side of him.
He studied their faces one by one. Many had survived because he and the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had been focused solely on each other.

“How strange,” the Emperor said at last. “The ruffian you speak of fought so hard he’s covered in blood. Yet you ministers of the court have come through this fierce battle looking remarkably untouched.”
Silence fell in an instant.
Having shut everyone up with a few words, the Emperor turned back to me.
“Now answer me. I want to hear what you think.”
I didn’t know.
I didn’t know why he’d singled me out, or what answer he wanted.
But I didn’t dwell on it. As always, I could just say what I had to say.
“If I opposed killing him, would you let him live?”
A single, explosive question that no one had expected. I heard people around us catch their breath.
Even the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord stopped laughing and opened his eyes wide.
The Emperor’s gaze didn’t waver.
*No.*
“Why not?”
I wasn’t asking because I didn’t know.
Everyone here needed to hear the answer, even if the people beyond the palace walls never did.
I trusted the Emperor to understand what I was doing.

“He is a traitor without equal in history. For years, he kept My Father blind and deaf to what was happening. He used poison to slowly drive most of the imperial family to their deaths, including My Eldest Brother, the Crown Prince.”
Shock rippled through the crowd.
Everyone held their breath as the Emperor revealed a history that had remained hidden. Until now, the world had believed that he himself was the root of all the evil.
“By the time I learned the truth, it was too late. Traitors bent on destroying the Great Nation had seized control of the imperial family and held most of the real power.”
Everyone here could imagine what had followed.
An Emperor reduced to a puppet. Princes already poisoned.
Those heirs to a noble bloodline had neither time nor people left to turn to.

Except for one old general who had protected the Embroidered Uniform Guard with unwavering loyalty, and the Great Nation’s fourth prince, who was far from the throne and had been wandering the provinces.
“There was only one way left.”
And so a restoration took place under the guise of a rebellion.
More than a decade ago, right here in this grand banquet hall.
In a single night, several hundred high-ranking court officials died. Before long, tens of thousands more were exiled or executed.
The fourth prince wielded the blade of the purge without hesitation.
He climbed the bodies of the traitors who had tried to destroy the Great Nation, with the unseen glares and curses of its people at his back.
All the while, he promised himself he would soon reveal the truth and wash away his disgrace.
“Then the late Emperor and the other members of the imperial family were confined because...”

“I tried everything to cure them, but even the Imperial Physicians couldn’t determine what was wrong. They spoke of a great physician who wandered the world like a cloud and could drive away even the Grim Reaper. If we found him, they said, there might be a way.”
“The Divine Physician.”
“Yes.” The Emperor’s expression turned bitter. “But in the end, I could never find him.”
I’d heard the story from the Slaughter Saint himself.
He and the Divine Physician had wandered the land treating its people. Those who remembered their kindness had hidden them from the imperial family’s search.
*If the imperial court had found them then...*
History would have changed.

Even if the poison that cast its long shadow of death over the imperial family had been the Blood Soul Gu, the Slaughter Saint and the Divine Physician I knew might have found some way to deal with it.

Instead, that twist of fate ended with the deaths of the late Emperor, the crown princes, and several other members of the imperial family. The fourth prince, once so far from the throne, became a usurper and an unfilial son in the eyes of the world.
“Why didn’t you tell anyone? Why keep the truth hidden?”

“It wasn’t that I wouldn’t. I couldn’t. At some point, anything I said or did sounded like a usurper making excuses. It was only when My Father regained his senses at the very end and told Me he would pass the throne to Me that I understood.”
It was a stain he could never erase.
Though the fourth prince had formally received the throne and become the ruler of all under Heaven, people turned their backs on a truth they couldn’t believe.
To them, he was a usurper blinded by ambition, a son who had dragged his father from the throne.
As if that weren’t enough, a murderer and parricide who had led countless families and members of the imperial clan to their deaths.
The traitors who had brought the Great Nation to the brink of ruin became loyal patriots. Those who had tried to protect it were left covered in filth.
And yet...
He had no choice but to go on. He had to pull out the enormous weed that had spread its shadow across the Great Nation, roots and all.
“I took the Imperial Capital and purged countless traitors, but the main stem survived. That restoration was only half a success.”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord hadn’t been the monster he was now.
He’d fought the Bow Saint and Baek Yeon, suffering injuries so severe he could never recover. Then he’d proposed a deal.
His life in exchange for the fate of the Great Nation.
“For Me... it was an offer I couldn’t refuse.”
The Emperor was the realm, and the Imperial Capital its center.
But the Emperor and the capital were not the whole realm.
If the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had been killed that day, the Great Nation would have split in two and plunged into a massive war.

With the country hanging by a thread, the only path the fourth prince could choose would have given those who had conspired with the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord long ago, and had waited for the right moment, another excuse to rebel.
“I had to prevent that. No more blood could be spilled.”
The fourth prince had taken up a sword as soon as he could walk.
By the time the calluses on his hands felt natural and the reins were familiar to his touch, he was marching off to war.
Time and again, he’d led armies with outstanding martial skill and strategy, earning great victories. But whenever he went to the battlefield, he would murmur to himself:
*This will be the last war.*
*It has to be the last.*
The throne? Glory as a general?
He needed neither. He’d let go of any desire for them long ago.

His brilliant, kind eldest brother would make a sage king. The fourth prince had fought in dozens of wars, great and small, for one reason alone: he wanted the realm his brother would rule to be at peace.
That was all.
But. But...
“So this is what it came to.”
*Shing.*
The fourth prince—the Emperor—drew his sword.
He looked at me over its shimmering blade, still spotless despite the countless dead it had cut down.
“Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan. I ask you again. Do I need another reason to kill him?”
“What you’ve told us is enough,” I said.
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord wasn’t the only one who had waited for his chance at revenge.
“Then that settles it.”
The Emperor’s voice was calm, though something fierce burned beneath it. He brought his sword down.
Toward his family’s enemy.
Against the traitor of all time, who had plunged his country and its people into misery.
Or he would have.
The Emperor’s treasured sword was moving with enough force to split the man in two when a clear young voice rang out.
“One thing is still missing.”
*Whoosh!*
The blade hissed through the air.
The Emperor stopped it a hair’s breadth from the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s throat. He turned. So did I, and everyone else.
We saw a boy in clothes spotted with blood, his eyes calm and sad.
Prince Shangshan. Zhu Bao.
Everyone was looking at the young prince. He looked only at one person, and his small, still-growing feet carried him toward that man.
“Your Highness! Your Highness!”
Hong Jin, nowhere to be seen until now, called out in alarm. He must have gone to his master’s side as soon as the battle began.
Prince Shangshan didn’t stop.
*Step.*
One step.
*Step.*
Another.
No one could stand in his way.
At that moment, the boy they saw was a man.
Not a young prince, but another ruler.
And that man, that ruler, slowly bowed his head.
To someone who could not let go of his anger even before death.
Toward the enemy who had killed his parents and siblings.
*Swish.*
The hem of Prince Shangshan’s robe brushed a pool of blood. He bent deeply toward the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord and spoke.
“I’m sorry. I know no words can comfort you, but... I sincerely apologize for what my grandfather did.”
Everyone was speechless.
The Emperor, the Bow Saint, the Fire King, and me.
Even the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord.
“Ah.”
A quiet groan slipped between his parted lips.
He looked at Prince Shangshan with trembling eyes, then smiled faintly.
“What a damnable thing.”
*Thrust!*
The blade resting against his skin sank into his throat.

sentences.text: How many people feel no fear in the face of death?
Very few.
No—none.
Of course, if you turned the whole world upside down and shook it out, you might find a few.
But even among Murim warriors, whose guts are in a league of their own compared to ordinary people, I’d swear there wasn’t a madman like that.
After all, it’s only natural to fear death when you’ve lived a life of your own.
A battle-hardened veteran who’s survived countless brushes with death and a green kid who hasn’t even lost the down on his face are equals before it.
Both are afraid.
All the more so if death comes with a full course of unspeakably horrific torture first.
But there are exceptions to everything.
Like the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, laughing at the top of his lungs before the Emperor.
“Ha!
Hahahahaha!”
Sprawled on the ground without his limbs, he was a wretched sight.
Yet his laughter rang out like a victor’s.
The final death he’d put off once—perhaps dozens of times—was at last upon him.
Still, I couldn’t find a trace of fear in him.
Was it simply because his body couldn’t feel pain?
*No.*
Even if he’d been an ordinary human instead of a monster, he would have laughed just the same.
He would have cursed the imperial family and the Great Nation that had taken everything from him, and gladly accepted torture and death.
After all those years, the only thing the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had left was his grievance.
Self-reproach and regret that he hadn’t completed his revenge with his own hands.
That was all.
The only truth, the only outcome.
Nothing more, nothing less.
“It’s over.
Completely.”
Jeok Cheongang’s mutter was clear enough.
No sweet words or kind gestures would get information out of the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord now.
Like a horse galloping across a wilderness without looking back, his path had been set long ago.
“I’ve seen eyes like that before.
Don’t waste time.
Kill him now, before he can cause any more trouble.”
He wasn’t speaking only to me.
Jeok Cheongang was speaking to everyone here.
It was the greatest respect he could show the people who had fought beside him on the same battlefield—and a proposal addressed to one man.
The ruler of this vast continent.
The Emperor.
“Your Majesty.”
Jeong Hogun, a Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, stepped forward with a sword broken in half.
Blood covered him from head to toe.
“Please, give your command.”
But the Emperor didn’t answer.
He stood with his lips pressed shut, gazing down at the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, exhaustion on his face.
Some time passed before he spoke.
“What do you think?”
At first, I didn’t know who he was asking.
But as the Emperor’s gaze settled squarely on me, and the people around us erupted as if a dam had burst, I understood.
The Emperor was asking *me*, of all people, what should be done with the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord.
“Y-Your Majesty!”
“You mustn’t!”
“How could Your Majesty, the sovereign of all under Heaven, ask a mere subject—not even a minister of the court, but a lawless ruffian from the martial world—”
“Lawless ruffians from the martial world, you say.”
The Emperor repeated the words quietly and looked around.
Officials in court robes had gathered on every side of him.
He studied their faces one by one.
Many had survived because he and the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had been focused solely on each other.
“How strange,” the Emperor said at last.
“The ruffian you speak of fought so hard he’s covered in blood.
Yet you ministers of the court have come through this fierce battle looking remarkably untouched.”
Silence fell in an instant.
Having shut everyone up with a few words, the Emperor turned back to me.
“Now answer me.
I want to hear what you think.”
I didn’t know.
I didn’t know why he’d singled me out, or what answer he wanted.
But I didn’t dwell on it.
As always, I could just say what I had to say.
“If I opposed killing him, would you let him live?”
A single, explosive question that no one had expected.
I heard people around us catch their breath.
Even the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord stopped laughing and opened his eyes wide.
The Emperor’s gaze didn’t waver.
*No.*
“Why not?”
I wasn’t asking because I didn’t know.
Everyone here needed to hear the answer, even if the people beyond the palace walls never did.
I trusted the Emperor to understand what I was doing.
“He is a traitor without equal in history.
For years, he kept My Father blind and deaf to what was happening.
He used poison to slowly drive most of the imperial family to their deaths, including My Eldest Brother, the Crown Prince.”
Shock rippled through the crowd.
Everyone held their breath as the Emperor revealed a history that had remained hidden.
Until now, the world had believed that he himself was the root of all the evil.
“By the time I learned the truth, it was too late.
Traitors bent on destroying the Great Nation had seized control of the imperial family and held most of the real power.”
Everyone here could imagine what had followed.
An Emperor reduced to a puppet.
Princes already poisoned.
Those heirs to a noble bloodline had neither time nor people left to turn to.

Except for one old general who had protected the Embroidered Uniform Guard with unwavering loyalty, and the Great Nation’s fourth prince, who was far from the throne and had been wandering the provinces.
“There was only one way left.”
And so a restoration took place under the guise of a rebellion.
More than a decade ago, right here in this grand banquet hall.
In a single night, several hundred high-ranking court officials died.
Before long, tens of thousands more were exiled or executed.
The fourth prince wielded the blade of the purge without hesitation.
He climbed the bodies of the traitors who had tried to destroy the Great Nation, with the unseen glares and curses of its people at his back.
All the while, he promised himself he would soon reveal the truth and wash away his disgrace.
“Then the late Emperor and the other members of the imperial family were confined because...”
“I tried everything to cure them, but even the Imperial Physicians couldn’t determine what was wrong.
They spoke of a great physician who wandered the world like a cloud and could drive away even the Grim Reaper.
If we found him, they said, there might be a way.”
“The Divine Physician.”
“Yes.” The Emperor’s expression turned bitter.
“But in the end, I could never find him.”
I’d heard the story from the Slaughter Saint himself.
He and the Divine Physician had wandered the land treating its people.
Those who remembered their kindness had hidden them from the imperial family’s search.
*If the imperial court had found them then...*
History would have changed.

Even if the poison that cast its long shadow of death over the imperial family had been the Blood Soul Gu, the Slaughter Saint and the Divine Physician I knew might have found some way to deal with it.
Instead, that twist of fate ended with the deaths of the late Emperor, the crown princes, and several other members of the imperial family.
The fourth prince, once so far from the throne, became a usurper and an unfilial son in the eyes of the world.
“Why didn’t you tell anyone?
Why keep the truth hidden?”
“It wasn’t that I wouldn’t.
I couldn’t.
At some point, anything I said or did sounded like a usurper making excuses.
It was only when My Father regained his senses at the very end and told Me he would pass the throne to Me that I understood.”
It was a stain he could never erase.
Though the fourth prince had formally received the throne and become the ruler of all under Heaven, people turned their backs on a truth they couldn’t believe.
To them, he was a usurper blinded by ambition, a son who had dragged his father from the throne.
As if that weren’t enough, a murderer and parricide who had led countless families and members of the imperial clan to their deaths.
The traitors who had brought the Great Nation to the brink of ruin became loyal patriots.
Those who had tried to protect it were left covered in filth.
And yet...
He had no choice but to go on.
He had to pull out the enormous weed that had spread its shadow across the Great Nation, roots and all.
“I took the Imperial Capital and purged countless traitors, but the main stem survived.

The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord hadn’t been the monster he was now.

chapters.title: Chapter 924
paragraphs: *Thuk.*
There was no resistance. Nothing to stop it.
The imperial family’s treasured sword cut through the flesh and bone against its edge like tofu, doing its job regardless of its master’s wishes.
Silence fell.
No one there had expected this.
Who could have imagined that a vengeful ghost who had devoted his entire life to bringing down the accursed imperial court and the Great Nation would choose this path?
That he would thrust his own neck onto the blade held out by his enemy’s descendant?
And yet, fate, once twisted, would not grant him death so easily.
*Grrk. Cough.*

Blood and phlegm bubbled through the gaping wound in his throat. Gasping for breath, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord felt his body slowly, little by little, beginning to recover. A rasping laugh escaped him.
What a farce.
He had made himself a monster to survive. Now he was struggling to die.
The power he had once considered a blessing had become a curse that held him captive.
*What kind of farce is this?*
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord stared up at the sky and laughed emptily.
He resented this body that would not die, however much he wanted it to.
He did not want to meet the inscrutable eyes of Jin Taekyung and the Emperor as they looked down at him.
And...
He could not bring himself to face the child still bowing deeply to him. The boy was barely more than a baby.
No. He was ashamed to face him.
“Twelve years. It was twelve years ago.”
*Cough.*
He spat out the bloody froth rising in his throat and slowly went on.
“I watched from a distance as a child, still young enough to be nursing, left the imperial palace in a eunuch’s arms.”
The eunuch was Hong Jin. The child was Zhu Bao.
“I wanted to kill him. More than once, even after that.”
But he had not done it.
It was not only because Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao would make the perfect puppet to depose the Emperor and take his place one day.

The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had dimly suspected that the Emperor’s decision to make his youngest brother Prince Shangshan and send him far away was a ruse. Even so, he could never bring himself to order the assassination.
He hadn’t even known why he agonized over it so much.
No. He had known and pretended otherwise.
“That child... reminded me of myself.”
In the little boy who had lost his parents and siblings, in that small child being carried out of the palace as if in flight, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had seen his own past.
Messenger pigeons arrived at regular intervals with news of the boy. In those few written lines, he could read his loneliness.
“They said that far away, more than ten thousand li from here, the five-year-old cried every night. His sobs were so loud they could be heard over the walls.”
For better or worse, the child was precocious. At five, he had learned the truth.
He was far more special than other children, and perhaps just as much more unfortunate.
Other children did not call their mothers their wet nurses.
“Time passed quickly. By seven, they said, he no longer cried. He’d grown lively instead, practicing martial arts day and night.”
But the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord knew better.
In those few lines of the missive, he could still see the child crying.
“He had only learned to hold back his tears. Just as I once did.”
Something he didn’t want to get used to.
Something he had no choice but to grow used to.
So the child held back his tears. Night after night, he hid from the eunuch and wet nurse who cared for him so devotedly, buried his face in his blanket, and cried without a sound.
If they heard him, they would be sad.
If his sobs carried beyond the walls, he would lose his dignity as a ruler.
Seven years old.
The child had grown up and faced reality.
Far sooner than anyone would have wished.
“That was when I finally understood. I could no longer kill him.”
Time flowed on like a river.

The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, unable to recover from the injuries he had suffered at the hands of the Bow Saint, performed his sect’s forbidden ritual and turned himself into a jiangshi. Meanwhile, the child, whose days had always been much the same, met a young man.
Jin Taekyung.
The Third Young Master of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
A wastrel who had only just taken his first step toward turning his life around.
And that third young master of an unremarkable martial family gave the boy something his life had never held before.
A dream.
“‘Dreams come true.’ That was what it said.”
When the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord read those words in the missive, he laughed despite himself.
The nerve of that young punk, spouting such nonsense to a prince—even if he was only a child. Funnier still was the boy turning that nonsense into a plaque and hanging it in his residence.
But it left a bitter taste, too.
He had once had a clear, shining dream of his own.
And as long as he lived, the child’s dream could never come true.
“Even then, I found myself wondering what dream he held deep in his heart. What he hoped to achieve.”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord slowly turned his head.
The boy was still bowed low, trembling faintly. At some point, his eyes had filled with tears, and he could not bring himself to straighten up and show them.
“Now I want to hear his answer. He must be thirteen by now.”
Twelve years had passed.
The child had become a boy. The old man had become a monster.
And now, Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao struggled to steady himself.
“My dream...”
He slowly straightened his back and gave voice to the dream he had kept in his heart.
“Is to make certain no one else suffers the misfortune you and I endured.”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes trembled.
So did everyone else’s.
“That... will be impossible.”
“That is why it is a dream.”
“Do you mean to wish for it, knowing you cannot achieve it?”
“It is a dream because I will not give up. Because I will keep trying, with all my might, to make it come true.”
“Do you know what it is you’re speaking of?”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord could no longer hide how shaken he was. Prince Shangshan answered quietly.
“An age of peace and prosperity.”
Four characters that had been the wish of all the people since ancient times, and had always betrayed them.
Yet here was a boy of thirteen speaking them aloud.
He was saying that he, at least, would not betray the people. That he would usher in another age like the reigns of Yao and Shun, when all had lived in peace and happiness.
Every word was sincere.
“I will punish the wicked and reward the good, regardless of their station.”
Uprightness.
“I will always watch over and cherish the people, and heed the counsel of those around me.”
Humanity and righteousness.
“I will respect every one of my people. I will look beyond their birth and accept their good hearts and wisdom.”
Propriety and wisdom.
“And I will sow no seeds of misfortune. Whatever consequences come of that, I will bear them and take responsibility for them.”
“Ah.”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord groaned.
The meaning behind the young prince’s final words—*forbearance*—cut into his heart like a blade.
“I... I could forgive nothing. At some point, I began to curse everything.”
At the end of a brutal age of turmoil, the warlords who had caused him to lose his family had turned to dust and disappeared.
Taizu, who had burned his sect and slaughtered his Master and fellow disciples, was dead as well.
But the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord remained. So did his thirst for revenge.
No, it burned more fiercely than ever.
Against those who were left. Against people who had done nothing wrong.
“But how... how can you...!”
Unable to bring himself to look straight at the boy, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord closed his eyes and cried out, his voice boiling over.
It was not the anger he had felt before.
He was simply more anguished than ever.
Even now, he could not let go of everything.
And he was ashamed.
The boy before him was holding out, in his small hands, the forgiveness the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had failed to find in a lifetime.
“Do you know something?”
At the sudden question, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord opened his eyes.
Prince Shangshan was looking at him, his gaze trembling.
“When I learned the whole truth today, I wanted to kill you more than anyone.”
“Then why...?”
“Because my heart ached for you. I realized what made us different: the good fortune I was given, and you were not.”
Prince Shangshan slowly turned his head. A man stood beside him, looking haggard but entirely at ease, as if there were nowhere else he could be. The young prince’s gaze fell on him.
“I had a subject closer to me than family.”
His name was Hong Jin. He had been at the prince’s side from his earliest memories until this very moment.
“And I had an elder brother and loyal subjects who endured countless humiliations for this country.”
The Emperor closed his eyes with a low groan.
The loyal old general and the Embroidered Uniform Guards, who had been forced to seize the throne to confront a greater injustice, clenched their teeth, trying to suppress their agitation.
“When I could not see even a glimmer of light, there were people who reached out to me without asking for anything in return.”
The martial artists of Murim.
People who had stepped outside the Great Nation’s laws and built a world apart.
Yet they had willingly torn down that boundary and rushed into a place where danger waited on every side.
Prince Shangshan’s gaze passed from one to the next. One awkwardly scratched his bald head. Another gave him a gentle nod. One was rubbing his stomach as if he were hungry.
And at the end of his gaze stood a young man.
He was neither the strongest nor the wisest among them. Even so, he stood at the center of them all as naturally as if he belonged there.
He had planted a dream in someone’s heart and promised to be his friend. Now he smiled at the boy who had grown so much.
His smile was so bright and warm that, for an instant, even the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord thought the world before his eyes had grown brighter.
*Chivalry.*
He had forgotten that single word for so long it felt strange to him. The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord turned it over in his empty heart.
Then he saw himself reflected in the young prince’s tear-filled eyes: warped and blurred, like a monster.
“The man I saw in you was not only a sinner of the ages, burdened with unforgivable karma. You were also an unfortunate person who had no choice but to walk a different path from mine.”
Unfortunate, he had chosen revenge instead of forgiveness.
Inhuman, he had become a monster.
He had thought revenge was the only path. It was the reason he had lived on, first as a human being and then as a monster.
But he had been wrong.
About his purpose. About his reason.
“Now... you can stop.”
The quiet words reached him, and the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord went rigid.
*You can stop now.*
*It’s all right to stop.*
Those simple words melted a heart that had spent so many years burning to ash and freezing over, again and again.
At last, they brought him peace.
*So that was it.*
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord looked silently up at the sky.
He had resented it without end.
The sky. The whole world.
But when the last veil of anger fell away from his heart, he saw a new world.
Countless stars shone in the sky that had seemed filled with nothing but darkness. A breeze from somewhere carried the scent of grass.
It mingled with the thick stench of blood rising from the hellscape he had made.
*Too late. I realized far too late.*
Thousands upon thousands of people had already been killed or wounded.
And how many more would be sacrificed because of his choices?
He couldn’t even begin to guess.
Nor could he measure the weight of the crime he would bear for the countless lives swallowed up in the great war he had set in motion.
Yet here, at the end, a new fork in the road lay before him. It whispered insistently that he should make the better choice, even if only by a little.
As if that choice could make his whole black-stained life pale beside it.
*—Listen carefully to what I’m about to say.*
*Whoosh.*
The Sound Transmission slipped between his moving lips and mingled with the wind.
It passed the young prince and the Emperor, crossed the ring of Embroidered Uniform Guards and the assembled civil and military officials, and reached one man.
Jin Taekyung.
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord smiled bitterly at the sight of Jin staring down at him, eyes wide.
It was far too late. But at the very end, he had made a slightly better choice.
That was all.
*—I’ve told you my story. Now it’s time to collect my fortune-telling fee.*
Jin Taekyung watched the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord in silence, his gaze sunk deep. Then he nodded and stepped forward.
*Splash.*
Ripples spread across a pool of thick, sticky blood.
Everyone watching knew what Jin Taekyung was about to do. Not one of the civil or military officials tried to stop him.
They did not dare.
The Emperor and Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao had stepped aside themselves to clear his path.
At this moment, Jin Taekyung was the Emperor’s appointed proxy, granted the authority to execute this great traitor on the Son of Heaven’s behalf.
*Shing.*
A cool breeze brushed the spearhead he held in a reverse grip. As the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord watched blue-white flames gather slowly at its tip, he spoke.
“Do you think someone like me will have a next life?”
“Probably. You’ll have to spend about three thousand jiazi as a cockroach or a mosquito first, though.”
*I see. I suppose so.*
At Jin Taekyung’s matter-of-fact answer, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord let out a dry laugh. Jin Taekyung continued in an even voice.
“But in your next life, make sure you’re born human again.”
“What do you mean...?”
“You never know. Maybe someone will help you then, unlike in this life.”
“If we get the chance, let’s meet again. Just don’t be too late.”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord—no, Wei Zhong—fell silent. Then he smiled faintly.
Without another word, he watched the dazzling flames fill his vision.
*Whoosh.*
Their warmth, strange as it was, wrapped around his entire body.
