He spat out the bloody froth rising in his throat and slowly went on.
“I watched from a distance as a child, still young enough to be nursing, left the imperial palace in a eunuch’s arms.”
The eunuch was Hong Jin.
The child was Zhu Bao.
“I wanted to kill him.
More than once, even after that.”
But he had not done it.
It was not only because Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao would make the perfect puppet to depose the Emperor and take his place one day.
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had dimly suspected that the Emperor’s decision to make his youngest brother Prince Shangshan and send him far away was a ruse.
Even so, he could never bring himself to order the assassination.
He hadn’t even known why he agonized over it so much.
No.
He had known and pretended otherwise.
“That child... reminded me of myself.”
In the little boy who had lost his parents and siblings, in that small child being carried out of the palace as if in flight, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had seen his own past.
Messenger pigeons arrived at regular intervals with news of the boy.
In those few written lines, he could read his loneliness.
“They said that far away, more than ten thousand li from here, the five-year-old cried every night.
His sobs were so loud they could be heard over the walls.”
For better or worse, the child was precocious.
At five, he had learned the truth.
He was far more special than other children, and perhaps just as much more unfortunate.
Other children did not call their mothers their wet nurses.
“Time passed quickly.
By seven, they said, he no longer cried.
He’d grown lively instead, practicing martial arts day and night.”
But the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord knew better.
In those few lines of the missive, he could still see the child crying.
“He had only learned to hold back his tears.
Just as I once did.”
Something he didn’t want to get used to.
Something he had no choice but to grow used to.
So the child held back his tears.
Night after night, he hid from the eunuch and wet nurse who cared for him so devotedly, buried his face in his blanket, and cried without a sound.
If they heard him, they would be sad.
If his sobs carried beyond the walls, he would lose his dignity as a ruler.
Seven years old.
The child had grown up and faced reality.
Far sooner than anyone would have wished.
“That was when I finally understood.
I could no longer kill him.”
Time flowed on like a river.
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, unable to recover from the injuries he had suffered at the hands of the Bow Saint, performed his sect’s forbidden ritual and turned himself into a jiangshi.
Meanwhile, the child, whose days had always been much the same, met a young man.
Jin Taekyung.
The Third Young Master of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
A wastrel who had only just taken his first step toward turning his life around.
And that third young master of an unremarkable martial family gave the boy something his life had never held before.
A dream.
“‘Dreams come true.’ That was what it said.”
When the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord read those words in the missive, he laughed despite himself.
The nerve of that young punk, spouting such nonsense to a prince—even if he was only a child.
Funnier still was the boy turning that nonsense into a plaque and hanging it in his residence.
But it left a bitter taste, too.
He had once had a clear, shining dream of his own.
And as long as he lived, the child’s dream could never come true.
“Even then, I found myself wondering what dream he held deep in his heart.
What he hoped to achieve.”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord slowly turned his head.
The boy was still bowed low, trembling faintly.
At some point, his eyes had filled with tears, and he could not bring himself to straighten up and show them.
“Now I want to hear his answer.
He must be thirteen by now.”
Twelve years had passed.
The child had become a boy.
The old man had become a monster.
And now, Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao struggled to steady himself.
“My dream...”
He slowly straightened his back and gave voice to the dream he had kept in his heart.
“Is to make certain no one else suffers the misfortune you and I endured.”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes trembled.
So did everyone else’s.
“That... will be impossible.”
“That is why it is a dream.”
“Do you mean to wish for it, knowing you cannot achieve it?”
“It is a dream because I will not give up.
Because I will keep trying, with all my might, to make it come true.”
“Do you know what it is you’re speaking of?”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord could no longer hide how shaken he was.
Prince Shangshan answered quietly.
“An age of peace and prosperity.”
Four characters that had been the wish of all the people since ancient times, and had always betrayed them.
Yet here was a boy of thirteen speaking them aloud.
He was saying that he, at least, would not betray the people.
That he would usher in another age like the reigns of Yao and Shun, when all had lived in peace and happiness.
Every word was sincere.
“I will punish the wicked and reward the good, regardless of their station.”
Uprightness.
“I will always watch over and cherish the people, and heed the counsel of those around me.”
Humanity and righteousness.
“I will respect every one of my people.
I will look beyond their birth and accept their good hearts and wisdom.”
Propriety and wisdom.
“And I will sow no seeds of misfortune.
Whatever consequences come of that, I will bear them and take responsibility for them.”
“Ah.”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord groaned.
The meaning behind the young prince’s final words—*forbearance*—cut into his heart like a blade.
I could forgive nothing.
At some point, I began to curse everything.”
At the end of a brutal age of turmoil, the warlords who had caused him to lose his family had turned to dust and disappeared.
Taizu, who had burned his sect and slaughtered his Master and fellow disciples, was dead as well.
But the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord remained.
So did his thirst for revenge.
No, it burned more fiercely than ever.
Against those who were left.
Against people who had done nothing wrong.
“But how... how can you...!”
Unable to bring himself to look straight at the boy, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord closed his eyes and cried out, his voice boiling over.
It was not the anger he had felt before.
He was simply more anguished than ever.
Even now, he could not let go of everything.
And he was ashamed.
The boy before him was holding out, in his small hands, the forgiveness the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had failed to find in a lifetime.
“Do you know something?”
At the sudden question, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord opened his eyes.
Prince Shangshan was looking at him, his gaze trembling.
“When I learned the whole truth today, I wanted to kill you more than anyone.”
“Then why...?”
“Because my heart ached for you.
I realized what made us different: the good fortune I was given, and you were not.”
Prince Shangshan slowly turned his head.
A man stood beside him, looking haggard but entirely at ease, as if there were nowhere else he could be.
The young prince’s gaze fell on him.
“I had a subject closer to me than family.”
His name was Hong Jin.
He had been at the prince’s side from his earliest memories until this very moment.
“And I had an elder brother and loyal subjects who endured countless humiliations for this country.”
The Emperor closed his eyes with a low groan.
The loyal old general and the Embroidered Uniform Guards, who had been forced to seize the throne to confront a greater injustice, clenched their teeth, trying to suppress their agitation.
“When I could not see even a glimmer of light, there were people who reached out to me without asking for anything in return.”
The martial artists of Murim.
People who had stepped outside the Great Nation’s laws and built a world apart.
Yet they had willingly torn down that boundary and rushed into a place where danger waited on every side.
Prince Shangshan’s gaze passed from one to the next.
One awkwardly scratched his bald head.
Another gave him a gentle nod.
One was rubbing his stomach as if he were hungry.
And at the end of his gaze stood a young man.
He was neither the strongest nor the wisest among them.
Even so, he stood at the center of them all as naturally as if he belonged there.
He had planted a dream in someone’s heart and promised to be his friend.
Now he smiled at the boy who had grown so much.
His smile was so bright and warm that, for an instant, even the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord thought the world before his eyes had grown brighter.
*Chivalry.*
He had forgotten that single word for so long it felt strange to him.
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord turned it over in his empty heart.
Then he saw himself reflected in the young prince’s tear-filled eyes: warped and blurred, like a monster.
“The man I saw in you was not only a sinner of the ages, burdened with unforgivable karma.
You were also an unfortunate person who had no choice but to walk a different path from mine.”
Unfortunate, he had chosen revenge instead of forgiveness.
Inhuman, he had become a monster.
He had thought revenge was the only path.
It was the reason he had lived on, first as a human being and then as a monster.
But he had been wrong.
About his purpose.
About his reason.
“Now... you can stop.”
The quiet words reached him, and the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord went rigid.
*You can stop now.*
*It’s all right to stop.*
Those simple words melted a heart that had spent so many years burning to ash and freezing over, again and again.
At last, they brought him peace.
*So that was it.*
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord looked silently up at the sky.
He had resented it without end.
The sky.
The whole world.
But when the last veil of anger fell away from his heart, he saw a new world.
Countless stars shone in the sky that had seemed filled with nothing but darkness.
A breeze from somewhere carried the scent of grass.
It mingled with the thick stench of blood rising from the hellscape he had made.
*Too late.
I realized far too late.*
Thousands upon thousands of people had already been killed or wounded.
And how many more would be sacrificed because of his choices?
He couldn’t even begin to guess.
Nor could he measure the weight of the crime he would bear for the countless lives swallowed up in the great war he had set in motion.
Yet here, at the end, a new fork in the road lay before him.
It whispered insistently that he should make the better choice, even if only by a little.
As if that choice could make his whole black-stained life pale beside it.
*—Listen carefully to what I’m about to say.*
*Whoosh.*
The Sound Transmission slipped between his moving lips and mingled with the wind.
It passed the young prince and the Emperor, crossed the ring of Embroidered Uniform Guards and the assembled civil and military officials, and reached one man.
Jin Taekyung.
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord smiled bitterly at the sight of Jin staring down at him, eyes wide.
It was far too late.
But at the very end, he had made a slightly better choice.
That was all.
*—I’ve told you my story.
Now it’s time to collect my fortune-telling fee.*
Jin Taekyung watched the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord in silence, his gaze sunk deep.
Then he nodded and stepped forward.
*Splash.*
Ripples spread across a pool of thick, sticky blood.
Everyone watching knew what Jin Taekyung was about to do.
Not one of the civil or military officials tried to stop him.
They did not dare.
The Emperor and Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao had stepped aside themselves to clear his path.
At this moment, Jin Taekyung was the Emperor’s appointed proxy, granted the authority to execute this great traitor on the Son of Heaven’s behalf.
*Shing.*
A cool breeze brushed the spearhead he held in a reverse grip.
As the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord watched blue-white flames gather slowly at its tip, he spoke.
“Do you think someone like me will have a next life?”
“Probably.
You’ll have to spend about three thousand jiazi as a cockroach or a mosquito first, though.”
*I see.
I suppose so.*
At Jin Taekyung’s matter-of-fact answer, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord let out a dry laugh.
Jin Taekyung continued in an even voice.
“But in your next life, make sure you’re born human again.”
“What do you mean...?”
“You never know.
Maybe someone will help you then, unlike in this life.”
“If we get the chance, let’s meet again.
Just don’t be too late.”
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord—no, Wei Zhong—fell silent.
Then he smiled faintly.
Without another word, he watched the dazzling flames fill his vision.
*Whoosh.*
Their warmth, strange as it was, wrapped around his entire body.

chapters.title: Chapter 925
paragraphs: Flames surged upward.
They burned with a fierce, terrible heat—and yet, somehow, they felt strangely warm.
*Fwoosh.*
The blue-white flames that had pierced his body along with the spearhead burned everything, melted everything, and, at the same time, embraced it all.
A man’s unhappy life.
A monster who had realized his mistake only at the very end.
*Goodbye, Wei Zhong.*
I murmured the name I’d seen on the pledge the day before.
And at that moment, the chains of immortality shattered—the imperfect blessing and curse that had bound him.
*Ding. Ding. Ding.*
As I listened to the clear chimes announcing the arrival of eternal rest, I drew back the Scorching Yang Qi I’d been pouring through White Flame’s spearhead.
Less than a handful of ash remained on the blackened ground.
*Whoosh.*
Was it a chance gust of wind, or a kindness from someone above who had watched it all?
I watched the ash drift far, far away.
Then a man’s voice broke the brief silence.
“He was a traitor who tried to bring down the imperial family for his own ends, and a criminal who colluded with foreign enemies to plunge the Great Nation into ruin.”
Without taking my eyes off the ash, I asked, “Do you think that was too peaceful an end for a man like that?”
“I do.”
“I think so, too.”

No matter how much he’d reflected and repented, the crimes he’d committed would not disappear. Everything he had done as the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, not Wei Zhong, was a burden he would have to carry even in Hell.
“Then why did you do it?”
“Why didn’t you stop me, Your Majesty?”
The Emperor answered.
“Because I didn’t want to.”
A short answer, but it said everything. I let out a dry laugh.
“I see.”
“Now it’s your turn to answer.”
I paused and bit my lip.
“...Some people came to mind, that’s all.”
“People like Wei Zhong, then. Sinners who committed wrongs they could never wash away.”
“Yes. And like him, they regretted the choices they’d made.”
The Head Elder of the Jin Family of Taiyuan had been one of them. So had Baeksang of the Nanman Beast Palace.
They’d followed the guiding light of Dark Heaven down the wrong path and could never retrace their steps.
Sometimes they looked back and regretted the road they’d taken. But they’d gone too far to turn around.
Even as I poured my anger out on them, I couldn’t help feeling sorry for them.
*They could have made a better choice.*
*If they had, innocent people wouldn’t have had to die.*
*But it was always too late.*
That wasn’t self-reproach or regret. What was done was done.
I could condemn the consequences of their choices. But I couldn’t presume to condemn the choices themselves.
Revenge is easy. Forgiveness is hard.
That’s what people are like.
“I will erect memorials.”
The Emperor spoke again into the silence.
“One for those who fell here today. Another for the people sacrificed in the vicious struggles among the heroes of the realm. And the last...”
He paused, turning his gaze west, toward the place where the wind had gone.
“The Maoshan Sect. Yes, the Maoshan Sect would be fitting.”
*Gasp.*
The officials around us sucked in their breath.
Erecting a memorial at the Maoshan Sect would tarnish the reputation of Taizu, the founder of the Great Nation, and the imperial family itself.
But before any of them could speak up, an even greater shock swept over them.
No—it struck them.
“And all of this shall be done in the name of the Crown Prince, not Mine.”
The air seemed to tremble. Everyone’s eyes flew wide.
The Crown Prince.
The new ruler who would one day inherit this vast continent.
I’d completely forgotten why this gathering had been arranged. What awaited us at the end of this blood-soaked banquet.
The seat of Crown Prince had stood vacant for more than a decade. Now, at this very moment, it was about to welcome its new occupant.
“Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao, receive the imperial command!”
The Emperor no longer looked exhausted.
His voice, filled with the majesty only the sovereign of a nation could possess, pierced the air. Riding the wind, it enveloped the entire grand banquet hall.
*Clang! Clang! Clang!*
Beginning with Baek Yeon, Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, thousands of guards drew their swords and pointed them at the sky.
Their golden armor flashed, as did their blood-soaked blades.
That brilliant tide of steel shone for one boy alone.
For the young prince who had chosen forgiveness over revenge even before his enemy. For the boy who dreamed of an age of peace no ruler in the past thousand years had achieved.
“Ah. Ah...”
The Emperor calmly addressed his younger brother, who stood at a loss before this sudden turn of events.
“Do you intend to defy the imperial command?”
“Y-Your Majesty.”
“Come closer.”
“But, but Your Majesty already...”
No one failed to understand what Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao meant to say, or where he was looking.
A woman stood surrounded by palace attendants, clutching her swollen belly.
I knew her name. She had gone from the favored concubine of the City Lord of Sichuan Province to a consort of the Emperor.
*Aehyang.*
She watched us through clenched teeth, anger plain in her eyes.
But the Emperor’s expression held not a trace of emotion as he looked at her.
It was as though she were a tool he had kept at his side because he needed it.
*Wait. Could it be?*
The thought had barely crossed my mind when the Emperor spoke.
“That child, when it comes into this world, will bear the blood of the late City Lord of Sichuan Province.”
“Therefore, neither that woman nor the child in her womb has anything to do with Me. No one is to raise questions about this.”
The court officials looked stunned by his declaration. But a few of us, myself included, were certain of one thing.
The Emperor hadn’t spoken a single lie.
*I suspected it, but it’s actually true.*
The Emperor had an Empress and consorts, yet had produced no heir in more than ten years.
Looking back, though, it wasn’t that he couldn’t have an heir. He had chosen not to.
For the sake of his one and only younger brother, Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao.
*He must have wanted to protect him from every threat. The throne—and his younger brother.*
The sole direct heir of the orthodox imperial lineage.
And, at the same time, a perfect puppet for Dark Heaven—a figure who gave them every justification they needed to overthrow the Emperor.

On the surface, it had seemed that the Emperor couldn’t bear to kill his little brother and had sent him into exile instead. But Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao had survived this long because of the Emperor’s plan.
“Do you still not understand?”
He had given up having an heir for his brother’s sake. For that same brother, he had had to become a coldhearted older brother. He went on slowly.
“I kept that seat empty for you from the beginning. Only you could take it.”
Though he had ascended the most exalted throne under Heaven, he had been branded a traitor and an unfilial son.
Though he tended to affairs of state day and night, that brand had made people call him a tyrant.
“I wanted you to survive. I didn’t want you to become My one weakness.”
Perhaps, when the child who had not yet been weaned was sent away from the imperial palace, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord hadn’t been the only one watching him go from afar.
“I had to send you away to protect you. And to root out the traitors I couldn’t eradicate before, I had to bring you back into this deadly place.”
More than a decade was no short stretch of time.
It had been long enough for the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord to shore up his weakened foundations. Long enough for the Emperor to prepare the decisive battle that would end everything.
And the Emperor had secretly brought his only younger brother back with the help of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, then protected him by keeping him confined.
He had even made an invincible master known as the Bow Saint serve as a mere bodyguard.
“Bao’er.”
The voice that passed between the Emperor’s dry lips was astonishingly warm.
Warm enough to make even Baek Yeon, who had stood beside him longer than anyone as comrade and subject, widen his eyes.
Warm enough to make the body and heart of a boy who had longed for his family for so long suddenly go rigid.
“It’s time.”
At those quiet words, the boy’s clear, river-bright eyes trembled.
But there was no hesitation in them. Only resolve, and the will of someone moving toward his dream.
“I, Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao...”
*Swish.*
The long hem of his robe brushed a pool of blood. Yet even on a battlefield stained red in every direction, the young prince’s light had not dimmed in the slightest.
“...humbly accept the command of His Majesty the Emperor.”
A smile unlike any anyone had ever seen spread across the Emperor’s wrinkled lips.
“Granted.”
“Waaaaah!”
Amid the earth-shaking roar, the two who had finally found each other after such a long, wandering road embraced.
Not as ruler and subject, but as brothers.
When the Emperor and the Great Nation’s new Crown Prince embraced, those watching trembled, unable to contain the emotion rising within them.
How desperately they had wished, for more than a decade, that it had all been a lie.
That the natural order, twisted and blackened like a monster, would one day be set right.
And yet.
And yet, it had.
What they had yearned for in silence was unfolding before their eyes.
They had witnessed the end of one era and the beginning of another. Emotions they could not name surged through them, then spilled out in a tremendous roar.
“Long live His Majesty the Emperor!”
“May His Highness the Crown Prince live a thousand years!”
“Please, please put this servant to death!”
Cheers and cries rang out on every side.
Some who had known the truth laughed and wept like children. Others, deceived by lies into condemning the Emperor, staggered with guilt and regret.
But some belonged to neither group.
“Long live! Long live! Long, long live!”
Dry lips called endlessly for the Emperor’s long life. Tears drenched wrinkled cheeks.
Yet the shrewd gray eyes taking in the scene remained dark and still.
*I never thought things would go this wrong.*
The old man swallowed the words he must never let escape his lips and considered the chance that remained to him.
*But it isn’t over yet.*

He had known the truth from the beginning and joined hands with the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord solely for wealth and glory. He had no intention of being exposed as a traitor and seeing his entire clan slaughtered.
*The pledge. I only need to get rid of the few people who know about the pledge and who I really am.*
The saying “Succeed and you’re a king; fail and you’re a traitor” was wrong.
Even if you actually plotted treason, it wasn’t a crime as long as you weren’t caught.
The old man had once tutored the former Crown Prince. Revered by Confucian scholars throughout the realm, he had risen to the rank of Grand Academician. And in matters like this, he was meticulous.
*I’ll survive. Just as I always have.*
Repeating that resolve to himself, the old man cried out “Long live!” amid the confusion of the crowd, inching backward.
He needed to reach the subordinates waiting outside the imperial palace as quickly as possible.

If he eliminated the handful of key figures who knew his identity and took possession of the pledge, he could keep his current position. And even if things became difficult, he could take his family’s wealth and flee.
Or so he believed.
Until someone’s voice, strangely clear amid the deafening roar, pierced his ears.
“Where are you off to in such a hurry? A time like this calls for sharing the joy.”
The old man went rigid.
He slowly turned his head and saw a young man approaching at an unhurried pace.
“Jin... Taekyung.”
“Come on. Just ‘Jin Taekyung’? That’s cold.”
Jin Taekyung gave him a small smile and added, “You should call me Comrade Jin Taekyung.”
“What, what are you...”
“You didn’t know? I signed the pledge, too.”
“Oh. Have I got the wrong person?”
Jin Taekyung tilted his head. At that moment, a cold voice sounded behind the old man.
“It’s been a while, Grand Academician.”
*Thwack!*
A blow struck the back of his neck. As his vision went black, one name came to mind.
*Hong Jin.*
It was over. All of it.

But a few of us, myself included, were certain of one thing.
The Emperor hadn’t spoken a single lie.
*I suspected it, but it’s actually true.*
The Emperor had an Empress and consorts, yet had produced no heir in more than ten years.
Looking back, though, it wasn’t that he couldn’t have an heir.
He had chosen not to.
For the sake of his one and only younger brother, Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao.
*He must have wanted to protect him from every threat.
The throne—and his younger brother.*
The sole direct heir of the orthodox imperial lineage.
And, at the same time, a perfect puppet for Dark Heaven—a figure who gave them every justification they needed to overthrow the Emperor.
On the surface, it had seemed that the Emperor couldn’t bear to kill his little brother and had sent him into exile instead.
But Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao had survived this long because of the Emperor’s plan.
“Do you still not understand?”
He had given up having an heir for his brother’s sake.
For that same brother, he had had to become a coldhearted older brother.
He went on slowly.
“I kept that seat empty for you from the beginning.
Only you could take it.”
Though he had ascended the most exalted throne under Heaven, he had been branded a traitor and an unfilial son.
Though he tended to affairs of state day and night, that brand had made people call him a tyrant.
“I wanted you to survive.
I didn’t want you to become My one weakness.”
Perhaps, when the child who had not yet been weaned was sent away from the imperial palace, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord hadn’t been the only one watching him go from afar.
“I had to send you away to protect you.
And to root out the traitors I couldn’t eradicate before, I had to bring you back into this deadly place.”
More than a decade was no short stretch of time.
It had been long enough for the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord to shore up his weakened foundations.
Long enough for the Emperor to prepare the decisive battle that would end everything.
And the Emperor had secretly brought his only younger brother back with the help of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, then protected him by keeping him confined.
He had even made an invincible master known as the Bow Saint serve as a mere bodyguard.
“Bao’er.”
The voice that passed between the Emperor’s dry lips was astonishingly warm.
Warm enough to make even Baek Yeon, who had stood beside him longer than anyone as comrade and subject, widen his eyes.
Warm enough to make the body and heart of a boy who had longed for his family for so long suddenly go rigid.
“It’s time.”
At those quiet words, the boy’s clear, river-bright eyes trembled.
But there was no hesitation in them.
Only resolve, and the will of someone moving toward his dream.
“I, Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao...”
*Swish.*
The long hem of his robe brushed a pool of blood.
Yet even on a battlefield stained red in every direction, the young prince’s light had not dimmed in the slightest.
“...humbly accept the command of His Majesty the Emperor.”
A smile unlike any anyone had ever seen spread across the Emperor’s wrinkled lips.
“Granted.”
“Waaaaah!”
Amid the earth-shaking roar, the two who had finally found each other after such a long, wandering road embraced.
Not as ruler and subject, but as brothers.
When the Emperor and the Great Nation’s new Crown Prince embraced, those watching trembled, unable to contain the emotion rising within them.
How desperately they had wished, for more than a decade, that it had all been a lie.
That the natural order, twisted and blackened like a monster, would one day be set right.
And yet.
And yet, it had.
What they had yearned for in silence was unfolding before their eyes.
They had witnessed the end of one era and the beginning of another.
Emotions they could not name surged through them, then spilled out in a tremendous roar.
“Long live His Majesty the Emperor!”
“May His Highness the Crown Prince live a thousand years!”
“Please, please put this servant to death!”
Cheers and cries rang out on every side.
Some who had known the truth laughed and wept like children.
Others, deceived by lies into condemning the Emperor, staggered with guilt and regret.
But some belonged to neither group.
“Long live!
Long live!
Long, long live!”
Dry lips called endlessly for the Emperor’s long life.
Tears drenched wrinkled cheeks.
Yet the shrewd gray eyes taking in the scene remained dark and still.
*I never thought things would go this wrong.*
The old man swallowed the words he must never let escape his lips and considered the chance that remained to him.
*But it isn’t over yet.*
He had known the truth from the beginning and joined hands with the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord solely for wealth and glory.
He had no intention of being exposed as a traitor and seeing his entire clan slaughtered.
*The pledge.
I only need to get rid of the few people who know about the pledge and who I really am.*
The saying “Succeed and you’re a king; fail and you’re a traitor” was wrong.
Even if you actually plotted treason, it wasn’t a crime as long as you weren’t caught.
The old man had once tutored the former Crown Prince.
Revered by Confucian scholars throughout the realm, he had risen to the rank of Grand Academician.
And in matters like this, he was meticulous.
*I’ll survive.
Just as I always have.*
Repeating that resolve to himself, the old man cried out “Long live!” amid the confusion of the crowd, inching backward.
He needed to reach the subordinates waiting outside the imperial palace as quickly as possible.
If he eliminated the handful of key figures who knew his identity and took possession of the pledge, he could keep his current position.
And even if things became difficult, he could take his family’s wealth and flee.
Or so he believed.
Until someone’s voice, strangely clear amid the deafening roar, pierced his ears.
“Where are you off to in such a hurry?
A time like this calls for sharing the joy.”
The old man went rigid.
He slowly turned his head and saw a young man approaching at an unhurried pace.
“Jin...
Taekyung.”
“Come on.
Just ‘Jin Taekyung’?
That’s cold.”
Jin Taekyung gave him a small smile and added, “You should call me Comrade Jin Taekyung.”
“What, what are you...”
“You didn’t know?
I signed the pledge, too.”
“Oh.
Have I got the wrong person?”
Jin Taekyung tilted his head.
At that moment, a cold voice sounded behind the old man.
“It’s been a while, Grand Academician.”
*Thwack!*
A blow struck the back of his neck.
As his vision went black, one name came to mind.
*Hong Jin.*
It was over.
All of it.

chapters.title: Chapter 926
paragraphs: Everyone makes the wrong choice sometimes.
At least a few times in life.
No—count the little choices we make every day, and the number might run into the thousands.
But a wrong choice doesn’t mean your life is over.
You can regret it, learn from it, and choose a better path next time.
Of course, that only works if you get a *next time*.
“I—I’ve done nothing wrong! This is a misunderstanding!”
“Your Majesty! Your Majesty!”
“You scoundrels! How dare you lay hands on me!”
Fear. Desperation. Anger.
Dozens of people shouted, each caught up in their own emotions.

Their silk robes had lost none of their sheen, and their plump bodies spoke to just how high their station had been—even in a place death had just torn through. But all the wealth and glory they had enjoyed until now were over, effective this very moment.
Such was the fate of those guilty of high treason.
“Arrest every last one of them!”
“Loyalty!”
*Swish, swish!*
No sooner had Baek Yeon given the order than the Embroidered Uniform Guards surrounding the area swung their binding ropes and scabbards into action.
One civil official, already resigned to his fate, let himself be bound without a word. An old general in dazzling armor resisted, showing off a fair amount of skill in martial arts.
Then he got his skull cracked.
*Whack!*
“You bastards, how dare you—Guh!”
“Let’s not wear ourselves out already. Come quietly. You’ll have plenty of chances to scream later.”
“W-what are you going to do with me?”
“You already know, don’t you, old Assistant Military Commissioner?”
At the Embroidered Uniform Guard’s cold smile, the old general sank to the ground, his face blank.
He had realized that the warm blood running from the crown of his head was nothing compared to what he would be made to shed later.
And one man was weaving his way through the chaos.
“It’s been a while. Last time we met, I think you called me a ball-less eunuch bastard.”
One man.
“You haven’t forgotten me, have you? Oh, we’ve never met? Cut the crap. I remember everything.”
Two men.
“Oh, look who it is. You’ve gotten so fat I almost didn’t recognize you. Don’t worry. I’ll slim you down this time.”
Every line out of his mouth sounded like a death threat.
Each time Hong Jin greeted someone as warmly as a man at his first school reunion in ten years, gold-armored diet supplements marched over and dragged that person away.
Their faces were flushed at the tantalizing prospect of a fresh batch of prisoners to fill the Embroidered Uniform Guard’s jails, which had stood empty for some time.
“W-wait! Torturer Hong!”

“I’m not a torturer anymore. It’s been ages since I was appointed Deputy Military Commissioner of Shanxi Province. Stop making a racket calling for me and go on ahead. Oh, and give your balls a good wash.”

The man who had once committed defamation by stating a fact—calling Hong Jin a ball-less eunuch—was dragged away. Watching him go, the second man—the one who had claimed they had never met—swallowed hard.
“Um, Comrade Hong. I think there’s been some misunderstanding...”
“Who’s your comrade?”
“Pardon?”
“Do you know me? And what misunderstanding? Drag this traitorous bastard to the jail and throw him in.”
Watching everything unfold at lightning speed right before my eyes, I murmured to myself.
*There’s going to be a bloodbath.*
I couldn’t even guess how many would die. Hundreds? Thousands?
Or tens of thousands, like last time?
And once the traitors who weren’t here today and their families were counted, the purge would be massive.
“Do you pity them?”
At the Emperor’s sudden question, I gave a small shake of my head.
“Those bastards committed crimes worthy of death. Of course they should pay for it. It’s just...”
“You’re worried that people with nothing to do with the treason will be sacrificed.”
“It cannot be helped. The law of the land must be upheld, especially where treason is concerned.”
“I know. I understand.”
Revenge begets revenge.
If someone survived the purge with a grudge and plotted for the future, they could become the seed of another disaster.
Just as the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had.
“But there may be exceptions.”
My eyes widened at the unexpected declaration.
“You mean...”
“Make every cause and connection crystal clear, and spare at least those who are innocent. That was what Bao’er asked of Me just now.”
The Emperor added with a faint smile, “It was also his first request of Me as Imperial Younger Brother and as My brother.”
“That boy will become a sage king who brings about an age of peace. He will care for his people more than anyone, and they will love him in return.”
Had this man always smiled so much?
The Emperor, whose face had always been cold and gloomy, looked much brighter now.
His eyes rested on Prince Shangshan—or rather, Zhu Bao, now the Imperial Younger Brother—as the boy met his gaze and awkwardly bowed his head. The warmth in the Emperor’s eyes was impossible to hide.
*Even the Emperor is still just an older brother, in the end.*
I gave a quiet snort and said, “That’s right. He’ll definitely be a sage king.”
“He is also highly skilled in martial arts. One day he will cross the Great Wall and conquer the vast grasslands, the lost lands of the Northern Sea, and the deserts as well.”
“Huh?”
“What is it?”
“Um. Nothing. It’s possible.”
I wanted to ask what martial arts had to do with any of that, but I held back.
Why was I starting to think of Jin Wikyung?
“Indeed. Entirely possible.”
“Of course.”
“And that is not all. He will build cities of gold and establish a great empire that will endure for a thousand years.”
“...A thousand years is a bit...”
“Do you think that’s impossible right now?”
No, even if I thought about it as hard as I could, that seemed a bit much.
But the Emperor’s eyes narrowed. I swallowed the words on the tip of my tongue and showed off my dazzling reflexes.
“I just thought you were aiming a little low. I was thinking ten thousand years.”
“Ten thousand years is impossible.”
“Perhaps it’s because you’re a Murim practitioner, but you do have a rather fanciful streak. You should try to develop a more realistic outlook.”
This son of a bitch.
I’d tried to play along, and he’d gone all serious on me. I was left speechless. Just then, a hand discreetly poked me in the side.
*Poke.*
I didn’t need to turn to know who it was.
I tamped down my anger at the Emperor and moved my lips.
—Don’t worry. Even if I am a Madman, do you really think I’d beat up the Emperor?
Jeok Cheongang replied through Sound Transmission.
—You’re certainly capable of it, but that’s not what I meant.
—If that’s not it, then... don’t tell me—
I turned, eyes wide, and Jeok Cheongang nodded gravely.
—You’re going to hit him yourself, Old Master?

—Good heavens, have you gone senile again? You can’t. If you lay a hand on the Emperor, it’s over for all of us. If he gets pissed off at us and cozies up to Dark Heaven, we won’t have a Great Nation anymore. We’ll have a Dark Heaven Nation. With Hell thrown in.

I was still desperately trying to talk him out of it, like a missionary at Yeongdeungpo Station shouting that believers go to Heaven and unbelievers go to Hell, when Jeok Cheongang gave me a withering look and jerked his chin over my shoulder.
—Before I pluck those dog eyes out, look who’s waiting behind you.
I turned. In the distance stood someone watching us with calm, still eyes.
*The Bow Saint.*
The instant our gazes met, the relief and joy that had surrounded me seemed to wash away.
An inexplicable chill seeped deep into my lungs.
—So it was you.
The question I had yet to answer—and that voice—lingered faintly in my ears like a breeze at dawn.
—The chosen one the Martial God spoke of.
What had she meant? What truth lay behind those words?
My gaze wavered despite myself.
The Bow Saint gave me a slight nod, then quietly turned and began walking.
Toward somewhere out of sight of the crowd.
Toward a secluded place where she could reveal the secret she had kept until now.
I followed the Bow Saint without a word.
As if to prove that the battle in the grand banquet hall had not been the whole of it, bodies and blood that no one had yet cleared away lay throughout the once-clean, spacious imperial palace.
Still, no one stopped me and the Bow Saint as we crossed the palace at an unhurried pace.
If anything, people hesitated, then bowed and stepped aside.
They recognized us.
They knew who we were, and which side we had fought on—the Emperor’s or the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s.
But unlike them, I still didn’t know.
I didn’t know what the Bow Saint’s cryptic words meant, or much of anything about the figure shrouded almost entirely in mystery.
*The Martial God.*
A peerless hero born of the Great Faction War, who had appeared out of nowhere one day and vanished just as suddenly.
No—he had become the very sky looking down upon all of Murim.
People said there had never been anyone like the Martial God, and there never would be again.
There were mighty figures known as the Three Saints and the Ten Kings, but the Martial God stood in a realm none of them could reach.
That was why they called him the sky. A god.
But...the Martial God was gone now.
The symbol and center of Murim had vanished like a phantom just after disbanding the Murim Alliance.
As though he had never existed.
As though he’d been waiting for this to happen from the beginning.
As the years passed after his sudden disappearance, rumors sprang up like weeds.

Some said he had died after failing to recover from the internal injury he sustained in his final life-and-death duel with the Heavenly Demon. Others said he was spending the rest of his life in some remote mountain valley.
And that wasn’t all.
Some claimed that, having attained enlightenment, he had finally become an immortal.
There were plenty of wilder rumors, too: that the Martial God had always been something like a divine beast protecting the Central Plains, and would never appear in human form again.
With so many mysteries surrounding him, the Martial God had always been a fascinating subject.
The tales of his deeds sounded like myths and legends.
Even to those who had seen him up close. And to me.
And yet...
*For that Martial God to come up so suddenly.*
I hadn’t seen so much as the Martial God’s little finger, but the mere mention of his title made every hair on my body stand on end.
Now that we had reached our destination and stopped, the feeling was stronger than ever.
*Rustle.*
The deep night was giving way to dawn.
Even the sound of wet grass brushing against us had a chill to it. The Bow Saint slowly looked around, then spoke without turning.
“You’ve been here before, haven’t you?”
She looked like a young woman barely into her thirties, but the Bow Saint was an old master who had lived through ages beyond my imagining.
I answered with the respect she was due.
“Yes.”
“I remember you charging at me as though you meant to kill me. It left quite an impression.”
The Bow Saint reached out and lightly tapped a flower bud that had yet to bloom.
Countless rare and beautiful plants filled this place. It was the same abandoned space where she and I had met a few days ago.
“Whenever I felt troubled, I would come here for a walk. People treated it as forbidden ground, so there wasn’t so much as an ant around.”
“Then that day, too...”
“That’s right. Something was troubling me. No matter how much I thought about it, I couldn’t reach a conclusion, so I came here to walk and think.”
The Bow Saint turned. Her eyes curved like crescents, but the gaze within them was grave and still.
“You were the chosen one the Martial God spoke of, someone who was supposed to possess the supernatural powers to escape even death...so why are you in an irrecoverable state?”

chapters.title: Chapter 927
paragraphs: An inexplicable shiver ran down my spine.
A supernatural power that could even evade death.
I knew better than anyone what it was. There was no other way to describe it than as something uncanny, like the work of ghosts.
*The System.*
A stroke of luck that had come into my life when it was sinking like a boat with a hole in its hull.
A power that had brought me both my greatest crisis and my greatest opportunity.
Yet in this world called Murim, only one person besides me knew the System existed.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
No one else could know the true nature of the power I possessed.
Not the Bow Saint, and not even the handful of people who had stayed closest to me.
*They might have some vague sense that there’s something there, but that’s as far as it goes.*
I’d crossed the line between life and death more times than I could count.
I’d survived situations that would have killed an ordinary person several times over, and I’d grown at a pace without precedent in Murim’s history.
Even so, no one knew exactly what my power was.
No—not unless I told them the truth myself.
That was the kind of power the System was.
An ability beyond anything a human could imagine, one that even the four characters meaning *supernatural powers* couldn’t fully capture.
*Even the Bow Saint is no exception.*

The shock I’d felt a moment ago had already settled. But one question remained, and I couldn’t answer it on my own: how had *they* learned there was something special about me when only a handful of people knew?
*The Bow Saint. And...*
The Martial God.
The shadows of two giants who had vanished from the world long ago fell over me now.
Not like shade that offered relief from the heat, but like darkness.
It made my skin crawl.
I licked my dry lips. My mouth felt as rough as if I’d chewed and swallowed a fistful of sand.
*What on earth do they know? How much?*
Just as I sent the unspoken question drifting through my mind, the Bow Saint—who had been watching me in silence with deeply shadowed eyes—suddenly spoke.
“You’re calmer than I expected. I thought you’d ramble on with excuses. Or pretend you didn’t know.”
I forced myself to answer evenly. “Would that change anything?”
“No. Nothing at all. You know that, too, don’t you?”
That answer made one thing certain.
The woman before me—the Bow Saint—had been watching me all along.
And she knew more than I’d imagined.
*Then could it be...? No. That can’t be.*
I pushed away the question that had flashed through my mind and asked sharply, “Since when?”
“That short question seems to hold several meanings. Let’s see... I’m not sure how to answer it. Why don’t I start with what happened today?”
The Bow Saint gently brushed the flowers lining either side of the path as she continued.
“Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung. When I saw you rise even though you should have died, I finally knew who the chosen one the Martial God spoke of was.”
“How could that man—no, how could he...”
“How does he know about you?”
I nodded, keeping my agitation in check.
Every nerve in my body felt drawn taut.
Depending on her answer, everything could change. What happened next could take a turn even I couldn’t predict.
Then the Bow Saint gave a short reply that stopped my thoughts cold.
“How would I know?”
“What does that—”
“Neither I nor he could have known. Of course not. I found the letter before you were even born.”
“...A letter? Before I was born?”
“Yes. I first found it after many years had passed since the Great Faction War ended—long enough for the mountains and rivers to change more than once.”
Her calm voice mingled with the dawn air and drifted to my ears.
“At first, I thought it was simply a trace left by some unknown person from long ago. But I was wrong. The Martial God had left that letter for me.”
“Then what exactly did it say?”
“An arrangement he had made. No—perhaps a kind of prophecy.”
“And there was one term that appeared throughout it.”
My chest felt tight, as though a great stone had settled inside it. I forced the words out.
“The chosen one.”
“That’s right. And ‘the chosen one’ didn’t necessarily refer to any one particular person.”
*Step. Step.*
Her careful footsteps carried her past the blades of grass. Faint moonlight fell over her as she walked through the garden.
“I couldn’t believe it, but I had no choice.”
Because he was the Martial God.
Awe she couldn’t conceal filled those words. Her voice as faint as the moonlight, the Bow Saint continued at the pace of her steps.

“So, after several decades, I went out into the world and traveled the land. I spent most of my time in the Central Plains, but once I went as far as the endless desert in the west. Another time, I crossed the grasslands and reached the Northern Sea, where moss and ice covered everything.”
Searching for the “chosen one” mentioned in the Martial God’s letter was like searching a field of sand for one special grain. The Bow Saint had to shoulder the entire burden alone.
“I couldn’t ask anyone for help. The letter said not a single detail about the mission could be revealed until I’d succeeded.”
But the Bow Saint hadn’t given up.
The Martial God’s arrangement, almost a prophecy, required someone called the chosen one.
“When the whole world is covered in darkness, that person will become a lamp and light the way. The only one who will open a new sky and bring the morning.”
The Bow Saint murmured the words, then turned her face toward the sky.
“But no matter how long I searched for someone whose age, face, name, and even gender I didn’t know, the chosen one never appeared.”
Of course not.
Finding one person in this vast land—someone who might not even have been born yet—was nearly impossible.
“But not entirely. If what he wrote in the letter was true, the chosen one would stand out with astonishing speed.”
A needle in a bag.
Sooner or later, the needle was bound to poke through. No matter where it was, or how deeply it was buried in a crowd.
“I followed rumors and sought out people I thought might be the chosen one. But even at Heaven’s Gate Temple, where the brightest talents in the land gather, I found no reason to be certain.”
Heaven’s Gate Temple was where Jin Mukyung, my second older brother and the Second Young Master of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, had spent some time.
It was a cradle of talent, crowded with the heirs of prominent sects and gifted people of every kind.
But even its cadets, remarkable as each of them was, fell far short of what the Bow Saint expected of the chosen one.
“They were all outstanding, but that was all. Every one of them had a clear limit. As did I.”
I’d listened in silence until then. At last, I understood why she, like the other Three Saints, had disappeared from public view—though her disappearance had been overshadowed by the Martial God’s.
And why she had been staying in the Imperial Palace.
“You used the imperial information network.”
“‘Cooperating with’ would be more accurate than ‘using.’ That was before the current Emperor, then the Fourth Prince, staged his coup.”
“Then does the Emperor know...?”
“No. He suspects something, vaguely, but he knows nothing. That was one of my conditions. What matters is that after he took the throne, I gained access to information from every corner of the land.”
The Bow Saint was a weight on the scales, powerful enough to tip the balance in an instant.

Disguised as a palace attendant, she stayed by the Emperor’s side and learned what was happening across the land, from the smallest incident to the largest. The presence of an unidentified Supreme Peak master also restrained the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s movements.
“In many ways, it was the right choice. Staying in the Imperial Palace let me learn things I’d never seen or heard before.”
One was Dark Heaven, which had sunk its roots deep into the imperial court. The other was...
“Someone who was growing beyond my sight.”
The Bow Saint looked away from the sky and toward me. Our eyes met, and I quietly swallowed.
“The Jin Family of Taiyuan. Jin Taekyung. At first, the names were unfamiliar, and I had no interest in them. Not until the second piece of news came from Shanxi.”
“What second report?”
“The unbelievable story that the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, had taken on a Disciple.”
The Bow Saint smiled faintly.
“Of course, the reports that came in quite some time after that were far more surprising.”
A year after the Jin Family of Taiyuan took control of Shanxi Province, I finished my secluded training on Mount Jiuhua and descended the mountain.
I was nothing like the person I’d been before.
In my martial prowess. In my state of mind.
And there were major events waiting for me, too.
“Each time I heard news of you, I grew more interested. No—it was more than interest.”
The chosen one.
The lamp that would light the night. The one who would open a new sky and bring the morning.
The unknown person the Bow Saint had searched for so long was slowly emerging from behind the curtain.
“That was why I had to see for myself. I needed to know which of the two people I was weighing in my mind was the chosen one.”
Two people.
The word cut through my ears with unusual clarity. A name flashed through my mind like lightning.
“...Cheongpung.”
At the name that escaped me, the Bow Saint gave a small nod.

“Yes. Cheongpung, the Huashan Divine Dragon. He had every chance of being the chosen one, too. If I hadn’t seen you in the grand banquet hall, I would have believed the Sword Saint’s Disciple was the one.”
But from her point of view, there had been no need to bring both of us here.
She was already fairly certain one of us was the chosen one.
And I had enough ties to draw me into what had happened.

“I already knew of your connection with Prince Shangshan—no, the Imperial Younger Brother. When Dark Heaven reached out to Hong Jin first, pretending to be on our side, I thought it might work in our favor. But I needed something more definite.”
Then I remembered.
Ma Sanbao had been the one who first contacted Hong Jin.
And saving Zhu Bao wasn’t the only reason I’d thrown myself into the death trap of the Imperial Palace.
“Blood Soul Gu...”
Was this what it felt like to be struck in the back of the head with a sledgehammer?
I spoke through a groan.
“Were you the one who planted the Blood Soul Gu in the City Lord of Sichuan Province?”
The Bow Saint’s bitter smile burned itself into my eyes.
