chapters.title: Chapter 928
paragraphs: Blood Soul Gu.
A cursed venomous creature created by the Five Poisons Sect, which had once drenched Nanman in blood.
When I realized what had driven the City Lord of Sichuan Province to his death, everyone—including me—had been certain it was Dark Heaven’s doing, and that it had deep ties to the Emperor.
But now I wasn’t so sure.
What was true, and what was false? How much of what I knew could I believe?
And was the woman standing before me, watching me with a bitter smile, really on our side?
And...
*If the Bow Saint was the one who planted the Blood Soul Gu, then what kind of being is the Martial God behind her—the one who foresaw my appearance?*
The Martial God was shrouded in mystery, and my questions about him seemed endless.
*Grind.*
I ground my teeth and glared at the Bow Saint.
“I asked you who planted the Blood Soul Gu in the City Lord of Sichuan Province.”
The Bow Saint watched me in silence, then abruptly spoke.
“What would you do if I said it was me?”
A jolt ran down my spine. I forced myself to keep my voice steady.
“You’d have to explain yourself. Well enough to convince all of us, including me.”
“And if it still doesn’t convince you?”
“Then...”
I swallowed. Almost by instinct, I lowered my stance a fraction, ready to strike at any moment.
There was no absolute good or evil in this world. But Dark Heaven—and the Lord of Heaven—came close enough to absolute evil.
If the Bow Saint had used the Blood Soul Gu, which was deeply connected to Dark Heaven, and it had close ties to Dark Heaven, there was only one thing I could do.
“I wouldn’t keep speaking to you this politely.”
At that moment, a fierce wind swirled around us.
*Whoosh.*
No. It wasn’t swirling. The winds were colliding.
The waves of qi pressing against each other were about to surge when the Bow Saint’s narrowed eyes curved like a full moon.
“Good. That’s how it should be.”
“What...?”
“You’ve exceeded my expectations. In every way.”
It didn’t take long to understand what her smile and those few words meant.
*A test.*
The thought flashed through my mind, and the tension gripping my whole body snapped loose.
*Damn it.*
The Bow Saint frowned in mock disapproval.
“Hm. Still wet behind the ears, and you talk to your elders like that?”
“If you were really an elder, you wouldn’t mess with someone who’s still wet behind the ears.”
“I’ve spent decades looking for you. What’s a little teasing after all that?”
The Bow Saint smiled faintly. As she looked at me, there was a hint of approval in her eyes.
“So you had nothing to do with the City Lord’s death or the Blood Soul Gu after all?”
“I had something to do with it.”
The Bow Saint tossed out the bombshell as if it were nothing. She stroked a flower and continued.
“I sent him back into danger, knowing full well he would die soon. I thought that if he died in Sichuan, someone close to you there would notice what had happened.”
“You knew he was going to die?”

“The City Lord of Sichuan Province was already infected with the Blood Soul Gu while he was staying in the Imperial Capital. Naturally, it was Dark Heaven’s doing—or, more precisely, the doing of the City Lord’s favorite concubine.”
“Wait. Aehyang?”
“Yes.”
My eyes widened. The Bow Saint went on in the same even tone.
“Don’t be surprised. If you need to control someone and that someone is a man, there’s no surer method than using a beautiful woman.”
“But how did you know she was working for Dark Heaven just from that?”

“I investigated her discreetly myself and found that she was highly skilled in Soul Bewitchment. I’d heard he was neglecting his duties because he was besotted with women. I was keeping an eye on him when I had him summoned to the Imperial Capital.”
A memory from not so long ago came back to me: the first time I’d met the City Lord, before the incident that came to be known as the Sichuan Blood Tragedy. He’d been half naked even then.
*So even back then...?*
A chill ran down my spine.
Not because I’d failed to notice that Aehyang, a Dark Heaven agent, was right beside him. Because I couldn’t begin to guess how far Dark Heaven’s shadow—its dark hand—had reached.
“Then does that mean...?”
“Yes.”
The Bow Saint nodded before I could finish.
“Dark Heaven has reached the roots of the Great Nation. It has worked its way into every corner, so thoroughly that we don’t know where its reach ends.”

“The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s death didn’t end this. There are likely still quite a few local officials with real power, great and small, working with Dark Heaven. Generals who command armies, too. And that would include some of the City Lords who govern the provinces.”
I swallowed.
A province might sound like a simple administrative division, but the land and population within one were enormous.
Why else had dozens of warlords proclaimed themselves kings and fought for supremacy in the chaotic age of the past? Just to claim legitimacy by calling themselves kings?
Half right, half wrong.
If you conquered a region and absorbed all the strength of its land, you could build enough power to claim the title of king of an entire nation.
These days, the City Lords were officials who answered to a powerful central government. But if they set their minds on rebellion, they could do tremendous damage to the Great Nation.
*He wasn’t exaggerating. He wasn’t lying.*
Before the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had accepted everything and let go, he’d poured out a curse in his rage.
*This is only the beginning. Even if you protected the Imperial Capital, the flames will sweep across the land.*
But they hadn’t been empty words spat out in anger. There was truth in them. A time bomb that might go off before long.
*Damn it.*
My head felt hot. My breath came ragged though I hadn’t moved, and my heart pounded.

I could almost see flames flickering before my eyes, ready to swallow both the modern world and Murim. And behind them stood the shadow of a giant who had swept aside the curtain and appeared when no one expected him.
“Then what do we do now? What do we do from here?”
I asked the Bow Saint, struggling to catch my breath.
No. The question was really for the person who had left a letter long ago and, through it, guided her to this moment.
The Martial God.
Born a man, yet called a god. He had saved the world once and left behind a plan to save it again.
I was asking him.
I wanted another prophecy from his letter to the Bow Saint. One ray of light to show me the way down this pitch-black road.
“What am I—fuck—what am I supposed to do?!”
I was practically shouting. The Bow Saint’s answer held no light at all.
“I don’t know. Neither does he.”
All the strength went out of me. My vision blurred, and my head sank.
I’d been sure there was something more. Something more to it.
I thought he would be different, if anyone could. He was the one who had been certain that a person like me would appear someday.
I’d even found myself thinking something impossible.
*What if the Martial God—the greatest of all time, with his dazzling achievements and divine authority—*
*Maybe...*
I clenched my teeth and was about to follow that unbelievable thought to its conclusion when a quiet voice reached my lowered head.
“But there is one thing.”
I slowly raised my head as if under a spell.
The Bow Saint was there, gazing at me with eyes sunk deep.
“He left a message for the chosen one.”
“What...what message?”
“Divine strength.”
Why did those two words make me freeze? An inexplicable chill crept down my spine.
The Bow Saint spoke calmly and quietly, but her voice rang in my ears like thunder.
“He said the chosen one must forge a path with the divine strength and Will only the chosen one can possess. Just as...”
Her voice trailed off. In that instant, the world slowed.
An invisible curtain seemed to fall over my eyes and ears. I could see only the Bow Saint—her lips moving slowly. I could hear only the words passing between them.
*Just as you yourself did.*
Time began to move again.
I didn’t. I stared at her, frozen as if I were trapped in ice.
*I...what did I just...*
What had I heard?
My mind felt as though it had emptied completely. A few words floated there, bright against the blankness.
*Just as you yourself did.*
Just as *you*, the Martial God, did.
That could mean only one thing.
The Martial God had been a chosen one like me.
No. More precisely...
*A System user.*
*Player.*
The word rushed in to fill my empty mind, swelling until it felt ready to burst. A clear chime rang out.
*Ding.*
And at that moment—
*Slip.*
I felt the sky and ground slowly turn over as I fell into pitch-black darkness.
Everything happened at once.

Jin Taekyung’s trembling form crumpled like a puppet with its strings cut. The Bow Saint’s hand shot out and seized his collar. And finally, the cold dawn air that had drifted through the abandoned garden suddenly grew hot.
*Grab. Fwoosh!*
The Bow Saint steadied Jin Taekyung, then spoke to the uninvited guest who had suddenly appeared.
“How strange. I don’t remember inviting you, too.”
The guest answered in a low voice.
“I do call him my Disciple. How could I leave him alone with some nasty old hag and not worry?”
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
His voice was calm, but flames flickered in his eyes.
“Fine. Let’s hear what kind of nonsense you’ve been up to.”
The Bow Saint gave a short laugh and shook her head.
“All these years, and you haven’t changed. Still charging in without thinking.”
“Do I have to say it twice?”
“You were hiding like a rat and listening. You already know. That was all I said. The boy was simply exhausted beyond his limits.”
She looked down at the unconscious Taekyung. Dried blood marked his face in several places, and the strain of his fierce struggle still showed there.
They were traces of how brilliantly—and nobly—he had fought.
“Take him with you. Let him get a little more rest.”

Jeok Cheongang didn’t hesitate for long. He carried Jin Taekyung on his back as if he’d been waiting for the chance, then used his movement technique to hurry away. The Bow Saint watched him until he was gone.
Then, suddenly, she saw a flower bud slowly opening in the light.
It was the first light of dawn.

sentences.text: Blood Soul Gu.
A cursed venomous creature created by the Five Poisons Sect, which had once drenched Nanman in blood.
When I realized what had driven the City Lord of Sichuan Province to his death, everyone—including me—had been certain it was Dark Heaven’s doing, and that it had deep ties to the Emperor.
But now I wasn’t so sure.
What was true, and what was false?
How much of what I knew could I believe?
And was the woman standing before me, watching me with a bitter smile, really on our side?
And...
*If the Bow Saint was the one who planted the Blood Soul Gu, then what kind of being is the Martial God behind her—the one who foresaw my appearance?*
The Martial God was shrouded in mystery, and my questions about him seemed endless.
*Grind.*
I ground my teeth and glared at the Bow Saint.
“I asked you who planted the Blood Soul Gu in the City Lord of Sichuan Province.”
The Bow Saint watched me in silence, then abruptly spoke.
“What would you do if I said it was me?”
A jolt ran down my spine.
I forced myself to keep my voice steady.
“You’d have to explain yourself.
Well enough to convince all of us, including me.”
“And if it still doesn’t convince you?”
“Then...”
I swallowed.
Almost by instinct, I lowered my stance a fraction, ready to strike at any moment.
There was no absolute good or evil in this world.
But Dark Heaven—and the Lord of Heaven—came close enough to absolute evil.
If the Bow Saint had used the Blood Soul Gu, which was deeply connected to Dark Heaven, and it had close ties to Dark Heaven, there was only one thing I could do.
“I wouldn’t keep speaking to you this politely.”
At that moment, a fierce wind swirled around us.
*Whoosh.*
No.
It wasn’t swirling.
The winds were colliding.
The waves of qi pressing against each other were about to surge when the Bow Saint’s narrowed eyes curved like a full moon.
“Good.
That’s how it should be.”
“What...?”
“You’ve exceeded my expectations.
In every way.”
It didn’t take long to understand what her smile and those few words meant.
*A test.*
The thought flashed through my mind, and the tension gripping my whole body snapped loose.
*Damn it.*
The Bow Saint frowned in mock disapproval.
“Hm.
Still wet behind the ears, and you talk to your elders like that?”
“If you were really an elder, you wouldn’t mess with someone who’s still wet behind the ears.”
“I’ve spent decades looking for you.
What’s a little teasing after all that?”
The Bow Saint smiled faintly.
As she looked at me, there was a hint of approval in her eyes.
“So you had nothing to do with the City Lord’s death or the Blood Soul Gu after all?”
“I had something to do with it.”
The Bow Saint tossed out the bombshell as if it were nothing.
She stroked a flower and continued.
“I sent him back into danger, knowing full well he would die soon.
I thought that if he died in Sichuan, someone close to you there would notice what had happened.”
“You knew he was going to die?”
“The City Lord of Sichuan Province was already infected with the Blood Soul Gu while he was staying in the Imperial Capital.
Naturally, it was Dark Heaven’s doing—or, more precisely, the doing of the City Lord’s favorite concubine.”
“Wait.
Aehyang?”
“Yes.”
My eyes widened.
The Bow Saint went on in the same even tone.
“Don’t be surprised.
If you need to control someone and that someone is a man, there’s no surer method than using a beautiful woman.”
“But how did you know she was working for Dark Heaven just from that?”
“I investigated her discreetly myself and found that she was highly skilled in Soul Bewitchment.
I’d heard he was neglecting his duties because he was besotted with women.
I was keeping an eye on him when I had him summoned to the Imperial Capital.”
A memory from not so long ago came back to me: the first time I’d met the City Lord, before the incident that came to be known as the Sichuan Blood Tragedy.
He’d been half naked even then.
*So even back then...?*
A chill ran down my spine.
Not because I’d failed to notice that Aehyang, a Dark Heaven agent, was right beside him.
Because I couldn’t begin to guess how far Dark Heaven’s shadow—its dark hand—had reached.
“Then does that mean...?”
“Yes.”
The Bow Saint nodded before I could finish.
“Dark Heaven has reached the roots of the Great Nation.
It has worked its way into every corner, so thoroughly that we don’t know where its reach ends.”
“The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s death didn’t end this.
There are likely still quite a few local officials with real power, great and small, working with Dark Heaven.
Generals who command armies, too.
And that would include some of the City Lords who govern the provinces.”
I swallowed.
A province might sound like a simple administrative division, but the land and population within one were enormous.
Why else had dozens of warlords proclaimed themselves kings and fought for supremacy in the chaotic age of the past?
Just to claim legitimacy by calling themselves kings?
Half right, half wrong.
If you conquered a region and absorbed all the strength of its land, you could build enough power to claim the title of king of an entire nation.
These days, the City Lords were officials who answered to a powerful central government.
But if they set their minds on rebellion, they could do tremendous damage to the Great Nation.
*He wasn’t exaggerating.
He wasn’t lying.*
Before the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had accepted everything and let go, he’d poured out a curse in his rage.
*This is only the beginning.
Even if you protected the Imperial Capital, the flames will sweep across the land.*
But they hadn’t been empty words spat out in anger.
There was truth in them.
A time bomb that might go off before long.
*Damn it.*
My head felt hot.
My breath came ragged though I hadn’t moved, and my heart pounded.
I could almost see flames flickering before my eyes, ready to swallow both the modern world and Murim.
And behind them stood the shadow of a giant who had swept aside the curtain and appeared when no one expected him.
“Then what do we do now?
What do we do from here?”
I asked the Bow Saint, struggling to catch my breath.
No.
The question was really for the person who had left a letter long ago and, through it, guided her to this moment.
The Martial God.
Born a man, yet called a god.
He had saved the world once and left behind a plan to save it again.
I was asking him.
I wanted another prophecy from his letter to the Bow Saint.
One ray of light to show me the way down this pitch-black road.
“What am I—fuck—what am I supposed to do?!”
I was practically shouting.
The Bow Saint’s answer held no light at all.
“I don’t know.
Neither does he.”
All the strength went out of me.
My vision blurred, and my head sank.
I’d been sure there was something more.
Something more to it.
I thought he would be different, if anyone could.
He was the one who had been certain that a person like me would appear someday.
I’d even found myself thinking something impossible.
*What if the Martial God—the greatest of all time, with his dazzling achievements and divine authority—*
*Maybe...*
I clenched my teeth and was about to follow that unbelievable thought to its conclusion when a quiet voice reached my lowered head.
“But there is one thing.”
I slowly raised my head as if under a spell.
The Bow Saint was there, gazing at me with eyes sunk deep.
“He left a message for the chosen one.”
“What...what message?”
“Divine strength.”
Why did those two words make me freeze?
An inexplicable chill crept down my spine.
The Bow Saint spoke calmly and quietly, but her voice rang in my ears like thunder.
“He said the chosen one must forge a path with the divine strength and Will only the chosen one can possess.
Just as...”
Her voice trailed off.
In that instant, the world slowed.
An invisible curtain seemed to fall over my eyes and ears.
I could see only the Bow Saint—her lips moving slowly.
I could hear only the words passing between them.
*Just as you yourself did.*
Time began to move again.
I didn’t.
I stared at her, frozen as if I were trapped in ice.
*I...what did I just...*
What had I heard?
My mind felt as though it had emptied completely.
A few words floated there, bright against the blankness.
*Just as you yourself did.*
Just as *you*, the Martial God, did.
That could mean only one thing.
The Martial God had been a chosen one like me.
No.
More precisely...
*A System user.*
*Player.*
The word rushed in to fill my empty mind, swelling until it felt ready to burst.
A clear chime rang out.
*Ding.*
And at that moment—
*Slip.*
I felt the sky and ground slowly turn over as I fell into pitch-black darkness.
Everything happened at once.
Jin Taekyung’s trembling form crumpled like a puppet with its strings cut.
The Bow Saint’s hand shot out and seized his collar.
And finally, the cold dawn air that had drifted through the abandoned garden suddenly grew hot.
*Grab.
Fwoosh!*
The Bow Saint steadied Jin Taekyung, then spoke to the uninvited guest who had suddenly appeared.
“How strange.
I don’t remember inviting you, too.”
The guest answered in a low voice.
“I do call him my Disciple.
How could I leave him alone with some nasty old hag and not worry?”
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
His voice was calm, but flames flickered in his eyes.
“Fine.
Let’s hear what kind of nonsense you’ve been up to.”
The Bow Saint gave a short laugh and shook her head.
“All these years, and you haven’t changed.
Still charging in without thinking.”
“Do I have to say it twice?”
“You were hiding like a rat and listening.
You already know.
That was all I said.
The boy was simply exhausted beyond his limits.”
She looked down at the unconscious Taekyung.
Dried blood marked his face in several places, and the strain of his fierce struggle still showed there.
They were traces of how brilliantly—and nobly—he had fought.
“Take him with you.
Let him get a little more rest.”
Jeok Cheongang didn’t hesitate for long.
He carried Jin Taekyung on his back as if he’d been waiting for the chance, then used his movement technique to hurry away.
The Bow Saint watched him until he was gone.
Then, suddenly, she saw a flower bud slowly opening in the light.
It was the first light of dawn.

chapters.title: Chapter 929
paragraphs: That night was unusually dark and long.
For the soldiers on both sides, who clashed again and again with blazing torches and sharpened weapons.
For the people, who trembled in fear and waited for the sudden upheaval to end.
*Clang! Clang! Clang!*
“Gah!”

The fighting was not confined to the Imperial Palace. The chilling clash of blades and the screams covered the entire Imperial Capital for several shichen. Countless people who heard them remembered the fourth prince’s coup just over a decade earlier, which had overturned the Great Nation’s order and changed the course of its history.
Amid the chaos, some were gripped by more anger and fear than anyone else.
“Those bastards! I could chew them to death and it still wouldn’t be enough...!”
“I-it’s over. The Embroidered Uniform Guard must have discovered us!”

Dozens of people faced one another across a table inside an abandoned shrine thick with dust and cobwebs. Shadows from a dim oil lamp flickered over them. They were of different ages and dressed in all manner of clothes.
An old man listened to their cries, then spoke.
“Enough noise.”
His voice was low but firm. As if on cue, everyone fell silent and turned toward him.

His slight frame and deeply wrinkled skin showed his age. Yet his eyes were clear and shrewd, and though his clothes showed wear here and there, not a fold was out of place. His bearing, like his dress, spoke of the life he had led.
“Don’t let yourselves be swept up in this. The path before us was decided long ago.”
The old man lifted his lukewarm teacup, seemingly unconcerned by the trail of torches drawing closer beyond the window or the great roar that came with them.
“I don’t know what’s happening out there, but it may be for the best. Now that chaos has broken out, it’s time for us to act.”
The time had come.
At his brief words, some eyes lit up. Others trembled, unable to suppress their fear.
Restoration.
It was why they had gathered here today, and the cause they had taken up to save one person.
“Now...we must put everything back where it belongs.”
The old man’s eyes flashed with a strength hard to believe in a man of ninety, and a resolve firmer than anyone’s.

“Let us drive those cruel traitors—who have abandoned what is right and overturned the natural order—out of the Imperial Palace. Let us raise His Highness Prince Shangshan to the throne by the strength of the people.”
An unseen surge swept through the shrine like a wave.
They had come of their own resolve, yet amid their rising excitement and fear, they had briefly forgotten what their undertaking meant.
*By the strength of the people. Raise a ruler of the people.*
They looked at one another.
They differed in age, status, and gender. But now they were comrades in the same boat.
Each had lived a separate life. They had come together to steer the great ship that was the Great Nation onto the right course.
A few days earlier, the words of someone whose identity they did not know had lit a fuse hidden deep in their hearts.
“The azure heaven that once shone blue is fading, and dark clouds are rolling in.”
As the tune slipped from someone’s lips, a young Confucian scholar joined in as though entranced.
“The storm soon to come will swallow the world.”
“But, people, do not tremble. Do not be afraid.”
An old laborer, his skin darkened by the sun, muttered in a rough voice. In his hand was an axe with a keen, blue-steel edge. Once, he had led an army.
“For there is a mountain, the highest in all the world.”
“There is a stream that never runs dry.”
“Fruit ripens there, and animals run free.”
“And a home to keep out the storms, and a forest to provide firewood.”
It was no longer any one person’s voice.
Reciting the song that had spread through the Imperial Capital’s marketplaces over the past few days, they rose to their feet.
“It can shelter all the people, and still have room for more.”
*Step. Creak.*
The old shrine groaned as they filed out. The song continued, louder and stronger than before.
“So, people, do not tremble. Do not be afraid.”
The old man led the way, his white robes fluttering as he stepped onto the damp earth.
As he made his way along the rugged mountain path, shadows crouched in the darkness rose and followed him.
From dozens to hundreds.
From hundreds to thousands.
Before long, they had become an army. They carried sickles still caked with dirt, and spears, swords, and axes red with rust.
*Step. Step.*
They marched toward the faint dawn light in the east and the trail of torches creeping up the mountain like a living dragon.
The song on their lips became a fervent plea, then a mighty roar.
“Go to Mount Shangshan, go to Mount Shangshan.”
Thousands of pairs of solemn eyes shone in the dark.
“Though the raging storm swallow the Five Sacred Mountains of the Central Plains, it will never dare reach Mount Shangshan.”
*Thud-thud-thud-thud.*
The low mountain trembled. Those torches drawing closer by the moment were likely the punitive force sent by the Emperor, who had realized a restoration was underway.
But...
“The lord of Mount Shangshan has Heaven’s protection!”
They raised their voices higher.
Highborn and lowborn alike strained their throats, fighting to suppress the fear still welling up inside them.
Only a few days ago, on a day like any other, an unknown man in a bamboo hat had cast those words into their hearts. Now they shouted them with all their strength.
“He is descended from the dragon that commands rain and lightning, and fit to be a just and benevolent ruler!”
And just as their great shout shook the land around them—
*Whoosh.*
An unusually sharp gust cut through the gray dawn mist. A man appeared from within it and spoke.
“That’s quite a fine song.”
Everyone’s eyes widened.
Dried blood marked the golden armor he wore, but could not hide it. That armor meant only one thing.
“The Embroidered Uniform Guard...!”
At the words, forced out like a groan, trembling eyes turned to the torches rippling a few hundred *jang* below.
Suspicion became certainty.
The Emperor had sent the Embroidered Uniform Guard to put down their restoration.
And perhaps Prince Shangshan had already...
“You monsters! Aren’t you afraid of Heaven?”
Some of the restoration army, consumed by rage, were about to rush at the man who was clearly an Embroidered Uniform Guard when the old man, who had led them all despite his age, suddenly spoke.
“Whose blood is on your armor?”
They stopped. The man answered evenly.
“The blood of traitors who endangered the ancestral temples and the state.”
“Then who are the traitors you speak of?”
“On the smaller scale, Wei Zhong, the East Depot’s Seal-Holding Eunuch, and those in league with him. On the larger scale, the foreign enemy called Dark Heaven.”
“...Dark Heaven. Dark Heaven, is it?”
The old man murmured the name. He knew of the force that had recently been drenching the martial world in blood.
And the voice of the man in bloodstained golden armor was familiar, too.
“Was it you?”
But unlike the restoration army, who could make no sense of this strange exchange, the Embroidered Uniform Guard understood what the old man’s brief question meant.
“It was.”
“Then what you said and did in the marketplace that day...”
“It was all done at His Majesty’s command—the imperial decree.”
“Ah.”
The old man let out a sigh. Some in the restoration army recognized the man at last, and their eyes widened.
“Could it be...?”
“Y-yes. That was his voice.”
They remembered it clearly: a voice that had carried over a crowd of hundreds, and a man in a bamboo hat who had dropped a great stone into their hearts before vanishing.
“My surname is Lee. I once served the late Emperor as Grand Preceptor. What is your name?”

The man, now wearing a golden helmet in place of his bamboo hat, answered with the respect due to an elder official. Decades ago, Lee had repeatedly urged the Emperor to keep eunuchs at a distance, only to be falsely accused and driven from office.
“Jeong Hogun, Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard. I have come to deliver His Majesty the Emperor’s command.”
His voice, charged with internal energy, pierced the dawn air and reached every ear.

“I was unworthy and failed to bring about an age of peace. I was unfilial and lost the late Emperor and the elders of the imperial family. But I have never once been disloyal. Now, at last, I seek to set the natural order right. Take up the banner of Imperial Younger Brother Zhu Bao and, with those who follow you, eliminate the traitors.”
The air seemed to stop. Shock swept through the restoration army like a great wave.
*Imperial Younger Brother Zhu Bao.*
Everyone understood what it meant.
Jeong Hogun walked slowly toward them with a banner in his hand. Beside a dragon embroidered in gold thread was Zhu Bao’s name. The sight erased their last shred of doubt.
Cries of wonder rose all around him. The old man swallowed and fought back the tears gathering in his wrinkled eyes.
Then he dropped to both knees and accepted the Imperial Younger Brother’s banner in trembling hands.
“I receive and obey His Majesty’s solemn command.”
As the light of dawn grew clearer in the far west, the roar of thousands who had joined the Embroidered Uniform Guard broke the early-morning stillness.

They roused the people who had been paralyzed with fear and the loyal men who had already given up hope. Then they fell upon the traitors still locked in bloody fighting throughout the Imperial Capital.
They became a wave of people numbering tens of thousands—no, hundreds of thousands.
“Waaah!”
“Long live His Highness Prince Shangshan!”
“Long live His Majesty the Emperor!”
*Crack!*
“Gah!”
“Retreat! Retreat!”
Dawn was stained with countless screams and blood.

When that unusually dark, long night ended and daylight came, there were no more battles. Only the shouts of those pursuing the rebels, who had lost the will to fight and scattered in every direction, and their overflowing joy remained.
One day. Two.
Then three days passed in the blink of an eye, and someone opened their eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 930
paragraphs: Strange.
The unfamiliar ceiling that should have been waiting for me, just like always, somehow felt familiar.
*What is this?*
As my vision slowly sharpened, I looked around.

The space was far too large to call a mere bedroom. Thick pillars stood between the curtains surrounding it, while braziers placed here and there and night-shining pearls set into the ceiling like stars bathed the room in a soft glow.
*Wait. Night-shining pearls?*
Then I realized where the déjà vu was coming from—and why the place felt familiar.
*This is...*
That’s right.
This was a vast pavilion built to serve as both living quarters and a place to handle state affairs—and a fortress filled with an ironclad guard.
Qianqing Palace.
*No wonder it felt familiar.*

Without the night-shining pearls, it might have taken me longer to figure it out. Only an emperor could plaster his ceiling with pearls big enough to fetch hundreds of silver nyang on Bok Choy Market as if they were glitter stickers.
*But...why am I here?*
The question surfaced in my strangely empty head.
*Whoosh.*
A faint breeze stirred the curtains around the bedroom. At the same moment, a man in black appeared like a ghost and bowed his head slightly.
“Have you awakened?”
His voice was muffled, almost a mumble.
I stared blankly at the unexpected intruder, then calmly assessed the situation.
The Emperor’s quarters. The Emperor’s blanket. The Emperor’s bed. The Emperor’s pillow.
My clothes were golden from head to toe, and when I lifted my pants for a peek, even my underwear was gleaming golden silk.
The full King-God-Emperor package.
And on top of that, No Shadow—the Emperor’s hidden guard, an assassin and Supreme Peak master—was speaking to me with such courtesy.
*Then could this be...*
Through clear-headed reasoning, I reached a conclusion. A shudder ran through me.
“Possession...!”
It had to be. There was no other explanation.
I’d gotten a good night’s sleep, woken up, and my life had changed genres from fusion Murim to a possession story. Just as I was reeling from the shock, No Shadow spoke in his usual muffled voice.
“Are you all right?”
*Would you be all right?* nearly burst out of me, but figuring out what had happened came first.
“What time is it? No, how many days have passed since the grand banquet?”
Apparently, that was a strange question from an emperor who’d just woken up. No Shadow stared at me before answering.
“Three days.”
“Three days?”
“Yes.”
“...Then how long was I asleep?”
“Three days as well.”
I squeezed my eyes shut.
Three days. In just three days, everything had gone to shit.

To hell with being an emperor. I’d gone from a handsome guy in his early twenties with his whole life ahead of him to a middle-aged man who looked ancient, and everything I’d achieved had gone up in smoke.
*System window...open.*
I silently tried the command, just in case.
But it scattered into the void.
There was no clear chime, no translucent holographic window.
*What the hell is going on? How did things get like this?*
I couldn’t breathe.
The levels I’d busted my ass to gain, my stats—I couldn’t even access the System window now. I might never make it back to the real world.
*Wait. Then what happened to the original me?*
The thought suddenly struck me, and my eyes flew open. I shouted at No Shadow in a panicked voice.
“Then what happened to me...? No, what happened to Jin Taekyung!”
No Shadow blinked above his pitch-black mask.
“You mean Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan?”
“Yes, the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung! The guy who’s handsome, tall, and perfectly muscled, and I have no idea why women aren’t all over him!”
His answer brought my thoughts to a halt.
“He has yet to awaken.”
“What?”
“For reasons unknown, he has not regained consciousness. I regret to report that, according to the examination of the one called the Divine Physician, he is as good as dead.”
“As a result, His Highness the Imperial Younger Brother has refused food and drink for three days. He said there was something he must return to a friend with whom he shared a bond...”
No Shadow trailed off and carefully held something out. I accepted it in a daze.
Rough, cold metal.
Gleaming like obsidian, it was the divine artifact of the Sichuan Tang Clan—the one I’d given Zhu Bao in case the worst happened.
*The Myriad-Poison Ring.*
I could see the boy who’d promised to survive and return it to me before long.
But...
*Damn it.*
I didn’t know how it had happened, but that shitty fate had twisted my life into knots once again.
Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan was gone.
And perhaps Jin Taekyung the Hunter’s life in Korea had ended here too.
*Crack.*
At some point, I’d clenched my fist so hard my knuckles had gone white. Then I saw the wrinkles covering the back of my hand, and the strength left me.
*Slide.*
My fingers loosened. The Myriad-Poison Ring rolled over my rough skin and fell onto the bluestone floor.
*Clang. Clang.*
The cold sound echoed alone through the vast room.
With hope drained from my eyes, I watched the Myriad-Poison Ring spin rapidly.
Each time the black gem caught the light of the night-shining pearls and flashed, faces I would never see again crossed my mind.
My family, more precious to me than my life. Team Leader Choi and so many other comrades.
All the people I trusted, and who trusted me.
And someone else I’d only just learned had been born to the same fate.
*The Martial God.*
Another System user. Another Player.
Someone chosen by this cruel fate long before I was.
Where was he now?
Had he gone through the same thing?
Or had the System chosen me as a new Player because he really was dead?
I didn’t know.
Not right now. Perhaps not ever.
I was no longer the chosen one or a Player. The System knew the truth, but it wouldn’t answer my questions.
No. I wouldn’t be able to hear its answer.
That was the kind of power the System was.
A power meant for one person alone.
*And so...another Player will appear.*
The hollow thought hovered on the tip of my tongue without becoming words.
With my eyes sunk deep, I kept watching the Myriad-Poison Ring spinning.
It was still turning and turning on the blue bluestone floor, without end.
Wait.
Something was wrong.
“H-how long is that thing going to keep spinning?”
No Shadow answered my cautious question.
“This is why I hate people who catch on too fast.”
What?
Quietly. Very quietly, I opened my eyes to slits as narrow as a flounder’s.
An unfamiliar ceiling came into view. Unlike the one from a moment ago, it was moderately luxurious and moderately Murim-like.
*Good. First check passed.*
I lifted a hand, moving so little I made no sound.
The glittering golden sleeve made my heart sink.
*Second check, pending.*
I ignored the cold sweat beading on my forehead and carefully lifted my pants.
I didn’t know which son of a bitch had put this on me and called it underwear, but sure enough, it was dazzlingly golden.
*Third check. This is getting shitty.*
Afraid to confirm what was real, I closed my barely open eyes again.
A bad sign. But it wasn’t over yet.
In the awful silence, I slipped a hand inside my pants and felt over my underwear.
The familiar weight—the one I’d have recognized anywhere, and was so glad to feel I could have cried—made my whole body shudder.
“Ah, ah...”
An indescribable electric thrill coursed through my whole body.
I was alive.
I was still alive.
This wasn’t that shitty dream from a moment ago. This was vivid reality, the present in which I was alive and breathing.
I was Jin Taekyung the Hunter and Jin Taekyung the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.
*Damn it. What a thing to be grateful for.*
Just being alive as myself felt overwhelming. I wiped a few tears away with my sleeve.
Then I opened my eyes to face the world with more gratitude than ever.
*Ah.*
I met the eyes of several familiar people who’d been watching me without making a sound.
The suffocating silence seemed as though it would last forever. The Divine Physician broke it first, his voice grave.
“That is perfectly understandable.”
Beside him, Jeok Cheongang avoided my gaze.
“Yes. It’s the Scorching Yang Qi. He’s done nothing wrong.”
The Bow Saint nodded and murmured, “Truly the chosen one...”
I took a quiet, deep breath.
It felt as though the world had stopped.
No—more accurately, I wished it would stop.
But even after I shut my eyes tight, made a fervent wish, and opened them again, the dreadful reality was still waiting for me right there.
The Divine Physician. Jeok Cheongang. The Bow Saint.
Fine. I could understand them. They were old enough to have been through every kind of trouble and seen every kind of thing they’d rather not have seen.
But they weren’t alone in the room.
The Fire Dragon Pavilion.
Fuck. The Fire Dragon Pavilion.
I was looking at them. They were looking at me.
More precisely, they were staring at me with their eyes wide, as though they couldn’t believe what they were seeing—at the sight of my hand inside the front of my pants.
*Ah.*
I barely swallowed the sigh that was about to burst out.
Then, as calmly as I could, I spoke.
“I know. It looks like there’s plenty of room for misunderstanding.”
“I don’t think it’s really a misunderstanding, mm.”
Song Ilseom cut himself off when he saw my expression.
Beside him, Sama Pyo looked distinctly surprised. He silently gave me a thumbs-up.
...You bastard.
Somehow feeling a little pleased and utterly humiliated at the same time, I tried again.
“But there were...circumstances.”
“Taishan knows! Taishan knows the circumstances! Taishan knows what that is!”
“Shut your mouth, you bastard!”
*Ah.*

Taishan had been bouncing with excitement, but shrank back at my thunderous shout. For some reason, Namho was still perched on his shoulders, riding him like a human throne. He spoke with a serious expression.
“But when are you going to take that hand out?”
Straight to the heart of it.
I kept my cool.
“I was just waiting for the right moment.”
“Mm. In a situation like this, it can’t be easy to pull it out.”
“Thank you for understanding.”
“Still, there are a lot of eyes on you. You should take it out now. Quickly, not slowly.”
“May I ask why?”
“The slower you move, the longer they’ll watch. I’ll count to three. Take it out exactly on three.”
“That’s a good idea, except I think saying it has drawn even more attention.”
Namho glanced around, then nodded as if I’d made a good point.
“That’s true.”
“Please don’t say anything else. Just for a moment. A very short moment.”
“All right.”
Namho fell silent. I took a small breath, then cautiously addressed the one person standing beside Hyuk Mujin and looking the other way.
“Young Lady Ju.”
The next moment—
*Whoosh. Bam!*
Ju Hwaran bolted out of the room faster than I’d ever seen her move. Hyuk Mujin came over and patted my shoulder.
“I understand exactly how you feel, Captain.”
“...Shut it.”
“Yes, sir.”
I wished it had just been a dream.

chapters.title: Chapter 931
paragraphs: Everyone needs time alone.
Say, when you need to check the System messages piled up until they’re ready to burst, like emails in a portal account you haven’t opened in years.
Especially if you’ve just groped your own private parts in front of a dozen people, then shuddered all over.
But even after that incomprehensible nightmare—and a situation worse than the nightmare itself—people seemed determined not to leave me alone.
“Now, raise your arm and follow my movements.”
“Very good. This time, turn it a little farther...”
“How many fingers am I holding up?”
My first visitors were the imperial physicians, who came charging in the moment word spread that I’d regained consciousness.

They’d apparently been standing by for three days under the Emperor’s strict orders. Reeking of herbal medicine, they had me do one thing after another, then huddled together with grave expressions and whispered.
Of course, I could hear every word perfectly.
“His condition is normal—no, perfect.”
“I heard there was an enormous battle, but he’s strangely unharmed. Not a single wound.”
“That’s not all. If you look more closely, the front of his robe is suspiciously bulging.”
“What? You don’t mean that’s...? No. Impossible.”
“To be honest, I’m not certain either. I’ll give you a signal when the opportunity arises. You can press it once, pretending it was an accident.”
“Hmm. Understood.”
Their discussion over, the physicians turned back to me with gentle smiles and suggested one more examination, just in case.
I answered without hesitation.
“Get out. Now.”
But even after they left, visitors kept coming to the pavilion where I was staying.
“Um, Captain. You have a visitor.”
“Who?”
“Just a moment. They say they were appointed Guanglu Dafu the day before yesterday.”
“What exactly does a Guanglu Dafu do?”
“If I knew that, I wouldn’t have become a martial artist.”
“Sounds like a scammer just from the title. Tell him I’m not taking out a loan.”
“Yes, I’ll pass that along.”
I only learned that the Guanglu Dafu was an official whose rank came just below the Three Excellencies after turning away dozens of officials. Then, at last, I welcomed a new visitor.
“I hope I’m not too late. Judging by the crowds at your door, you’re already quite popular.”
The voice was warm and familiar. Hong Jin came in joking, and I couldn’t help smiling.
“Comrade Hong.”
“Comrade, hm? Have I ever told you? Even though it was an official title, I always felt I could count on you whenever you called me that, Young Master Jin.”
His expression was playful, but his eyes and voice held feelings I couldn’t put into words.
“Thank you. Truly. His Highness, the Imperial Younger Brother, couldn’t come with me today, but I hope you know he feels the same way.”
*Swish.*
Hong Jin straightened his ornately embroidered navy-blue robe and bowed with the utmost respect. Then he lifted his head and smiled as though nothing had happened.
“Oh, and I got promoted. From now on, everyone’s to call me Eunuch Hong, not Comrade Hong.”
“Eunuch? You don’t mean...?”

“Exactly what you’re thinking, Young Master Jin. I felt so guilty and ashamed for suspecting His Majesty all those years without knowing the truth that I turned the position down several times. I even tried to retire to the countryside, but...”
Hong Jin, now dressed in the East Depot uniform I’d grown fairly used to seeing, continued with a faint smile.
“His Majesty said, ‘There’s so much to take care of. Where do you think you’re going, running off on your own? I won’t let you go, if only for having the nerve to try.’”
“That’s good. Truly.”
It was good news, and the right outcome.

Hong Jin could hardly be blamed for the hostility he’d felt toward the Emperor for the past decade or so. The Emperor had deliberately hidden the truth. Besides, keeping Hong Jin at Zhu Bao’s side showed just how much he trusted Hong Jin’s loyalty.
“So, Comrade Hong—no, Eunuch Hong—are you the East Depot’s new Cang Gong?”
“I’m in charge of the East Depot, yes. But the position of Cang Gong—the Seal-Holding Eunuch—will likely remain vacant forever. The Great Nation leaves no trace of a traitor behind. Besides...”
For a moment, Hong Jin’s eyes turned cold.
“There are still roots we haven’t pulled up.”

I thought I knew what he meant. Broadly, he could mean the entire East Depot, where the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s shadow had fallen most heavily. More narrowly, he could mean the one man whose death was still unconfirmed when I lost consciousness.
“Ma Sanbao.”
Hong Jin gave a small nod at the name.
“We’ve searched the Imperial Capital and hundreds of *li* around it for three days, but there’s no trace of him. It’s as if he rose straight into the sky.”
Honestly, I couldn’t help admiring Ma Sanbao a little. Escaping that desperate situation was one thing. Evading the Imperial Army’s pursuit for three days afterward was another.
*He must have been badly wounded already. How did he disappear?*

Of course, it was possible. Ma Sanbao fell far short of his master, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, but he’d still reached the Supreme Peak realm and had monstrous powers of recovery. His disguise technique could change both his face and his build so thoroughly that even I had to marvel at it.
*Lastly, he could’ve used a Moving Formation Dark Heaven had hidden somewhere nearby.*
Ma Sanbao had to die if we wanted to prevent future trouble. But if he’d already fled beyond our reach, there wasn’t much we could do.
For now, the best we could do was prepare for the prey that hadn’t escaped the net—and the predators approaching from far away with their presence concealed.
“Comrade Hong... no, Eunuch Hong.”
Hong Jin smiled.
“Call me whatever you like. You can, Young Master Jin.”
“Hey, Hong.”
“...You really do make yourself at home. What is it?”
“Can I ask you a favor?”
“Do you even need to ask? I’d do anything for you, Young Master Jin—anything short of treason. Name it.”
“Then...”
He’d answered readily enough, but when he heard my request, his eyes widened.
“Hm?”
“Can’t you do it?”
“No, it’s easy enough. I’m just wondering what it means.”
“It’s important. I’ll explain once I’ve checked it myself.”
“Of course you will. You can’t just expect me to do it for nothing. You’re making use of an East Depot eunuch, after all.”
Hong Jin rose with a joking smile and left. Hyuk Mujin, who’d been watching for an opening, sidled over.
“Um, Captain.”
“You want to know what I asked him to do?”
“Ha! You really are a mind reader.”
He even gave me a thumbs-up, trying to butter me up. I let out a short laugh and shook my head.
“There is something.”
“Wait, you’re keeping it secret from me too?”
“It’s not exactly that...”
“Not exactly?”
“I don’t know either.”
Hyuk Mujin stared at me, thoroughly unimpressed.
“If you don’t want to tell me, just say so. Don’t make me feel even more pathetic.”
“I’m serious, you idiot.”
“Forget it. Don’t talk to me for a while. I won’t talk to you either.”
He made a show of his hurt feelings as he headed for the door. I called after him apologetically.
“Back to your spot before I count to three. One.”
*Whoosh.*
Hyuk Mujin returned to his spot before I could count to two, then asked while pretending to look elsewhere,
“So, what is it?”
“I told you. I don’t know exactly what it is either.”
“...Really?”
“Yeah. Someone told me about it, but only in broad strokes.”
“Who?”
“Someone you know, too.”
Hyuk Mujin cocked his head, then thumped his chest confidently.
“Tell me who it is, and I’ll bring them here right away. Then you can hear all about it in greater detail...”
“That won’t work.”
I cut him off.
“That person’s already dead.”
“What?”
“Dead. I killed him myself.”
Hyuk Mujin stared at me with his mouth hanging open. Then his eyes went wide.
“Y-you don’t mean...? No, right?”
“I told you. Now go and leave me alone.”
“Wait. Why would that bastard tell you—?”
“Get out before I count to three. Whatever happens after that is your problem. One.”
*Whoosh.*
Works like a charm.

Then I sank into the soft silk bedding and gazed out the window. It was bright enough outside to make it hard to believe it was night.
*Bright. Noisy, too.*
Even from this pavilion deep inside the Inner Palace, I could hear distant cheers and songs carried on the wind.

Fireworks shot up here and there, painting the night sky in brilliant colors. The people, welcoming a new era, would have forgotten sleep and poured into the streets, laughing, talking, and drinking all night.
Leaving tomorrow’s worries behind to enjoy today’s happiness to the fullest.
*You wanted a world like this once, too.*
I thought of someone no longer in this world.
A man who had let go of all the anger left in his heart at the very end and died as a human being. The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord.
And the Sound Transmission that had been all but his last words.
*Remember every word I say from this moment on.*
What followed was short and simple.
Find one thing in a certain place.
That was all.
*And I’d find out what that thing was soon enough.*
I didn’t know either. I had no idea what that thing was, the one the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had mentioned at the very end, or what it contained or meant.
But I’d decided to stop thinking about it until I saw it with my own eyes. I had other things to deal with right now.
“Open System window.”
The quiet words had barely left my lips when—
*Ding. Ding. D-d-ding!*
Chimes rang out like mad, and countless holographic windows filled my vision.
For a very long time.
As if they’d been waiting for this moment all along.

sentences.text: Everyone needs time alone.
Say, when you need to check the System messages piled up until they’re ready to burst, like emails in a portal account you haven’t opened in years.
Especially if you’ve just groped your own private parts in front of a dozen people, then shuddered all over.
But even after that incomprehensible nightmare—and a situation worse than the nightmare itself—people seemed determined not to leave me alone.
“Now, raise your arm and follow my movements.”
“Very good.
This time, turn it a little farther...”
“How many fingers am I holding up?”
My first visitors were the imperial physicians, who came charging in the moment word spread that I’d regained consciousness.
They’d apparently been standing by for three days under the Emperor’s strict orders.
Reeking of herbal medicine, they had me do one thing after another, then huddled together with grave expressions and whispered.
Of course, I could hear every word perfectly.
“His condition is normal—no, perfect.”
“I heard there was an enormous battle, but he’s strangely unharmed.
Not a single wound.”
“That’s not all.
If you look more closely, the front of his robe is suspiciously bulging.”
“What?
You don’t mean that’s...?
No.
Impossible.”
“To be honest, I’m not certain either.
I’ll give you a signal when the opportunity arises.
You can press it once, pretending it was an accident.”
“Hmm.
Understood.”
Their discussion over, the physicians turned back to me with gentle smiles and suggested one more examination, just in case.
I answered without hesitation.
“Get out.
Now.”
But even after they left, visitors kept coming to the pavilion where I was staying.
“Um, Captain.
You have a visitor.”
“Who?”
“Just a moment.
They say they were appointed Guanglu Dafu the day before yesterday.”
“What exactly does a Guanglu Dafu do?”
“If I knew that, I wouldn’t have become a martial artist.”
“Sounds like a scammer just from the title.
Tell him I’m not taking out a loan.”
“Yes, I’ll pass that along.”
I only learned that the Guanglu Dafu was an official whose rank came just below the Three Excellencies after turning away dozens of officials.
Then, at last, I welcomed a new visitor.
“I hope I’m not too late.
Judging by the crowds at your door, you’re already quite popular.”
The voice was warm and familiar.
Hong Jin came in joking, and I couldn’t help smiling.
“Comrade Hong.”
“Comrade, hm?
Have I ever told you?
Even though it was an official title, I always felt I could count on you whenever you called me that, Young Master Jin.”
His expression was playful, but his eyes and voice held feelings I couldn’t put into words.
“Thank you.
Truly.
His Highness, the Imperial Younger Brother, couldn’t come with me today, but I hope you know he feels the same way.”
*Swish.*
Hong Jin straightened his ornately embroidered navy-blue robe and bowed with the utmost respect.
Then he lifted his head and smiled as though nothing had happened.
“Oh, and I got promoted.
From now on, everyone’s to call me Eunuch Hong, not Comrade Hong.”
“Eunuch?
You don’t mean...?”
“Exactly what you’re thinking, Young Master Jin.
I felt so guilty and ashamed for suspecting His Majesty all those years without knowing the truth that I turned the position down several times.
I even tried to retire to the countryside, but...”
Hong Jin, now dressed in the East Depot uniform I’d grown fairly used to seeing, continued with a faint smile.
“His Majesty said, ‘There’s so much to take care of.
Where do you think you’re going, running off on your own?
I won’t let you go, if only for having the nerve to try.’”
“That’s good.
Truly.”
It was good news, and the right outcome.
Hong Jin could hardly be blamed for the hostility he’d felt toward the Emperor for the past decade or so.
The Emperor had deliberately hidden the truth.
Besides, keeping Hong Jin at Zhu Bao’s side showed just how much he trusted Hong Jin’s loyalty.
“So, Comrade Hong—no, Eunuch Hong—are you the East Depot’s new Cang Gong?”
“I’m in charge of the East Depot, yes.
But the position of Cang Gong—the Seal-Holding Eunuch—will likely remain vacant forever.
The Great Nation leaves no trace of a traitor behind.
Besides...”
For a moment, Hong Jin’s eyes turned cold.
“There are still roots we haven’t pulled up.”
I thought I knew what he meant.
Broadly, he could mean the entire East Depot, where the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s shadow had fallen most heavily.
More narrowly, he could mean the one man whose death was still unconfirmed when I lost consciousness.
“Ma Sanbao.”
Hong Jin gave a small nod at the name.
“We’ve searched the Imperial Capital and hundreds of *li* around it for three days, but there’s no trace of him.
It’s as if he rose straight into the sky.”
Honestly, I couldn’t help admiring Ma Sanbao a little.
Escaping that desperate situation was one thing.
Evading the Imperial Army’s pursuit for three days afterward was another.
*He must have been badly wounded already.
How did he disappear?*
Of course, it was possible.
Ma Sanbao fell far short of his master, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, but he’d still reached the Supreme Peak realm and had monstrous powers of recovery.
His disguise technique could change both his face and his build so thoroughly that even I had to marvel at it.
*Lastly, he could’ve used a Moving Formation Dark Heaven had hidden somewhere nearby.*
Ma Sanbao had to die if we wanted to prevent future trouble.
But if he’d already fled beyond our reach, there wasn’t much we could do.
For now, the best we could do was prepare for the prey that hadn’t escaped the net—and the predators approaching from far away with their presence concealed.
“Comrade Hong... no, Eunuch Hong.”
Hong Jin smiled.
“Call me whatever you like.
You can, Young Master Jin.”
“Hey, Hong.”
“...You really do make yourself at home.
What is it?”
“Can I ask you a favor?”
“Do you even need to ask?
I’d do anything for you, Young Master Jin—anything short of treason.
Name it.”
“Then...”
He’d answered readily enough, but when he heard my request, his eyes widened.
“Hm?”
“Can’t you do it?”
“No, it’s easy enough.
I’m just wondering what it means.”
“It’s important.
I’ll explain once I’ve checked it myself.”
“Of course you will.
You can’t just expect me to do it for nothing.
You’re making use of an East Depot eunuch, after all.”
Hong Jin rose with a joking smile and left.
Hyuk Mujin, who’d been watching for an opening, sidled over.
“Um, Captain.”
“You want to know what I asked him to do?”
“Ha!
You really are a mind reader.”
He even gave me a thumbs-up, trying to butter me up.
I let out a short laugh and shook my head.
“There is something.”
“Wait, you’re keeping it secret from me too?”
“It’s not exactly that...”
“Not exactly?”
“I don’t know either.”
Hyuk Mujin stared at me, thoroughly unimpressed.
“If you don’t want to tell me, just say so.
Don’t make me feel even more pathetic.”
“I’m serious, you idiot.”
“Forget it.
Don’t talk to me for a while.
I won’t talk to you either.”
He made a show of his hurt feelings as he headed for the door.
I called after him apologetically.
“Back to your spot before I count to three.
One.”
*Whoosh.*

chapters.title: Chapter 932
paragraphs: “Open System window.”
At that brief command, the dam holding everything back gave way.
*Ding. Ding. D-d-ding!*
Chimes rang out, one over another. At the same time, countless holographic windows surged toward me like a giant wave. My mouth fell open.
*Holy shit. Why are there so many?*
It felt like facing all the homework I’d put off over an entire summer vacation in elementary school. No—this was worse.
Even at a glance, well over a hundred holographic windows filled the air.
*It’d be nice if they were all Level-up notifications.*
Wishful thinking, of course. There was no way they’d all piled up in just the past three days.
I started with the first System message to appear and read them in order.
**System** Congratulations! The Update is complete! We sincerely regret any minor inconvenience caused by the Update.
Minor inconvenience. Sincere regret.
What a way to piss me off right from the start.
I vividly remembered nearly dying because of that “minor inconvenience.” But the next message quickly cooled my anger.
**System** Therefore, as an apology, we would like to provide you with an appropriate Reward.
“Oh.”
Right. That’s more like it.

This System was fundamentally different from those garbage games that wielded the Four Great Swords—scheduled maintenance, unscheduled maintenance, extended maintenance, and emergency maintenance—like an heirloom blade.
Giving users fitting Rewards for all their hard work and doing everything it could to make their experience enjoyable—that was what a kingly, god-tier System was for.
**System** Update Reward has been delivered to your Inventory. Would you like to check your new Item? **Y / N**
*Reward. New Item.*
Those two little words awakened the childlike wonder I’d long forgotten.
I was more excited than I’d been opening my Christmas present at seven years old. With excitement and joy mingling inside me, I answered.
“Open.”
*Ding.*

**System Item Window** Pocket Watch of Unknown Make **Type:** Item **Grade:** None **Restriction:** None **Description:** A pocket watch made by someone unknown. Very sturdy. At a glance, it looks like an old, broken watch. On closer inspection, it still looks like an old, broken watch.
What the hell is this?
My brain stalled. I stared blankly at the pocket watch in my hand.
It was exactly as the Item description said. At a glance, it looked broken. On closer inspection, it still looked broken. I could’ve written a poem about it on the spot.
*Title: Pocket Watch.*
*Old, even on closer inspection.*
*Broken, no matter how long I look.*
*Fucking sucks.*
I felt like I was going insane.

It was on par with the betrayal I’d felt when Santa Claus—the old man who’d brought my Christmas present when I was seven—had punched in the front door’s passcode and strolled in like he owned the place, then kissed my mom right in front of me.
*This is my... Update Reward?*
My head still reeling, I tried to pull myself out of the shock.
*No, no. This can’t be right.*

There were only two possibilities. Either the System had prepared a surprise hidden-camera prank for me after everything I’d been through, or there was something special about the watch that I hadn’t found yet.
*There was only one notification, so it’s not a prank. Which means...*
I gathered my wits and examined the watch carefully. Before long, I noticed something I’d missed on its back, worn shiny by someone’s hands.
*Wait.*

It was a faint mark, almost completely rubbed away—probably too faint for an ordinary person to see. I stirred up my internal energy and channeled it into my eyes. With my enhanced vision, I made out a dim inscription.
“N-no way...”
Even a broken clock is right twice a day.
“That doesn’t mean a damn thing, you bastards!”
*BANG!*
I hurled the pocket watch with all my strength. It flew like a cannonball and struck the wall.
Or, to be precise, it smashed through the wall.
*Rumble!*
The wall crumbled. Beyond it stood Hyuk Mujin, staring at me with his mouth hanging open.
“What the—Gasp! Was that an assassination attempt?!”
In a way, it was.
I’d taken a hit to the back of the head without warning, and now my insides ached as if I’d been stabbed.
“Mujin. I’m dizzy. Mujin.”
“Captain! Stay still! I’ll protect you!”
“You? Protect me?”
Hyuk Mujin hesitated, then cautiously offered, “Should I bring Great Hero Jeok over?”
“...If you call him, we’re the ones who’ll get put through the wringer. Don’t.”
“Oh, come on. You scared me. It wasn’t an assassination attempt, right?”
“Yeah, idiot. So quit making a scene and pick that thing up.”
Coughing in the cloud of dust, Hyuk Mujin cautiously retrieved the pocket watch.
“C-Captain. You don’t mean this piece of iron junk, do you?”
“Sorry. I guess you do. And, just in case, I take back the ‘junk’ part.”
Like an unlucky member of the Ten Attendants, Hyuk Mujin sensed my foul mood and hurried over to hand me the watch.
“But what exactly is it?”
“A broken watch.”
“A watch? This little thing?”
Hyuk Mujin eyed the pocket watch’s unfamiliar shape. I answered mournfully.
“It’s still junk. Very sturdy, completely useless junk.”
“Why would you keep something like this? It’s even broken.”
“...I got it somehow, okay? Watch your mouth.”
Every word was a blade digging into my heart. Having confirmed the watch’s durability by accident, I swallowed back my tears.
*The Item description was telling the truth after all.*
Some truths were unbearably cruel. Right now, this pocket watch was one of them.
*But why would the System give me something like this?*
This wasn’t some ordinary Quest. It was the Reward I’d received for completing an entire Update, and it was garbage like this.
Clinging to one last sliver of hope, I examined the watch again. All I found was more reason to despair.
*This thing really is broken.*

For starters, the time was completely wrong. It was already nearing midnight, but the hour hand pointed somewhere around five. Even that was only a guess—the numbers that ought to have been there were missing.
*And where the hell did the minute hand go?*
At this point, I wasn’t sure I could even call it a pocket watch. Pocket time? Pocket piece? Even those seemed too generous.
*I can’t adjust the time, either. And it doesn’t seem to keep moving. What the hell is this thing?*
I shook it this way and that, then held it close to my ear. There wasn’t so much as a tick—not even the faint noise of parts moving inside.
It had exactly one advantage. I couldn’t crush it no matter how hard I squeezed, or even leave a scratch.
*Did they give it to me as a weapon? Or a shield for emergencies?*
A familiar scene from a war movie flashed through my mind.
A sharp gunshot rang out. Private Johnson collapsed.
Certain their comrade was dead, his squadmates rushed over. But what they found was a bullet lodged in the little Bible that the devout Private Johnson always carried over his heart...
“Wow. It’s already driving me insane.”
Hyuk Mujin, who’d been watching me warily for a while, cautiously spoke up.
“Um, Captain?”
“Don’t call me in that sly, eunuch-like voice. I’ll kill you. Seriously.”
“Yes, sir. May I ask you something?”
“Spit it out.”
“Um... are you going to throw that away?”
Hyuk Mujin pointed discreetly at the pocket watch in my palm, then went on as though he were making casual conversation.
“If you are, I’d like to humbly suggest giving it to someone who’s your right arm, your heart, and unwaveringly loyal to you.”
“Was that supposed to be humble? You sound pretty confident.”
“Well, I’m just saying. If you’re not going to use it, there’s no reason to keep it.”
“Why the hell do you want this thing?”
“It’s a watch, isn’t it? And judging by the look of it, it’s a rare item from the Western Regions. Even if it’s broken, wouldn’t it look good to carry around?”
Hyuk Mujin made a surprisingly coherent argument. I smacked my lips.
*I guess it wouldn’t really matter if I gave it to him...*

But something about it bothered me, like a fish bone stuck in my throat. If I handed this godforsaken pocket watch to Hyuk Mujin right now, I’d feel even less satisfied than I would eating fried rice at a Chinese restaurant without a bowl of spicy jjambbong broth.
*There might be something I don’t know about it yet. I can wait and see. If it really is junk, I can give it to him then.*

It wasn’t as if the System always gave out incredible Rewards. I didn’t know exactly how it decided what to hand out, but I’d received plenty of useless junk Items from the countless Quests I’d completed. Little by little, enough had piled up in my Inventory to fill a truck.
The one thing I couldn’t get past was that the broken pocket watch in my hand was a Reward for completing an Update.
“Hmm.”
I nodded without saying anything. Then Hyuk Mujin’s sly voice reached my ear again.
“Um, Captain?”
“What?”
“Could you say something...?”
“Not yet. Wait a little. A month—no, fifteen days.”
Fifteen days. Half a month.
That was the final trial period I’d settled on. Hyuk Mujin’s face lit up.
“So you’ll give it to me in fifteen days?”
“Yeah. Assuming I’ve confirmed it’s useless to me.”
“Come on. It came from the Western Regions. There probably isn’t a craftsman around here who can fix it. At most, you could carry it because it looks pretty.”
Hyuk Mujin grinned unpleasantly as he went on.
“But what do you call it?”
“Pocket-watch, shi—pocket watch.”
“Wow. Even the name’s pretty. Thread a leather cord through that ring and wear it around your neck. You’d draw eyes wherever you went.”
“Yeah?”
“Yes. Shiny silk would look even better than leather.”
“Oh, yeah?”

It was a suggestion worthy of the eldest grandson of a wealthy textile-merchant family. It was a good one, too. Without hesitation, I tore a strip from the gold silk robe I was wearing, threaded it through the ring, and hung the watch around my neck.
“How do I look? Pretty?”
“Whew. Is your name Mr. Golden Sun? You’re practically glowing.”
“They’d like it if I gave it to them like this, wouldn’t they?”
“Captain, you’d go that far for me...”
Hyuk Mujin’s eyes trembled with emotion. I gazed fondly at the pocket watch hanging around my neck.
“Not you. Young Lady Ju.”
“Maybe Young Lady Ju would be less upset if she got a gift like this. Don’t you think?”
“Answer me.”
“...I’m sure she’d love it. Yes.”
His eyes went cold in an instant.
As Hyuk Mujin silently berated me with his gaze, I sensed dozens of people approaching the pavilion. I leaned out the window.
“Stop! Stop! Stop! Move and I’ll cut you down. Pocket!”
At the head of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, their torches flickering, Jeong Hogun fell silent for a moment before replying.
“What nonsense are you talking about?”
“You stupid, useless Embroidered Uniform Guard bastard! You showed up without even learning the password!”
“No, I mean, what is this all of a sudden...?”
“Shut up! Say ‘watch’! Hurry!”
“...Watch.”
“I said shut up!”
His eyes were full of venom, like an angry pufferfish. I supposed I’d better stop messing with him.
Generously letting him off the hook, I asked Jeong Hogun, who’d clamped his mouth shut, “So, why are you here?”
“You need to come with me for a moment.”
“Am I someone who comes and goes just because you tell me to? Besides, I’m really busy. I’ve got a lot to do.”
“His Majesty has summoned you.”
“Oh.”
Then I’d better go.
