It’s even broken.”
“...I got it somehow, okay?
Watch your mouth.”
Every word was a blade digging into my heart.
Having confirmed the watch’s durability by accident, I swallowed back my tears.
*The Item description was telling the truth after all.*
Some truths were unbearably cruel.
Right now, this pocket watch was one of them.
*But why would the System give me something like this?*
This wasn’t some ordinary Quest.
It was the Reward I’d received for completing an entire Update, and it was garbage like this.
Clinging to one last sliver of hope, I examined the watch again.
All I found was more reason to despair.
*This thing really is broken.*
For starters, the time was completely wrong.
It was already nearing midnight, but the hour hand pointed somewhere around five.
Even that was only a guess—the numbers that ought to have been there were missing.
*And where the hell did the minute hand go?*
At this point, I wasn’t sure I could even call it a pocket watch.
Pocket time?
Pocket piece?
Even those seemed too generous.
*I can’t adjust the time, either.
And it doesn’t seem to keep moving.
What the hell is this thing?*
I shook it this way and that, then held it close to my ear.
There wasn’t so much as a tick—not even the faint noise of parts moving inside.
It had exactly one advantage.
I couldn’t crush it no matter how hard I squeezed, or even leave a scratch.
*Did they give it to me as a weapon?
Or a shield for emergencies?*
A familiar scene from a war movie flashed through my mind.
A sharp gunshot rang out.
Private Johnson collapsed.
Certain their comrade was dead, his squadmates rushed over.
But what they found was a bullet lodged in the little Bible that the devout Private Johnson always carried over his heart...
“Wow.
It’s already driving me insane.”
Hyuk Mujin, who’d been watching me warily for a while, cautiously spoke up.
“Um, Captain?”
“Don’t call me in that sly, eunuch-like voice.
I’ll kill you.
Seriously.”
“Yes, sir.
May I ask you something?”
“Spit it out.”
“Um... are you going to throw that away?”
Hyuk Mujin pointed discreetly at the pocket watch in my palm, then went on as though he were making casual conversation.
“If you are, I’d like to humbly suggest giving it to someone who’s your right arm, your heart, and unwaveringly loyal to you.”
“Was that supposed to be humble?
You sound pretty confident.”
“Well, I’m just saying.
If you’re not going to use it, there’s no reason to keep it.”
“Why the hell do you want this thing?”
“It’s a watch, isn’t it?
And judging by the look of it, it’s a rare item from the Western Regions.
Even if it’s broken, wouldn’t it look good to carry around?”
Hyuk Mujin made a surprisingly coherent argument.
I smacked my lips.
*I guess it wouldn’t really matter if I gave it to him...*
But something about it bothered me, like a fish bone stuck in my throat.
If I handed this godforsaken pocket watch to Hyuk Mujin right now, I’d feel even less satisfied than I would eating fried rice at a Chinese restaurant without a bowl of spicy jjambbong broth.
*There might be something I don’t know about it yet.
I can wait and see.
If it really is junk, I can give it to him then.*
It wasn’t as if the System always gave out incredible Rewards.
I didn’t know exactly how it decided what to hand out, but I’d received plenty of useless junk Items from the countless Quests I’d completed.
Little by little, enough had piled up in my Inventory to fill a truck.
The one thing I couldn’t get past was that the broken pocket watch in my hand was a Reward for completing an Update.
“Hmm.”
I nodded without saying anything.
Then Hyuk Mujin’s sly voice reached my ear again.
“Um, Captain?”
“What?”
“Could you say something...?”
“Not yet.
Wait a little.
A month—no, fifteen days.”
Fifteen days.
Half a month.
That was the final trial period I’d settled on.
Hyuk Mujin’s face lit up.
“So you’ll give it to me in fifteen days?”
“Yeah.
Assuming I’ve confirmed it’s useless to me.”
“Come on.
It came from the Western Regions.
There probably isn’t a craftsman around here who can fix it.
At most, you could carry it because it looks pretty.”
Hyuk Mujin grinned unpleasantly as he went on.
“But what do you call it?”
“Pocket-watch, shi—pocket watch.”
“Wow.
Even the name’s pretty.
Thread a leather cord through that ring and wear it around your neck.
You’d draw eyes wherever you went.”
“Yeah?”
“Yes.
Shiny silk would look even better than leather.”
“Oh, yeah?”
It was a suggestion worthy of the eldest grandson of a wealthy textile-merchant family.
It was a good one, too.
Without hesitation, I tore a strip from the gold silk robe I was wearing, threaded it through the ring, and hung the watch around my neck.
“How do I look?
Pretty?”
“Whew.
Is your name Mr.
Golden Sun?
You’re practically glowing.”
“They’d like it if I gave it to them like this, wouldn’t they?”
“Captain, you’d go that far for me...”
Hyuk Mujin’s eyes trembled with emotion.
I gazed fondly at the pocket watch hanging around my neck.
“Not you.
Young Lady Ju.”
“Maybe Young Lady Ju would be less upset if she got a gift like this.
Don’t you think?”
“Answer me.”
“...I’m sure she’d love it.
Yes.”
His eyes went cold in an instant.
As Hyuk Mujin silently berated me with his gaze, I sensed dozens of people approaching the pavilion.
I leaned out the window.
“Stop!
Stop!
Stop!
Move and I’ll cut you down.
Pocket!”
At the head of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, their torches flickering, Jeong Hogun fell silent for a moment before replying.
“What nonsense are you talking about?”
“You stupid, useless Embroidered Uniform Guard bastard!
You showed up without even learning the password!”
“No, I mean, what is this all of a sudden...?”
“Shut up!
Say ‘watch’!
Hurry!”
“...Watch.”
“I said shut up!”
His eyes were full of venom, like an angry pufferfish.
I supposed I’d better stop messing with him.
Generously letting him off the hook, I asked Jeong Hogun, who’d clamped his mouth shut, “So, why are you here?”
“You need to come with me for a moment.”
“Am I someone who comes and goes just because you tell me to?
Besides, I’m really busy.
I’ve got a lot to do.”
“His Majesty has summoned you.”
“Oh.”
Then I’d better go.

chapters.title: Chapter 933
paragraphs: I followed Jeong Hogun, taking a careful look around as we went.
I’d expected some dramatic change, but the Imperial Palace looked much the same as it had on my first visit.
Palace attendants in neat uniforms hurried back and forth, while heavily armed Embroidered Uniform Guards stood watch at their posts like iron towers.
If anything had changed, it was me.
*Swish.*
When a group of palace attendants approaching from the other direction bowed deeply as they passed, I thought it was a coincidence.
*Clank.*

Even when the Embroidered Uniform Guards struck their armor and saluted, I didn’t think much of it. Jeong Hogun had considerable pull among the Guard, so it seemed only natural that they’d salute him.
“Guess being a Thousand Captain means you can throw your weight around, huh?”
Jeong Hogun’s reply to my joking remark was utterly calm.
“You’re less observant than you look.”
“Hm?”
“They aren’t paying their respects because I’m here.”
Only then did it hit me. Only then did I see it.
The people passing us were looking at me. The gratitude and respect in their eyes were meant for me alone.
What was I supposed to say?
I was still at a loss for words when Jeong Hogun came to an abrupt halt.
No—not just him. Everyone who’d come with him stopped at the same time.
*Step.*
They moved as one, with a heavy ring of metal.
Jeong Hogun glanced at the plaque reading *Qianqing Palace* a dozen or so jang ahead, then turned to me.
“I don’t know when we’ll see each other again, so I should say this now.”
The sharp eyes beneath his low-pulled helmet softened, curving like a crescent moon.
“It was an honor to fight alongside you, Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung.”
I stared at him, eyes wide.
Jeong Hogun had never bowed to anyone but the Emperor. Now his rigid back and neck inclined toward me as he offered a deeply respectful fist-and-palm salute.
“Until we meet again, I wish you good fortune in battle.”
“We wish you good fortune!”
*Shing! Shing! Shing!*
Dozens of Embroidered Uniform Guards echoed him and drew their swords, gripping them in reverse.
They stood in two neat rows on either side of the path to Qianqing Palace. I couldn’t help laughing.
“Come on, you’re making me blush.”
But I stopped laughing almost at once and returned their salute, bringing my hands together.
“We’ll meet again. We will.”
I meant it. That was enough.
No one knew when we’d meet again. I’d leave everything else until then. Every meeting and every bond came with a parting, after all.
*Step. Step.*
I walked slowly down the path Jeong Hogun and the guards had made for me.
Beneath the high eaves of Qianqing Palace, the twin armed guards were waiting. Thanks to a new scar, I could finally tell their faces apart.
As I climbed the stairs, they quietly stepped aside, as though there were no formalities to observe.
The enormous iron door they guarded stood wide open, unlike the last time I’d visited.
Qianqing Palace stood in the deepest part of the Imperial Palace.
And in the innermost chamber of Qianqing Palace, the Emperor was waiting for me.
“Oh, you’re here.”
His voice was gentler than before, warm with welcome. His eyes were smiling too.
But even faced with such a welcome from the Emperor—a man called Iron Blood for the countless purges and ruthless decisions he’d made since before taking the throne—I didn’t smile.
No. I couldn’t.
*Why?*
I hadn’t said it aloud, but my bewilderment must have shown. The Emperor watched me struggle for words, then gave a quiet laugh and spoke first.
“You seem rather taken aback. Understandable, I suppose, when the Son of Heaven looks like this.”
He tapped the bandages wrapped around his upper body. The faint smile on his lips made his sunken cheeks stand out even more.
“A piece of advice: at times like this, lower your head first.”
He was impossibly gaunt compared to just three days ago. I was still shaken, but I forced myself to reply calmly.
“Is there a reason for that?”
“Two. You can hide your expression, and you buy yourself a moment to think.”
“I see. I might as well try it.”
I lowered my head, then lifted it again less than ten seconds later.
“You’ve already seen my expression, so it’s too late to hide that. But the time to think does help.”
“May I ask what you thought about?”
“Why Your Majesty looks like this. What caused it.”
“A waste of thought. I simply overexerted myself in that battle.”
The Emperor smiled and waved a hand. The smile vanished when he heard my next words.
“So you’ve been smoking poppy again?”
“I was slow to notice. The sight of you caught me off guard, and I didn’t pay attention to the smell.”
I drew a slow breath as I watched his face go rigid. The strong, peculiar scent that reached me was unmistakably the one I remembered.
“How long... have you known?”

His voice had dropped. I thought back to the first time I’d entered Qianqing Palace: the strangely familiar scent I’d noticed when I finally met the Emperor, and the moment someone who occasionally smoked poppy had helped me place it.
“I didn’t know at first.”
“I can’t imagine how you figured it out. It isn’t easy to obtain, and I’ve heard Murim practitioners avoid anything that harms the mind and spirit.”
“You heard right. Murim practitioners generally do.”
I added calmly, “But I hear eunuchs sometimes use it.”
“...Hong Jin, then.”
A wound, once inflicted, has a long shelf life.

Whether it’s psychological or physical, the mind and body remember. Old wounds can still ache decades later, even after the scars have faded. How much worse must it be for eunuchs, who’ve had their private parts cut off?
Hong Jin was no exception. When the pain came without warning and he couldn’t bear it, he turned to poppy. Thanks to him, I’d stumbled onto one of the Emperor’s secrets.
“How long have you been using it? And why?”
“I don’t see why you need to know.”
Before I could respond, the Emperor gave a bitter smile and pointed to his head.
“Besides, nothing I say will change much.”
“...No way.”
He seemed to have already given up. And that gesture had meaning, too.
I stared at him, eyes wide, as he parted his dry lips.
“That’s right. It’s what you’re thinking.”
“The Blood Soul Gu. That cursed poison has reached my very marrow.”
My suspicion hardened into certainty, and a curse escaped me like a groan.
“Damn it.”
“Impertinent. Such vulgar language before the father of all the people? If Commander Baek were here, he’d have you dragged to prison at once.”
Someone else might have trembled and begged forgiveness. I only sighed at the Emperor, who was making a show of frowning.
“Is this really the time for jokes?”
“Have I ever told you I’m good at them?”
“This is the first I’ve heard of it. You’re so bad it gives me goose bumps.”
“That’s because you’re a dull fellow. Back when I was campaigning, I’d drink and laugh with my men every night. Those were good times.”
“I hate to say this to a critically ill man, but you were probably the only one having fun.”
“That can’t be. Every time I said something, they’d laugh until they doubled over.”
“...I see.”
I didn’t know who those men had been, but they must have worked hard to laugh along.
Not that it mattered right now.
I shook my head at the clueless division commander—no, Emperor—and asked what I most wanted to know.
“When did it start?”
“More than ten years ago. Just after the coup, to be exact.”
As though there was nothing left to hide, the Emperor continued calmly.
“A loyal servant I trusted did it. By the time I realized, it was too late.”
“Who among Your Majesty’s closest people knows?”
“Only two. Baek Yeon and So Gyo. Though perhaps I should call her the Bow Saint now.”
He looked at me and added, “And today, one more person has learned a truth that must never be known.”
I caught his meaning at once and clicked my tongue.
“Are you going to kill me to keep me quiet?”
“If I tried, would you let me?”
“Not a chance. I’m going to live until I’m so old I’m smearing shit on the walls.”
“Then I’m better off than you. As Emperor, I can’t make such a disgrace of myself.”
He gave a soft chuckle. Then, without warning, he coughed.
*Cough.*
His golden sleeve stained red. I looked around, my face hardening at the sudden spitting of blood, but the Emperor shook his head before I could move.
“Don’t bother.”
“Bother with what?”
“If you’re thinking of calling an imperial physician, don’t.”
“If they could cure this, I’d have done something about it long ago. Why do you think I hid it even from them?”
The Emperor gazed at his blood-soaked sleeve and murmured as if to himself.

“My father and mother. My three elder brothers. The senior members of the imperial family who worked so faithfully to uphold the ancestral shrines and the state... Not one was spared. None escaped death.”
He was right. No one had escaped the Blood Soul Gu’s grasp.

That was why his attempt to set everything right after the coup had failed. The late Emperor, the Empress, and several direct members of the imperial family, including the Crown Prince, had died one after another. The Fourth Prince who’d started the coup had been branded an unforgivable, unfilial son and a usurper.
“I have no regrets left. I took every elixir I could to stay alive and trained in martial arts at a bone-grinding pace to withstand the Blood Soul Gu’s poison. I held on like that for ten years.”
At last, I understood why he—the man who held the greatest territory in the world and commanded countless troops—had reached his current realm.
“After enduring a winter of more than ten years, spring has finally come. That’s enough for me.”
At that moment, a clear smile rested on the Emperor’s lips.

chapters.title: Chapter 934
paragraphs: Winter comes for everyone.
But the winter one man—an emperor, or rather a man named Zhu Di—had to endure was exceptionally harsh.
More than ten long years.

For all that time, long enough for the world to change beyond recognition, he fought illness. He had to learn martial arts just to stay alive, and with the blades of rebellion lurking on every side, not a single day passed when he could sleep easy.
*Spring, regained after such a long wait.*
The Emperor smiled bitterly.
At last, the long winter had ended and warm spring had come. Yet he still shivered with cold.
“I was prepared for this. Have been for a long time. So...”
The Emperor murmured the words calmly, then fixed his gaze on the young man before him.
“You don’t need to look at me like that.”
Someone had once said there was beauty in the sight of a person who had given their all.
But there was nothing beautiful about someone wasting away after giving everything they had.
The sight stirred only a bitter feeling that was hard to name.
That was the look in the eyes of the young man staring at the Emperor now: Jin Taekyung.
“How much time do you have left?”
“That’s a question for the heavens.”
“This isn’t the time for jokes.”
“Did it sound like a joke?”
“Even making it this far is a miracle. If I hadn’t learned martial arts, and if I hadn’t had the help of Baek Yeon and the Bow Saint, I’d already be dead.”
The vitality and physical strength of a Supreme Peak master were beyond comparison with those of ordinary people.
That was why the Emperor had learned martial arts—not to become stronger for its own sake, but solely to survive.
He had to grow stronger to resist the Blood Soul Gu’s poison.
But even the precious time he had bought himself was now drawing to a close.
“Not long ago, I found myself wondering something. If I’d been born with martial talent like yours, perhaps I could’ve completely suppressed the Blood Soul Gu.”
“Don’t talk like you’re helpless. Making it this far is already incredible. If you don’t give up and keep working at it...”
“Do you really believe that? Honestly, without the slightest bit of pity or a single lie?”
Jin Taekyung was at a loss for words. The Emperor continued, his voice calm.
“I don’t need half-hearted comfort. I know reality better than anyone.”
Despite having been taught by two peerless masters—the Bow Saint and Baek Yeon—and having absorbed all manner of elixirs, he had only reached the early stage of Supreme Peak.

Of course, the Blood Soul Gu’s poison had made learning martial arts no easy task. But the fact that even bone-deep effort and the finest possible conditions hadn’t brought him any further meant one thing.
A limit.
This was as far as he could go.
The Emperor had neither the talent to break through the enormous wall in front of him nor the time to do it.
*Ka-koff. Koff.*
The Emperor’s complexion was pale as he let out a series of small coughs. That was when Jin Taekyung’s quiet voice reached him.
“What if there’s still... a chance?”
“A chance.”
It was a word he hadn’t heard in a long time.
And the Emperor already knew what Taekyung meant by it.
“It’s too soon to give up.”
“Yes, I suppose you could think that. You trust the Divine Physician that much.”
“Now that I think about it, there were three of you, not two. Three people who knew about my condition.”
At the sight of Jin Taekyung frozen with wide eyes, the Emperor gave a quiet laugh.
“He came to see me three days ago.”
Taekyung fell silent.
There was no need to ask how the examination had gone. Everything the Emperor had said and done until now was proof enough.
“He said it was too late. He shook his head and said there was nothing he could do for me right now.”
It was the judgment of the Divine Physician, whose medical skill was the greatest under heaven.
Unless the Great Firmament Immortal himself intervened, it was as good as confirmation that no human being could overcome this illness.
“And yet, all of a sudden, I felt ridiculous.”
The Emperor continued with a bitter smile.
“I thought I’d prepared myself and accepted everything long ago. But when the Divine Physician confirmed it, I felt as though a part of my chest had gone hollow.”
At last, spring had come.
No—he had reclaimed spring.
He had lived fiercely, and he wanted to keep doing so.
But he didn’t have much time left.
“Earlier, I told you I had no regrets left. That I was content.”
Taekyung finally spoke.
“I know. I knew you didn’t mean it.”
“Yes. You’re right. It was all a complete lie.”
The Emperor breathed heavily.

“There’s... so much I have to take care of before I die.”
The Emperor knew.
The spring he’d fought so hard to reclaim, its warmth, was only a passing spring breeze—a brief respite.
Before long, a cold frost would fall over the land and cover it all.
“There will be a war. One more brutal and vast than any before it.”
The calm before the storm.
Four characters that described the present situation more accurately than anything else.
And the weight of that coming storm would fall on whoever stood as ruler of the continent after the Emperor.
“Bao’er.”
One name slipped from the Emperor’s dry lips.
Prince Shangshan. No—the Imperial Younger Brother, Zhu Bao.
His last lingering attachment, the one who made him look back again and again as he neared the end of his life. His own flesh and blood, so precious he could never bear to see him hurt.
The little boy who wasn’t here had become a great boulder pressing down on the Emperor’s chest.

But peace had already been broken.
To survive the flames of war that would sweep across the continent, the boy would have to become a conqueror, not a sage king.
“That burden will be too much for him.”
The Emperor knew better than anyone how heavy and overwhelming the title *Son of Heaven* could be.
Perhaps by the heavens’ grace, his youngest brother had been born with the qualities of a sage king. But he was still far too young.
Too young to rule a nation.
And too young to weather a war.
*I want to live. I still have things to do for that boy, for this country and its people.*
The Emperor said it only in his heart.
He knew reality wouldn’t change no matter how desperately he wished it would, so he swallowed the words. As the ruler, who must never waver, he couldn’t say them aloud.
*What’s the point of lamenting? It’s all futile anyway.*
The Emperor gave a bitter laugh. That was when—
“Did you know?”
Jin Taekyung spoke up without warning, fixing his gaze on the Emperor as he continued.
“There are two main ways to piss someone off. The first is to start saying something and then stop, and the second is...”
His voice trailed off, and silence followed.
The Emperor waited patiently for the rest. Then he couldn’t hold back any longer.
“The second is what?”
“Hm?”
“I asked what the second one is.”
“Oh, that.”
Taekyung blinked as though he’d just remembered something he’d forgotten long ago, then scratched his chin.
“I just won’t tell you. Let’s move on.”
“...What?”
“What does it matter? You didn’t finish what you were saying, either.”
“What are you talking about—”
The Emperor was so dumbfounded he was about to continue, but Taekyung spoke first.
“Just be honest. Say you want to live.”
“Is that so hard?”
The Emperor’s pupils trembled.
It wasn’t because of Taekyung’s outrageous disrespect.
It was the embarrassment of having the truth he’d kept so tightly hidden laid bare, as if he’d been stripped naked.
“I am... the Son of Heaven.”
“So what? The Son of Heaven isn’t a person?”
“That’s enough!”
The Emperor’s low shout didn’t faze Taekyung. His words came in a rush.

“When someone says something hurtful, it hurts. When you get cut by a blade, you bleed. When you’re facing a hard reality, you lose heart. It’s the same for everyone. What’s different about wearing golden silk embroidered with dragons and looking down on all the civil and military officials?”
“You said you didn’t need half-hearted comfort. Fine. I won’t give you any. But you need to be more honest, too. Forget being the Emperor or anything else—just act like a person for a little while.”
The Emperor, his face clouded with confusion, wondered to himself:
Why had he summoned Jin Taekyung here today? Why had he let out thoughts he’d never shared with anyone?
And why, after such insolence, did he feel no anger?
Then he let out a quiet laugh.
“Do you know something?”
“I don’t. Except that you’re feeling better than I expected.”
“But I haven’t even said anything yet.”
“That’s why I said I don’t know. I’d have to hear it to know. How could I know if I haven’t heard it?”
“Ha! Ha-ha-ha!”
The Emperor suddenly burst into loud laughter. Before long, he coughed up blood and muttered,
“Damn it.”
“I didn’t know you knew how to swear.”
“You said the Son of Heaven was a person, didn’t you?”
“Oh. Yeah, I did.”
“...Still, don’t drop the formalities.”
“I was talking to myself.”
“What do you think would happen if I muttered to myself that you’d just tried to assassinate me?”
“That wouldn’t work. That’d be spreading false information.”
“You made me cough up blood, so it wouldn’t be entirely false.”
“You’ve got a real talent for twisting things.”
“This is getting more and more absurd. Is that any way to speak to the father of all the people and the Emperor of the Great Nation?”
“Dad.”
“What?”
“You said you were a father. If you don’t like me calling you Dad, I’ll call you Mom.”
“What kind of madman are you?”
The Emperor laughed so hard he could barely breathe. Still grinning, he spoke again.
“Do you know what I was about to say a moment ago?”
“You mean the thing I said I didn’t know?”
“That’s right.”
“Not really.”
“We—no, I...”
The Emperor stared at Taekyung, who was still playing coy, then slowly parted his lips.
“I want to live. More desperately than anyone.”
Jin Taekyung grinned.
“Now you sound like a person.”
“But reality hasn’t changed. I didn’t want to make a pitiful spectacle of myself.”
“So, are you crying now?”
“Where did that come from all of a sudden—”
“I cried. Three days ago.”
Despite what he was saying, Taekyung’s voice held a hint of laughter.

“I’m not exaggerating one bit. I bawled my eyes out, with snot running everywhere. I writhed around like a grub and begged the heavens to save me. I told them I still had so much left to do. That there were precious people I absolutely had to see one more time.”
“I must’ve looked too pathetic to bear watching. But I wasn’t ashamed of myself.”
He’d fought to stay alive, and survived.
That was how he’d been given a second chance. How he’d ended up here.
“You don’t need to be ashamed, and you don’t need to despair.”
Jin Taekyung held out his hand to the Emperor.
“I’ll save you, one way or another.”

chapters.title: Chapter 935
paragraphs: “I heard Jin Taekyung came by.”
The Emperor sat alone in his vast bedchamber, lost in thought. The man’s sudden voice didn’t startle him.
Baek Yeon was one of the very few—perhaps the only person—who could come and go anywhere in Qianqing Palace without asking permission.
“You’re a step too late, Baek Yeon. He left half a shichen ago.”
“That doesn’t matter. I came to see Your Majesty.”
At Commander Baek Yeon’s calm reply, the Emperor affected a frown.
“I’d rather you hadn’t. I’ve seen enough of your face already.”
“Then have you been well these past three days?”
“What kind of question is that? It’s been a relief not having a nag around.”
“I’m hurt.”
“Don’t sulk. Someone who used to watch me day and night is in much the same position as you.”
“No Shadow would be even more hurt if he heard that.”
“That’s why I’m saying it while he’s away. He’s no longer my bodyguard, so I can talk behind his back now and then.”
“Well. There’s no winning against Your Majesty.”
Baek Yeon shook his head in defeat, and the Emperor gave a quiet laugh.
“So, is Bao’er doing well?”
“Of course. He couldn’t be better.”
But the worry didn’t leave the Emperor’s face.
“He’s been through so much at such a young age. His mind and body must still be unsettled. Stay by his side.”
Baek Yeon heard the concern in his voice. He understood it, too.

The Emperor’s own flesh and blood had returned after more than a decade. Though it had been for the boy’s safety, his youngest brother had, in effect, been left on his own. No amount of love or worry could feel like enough now.
Why else would the Emperor have assigned both No Shadow, his hidden bodyguard, and Baek Yeon, his closest confidant, directly to the Imperial Younger Brother?
*Look after the boy. I can trust you two with him.*
Remembering the request the Emperor had made three days ago—a request, not an order—Baek Yeon spoke.
“His Highness isn’t even fifteen yet, but of everyone I’ve met, only one person has a stronger, more upright spirit. It’s hard to believe he’s so young.”
“Only one?”
“Your Majesty.”
The answer came without hesitation. For a moment, the Emperor was at a loss for words. Then he raised both hands.
“I concede. Flattery from you, of all people. You’ve changed, Baek Yeon.”
“That’s true. Much like how Your Majesty has started making jokes.”
“Come now. I said I conceded. Enough nonsense.”
“Did what I just said sound like flattery or nonsense?”
Baek Yeon smiled faintly.
“I meant it. I’ve always admired and respected Your Majesty. Others would have given up on that thorn-covered road many times over, but you kept going, even with your feet covered in blood.”
The sincerity in his words left the Emperor silent.
Something welled up and caught in his throat. For the moment, he could barely speak. He fought the feeling down and forced out a reply.
“If I’d had to walk that road alone, I would have given up along the way. I couldn’t have done it without you all.”
“I don’t believe that.”
Baek Yeon shook his head and continued slowly.
“We could trust and follow you because you were who you are. This day was only possible because Your Majesty bore the greatest responsibility and the greatest pain.”

“Even while watching for traitors hiding their blades, did you ever neglect the affairs of state? I watched you sacrifice sleep to practice martial arts, handle petitions, and fight your illness—all at once.”
A jumble of emotions crossed the Emperor’s face.
Yes. That was how it had been. There had been days when it could be no other way.
“It was only natural. Sleep was a luxury.”
For more than ten years, he had never slept more than one shichen a day.
No—even that sleep had never been peaceful. He had to keep his mind alert while he felt his body slowly dying.

That was what it meant to be the Son of Heaven. From the highest position under heaven, he had to face the fiercest storms before anyone else, while watching over and caring for all that lay beneath him.
That was how the Emperor saw his duty. And it was why Baek Yeon respected him so deeply.
“Deciding to do something is as easy as turning over your hand. Following through is as hard as moving a mountain.”
At first, Baek Yeon hadn’t been certain either.
Could the Great Nation’s fourth prince, their last remaining choice, join them in their great undertaking? Was he fit to hold the Son of Heaven’s absolute power?
But he had proved himself. Better than anyone.

Though the Imperial treasury was piled high with mountains of gold and silver, he had always lived frugally. Though peerlessly beautiful women had been presented before him, he had never indulged in women. He had even chosen not to produce an heir, for fear of putting his youngest brother in danger.

That way, Dark Heaven couldn’t harm Zhu Bao. They couldn’t recklessly kill a child with the legitimacy to replace the Emperor, nor could they inject him with Blood Soul Gu, which would swiftly kill its host.
“Every one of the things Your Majesty considered only natural was anything but.”
The Emperor’s eyelids trembled at Baek Yeon’s quiet words.
He hadn’t known. He hadn’t known Baek Yeon thought of him that way.
Looking back over the road he’d traveled, the Emperor realized he wasn’t the only one who had kept his true feelings hidden. Baek Yeon had, too.
“I... don’t know what to say.”
At the strain in the Emperor’s voice, Baek Yeon let out a hearty laugh.
“You don’t have to say anything.”
“Shouldn’t I say something?”
“I’m not sure. It might only make things more awkward.”
The Emperor shook his head, then clicked his tongue.
“Baek Yeon, are you really the man I’ve always known?”
“What on earth do you mean?”
“Do you have to ask? You’ve always been merciless.”
“Are you talking about when you were learning martial arts?”
“I am. You said, ‘Please forgive me for laying hands on Your Majesty’s precious body,’ then proceeded to beat me all over.”
“Why bring that up all of a sudden?”
Baek Yeon frowned at the unexpected reminder.
“And as I told you then, you improve at martial arts by getting hit. So Gyo... I mean, the Bow Saint agreed with me, didn’t she?”
“She did. The two of you even teamed up to beat me later. It hurt so much I spent ages wondering whether to quit on the spot.”
“Did I threaten you with a sword? You were the one who asked me to teach you.”

“And there’s the way you speak to me. Whenever I struggled, you’d come by and lay into me without fail. You’d even use the familiar *hao* form, as if you’d forgotten how one addresses the Son of Heaven.”
“That was...”
Baek Yeon trailed off and glanced away at the empty air.

He could excuse laying hands on the Emperor during martial arts training as part of teaching him. This was different. Even if he had meant to encourage the Emperor, some of the things he’d said and done had been anything but proper conduct for a subject.
“Your Majesty, I—”
“Don’t pretend you’ve forgotten. You were doing it until quite recently. Only a few days after Bao’er entered the palace, you came to me and gave me a thorough tongue-lashing.”
“You were taking poppy with our great undertaking so close at hand. I was afraid it would ruin your mind and body.”

“What does that have to do with using the familiar form of address? I’d been bedridden and suffering for days, and had only just recovered some strength. I had to take poppy to ease the pain, even a little.”
“I know. I knew then, too, but I was worried about you, Your Majesty.”
Baek Yeon kept speaking while his eyes wandered over the empty space ahead of him. Then he fell silent.
At the edge of his vision, he’d caught the Emperor smiling.
“Do you concede defeat?”
Baek Yeon realized the Emperor had been teasing him all along and sighed.
“I do.”
“That makes one victory for you and two for me.”
“Are you keeping score?”
“I was once a general like you. What matters more to a general than victory or defeat?”
At the sight of the Emperor laughing with evident delight, Baek Yeon couldn’t help joining in with a hearty laugh.
What else mattered? If the Emperor was happy, that was enough.
Three days ago, his face had been shadowed by approaching death. Now it shone as brightly as the full moon. That was what mattered to Baek Yeon.
And yet part of him felt bitter.
The Emperor looked as though he had already accepted, deep down, the death awaiting him. Baek Yeon could do nothing but look at him and laugh along.
*I know why you sent No Shadow and me to His Highness.*
It wasn’t only to guard against some unforeseen danger and protect the Emperor’s only brother and heir.
The Emperor was preparing for what would come after his death. Before it was too late, he was handing his loyal retainers and his power base over to Imperial Younger Brother Zhu Bao.
Yet in the past three days, he hadn’t shown his face once to the brother he loved so dearly.
*You don’t want him to see you like this.*
For brothers reunited after more than a decade, the coming death would not be a parting for the Emperor alone.
Zhu Bao, the Great Nation’s new heir, would have to endure it too. Just when he had finally come to know the love and sincerity of family, he would have to let go of his only blood relative.
The Emperor must have known. He needed to tell his brother to prepare for their parting, but he was afraid to face the boy’s grief. So he stayed away.
*...I see.*
Baek Yeon forced the corners of his mouth back up. Not wanting to spoil the Emperor’s brief happiness, he spoke as brightly as he could.
“By the way, something good must have happened today. Did Jin Taekyung bring you some amusing news?”
“Amusing news? He did.”
“I’d like to hear it.”
“It’s nothing much.”
The Emperor smiled as he added the next words. Baek Yeon’s smile vanished.
“He said he’d save me. One way or another.”
“It was amusing. He knows nothing about medicine, yet he made such a bold promise. But Baek Yeon, do you know what’s even more amusing?”
The Emperor didn’t wait for an answer.
“Those few absurd words made me feel hopeful.”
It was strange. How could Jin Taekyung promise such a thing with such certainty on his face, such a gleam in his eyes?
The Emperor had enjoyed seeing him like that. He was grateful, too. That irreverent martial artist was determined to save a life the Emperor himself had given up on.
But the reality as the Emperor knew it remained cold.
*It’s probably impossible.*
How cruel hope could be to someone facing a death already foretold.
He had folded that brief hope away and tucked it deep in his heart. For now, he simply wanted to speak to his loyal subject with a lighter heart.
“You look troubled. I’m fine, Baek Yeon. Don’t worry about me.”
“But if word of this gets out...”
The Emperor smiled at Baek Yeon’s worried look and waved a hand.

sentences.text: “I heard Jin Taekyung came by.”
The Emperor sat alone in his vast bedchamber, lost in thought.
The man’s sudden voice didn’t startle him.
Baek Yeon was one of the very few—perhaps the only person—who could come and go anywhere in Qianqing Palace without asking permission.
“You’re a step too late, Baek Yeon.
He left half a shichen ago.”
“That doesn’t matter.
I came to see Your Majesty.”
At Commander Baek Yeon’s calm reply, the Emperor affected a frown.
“I’d rather you hadn’t.
I’ve seen enough of your face already.”
“Then have you been well these past three days?”
“What kind of question is that?
It’s been a relief not having a nag around.”
“I’m hurt.”
“Don’t sulk.
Someone who used to watch me day and night is in much the same position as you.”
“No Shadow would be even more hurt if he heard that.”
“That’s why I’m saying it while he’s away.
He’s no longer my bodyguard, so I can talk behind his back now and then.”
“Well.
There’s no winning against Your Majesty.”
Baek Yeon shook his head in defeat, and the Emperor gave a quiet laugh.
“So, is Bao’er doing well?”
“Of course.
He couldn’t be better.”
But the worry didn’t leave the Emperor’s face.
“He’s been through so much at such a young age.
His mind and body must still be unsettled.
Stay by his side.”
Baek Yeon heard the concern in his voice.
He understood it, too.
The Emperor’s own flesh and blood had returned after more than a decade.
Though it had been for the boy’s safety, his youngest brother had, in effect, been left on his own.
No amount of love or worry could feel like enough now.
Why else would the Emperor have assigned both No Shadow, his hidden bodyguard, and Baek Yeon, his closest confidant, directly to the Imperial Younger Brother?
*Look after the boy.
I can trust you two with him.*
Remembering the request the Emperor had made three days ago—a request, not an order—Baek Yeon spoke.
“His Highness isn’t even fifteen yet, but of everyone I’ve met, only one person has a stronger, more upright spirit.
It’s hard to believe he’s so young.”
“Only one?”
“Your Majesty.”
The answer came without hesitation.
For a moment, the Emperor was at a loss for words.
Then he raised both hands.
“I concede.
Flattery from you, of all people.
You’ve changed, Baek Yeon.”
“That’s true.
Much like how Your Majesty has started making jokes.”
“Come now.
I said I conceded.
Enough nonsense.”
“Did what I just said sound like flattery or nonsense?”
Baek Yeon smiled faintly.
“I meant it.
I’ve always admired and respected Your Majesty.
Others would have given up on that thorn-covered road many times over, but you kept going, even with your feet covered in blood.”
The sincerity in his words left the Emperor silent.
Something welled up and caught in his throat.
For the moment, he could barely speak.
He fought the feeling down and forced out a reply.
“If I’d had to walk that road alone, I would have given up along the way.
I couldn’t have done it without you all.”
“I don’t believe that.”
Baek Yeon shook his head and continued slowly.
“We could trust and follow you because you were who you are.
This day was only possible because Your Majesty bore the greatest responsibility and the greatest pain.”
“Even while watching for traitors hiding their blades, did you ever neglect the affairs of state?
I watched you sacrifice sleep to practice martial arts, handle petitions, and fight your illness—all at once.”
A jumble of emotions crossed the Emperor’s face.
Yes.
That was how it had been.
There had been days when it could be no other way.
“It was only natural.
Sleep was a luxury.”
For more than ten years, he had never slept more than one shichen a day.
No—even that sleep had never been peaceful.
He had to keep his mind alert while he felt his body slowly dying.
That was what it meant to be the Son of Heaven.
From the highest position under heaven, he had to face the fiercest storms before anyone else, while watching over and caring for all that lay beneath him.
That was how the Emperor saw his duty.
And it was why Baek Yeon respected him so deeply.
“Deciding to do something is as easy as turning over your hand.
Following through is as hard as moving a mountain.”
At first, Baek Yeon hadn’t been certain either.
Could the Great Nation’s fourth prince, their last remaining choice, join them in their great undertaking?
Was he fit to hold the Son of Heaven’s absolute power?
But he had proved himself.
Better than anyone.
Though the Imperial treasury was piled high with mountains of gold and silver, he had always lived frugally.
Though peerlessly beautiful women had been presented before him, he had never indulged in women.
He had even chosen not to produce an heir, for fear of putting his youngest brother in danger.
That way, Dark Heaven couldn’t harm Zhu Bao.
They couldn’t recklessly kill a child with the legitimacy to replace the Emperor, nor could they inject him with Blood Soul Gu, which would swiftly kill its host.
“Every one of the things Your Majesty considered only natural was anything but.”
The Emperor’s eyelids trembled at Baek Yeon’s quiet words.
He hadn’t known.
He hadn’t known Baek Yeon thought of him that way.
Looking back over the road he’d traveled, the Emperor realized he wasn’t the only one who had kept his true feelings hidden.
Baek Yeon had, too.
“I... don’t know what to say.”
At the strain in the Emperor’s voice, Baek Yeon let out a hearty laugh.
“You don’t have to say anything.”
“Shouldn’t I say something?”
“I’m not sure.
It might only make things more awkward.”
The Emperor shook his head, then clicked his tongue.
“Baek Yeon, are you really the man I’ve always known?”
“What on earth do you mean?”
“Do you have to ask?
You’ve always been merciless.”
“Are you talking about when you were learning martial arts?”
“I am.
You said, ‘Please forgive me for laying hands on Your Majesty’s precious body,’ then proceeded to beat me all over.”
“Why bring that up all of a sudden?”
Baek Yeon frowned at the unexpected reminder.
“And as I told you then, you improve at martial arts by getting hit.
So Gyo...
I mean, the Bow Saint agreed with me, didn’t she?”
“She did.
The two of you even teamed up to beat me later.
It hurt so much I spent ages wondering whether to quit on the spot.”
“Did I threaten you with a sword?
You were the one who asked me to teach you.”
“And there’s the way you speak to me.
Whenever I struggled, you’d come by and lay into me without fail.
You’d even use the familiar *hao* form, as if you’d forgotten how one addresses the Son of Heaven.”
“That was...”
Baek Yeon trailed off and glanced away at the empty air.
He could excuse laying hands on the Emperor during martial arts training as part of teaching him.
This was different.
Even if he had meant to encourage the Emperor, some of the things he’d said and done had been anything but proper conduct for a subject.
“Your Majesty, I—”
“Don’t pretend you’ve forgotten.
You were doing it until quite recently.
Only a few days after Bao’er entered the palace, you came to me and gave me a thorough tongue-lashing.”
“You were taking poppy with our great undertaking so close at hand.
I was afraid it would ruin your mind and body.”
“What does that have to do with using the familiar form of address?
I’d been bedridden and suffering for days, and had only just recovered some strength.
I had to take poppy to ease the pain, even a little.”
“I know.
I knew then, too, but I was worried about you, Your Majesty.”
Baek Yeon kept speaking while his eyes wandered over the empty space ahead of him.
Then he fell silent.
At the edge of his vision, he’d caught the Emperor smiling.
“Do you concede defeat?”
Baek Yeon realized the Emperor had been teasing him all along and sighed.
“I do.”
“That makes one victory for you and two for me.”
“Are you keeping score?”
“I was once a general like you.
What matters more to a general than victory or defeat?”
At the sight of the Emperor laughing with evident delight, Baek Yeon couldn’t help joining in with a hearty laugh.
What else mattered?
If the Emperor was happy, that was enough.
Three days ago, his face had been shadowed by approaching death.
Now it shone as brightly as the full moon.
That was what mattered to Baek Yeon.
And yet part of him felt bitter.
The Emperor looked as though he had already accepted, deep down, the death awaiting him.
Baek Yeon could do nothing but look at him and laugh along.
*I know why you sent No Shadow and me to His Highness.*
It wasn’t only to guard against some unforeseen danger and protect the Emperor’s only brother and heir.
The Emperor was preparing for what would come after his death.
Before it was too late, he was handing his loyal retainers and his power base over to Imperial Younger Brother Zhu Bao.
Yet in the past three days, he hadn’t shown his face once to the brother he loved so dearly.
*You don’t want him to see you like this.*
For brothers reunited after more than a decade, the coming death would not be a parting for the Emperor alone.
Zhu Bao, the Great Nation’s new heir, would have to endure it too.
Just when he had finally come to know the love and sincerity of family, he would have to let go of his only blood relative.
The Emperor must have known.
He needed to tell his brother to prepare for their parting, but he was afraid to face the boy’s grief.
So he stayed away.
*...I see.*
Baek Yeon forced the corners of his mouth back up.
Not wanting to spoil the Emperor’s brief happiness, he spoke as brightly as he could.
“By the way, something good must have happened today.
Did Jin Taekyung bring you some amusing news?”
“Amusing news?
He did.”
“I’d like to hear it.”
“It’s nothing much.”
The Emperor smiled as he added the next words.
Baek Yeon’s smile vanished.
“He said he’d save me.
One way or another.”
“It was amusing.
He knows nothing about medicine, yet he made such a bold promise.
But Baek Yeon, do you know what’s even more amusing?”
The Emperor didn’t wait for an answer.
“Those few absurd words made me feel hopeful.”
It was strange.
How could Jin Taekyung promise such a thing with such certainty on his face, such a gleam in his eyes?
The Emperor had enjoyed seeing him like that.
He was grateful, too.
That irreverent martial artist was determined to save a life the Emperor himself had given up on.
But the reality as the Emperor knew it remained cold.
*It’s probably impossible.*
How cruel hope could be to someone facing a death already foretold.
He had folded that brief hope away and tucked it deep in his heart.
For now, he simply wanted to speak to his loyal subject with a lighter heart.
“You look troubled.
I’m fine, Baek Yeon.
Don’t worry about me.”
“But if word of this gets out...”
The Emperor smiled at Baek Yeon’s worried look and waved a hand.
“He promised me he wouldn’t tell anyone else.
Jin Taekyung is a man I can trust.”
Jeok Cheongang’s voice was heavy when I finished telling him everything.
“The Emperor’s been poisoned with Blood Soul Gu?”
I nodded without hesitation.
“Yes.”
Promises are made to be broken.

chapters.title: Chapter 936
paragraphs: Jeok Cheongang’s reaction to the truly grave news that the Emperor had been poisoned with Blood Soul Gu was short and to the point.
“That must hurt.”
“What? Am I wrong?”
“Well, no, but it’s a little more serious than *hurting*.”
Anyone listening would think the Emperor had a cold instead of Blood Soul Gu.
Jeok Cheongang shrugged at my baffled look.
“Same difference. He’s in so much pain he’s at death’s door, isn’t he? Even that needlessly tight-lipped quack can’t cure him.”
At the sudden jab, the Divine Physician—who’d looked uncomfortable throughout my account—spoke up.
“The patient told me not to inform anyone until he spoke of it himself. I merely respected his wishes. And why am I a quack?”
“If a physician can’t cure an illness, he’s a quack. Take that Divine Physician name tag off today.”
“I never put one on. It wasn’t mine to begin with.”
“Since we’re on the subject, let me ask you something. What if...”
“I know what you’re thinking, but even if my master came, it wouldn’t change anything.”
I’d wanted to ask the same thing. The Divine Physician had answered a beat before I could, calmly and firmly.
“Blood Soul Gu... is unlike any of the deadly poisons known to us. It’s almost as if it was created solely to kill its host.”
Jeok Cheongang gave a low groan.
“You mean there’s no antidote?”
“Poison and medicine come from much the same root. There must be a way to treat it. The problem is time.”
He was right. The Emperor was dying even now.
Three days ago, just after the battle in the grand banquet hall, he’d looked unusually exhausted. I hadn’t imagined it.
“From what I’ve seen, his vitality is already at its limit. I can’t even guarantee he’ll last another couple of months.”
For the Divine Physician to say that meant the poison had advanced beyond anything elixirs or internal energy could hold back.
Like a jar full of holes that wouldn’t fill no matter how much water you poured into it, the Emperor’s life force was draining away fast.
*At this rate, he’ll die before long. If the Emperor dies suddenly, the Great Nation will be thrown into chaos.*
Personal feelings aside, the Emperor couldn’t die.
He’d borne every kind of disgrace and ruled the Great Nation for over ten years without any serious unrest.
And he’d held on to the throne despite the powerful opposition led by the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord. That alone showed what an exceptional ruler he was.
*I have to save him. For what’s coming, if nothing else.*
I’d heard that outside the palace, things were already boiling like a cauldron over hot coals.
Two days before I woke up, the Emperor had carried out another large-scale purge, then posted hundreds of proclamations across the Imperial Capital.
The huge sheets, clearly stamped with the Imperial Seal, laid out the whole truth in detail.
They also carried the Emperor’s declaration that he would crush the vile traitors known as Dark Heaven.
*The war is about to begin.*
No—it had already begun.
The Emperor’s resolve was clear, and the people’s anger toward Dark Heaven was spreading like wildfire.
To them, Dark Heaven was an outside enemy threatening their homes and their lives. No one wanted war, but they had to fight to protect the peace.
And this war needed someone to lead them all.
A powerful leader, cool-headed and thorough, with the authority to push through bold decisions when necessary.
Experience on many battlefields would make that leader all the better.
“What do you intend to do, Young Master Jin?”
I answered the Divine Physician’s grave question calmly.
“We have to save him somehow.”
“But we have no way to do that. As I said, there isn’t enough time.”
“That’s all right. The method I’m going to try probably won’t take long.”
“You sound quite certain... Do you have a plan I don’t know about?”
“I do. A brilliant one.”
Jeok Cheongang, who’d been listening in silence, suddenly widened his eyes.
“Wait. This plan of yours...”
“It’s what you’re thinking.”
“I’d forgotten all about it. Yes, that treasure changes everything.”
Jeok Cheongang tapped his forehead. Only then did the Divine Physician blink in apparent surprise.
“Don’t tell me you have the Myriad-Poison Ring in mind?”
“Of course. What else?”
At his low sigh, I gave a short laugh and continued.
“Even against Blood Soul Gu, the Myriad-Poison Ring gives us a good chance. No—it can definitely cure him.”
The ring had absorbed even the Formless Ultimate Poison that had once threatened Jeok Cheongang, and without much difficulty.
The Divine Physician had treated Jeok Cheongang alongside the Slaughter Saint back then. He knew better than anyone what the ring could do, so it was strange that he hadn’t thought of it until now.
“I guess you’ve had a lot on your mind, given the circumstances. I understand. It happens.”
“Y-Young Master Jin.”
“It’s fine. As you know, I left it with Prince Shangshan—or rather, the Imperial Younger Brother. I’ll go get it now. It’ll only take a moment, so you can prepare the treatment while I’m gone.”
“Young Master Jin?”
“Oh, come on. Anyone can forget something now and then. Why are you making such a big deal of it? I’ll be off, then.”
I gave him a friendly smile and turned.
Or I tried to—until I noticed what he was holding.
Wait. What’s that?
I stared at the all-too-familiar ring for a moment before breaking the silence.
“That’s strange. It looks a lot like something I know.”
The Divine Physician gave me a flat look.
“It would.”
“I guess they make incredible knockoffs on this continent. Where’d you buy it?”
“I didn’t buy it.”
“Oh, someone gave it to you as a gift?”
“It wasn’t a gift, either. I borrowed it for a while.”
“From whom?”

“I explained the general situation to His Highness the Imperial Younger Brother. When I said I needed it for something important and had come on your behalf, he handed it over without asking for details.”
My vision swam.
I steadied my breathing and managed to ask, “And that important thing was...?”
“What else? I’ve been to Qianqing Palace twice today.”
“I didn’t hear anything about that from His Majesty...”
“Did he need to?”
“Then the result was...?”
“Just what I told you earlier.”
Silence fell again, heavier and more suffocating than before.
No one ventured to speak. Then Jeok Cheongang’s low voice rang out.
“That plan was so brilliant it plugged up your nose, too.”
Yeah.
What now?

**System Quest Dr. Choi Taekyung** You made a profound impression on the Emperor, who suffers from illness, by promising to treat him. But for someone facing death, nothing is crueler than premature hope. A man’s word is worth a thousand gold. Keep your promise. Remove the Blood Soul Gu lodged in the Emperor’s head and free him from the pain that has tormented him for so many years. If you fail to treat the Emperor... **Grade:** Supreme Peak **Restriction:** Jin Taekyung **Mission:** Successful treatment (Incomplete) **Reward:** ??? **Failure:** ???
I stared at the empty air, then quietly closed the holographic window.
Only one thought filled my head.
*I’m screwed.*
Really screwed.
Who could’ve guessed even the Myriad-Poison Ring wouldn’t work?
No matter how much I pressed him, unable to accept it, the Divine Physician’s answer never changed.
“It failed.”
“But it looked like it was going to work, right?”
“No. It failed.”
“So it almost worked? Missed by a hair?”
“It failed completely. It simply doesn’t work. In fact, the Blood Soul Gu sensed the ring’s energy, felt threatened, and struggled even harder. I still break into a cold sweat thinking about it.”
“Liar. Playing such a nasty prank on me, you little scamp.”
“...Young Master Jin. Would you come over there and speak with me for a moment?”
Something had glinted inside the Divine Physician’s sleeve. When I looked, I saw an acupuncture needle big enough to pierce the sole of an elephant’s foot.
A chill ran down my spine, and I made my way back to my quarters as if fleeing. That had been barely fifteen minutes ago.
*Damn it.*
What had made me bold enough to promise the Emperor he’d be discharged safe and sound?
I’d put all my faith in that overpowered item, the Myriad-Poison Ring. It had dealt with the Formless Ultimate Poison easily enough. Surely it could kill one lousy bug.
And yet.
*I’m screwed.*
Yeah. Screwed.
Worse than screwed.
Forget the quest—the Emperor’s death had to be prevented. But with my last hope, the Myriad-Poison Ring, gone, my vision had gone yellow.
“What the hell... am I supposed to do?”

I stared blankly at the ceiling I’d grown accustomed to, muttering to myself. Then Hyuk Mujin—who seemed to have claimed one corner of the room as his own—came over and patted my shoulder, as if this were only natural.
“It’s all right, Captain. Everything’s all right.”
“Mujin.”
“Yes?”
“Do you even know what the hell you’re talking about?”
“I do.”
Mujin nodded confidently.
“You got dumped by Young Lady Ju, didn’t you?”
“Ah. Guess not. I’m sorry for overstepping.”
When it came to apologizing, he was a Supreme Peak master.
He bowed at the speed of light, then looked wistfully at the pocket watch hanging from my neck.
“But seriously, what happened?”
“Mujin. When you’re talking to someone, look them in the eye. Not at their watch.”
“It gleams so beautifully that I couldn’t help myself.”
I badly wanted to whack him on the back of the head, but I didn’t have the energy.
I let out a long sigh and explained the situation in broad strokes, taking care not to reveal that the Emperor was the person at the center of the story.
“So someone promised to treat a seriously ill person.”
“Yeah.”
“But after making all those grand claims, they have no plan or way to do it.”
Every word hurt.
I flinched and added cautiously, “That’s true, but to be precise, they had a way. Then it was gone.”
“Either way, there’s no way to treat the person now, right?”
“Right.”
“Hmm. Got it.”
Mujin nodded and delivered his judgment in a stern voice.
“What a total piece of shit.”

“Don’t you think so too, Captain? How could someone give that kind of hope to a person who’d only just made peace with dying? With nothing certain to back it up. I don’t know what kind of bastard would...”
He saw me trembling. His voice dropped at once.
“I think he’s a very handsome, dignified, upstanding young man who always gives others hope.”
“...Are you done?”
“...Should I say more?”
*Stop. You’re making me feel worse, you bastard.*
I gave him a sad look, silently telling him to stop, then lowered my head, unable to face Hyuk Mujin.
Tap-tap-tap.
Someone approached at a run. The door opened, and a familiar face appeared.
“I heard it was important, so I took care of it as quickly as I could... Oh my, why’s the mood so grim?”
It was Hong Jin.

If you fail to treat the Emperor... **Grade:** Supreme Peak **Restriction:** Jin Taekyung **Mission:** Successful treatment (Incomplete) **Reward:** ??? **Failure:** ???
I stared at the empty air, then quietly closed the holographic window.
Only one thought filled my head.
*I’m screwed.*
Really screwed.
Who could’ve guessed even the Myriad-Poison Ring wouldn’t work?
No matter how much I pressed him, unable to accept it, the Divine Physician’s answer never changed.
“It failed.”
“But it looked like it was going to work, right?”
“No.
It failed.”
“So it almost worked?
Missed by a hair?”
“It failed completely.
It simply doesn’t work.
In fact, the Blood Soul Gu sensed the ring’s energy, felt threatened, and struggled even harder.
I still break into a cold sweat thinking about it.”
“Liar.
Playing such a nasty prank on me, you little scamp.”
“...Young Master Jin.
Would you come over there and speak with me for a moment?”
Something had glinted inside the Divine Physician’s sleeve.
When I looked, I saw an acupuncture needle big enough to pierce the sole of an elephant’s foot.
A chill ran down my spine, and I made my way back to my quarters as if fleeing.
That had been barely fifteen minutes ago.
*Damn it.*
What had made me bold enough to promise the Emperor he’d be discharged safe and sound?
I’d put all my faith in that overpowered item, the Myriad-Poison Ring.
It had dealt with the Formless Ultimate Poison easily enough.
Surely it could kill one lousy bug.
And yet.
*I’m screwed.*
Yeah.
Screwed.
Worse than screwed.
Forget the quest—the Emperor’s death had to be prevented.
But with my last hope, the Myriad-Poison Ring, gone, my vision had gone yellow.
“What the hell... am I supposed to do?”
I stared blankly at the ceiling I’d grown accustomed to, muttering to myself.
Then Hyuk Mujin—who seemed to have claimed one corner of the room as his own—came over and patted my shoulder, as if this were only natural.
“It’s all right, Captain.
Everything’s all right.”
“Mujin.”
“Yes?”
“Do you even know what the hell you’re talking about?”
“I do.”
Mujin nodded confidently.
“You got dumped by Young Lady Ju, didn’t you?”
“Ah.
Guess not.
I’m sorry for overstepping.”
When it came to apologizing, he was a Supreme Peak master.
He bowed at the speed of light, then looked wistfully at the pocket watch hanging from my neck.
“But seriously, what happened?”
“Mujin.
When you’re talking to someone, look them in the eye.
Not at their watch.”
“It gleams so beautifully that I couldn’t help myself.”
I badly wanted to whack him on the back of the head, but I didn’t have the energy.
I let out a long sigh and explained the situation in broad strokes, taking care not to reveal that the Emperor was the person at the center of the story.
“So someone promised to treat a seriously ill person.”
“Yeah.”
“But after making all those grand claims, they have no plan or way to do it.”
Every word hurt.
I flinched and added cautiously, “That’s true, but to be precise, they had a way.
Then it was gone.”
“Either way, there’s no way to treat the person now, right?”
“Right.”
“Hmm.
Got it.”
Mujin nodded and delivered his judgment in a stern voice.
“What a total piece of shit.”
“Don’t you think so too, Captain?
How could someone give that kind of hope to a person who’d only just made peace with dying?
With nothing certain to back it up.
I don’t know what kind of bastard would...”
He saw me trembling.
His voice dropped at once.
“I think he’s a very handsome, dignified, upstanding young man who always gives others hope.”
“...Are you done?”
“...Should I say more?”
*Stop.
You’re making me feel worse, you bastard.*
I gave him a sad look, silently telling him to stop, then lowered my head, unable to face Hyuk Mujin.
Tap-tap-tap.
Someone approached at a run.
The door opened, and a familiar face appeared.
“I heard it was important, so I took care of it as quickly as I could...
Oh my, why’s the mood so grim?”
It was Hong Jin.

chapters.title: Chapter 937
paragraphs: “I heard it was important, so I took care of it as quickly as I could... Oh my, why’s the mood so grim?”
Hong Jin sensed the tension as soon as he entered the room. I answered with a troubled expression.
“It’s nothing.”
“Nothing? It sure looks like something happened.”
Hong Jin glanced between Hyuk Mujin and me, then murmured, his expression suddenly serious.
“Oh, that’s what it is? Hmm. But there’s nothing you can do about that.”
“It’s all right, so don’t take it too hard. These things happen sometimes. It’s part of life.”
Could Hong Jin know, too?
He was now the East Depot eunuch, so it was entirely possible he knew about the Emperor’s illness.
*Maybe he’d heard something while enthusiastically torturing rebels for the last three days.*
Having reached what seemed like a reasonable conclusion, I cautiously asked, “You already knew?”
Hong Jin hesitated for a moment, then nodded.
“Yeah. I happened to hear.”
“It’s supposed to be top secret... More people know than I expected.”
“Eyes and ears are everywhere. No matter how tightly you try to keep something under wraps, word gets out eventually.”
Fair enough. The Emperor keeping quiet couldn’t protect every secret.
Every incident had victims and perpetrators, and perpetrators had mouths, too.
The rebels who were already dead—or waiting for death.

Some of those who’d passed through Hong Jin’s and the Embroidered Uniform Guard’s hands must have been close aides to the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, and known the Emperor had been poisoned with Blood Soul Gu.
“You must’ve found out while interrogating the prisoners. Which ones knew?”
“What?”
“The prisoners who knew about it. They must have been closely connected to the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord.”
“Uh, well...”
Maybe it was a sensitive subject.
I realized my mistake too late and was about to wave it off when Hong Jin, who’d been blinking quietly, continued.
“I heard it from Taishan.”
“Ah. I see... Wait. Who?”
“Taishan. That huge guy.”
No, something wasn’t right here.
Hyuk Mujin spoke up in my place.
“You mean the Taishan I know?”
“Yeah.”
“Built like a mountain, just like his name?”
“That’s right.”
“Usually an idiot, but smart whenever food comes up?”
“I don’t know about that part.”
“Obsessed with five-spice pork?”
“That part’s definitely true. Actually, some intelligence came in yesterday. According to my men, the imperial cooks tried to poison his food.”
If he was the imperial cooks’ number one assassination target, then it had to be the Taishan I knew.
Utterly confused, I asked, “How would he know about that?”
“How else? He saw it.”
“That can’t be right. He couldn’t have seen it.”
“He said he saw it clearly.”
“...What are you even talking about?”
“...That’s what I’d like to ask you. What’s all this about prisoners and interrogations?”
Hong Jin frowned at me, then went on.
“Weren’t you talking about ‘that thing’ that happened right after Young Master Jin woke up?”
“W-what?”
“You look really unsettled. Is that why? I told you it’s fine, so why are you still worrying? You just have a little more energy than other people.”
Oh, shit.
My vision went dark in an instant, and my whole body trembled.
“How... how did you know?”
“It’s all over the palace. Didn’t you know?”
“It’s all over...?”
“I was away for a while, so I’m one of the last to hear. Less than two shichen after you woke up, half the people in the Inner Palace probably knew.”
I couldn’t breathe. My hands and feet shook, and I felt like I was about to cry.
It was like turning on the TV one day out of boredom and finding a national broadcast channel throwing a wet-dream party for me.
Twitching like I was sick, I barely managed to force the words out.
“Taishan. Bring that bastard here right now.”
Hyuk Mujin, who’d frozen with his mouth hanging open, answered.
“I’m really sorry to say this, but Taishan’s stronger than I am.”
“Bring him here, no matter what!”
“Come on, Captain. You know he tears people apart with both hands.”
“I can tear you apart with one.”
“Ah. Aah.”
Hyuk Mujin let out a brief yelp and dashed out. Sensing the mood turn heavy, Hong Jin spoke with a troubled expression.
“Young Master Jin. Don’t take it so hard.”
For the moment, even my worries about treating the Blood Soul Gu had been driven from my mind.
I groaned at his attempt to comfort me. “Easy for you to say when it’s not happening to you.”
“I told you it’s fine.”
“What’s fine? Have you ever been in a situation like mine?”
At my sharp question, Hong Jin answered with a sad smile.
“Of course not. I had it cut off a long time ago.”
“Just look on the bright side. I’m actually jealous of you, Young Master Jin. Especially during the rainy season, it aches so much down there that sometimes I can barely walk without poppy...”
“Okay, I get it. I get it, so please stop.”
Using his eunuch trump card—one he pulled out whenever he was bored—to shut me up, Hong Jin held out something he’d been carrying and continued.
“I was going to do that anyway. I’m a busy man, too. I only came to hand over the item I was asked to deliver.”
My badly backfired question had snapped me to my senses. Only then did I notice the small iron chest in Hong Jin’s hand and remember why he’d come back.
The mysterious place the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had told me about in his final moments.
The item he’d said to find there.
*This is...*
“It’s an iron chest, as you can see. I don’t know what’s inside or who left it there, though.”
“You didn’t open it?”
“Of course not. I promised you I wouldn’t.”
Hong Jin shrugged and added with a smile, “Besides, I wasn’t sure I could open it.”
He’d said it like a joke, but the moment I took the chest from him, I realized it wasn’t entirely one.
*Ding.*
**System** Very Sturdy Iron Chest acquired. New Item acquired. Would you like to appraise the Item and view its information?
I gave a slight nod, and a translucent holographic window opened between Hong Jin and me.

**System Item Window Very Sturdy Iron Chest Grade:** Peak **Restriction:** None **Description:** An iron chest made by mixing in a small amount of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron. As you’d expect, it’s incredibly durable—perfect for use as a shield or for storing precious belongings. However, it has no fewer than five locks, so using it often may be a bit of a hassle.
I read the text quickly and swallowed a dry laugh.
*Seriously? Even if it’s only a little, why use Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron in an iron chest...?*
Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron was incredibly rare—and filthy expensive to match.

If a reasonably well-known smith used even four nyang of it to forge a weapon, people would call it a fine sword. Use any more than that, and foul-tempered masters with a habit of spitting would descend on it like A-Gwi.
In short, it wasn’t something you could easily get just because you had money. And no matter how rich you were, any sane person would use it to forge a weapon.
There weren’t many people crazy and rich enough to mix Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron into an iron chest that was nothing more than a storage box.
Of course...
*I can think of one right away.*
I gave a bitter smile and ran my hand over the chest.
As if to prove it had been buried deep underground, its surface was damp, and patches of soil that hadn’t been brushed off gave off a strong earthy smell.
*What could it be? What did you want to hide so badly?*
I was thinking of the chest’s former owner, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, when Hong Jin rose to his feet with a wink.
“I’ll get going. I’d only be in your way if I stayed.”
He didn’t wait for my answer before leaving the room. Before closing the door, he passed along one more message.
“Oh, His Highness the Imperial Younger Brother asked me to tell you something.”
“What...?”
“He misses his one and only friend. He can’t come see you right now because of the circumstances, but he wants to make sure he sees you before he leaves.”
His one and only friend.
Remembering what he’d said when he gave me the Myriad-Poison Ring at Qianqing Palace, I couldn’t help laughing softly.
“Tell him I feel the same way.”
Hong Jin answered with a slight smile of his own, then left. Once I’d confirmed that all signs of life around me had disappeared, I set the iron chest on the floor and abruptly held out my hand.
*Inventory open. Summon.*
*Ding.*
With the brief command recited in my mind, familiar, cold metal settled into my grip.
White Flame.
My personal weapon, a divine weapon forged by the world’s greatest smith after a year of arduous work.
And the key—the physical kind—to that tightly locked iron chest and its five padlocks.
“Let’s see what you were so determined to keep hidden.”
I murmured, then brought the spearhead down without hesitation.
*Slice.*
A flash of light, and the metal split apart.
The blade passed cleanly through all five padlocks in a single stroke. I looked inside the chest.
*This is...*
I’d known from the moment I first picked up the iron chest, but its contents were as spare as its weight was light.
A dozen or so bamboo slips, so old they were practically rotting away.
Alongside them lay bundles of relatively recent-looking paper, still white and clean, and a small silk pouch.
*What is this?*
The moment I saw them, an inexplicable shiver ran down my spine.
These were the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s—or, to put it another way, what he’d left behind.
They had to be worth more than gold and more dangerous than gunpowder, in ways that couldn’t be measured by their weight or shape alone.
It didn’t take long for me to realize my instinct was right.
No—it took only moments.
*Rustle.*
The moment I untied the string around the bundle of papers on top, still pristine white, a bolt of lightning shot through the crown of my head.
My entire body went rigid.
As I read the writing covering the pages, my eyes trembling, Hyuk Mujin’s voice reached me. I hadn’t heard him come back.
“Um, Captain. I don’t think I can bring him...”
His voice echoed as if from far away.
I struggled to contain the turmoil inside me and spoke.
“...Bring them.”
“What?”
“Bring everyone here. Now!”
Hyuk Mujin’s face went rigid. He’d sensed something was wrong.
